01-01.title: Roman consuls take office on 1 January for the first time
01-01.description: Rome's consuls began their year of office on 1 January rather than in March, a change made to speed armies to the war in Hispania. The date became the start of the civil year and, eventually, of the modern new year.

01-01.title: Julius Caesar's Julian calendar comes into force
01-01.description: The solar calendar devised for Julius Caesar replaced Rome's erratic lunisolar reckoning. With a leap day every fourth year, it governed Europe for over sixteen centuries and underlies the Gregorian calendar used today.

01-01.title: Roman Senate deifies the murdered Julius Caesar
01-01.description: Two years after his assassination, the Senate declared Julius Caesar a god of the Roman state as Divus Iulius. The honour let his adopted heir Octavian, the future Augustus, style himself 'son of a god'.

01-01.title: Monk Telemachus killed trying to halt gladiatorial games in Rome
01-01.description: According to Theodoret, the monk Telemachus leapt into the arena to separate fighting gladiators and was stoned to death by the crowd. Emperor Honorius is said to have banned gladiatorial combat in response.

01-01.title: Stephen I crowned as the first King of Hungary
01-01.description: By traditional reckoning Grand Prince Stephen was crowned with a crown sent by Pope Sylvester II, making Hungary a Christian kingdom. Stephen's reign anchored the Magyars within Latin Christendom.

01-01.title: Portuguese navigators enter Guanabara Bay and name it Rio de Janeiro
01-01.description: Sailing along the Brazilian coast, a Portuguese expedition entered Guanabara Bay and, taking it for a river mouth, called it the 'River of January'. The city founded there in 1565 would become colonial Brazil's capital.

01-01.title: Francis I becomes King of France on the death of Louis XII
01-01.description: Louis XII died without a son, and his twenty-year-old cousin and son-in-law Francis of Angoulême succeeded him. Francis became a great patron of the French Renaissance and a lifelong rival of Charles V.

01-01.title: Scotland begins its year on 1 January instead of 25 March
01-01.description: By decree of James VI, Scotland moved the start of its legal year from Lady Day to 1 January. England did not follow until 1752, so for 150 years the two kingdoms numbered their years differently.

01-01.title: Charles II crowned King of Scots at Scone
01-01.description: Two years after his father's execution, Charles II was crowned at Scone by the Scottish Covenanters, the last coronation held there. His bid to regain England ended in defeat at Worcester that September.

01-01.title: Peter the Great's Russia adopts the Anno Domini year count
01-01.description: On Peter the Great's orders, Russia abandoned counting years from the Creation and began numbering them from the birth of Christ, starting the year on 1 January. It was an early step in his drive to Westernise Russia.

01-01.title: Jean-Baptiste Bouvet sights the world's most remote island
01-01.description: The French navigator Bouvet de Lozier sighted the ice-capped island that bears his name in the South Atlantic. Lying about 1,600 km from Antarctica, Bouvet Island is the most isolated island on Earth.

01-01.title: John Newton's 'Amazing Grace' is first used at Olney
01-01.description: The curate John Newton, a former slave-ship captain, introduced the hymn later known as 'Amazing Grace' at a New Year's Day service in Olney, Buckinghamshire. Newton later became an outspoken opponent of the slave trade.

01-01.title: Washington's army raises the Grand Union Flag at Prospect Hill
01-01.description: During the siege of Boston, the Continental Army hoisted the Grand Union Flag on Prospect Hill near Cambridge, Massachusetts. Combining thirteen stripes with the British Union, it served as the first flag of the united colonies.

01-01.title: The Daily Universal Register becomes The Times
01-01.description: John Walter's three-year-old London paper published its first issue under the title The Times. It went on to become Britain's newspaper of record and one of the most influential journals in the world.

01-01.title: Giuseppe Piazzi discovers Ceres from Palermo
01-01.description: Searching the night sky from Palermo Observatory, Piazzi spotted a moving point of light: Ceres, the first object found in the asteroid belt. Long classed as a planet, then an asteroid, it is now termed a dwarf planet.

01-01.title: Act of Union creates the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
01-01.description: The union of Great Britain and Ireland took effect, abolishing the Irish Parliament and sending Irish members to Westminster. The arrangement lasted until the creation of the Irish Free State in 1922.

01-01.title: Haiti declares independence from France
01-01.description: Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed the independence of Haiti at Gonaïves after more than a decade of revolution. It became the first state founded by formerly enslaved people and the second independent nation in the Americas.

01-01.title: United States bans the importation of enslaved Africans
01-01.description: The Act Prohibiting Importation of Slaves came into force, outlawing the transatlantic slave trade to the United States. Slavery itself and the domestic slave trade continued until the Civil War.

01-01.title: Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' is published anonymously
01-01.description: 'Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus' appeared in London in three volumes without its author's name. Mary Shelley's tale of a scientist and his creation is often called the first science-fiction novel.

01-01.title: The Zollverein customs union takes effect in Germany
01-01.description: Led by Prussia, most German states abolished tariffs between them and formed a single customs area. The Zollverein bound their economies together and prepared the ground for political unification in 1871.

01-01.title: Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation comes into force
01-01.description: Abraham Lincoln's proclamation declared enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states free. It turned the Civil War into a war against slavery and opened the Union army to Black soldiers.

01-01.title: Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar
01-01.description: At a vast imperial assembly in Delhi, Viceroy Lord Lytton proclaimed Victoria Empress of India. The new title, devised by Disraeli, marked the British Raj's claim to succeed the Mughal emperors.

01-01.title: Italy proclaims the colony of Eritrea
01-01.description: Italy united its possessions on the Red Sea coast, centred on Massawa, into the colony of Eritrea. It became the base for Italian ambitions in the Horn of Africa, checked at Adwa in 1896.

01-01.title: Ellis Island opens as America's main immigration station
01-01.description: The federal immigration station on Ellis Island in New York Harbor processed its first arrivals, beginning with 17-year-old Annie Moore from Ireland. Some 12 million immigrants passed through it before 1954.

01-01.title: Six British colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
01-01.description: New South Wales, Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and Tasmania united under a federal constitution. Edmund Barton was sworn in as the first Prime Minister in Sydney's Centennial Park.

01-01.title: Sun Yat-sen proclaims the Republic of China in Nanjing
01-01.description: Sun Yat-sen was sworn in as provisional president of the new Republic of China. Six weeks later the last Qing emperor abdicated, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule.

01-01.title: World's first scheduled airline flight crosses Tampa Bay
01-01.description: The St Petersburg-Tampa Airboat Line flew its first paying passenger across Tampa Bay in a Benoist flying boat. The 23-minute hop launched scheduled commercial aviation, though the airline lasted only four months.

01-01.title: Twenty-six Allied nations sign the Declaration by United Nations
01-01.description: Meeting in Washington, the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union, China and others pledged to fight the Axis together and make no separate peace. The term 'United Nations' later named the post-war organisation.

01-01.title: American and British zones of Germany merge into the Bizone
01-01.description: The United States and Britain combined the economic administration of their occupation zones in Germany. The Bizone, joined by the French zone in 1949, became the nucleus of West Germany.

01-01.title: Sudan becomes independent from Britain and Egypt
01-01.description: Sudan's parliament ended the Anglo-Egyptian condominium and the country became a sovereign republic. It was among the first African states to gain independence after the Second World War.

01-01.title: The European Economic Community comes into being
01-01.description: The Treaty of Rome took effect, creating a common market among France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. The EEC was the forerunner of today's European Union.

01-01.title: Batista flees Cuba as Castro's revolution triumphs
01-01.description: Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Havana in the early hours, handing victory to Fidel Castro's guerrillas. The new revolutionary government later aligned with the Soviet Union, reshaping the Cold War in the Americas.

01-01.title: The Unix epoch: the zero point of computer time
01-01.description: Midnight UTC on this date was later chosen as the reference point from which Unix and its descendants count time in seconds. The convention still underpins timekeeping on most of the world's computers and phones.

01-01.title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the birth of the modern internet
01-01.description: On this 'flag day' the US defence research network ARPANET required all hosts to use the TCP/IP protocols. The common standard allowed separate networks to interconnect, forming the internet.

01-01.title: Brunei becomes fully independent from Britain
01-01.description: The oil-rich sultanate of Brunei ended nearly a century as a British protectorate and became a sovereign state under Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. It joined ASEAN within the week.

01-01.title: Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer enters into force
01-01.description: The treaty phasing out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting chemicals came into effect. Ratified by every UN member, it is widely regarded as the most successful environmental agreement ever made.

01-01.title: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully into two states
01-01.description: In the 'Velvet Divorce', Czechoslovakia dissolved by agreement into the Czech Republic and Slovakia. The separation was negotiated by politicians without a referendum and passed without violence.

01-01.title: NAFTA takes effect between the United States, Canada and Mexico
01-01.description: The North American Free Trade Agreement came into force, phasing out most tariffs among the three countries and creating one of the world's largest free-trade areas. It was replaced by the USMCA in 2020.

01-01.title: The World Trade Organization is established
01-01.description: The WTO began work in Geneva, succeeding the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade of 1947. Unlike GATT, it covered services and intellectual property and had a binding system for settling trade disputes.

01-01.title: The euro is launched in eleven European countries
01-01.description: The euro became the official currency of eleven EU states, used at first for electronic transactions and financial markets. National notes and coins remained in circulation for three more years.

01-01.title: Euro notes and coins enter circulation
01-01.description: Euro banknotes and coins went into circulation in twelve countries, the largest currency changeover in history. Within two months the franc, mark, lira, peseta and other national currencies had ceased to be legal tender.

01-01.title: Bulgaria and Romania join the European Union
01-01.description: The two Balkan states became the European Union's 26th and 27th members. Their accession completed the EU's great eastward enlargement into the former communist bloc that began in 2004.

01-01.title: Powerful earthquake devastates Japan's Noto Peninsula
01-01.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck Ishikawa Prefecture on New Year's Day, triggering tsunami warnings, fires and landslides. Including later disaster-related deaths, more than 500 people lost their lives.

01-02.title: Mercurius becomes Pope John II, the first pope to change his name
01-02.description: The Roman priest Mercurius, reluctant to reign under the name of a pagan god, took the name John II on his consecration. Adopting a papal name later became the settled custom of the Church.

01-02.title: Granada surrenders to Ferdinand and Isabella
01-02.description: Emir Muhammad XII handed the keys of Granada to the Catholic Monarchs, ending the last Muslim state in Iberia after nearly eight centuries. Months later the same monarchs sponsored Columbus's first voyage.

01-02.title: Maria Theresa abolishes judicial torture in Austria
01-02.description: Persuaded by reformers such as Joseph von Sonnenfels, Empress Maria Theresa ended the use of torture in criminal proceedings in her Austrian and Bohemian lands. It was a landmark of Enlightenment legal reform.

01-02.title: Washington repulses Cornwallis at Assunpink Creek
01-02.description: At the Second Battle of Trenton, Washington's army held the bridge over Assunpink Creek against repeated British attacks. That night the Americans slipped away to strike Princeton the next morning.

01-02.title: Georgia ratifies the US Constitution
01-02.description: Georgia's convention voted unanimously to ratify the new federal Constitution, making it the fourth state to do so. A frontier state facing conflict with the Creek, Georgia valued the protection of a stronger union.

01-02.title: Institution of Civil Engineers founded in London
01-02.description: Three young engineers met at a London coffee house to found the Institution of Civil Engineers. Under Thomas Telford, its president from 1820, it became the model for professional engineering bodies worldwide.

01-02.title: Union holds the field at the Battle of Stones River
01-02.description: A failed Confederate assault on the final day of fighting near Murfreesboro, Tennessee, led Braxton Bragg to withdraw. The costly Union success lifted Northern morale after the defeat at Fredericksburg.

01-02.title: John Hay promotes the Open Door Policy towards China
01-02.description: US Secretary of State John Hay pressed the great powers to grant equal trading rights in China and respect its territorial integrity. The Open Door became a cornerstone of American policy in East Asia.

01-02.title: Palmer Raids sweep up thousands of suspected radicals
01-02.description: Federal agents directed by Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer arrested thousands of suspected communists and anarchists in cities across the United States. The raids marked the height of the first Red Scare.

01-02.title: Japanese forces occupy Manila
01-02.description: Japanese troops entered Manila, declared an open city after American and Filipino forces withdrew to Bataan. The Philippine capital remained under Japanese occupation until its devastating liberation in 1945.

01-02.title: India institutes the Bharat Ratna, its highest civilian award
01-02.description: President Rajendra Prasad established the Bharat Ratna to honour exceptional national service. The first recipients were C. Rajagopalachari, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and the physicist C. V. Raman.

01-02.title: Soviet Union launches Luna 1 towards the Moon
01-02.description: Luna 1 lifted off from Baikonur and became the first spacecraft to reach escape velocity. It missed the Moon but passed close by and entered orbit around the Sun, the first human-made object to do so.

01-02.title: Viet Cong defeat a larger South Vietnamese force at Ap Bac
01-02.description: Communist guerrillas in the Mekong Delta beat off a South Vietnamese attack backed by American helicopters and advisers. The battle exposed weaknesses in the Saigon army and US optimism about the war.

01-02.title: NASA's Stardust probe flies through the tail of comet Wild 2
01-02.description: Stardust passed within about 240 km of comet Wild 2's nucleus, collecting dust in blocks of aerogel. The samples, returned to Earth in 2006, were the first material ever brought back from a comet.

01-03.title: Emperor Decius orders all Romans to sacrifice to the gods
01-03.description: Decius required every inhabitant of the empire to sacrifice before officials and obtain a certificate proving it. Christians who refused faced death, in the first empire-wide persecution of the Church.

01-03.title: Pope Leo X excommunicates Martin Luther
01-03.description: The bull Decet Romanum Pontificem formally cut Martin Luther off from the Catholic Church after he refused to recant. The break hardened the divide that became the Protestant Reformation.

01-03.title: Washington defeats the British at the Battle of Princeton
01-03.description: After a night march from Trenton, Washington's army routed a British force at Princeton, New Jersey. Coming days after Trenton, the victory revived the American cause and pushed the British out of most of New Jersey.

01-03.title: Britain reasserts control over the Falkland Islands
01-03.description: HMS Clio under Captain James Onslow arrived at the Falklands and required the small Argentine garrison at Port Louis to leave. Argentina has disputed British sovereignty over the islands ever since.

01-03.title: Joseph Jenkins Roberts becomes Liberia's first president
01-03.description: Joseph Jenkins Roberts, born free in Virginia, was inaugurated as president of the newly independent Republic of Liberia. Liberia became the first independent republic in Africa.

01-03.title: Meiji Restoration returns power to Japan's emperor
01-03.description: Forces from Satsuma and Choshu seized the imperial palace in Kyoto and an imperial decree abolished the Tokugawa shogunate. The young Emperor Meiji's government launched Japan's rapid modernisation.

01-03.title: Construction of the Brooklyn Bridge begins
01-03.description: Work started on John Roebling's suspension bridge across New York's East River. Completed in 1883 under his son Washington and daughter-in-law Emily, it was then the longest suspension bridge in the world.

01-03.title: Mussolini's speech to parliament opens his dictatorship
01-03.description: In a speech to the Italian Chamber of Deputies, Mussolini declared he alone took responsibility for all that had happened, including the murder of Giacomo Matteotti. The speech launched his open dictatorship.

01-03.title: US Congress proceedings are televised for the first time
01-03.description: The opening session of the 80th Congress was broadcast on television, a first for the American legislature. Regular television coverage of both chambers followed only decades later.

01-03.title: Alaska becomes the 49th US state
01-03.description: President Eisenhower signed the proclamation admitting Alaska to the Union. Purchased from Russia in 1867, it became the largest state by area, more than twice the size of Texas.

01-03.title: Bush and Yeltsin sign the START II arms treaty
01-03.description: In Moscow, George H. W. Bush and Boris Yeltsin agreed to cut their strategic nuclear arsenals by about two-thirds and ban multiple-warhead land-based missiles. The treaty never fully entered into force.

01-03.title: NASA's Spirit rover lands in Mars's Gusev Crater
01-03.description: Cushioned by airbags, Spirit bounced to a halt on Mars on the evening of 3 January, US time. Planned to last 90 days, it explored for over six years and found evidence of past water.

01-04.title: Caesar narrowly escapes defeat at the Battle of Ruspina
01-04.description: In North Africa, Julius Caesar's outnumbered army was surrounded by Republican forces under Titus Labienus. Caesar fought his way back to camp, surviving to defeat his enemies at Thapsus three months later.

01-04.title: Russian troops take Sofia from the Ottomans
01-04.description: During the Russo-Turkish War, Russian forces under General Gurko entered Sofia, ending nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule. The city became the capital of the new Bulgarian state the following year.

01-04.title: Fabian Society founded in London
01-04.description: A group of middle-class reformers founded the Fabian Society to promote socialism through gradual reform rather than revolution. Members such as the Webbs and George Bernard Shaw later helped shape the Labour Party.

01-04.title: Soviet Russia recognises Finland's independence
01-04.description: Lenin's government confirmed Finnish independence, declared in December 1917. Sweden, Germany and France recognised the new state the same day, though Finland soon slid into civil war.

01-04.title: Burma becomes independent from Britain
01-04.description: Burma left British rule as an independent republic outside the Commonwealth, at an hour chosen by astrologers. Independence hero Aung San had been assassinated six months earlier, and civil conflict soon followed.

01-04.title: Chinese and North Korean forces capture Seoul
01-04.description: United Nations troops abandoned Seoul as Chinese and North Korean armies advanced, the third time the city had changed hands in the Korean War. UN forces retook it in March.

01-04.title: Sputnik 1 falls from orbit
01-04.description: The first artificial satellite burned up in the atmosphere after three months and some 1,400 orbits. Its launch the previous October had shocked the United States and started the space race.

01-04.title: Luna 1 becomes the first spacecraft to pass the Moon
01-04.description: The Soviet probe flew within about 6,000 km of the Moon's surface before heading into orbit around the Sun. Its instruments made the first direct measurements of the solar wind.

01-05.title: Edward the Confessor dies, leaving England's throne disputed
01-05.description: King Edward died at Westminster without children. Rival claims by Harold Godwinson, Harald Hardrada and William of Normandy led to two invasions and the Norman Conquest that autumn.

01-05.title: Charles the Bold of Burgundy killed at the Battle of Nancy
01-05.description: Duke Charles the Bold died fighting Swiss and Lorrainer troops outside Nancy. His death ended Burgundian ambitions to become a kingdom, and his lands were divided between France and the Habsburgs.

01-05.title: Robert-François Damiens attempts to assassinate Louis XV
01-05.description: At Versailles, Damiens stabbed Louis XV with a penknife, causing only a slight wound. He was later executed with notorious cruelty, the last person in France to be put to death by quartering.

01-05.title: German Workers' Party founded in Munich
01-05.description: Railway locksmith Anton Drexler founded the small nationalist German Workers' Party. Adolf Hitler joined that autumn and in 1920 the party was renamed the National Socialist German Workers' Party.

01-05.title: Construction of the Golden Gate Bridge begins
01-05.description: Work began on a bridge across the Golden Gate strait at the entrance to San Francisco Bay. Opened in 1937, its 1,280-metre main span was the longest in the world until 1964.

01-05.title: Alexander Dubček takes charge in Czechoslovakia
01-05.description: Dubček replaced Antonín Novotný as leader of the Czechoslovak Communist Party. His reforms, 'socialism with a human face', inspired the Prague Spring, ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August.

01-06.title: Harold Godwinson crowned King of England
01-06.description: The day after Edward the Confessor's death, Harold was crowned, probably in Westminster Abbey. William of Normandy disputed the succession and invaded that autumn, killing Harold at Hastings.

01-06.title: Joan of Arc is born at Domrémy
01-06.description: By tradition Joan of Arc was born on Epiphany in the village of Domrémy, in north-eastern France. She led French forces to relieve Orléans in 1429, was burned in 1431 and canonised in 1920.

01-06.title: Alfred Vail and Samuel Morse demonstrate their telegraph
01-06.description: At the Speedwell Ironworks in New Jersey, Vail and Morse sent messages over two miles of wire using an early form of their code. Telegraph lines soon spread across America and the world.

01-06.title: Maria Montessori opens her first Casa dei Bambini
01-06.description: In a tenement in Rome's San Lorenzo district, Montessori opened a 'children's house' for working families. The child-led methods she developed there spread to schools across the world.

01-06.title: Alfred Wegener presents his theory of continental drift
01-06.description: At a geology meeting in Frankfurt, Wegener argued that the continents had once formed a single landmass and drifted apart. Long rejected, the idea was vindicated by plate tectonics in the 1960s.

01-06.title: Roosevelt sets out the 'Four Freedoms'
01-06.description: In his State of the Union address, Franklin Roosevelt named freedom of speech, freedom of worship, freedom from want and freedom from fear as universal rights. The speech shaped Allied war aims and the UN.

01-06.title: Britain recognises the People's Republic of China
01-06.description: The United Kingdom became the first major Western power to recognise Mao Zedong's communist government in Beijing. The decision, partly aimed at protecting Hong Kong, split Britain from US policy.

01-07.title: France captures Calais, England's last mainland possession
01-07.description: French troops under the Duke of Guise forced the surrender of Calais, held by England since 1347. Mary I reportedly said that when she died 'Calais' would be found lying in her heart.

01-07.title: Galileo first observes the moons of Jupiter
01-07.description: Through his improved telescope, Galileo saw small 'stars' beside Jupiter that he soon realised were orbiting it. Bodies circling another planet undermined the belief that everything revolved around Earth.

01-07.title: Blanchard and Jeffries fly a balloon across the English Channel
01-07.description: The Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and the American John Jeffries crossed from Dover to the Forest of Guînes in a hydrogen balloon. They jettisoned almost everything, including clothes, to stay aloft.

01-07.title: First commercial transatlantic telephone service opens
01-07.description: A radio-telephone link connected New York and London for paying customers. A three-minute call cost 75 dollars, and transatlantic telephone cables did not arrive until 1956.

01-07.title: Truman announces the United States has built a hydrogen bomb
01-07.description: In his final State of the Union message, Harry Truman disclosed that the US had developed the hydrogen bomb, tested in November 1952. Its power dwarfed the atomic bombs used against Japan.

01-07.title: Vietnamese forces capture Phnom Penh and topple the Khmer Rouge
01-07.description: Vietnam's army took the Cambodian capital, ending Pol Pot's regime, under which some 1.5 to 2 million people had died. A decade of Vietnamese occupation and guerrilla war followed.

01-07.title: Gunmen kill twelve at the Paris offices of Charlie Hebdo
01-07.description: Two Islamist gunmen attacked the satirical weekly Charlie Hebdo, killing twelve people including leading cartoonists. Millions marched in France days later under the slogan 'Je suis Charlie'.

01-08.title: François Grimaldi seizes the fortress of Monaco
01-08.description: Disguised as a Franciscan friar, the Genoese Guelph François Grimaldi talked his way into the Rock of Monaco and took it. His descendants, the House of Grimaldi, still rule the principality.

01-08.title: Andrew Jackson defeats the British at New Orleans
01-08.description: Jackson's mixed force repulsed a British assault on New Orleans, inflicting some 2,000 casualties. Fought after the Treaty of Ghent was signed but before news arrived, it made Jackson a national hero.

01-08.title: Woodrow Wilson presents his Fourteen Points
01-08.description: Addressing Congress, President Wilson outlined a peace programme including open diplomacy, free seas, self-determination and a league of nations. It framed the armistice and the Paris Peace Conference.

01-08.title: Abdulaziz ibn Saud proclaimed King of the Hejaz
01-08.description: After conquering Mecca and Medina, the Sultan of Nejd was proclaimed King of the Hejaz in the Great Mosque of Mecca. In 1932 he merged his realms into the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

01-08.title: Britain introduces food rationing
01-08.description: Bacon, butter and sugar became the first foods rationed in wartime Britain. Rationing extended to most foods during the war and did not end entirely until 1954.

01-08.title: Charles de Gaulle takes office as President of France
01-08.description: De Gaulle became the first President of the Fifth Republic, whose constitution greatly strengthened the executive. He governed France until 1969, ending the war in Algeria in 1962.

01-09.title: Jin armies sack Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song
01-09.description: In the Jingkang incident, Jurchen troops of the Jin dynasty sacked Kaifeng and carried off the Song emperors Qinzong and Huizong. The Song court fled south, where it ruled as the Southern Song.

01-09.title: Trial of Joan of Arc opens in Rouen
01-09.description: A church court led by Bishop Pierre Cauchon, an ally of the English, began proceedings against Joan of Arc on charges of heresy. She was condemned and burned at the stake on 30 May.

01-09.title: First shock of the great Sicilian earthquake strikes
01-09.description: A strong foreshock damaged towns across south-eastern Sicily. Two days later the main earthquake devastated the region, killing some 60,000 people and leading to the Baroque rebuilding of Noto and Catania.

01-09.title: Connecticut ratifies the US Constitution
01-09.description: Connecticut's convention approved the Constitution by 128 votes to 40, making it the fifth state to ratify. Nine states were needed for the new frame of government to take effect.

01-09.title: Treaty of Jassy ends the Russo-Turkish War
01-09.description: The Ottoman Empire recognised Russia's annexation of Crimea and ceded the coast between the Bug and Dniester rivers. The treaty confirmed Russia as the dominant power on the northern Black Sea.

01-09.title: Blanchard makes the first balloon flight in North America
01-09.description: Watched by President George Washington, the French aeronaut Jean-Pierre Blanchard ascended from a prison yard in Philadelphia. He landed some 46 minutes later in Deptford, New Jersey.

01-09.title: Pitt's income tax becomes law in Britain
01-09.description: William Pitt the Younger's income tax, set at two shillings in the pound on higher incomes, received royal assent to fund the war against Revolutionary France. Abolished in 1816, it returned for good in 1842.

01-09.title: Admiral Nelson is buried in St Paul's Cathedral
01-09.description: After a vast procession through London, Horatio Nelson was laid to rest in the crypt of St Paul's. He had been killed at his victory at Trafalgar the previous October.

01-09.title: Cadets fire on the Star of the West in Charleston Harbor
01-09.description: Southern guns fired on the merchant ship Star of the West as it tried to resupply Fort Sumter, forcing it to turn back. The shots are sometimes called the first of the American Civil War.

01-09.title: Last Allied troops evacuate Gallipoli
01-09.description: British troops left Cape Helles, ending the Gallipoli campaign in an Ottoman victory. The evacuation was the most successful part of an eight-month operation that cost well over 100,000 lives on both sides.

01-09.title: Juan de la Cierva's autogiro makes its first successful flight
01-09.description: At Getafe near Madrid, the Spanish engineer's C.4 autogiro flew using a freely turning rotor for lift. The design pioneered rotor technology later used in helicopters.

01-09.title: Anthony Eden resigns as British Prime Minister
01-09.description: Citing ill health, Eden stepped down two months after the Suez Crisis, in which Britain and France had been forced by American pressure to withdraw from Egypt. Harold Macmillan succeeded him.

01-10.title: Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon
01-10.description: Leading a legion across the small river that marked the border of Italy, Caesar defied the Senate and made civil war inevitable. 'The die is cast', he reportedly said. The war ended the Roman Republic.

01-10.title: Normans under Robert Guiscard capture Palermo
01-10.description: After a five-month siege, Robert Guiscard and his brother Roger took Palermo from its Muslim rulers. The conquest paved the way for the Norman Kingdom of Sicily, a meeting place of Latin, Greek and Arab cultures.

01-10.title: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Fleece
01-10.description: At his wedding celebrations in Bruges, the Duke of Burgundy created an exclusive order of knighthood. It passed to the Habsburgs and survives today in Spanish and Austrian branches.

01-10.title: Thomas Paine publishes 'Common Sense'
01-10.description: Paine's plain-spoken pamphlet argued that the American colonies should declare independence from Britain. It sold tens of thousands of copies within months and helped turn opinion towards independence.

01-10.title: Uniform Penny Post introduced in Britain
01-10.description: Rowland Hill's reform let a letter travel anywhere in Britain for one penny, paid by the sender. Letter volumes soared, and the Penny Black, the first adhesive stamp, followed in May.

01-10.title: Florida secedes from the Union
01-10.description: Florida's convention voted 62 to 7 to leave the United States, the third state to do so after South Carolina and Mississippi. It joined the Confederate States the following month.

01-10.title: Spindletop gusher erupts in Texas
01-10.description: Oil burst from the Lucas well at Spindletop near Beaumont, spouting over 40 metres high for nine days. The strike created the Texas oil boom and made petroleum cheap enough to fuel the motor age.

01-10.title: League of Nations comes into existence
01-10.description: The Treaty of Versailles came into force, and with it the Covenant of the League of Nations, the first permanent organisation for keeping world peace. The United States never joined.

01-10.title: First UN General Assembly meets in London
01-10.description: Delegates from 51 nations gathered at Methodist Central Hall, Westminster, for the first session of the United Nations General Assembly. The UN later moved its headquarters to New York.

01-10.title: BOAC Comet airliner breaks up over the Mediterranean
01-10.description: A de Havilland Comet, the world's first jet airliner, disintegrated near Elba, killing all 35 aboard. Investigations traced the disaster to metal fatigue, transforming aircraft design and testing.

01-10.title: United States and the Holy See establish full diplomatic relations
01-10.description: President Reagan's administration and the Vatican agreed to exchange ambassadors, ending a gap in formal relations since 1867. The move reflected close cooperation with Pope John Paul II during the Cold War.

01-11.title: Muhammad enters Mecca and clears the Kaaba of idols
01-11.description: By the usual reckoning, Muhammad and some 10,000 followers took Mecca with little bloodshed. The idols around the Kaaba were destroyed and it was rededicated as the centre of Islamic worship.

01-11.title: Vladislaus II becomes King of Bohemia
01-11.description: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa granted Duke Vladislaus II a royal crown in return for support in Italy. He was crowned at Regensburg, only the second Bohemian ruler to hold the title of king.

01-11.title: England's first recorded state lottery is drawn
01-11.description: Chartered by Elizabeth I to raise money for harbours and public works, England's first state lottery was drawn at the west door of St Paul's Cathedral. Ticket holders were promised immunity from arrest for minor crimes.

01-11.title: William Herschel discovers Titania and Oberon
01-11.description: Six years after finding Uranus, Herschel spotted its two largest moons. They were later named after the king and queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'.

01-11.title: Alabama secedes from the Union
01-11.description: Alabama's convention voted 61 to 39 to leave the United States, the fourth state to secede. Its capital Montgomery hosted the founding of the Confederate States the next month.

01-11.title: Insulin is first given to a diabetic patient
01-11.description: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson received an insulin extract at Toronto General Hospital. The first dose failed, but a purer extract made by James Collip saved his life later that month.

01-11.title: Amelia Earhart sets out on the first solo flight from Hawaii
01-11.description: Earhart took off from Honolulu and landed in Oakland, California, about 18 hours later. She became the first person to fly solo across this stretch of the Pacific, some 3,900 km.

01-11.title: Albania proclaimed a People's Republic
01-11.description: Albania's assembly abolished the monarchy and declared a People's Republic under communist leader Enver Hoxha. His regime became one of the most isolated and repressive in Europe.

01-11.title: US Surgeon General reports that smoking causes cancer
01-11.description: Luther Terry's advisory committee concluded that cigarette smoking causes lung cancer in men. The report led to health warnings on cigarette packets and decades of anti-smoking policy.

01-12.title: Gustav Vasa crowned King of Sweden at Uppsala
01-12.description: Five years after his election ended the Kalmar Union with Denmark, Gustav I was crowned in Uppsala Cathedral. He went on to build a strong hereditary monarchy and introduce the Lutheran Reformation.

01-12.title: Empress Elizabeth founds Moscow University
01-12.description: Empress Elizabeth signed the decree founding Moscow University, proposed by Ivan Shuvalov and Mikhail Lomonosov (12 January Old Style). Russia's oldest university now bears Lomonosov's name.

01-12.title: Aeronautical Society of Great Britain founded
01-12.description: The society, later the Royal Aeronautical Society, was founded in London to study flight decades before the first aeroplane. It is the oldest aeronautical society in the world.

01-12.title: First long-distance radio message sent from the Eiffel Tower
01-12.description: A transmitter on the Eiffel Tower sent a wireless message over a record distance. The tower's value for military radio helped secure its future after its original 20-year permit.

01-12.title: Hattie Caraway becomes the first woman elected to the US Senate
01-12.description: Appointed to succeed her late husband, Hattie Caraway of Arkansas won a special election to keep the seat. She went on to win two full terms and served until 1945.

01-12.title: Red Army launches the Vistula-Oder Offensive
01-12.description: Soviet forces burst out of their bridgeheads in Poland and advanced some 500 km in under three weeks. By early February they stood on the Oder, about 70 km from Berlin.

01-12.title: Biafra announces its surrender, ending the Nigerian Civil War
01-12.description: Biafra's acting leader Philip Effiong announced the end of the secessionist state's resistance. Between half a million and two million people had died, many from famine caused by the blockade.

01-12.title: Catastrophic earthquake strikes Haiti
01-12.description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake hit near Port-au-Prince, destroying much of the capital. Estimates of the dead range from about 100,000 to over 300,000, and more than a million people were left homeless.

01-13.title: Nika riots break out in Constantinople
01-13.description: Rival chariot-racing factions united against Emperor Justinian and burned much of the city. Urged by Empress Theodora not to flee, Justinian had the rising crushed, with some 30,000 killed.

01-13.title: Council of Troyes endorses the Knights Templar
01-13.description: A church council at Troyes, led by a papal legate and inspired by Bernard of Clairvaux, approved a rule for the Knights Templar. The order of warrior monks became a major force in the Crusades.

01-13.title: Treaty of Cahuenga ends the fighting in California
01-13.description: Californio leader Andrés Pico and John C. Frémont signed an informal capitulation near Los Angeles. It ended hostilities in California, which Mexico ceded to the United States in 1848.

01-13.title: Émile Zola publishes 'J'accuse...!'
01-13.description: Zola's open letter in L'Aurore accused the French army of convicting the Jewish officer Alfred Dreyfus wrongly and covering up the truth. It turned the Dreyfus affair into a national crisis.

01-13.title: Avezzano earthquake devastates central Italy
01-13.description: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck the Abruzzo region, killing about 30,000 people. In Avezzano itself almost all of the population perished.

01-13.title: Henry Ford patents a plastic car body
01-13.description: Henry Ford received a patent for a car body built from plastic panels on a tubular frame, part of his experiments with materials derived from soybeans. Wartime restrictions ended the project.

01-13.title: Johnny Cash performs at Folsom State Prison
01-13.description: Johnny Cash played two shows for inmates at Folsom Prison in California, recorded for a live album. 'At Folsom Prison' revived his career and became one of the best-known albums in country music.

01-13.title: Soviet troops storm the Vilnius television tower
01-13.description: Soviet forces attacked unarmed crowds defending Lithuanian broadcasting sites in Vilnius, killing 14 civilians. The violence strengthened support for Baltic independence at home and abroad.

01-14.title: Henry III of England marries Eleanor of Provence
01-14.description: Henry III married the twelve-year-old Eleanor of Provence at Canterbury Cathedral. Her many relatives at court provoked resentment among English barons in the years before the Second Barons' War.

01-14.title: Death of Andrew III ends Hungary's Árpád dynasty
01-14.description: Andrew III died without a son, ending the male line of the Árpád dynasty, which had led the Magyars since the conquest of the Carpathian Basin. Years of succession war followed.

01-14.title: Connecticut adopts the Fundamental Orders
01-14.description: Settlers of Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield agreed the Fundamental Orders, setting up an elected government. The document is often called the first written constitution in the Western tradition.

01-14.title: Afghan army defeats the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat
01-14.description: Ahmad Shah Durrani's army crushed the Maratha forces north of Delhi in one of the largest battles of the century. The defeat halted Maratha expansion and helped open the way to British power in India.

01-14.title: Felice Orsini attempts to assassinate Napoleon III
01-14.description: The Italian nationalist Orsini and his accomplices threw bombs at the Emperor's carriage outside the Paris Opéra, killing eight people. Napoleon III escaped and soon backed Piedmont against Austria.

01-14.title: Earthquake and fire destroy much of Kingston, Jamaica
01-14.description: An earthquake and the fires that followed wrecked Jamaica's capital, killing about 1,000 people. Much of the city's historic core was rebuilt in reinforced concrete.

01-14.title: Roosevelt and Churchill meet at Casablanca
01-14.description: The Casablanca Conference agreed to invade Sicily and intensify the bombing of Germany. At its close Roosevelt announced that the Allies would accept only unconditional surrender.

01-14.title: Marilyn Monroe marries Joe DiMaggio
01-14.description: The film star and the retired New York Yankees hero married at San Francisco City Hall. The marriage lasted less than a year, though DiMaggio remained devoted to Monroe until her death.

01-14.title: De Gaulle vetoes Britain's entry into the Common Market
01-14.description: At a press conference in Paris, Charles de Gaulle rejected Britain's application to join the EEC. He vetoed a second application in 1967, and Britain joined only in 1973.

01-15.title: Emperor Galba murdered in the Roman Forum
01-15.description: Praetorians loyal to Otho killed the elderly Galba after just seven months as emperor. Otho, then Vitellius and finally Vespasian took power in the turmoil known as the Year of the Four Emperors.

01-15.title: Elizabeth I is crowned at Westminster Abbey
01-15.description: Elizabeth, daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, was crowned on a date chosen by her astrologer John Dee. Her 44-year reign saw a Protestant settlement, the Armada's defeat and a flowering of literature.

01-15.title: Truce of Jam Zapolski ends Russia's war with Poland-Lithuania
01-15.description: Ivan the Terrible gave up his conquests in Livonia to Stefan Batory's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The truce ended Russia's long attempt to win a foothold on the Baltic.

01-15.title: British Museum opens to the public
01-15.description: Founded on the collections of the physician Sir Hans Sloane, the British Museum opened in Montagu House, Bloomsbury. It was one of the first national museums open to all 'studious and curious persons'.

01-15.title: Vermont declares itself an independent republic
01-15.description: Settlers in the New Hampshire Grants declared independence as New Connecticut, renamed Vermont that summer. The republic outlawed adult slavery and joined the United States as the 14th state in 1791.

01-15.title: Thomas Nast's cartoon links the Democrats with a donkey
01-15.description: Nast's cartoon 'A Live Jackass Kicking a Dead Lion' in Harper's Weekly portrayed anti-war Democrats as a donkey. The donkey later became the accepted symbol of the Democratic Party.

01-15.title: Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht murdered in Berlin
01-15.description: After the defeat of the Spartacist uprising, the two communist leaders were seized and killed by Freikorps soldiers. The murders deepened the bitter split on the German left.

01-15.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is born in Atlanta
01-15.description: Born Michael King Jr., the son of a Baptist minister, he became the leading voice of the American civil rights movement. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964 and was assassinated in 1968.

01-15.title: The Pentagon is completed in Arlington, Virginia
01-15.description: Built in just 16 months, the five-sided headquarters of the US War Department was dedicated. With some 6.5 million square feet of floor space, it was the world's largest office building.

01-15.title: Nixon suspends offensive action against North Vietnam
01-15.description: Citing progress in the Paris peace talks, Richard Nixon halted US bombing and mining of North Vietnam. The Paris Peace Accords, signed twelve days later, ended direct American involvement in the war.

01-16.title: The 'Great Drowning of Men' storm surge hits the North Sea coast
01-16.description: A severe south-westerly gale drove the sea over the coasts of England, the Low Countries, Germany and Denmark. At least 25,000 people died, and the trading town of Rungholt vanished beneath the waves.

01-16.title: Ivan IV crowned the first Tsar of All Russia
01-16.description: Aged 16, Ivan IV was crowned in the Kremlin's Dormition Cathedral with the title of tsar. His reign brought the conquest of Kazan and Astrakhan as well as the terror of the oprichnina.

01-16.title: Rodney defeats the Spanish in the 'Moonlight Battle'
01-16.description: Admiral George Rodney's larger British fleet overwhelmed a Spanish squadron off Cape St Vincent in an unusual night action. The victory allowed him to resupply besieged Gibraltar.

01-16.title: Ratification of the Eighteenth Amendment sets up Prohibition
01-16.description: Nebraska became the 36th state to ratify the amendment banning the manufacture and sale of alcohol, making it part of the US Constitution. Prohibition took effect a year later and lasted until 1933.

01-16.title: League of Nations Council holds its first meeting
01-16.description: The League's Council met for the first time in Paris, at the French Foreign Ministry. The League settled some minor disputes but failed to stop aggression in the 1930s.

01-16.title: Hitler moves into the Führerbunker in Berlin
01-16.description: Adolf Hitler took up residence in the air-raid shelter beneath the Reich Chancellery garden. He directed the final months of the war from there and killed himself in the bunker on 30 April.

01-16.title: Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 make the first crewed docking
01-16.description: Two Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit and two cosmonauts spacewalked from Soyuz 5 to Soyuz 4. It was the first exchange of crew between spacecraft, a rehearsal for building space stations.

01-16.title: Space Shuttle Columbia launches on its final mission
01-16.description: Columbia lifted off on mission STS-107 with seven astronauts. Foam debris struck its wing during launch, and the shuttle broke apart on re-entry sixteen days later, killing the crew.

01-17.title: Pope Gregory XI returns the papacy to Rome
01-17.description: Urged on by Catherine of Siena, Gregory XI entered Rome, ending almost seven decades in which the popes had lived at Avignon. His death the next year set off the Great Western Schism.

01-17.title: James Cook makes the first recorded crossing of the Antarctic Circle
01-17.description: HMS Resolution and HMS Adventure sailed south of 66°33' S, the first ships known to do so. Cook's voyage showed that any southern continent must lie far to the south, beyond the pack ice.

01-17.title: Daniel Morgan routs Tarleton at the Battle of Cowpens
01-17.description: In South Carolina, Daniel Morgan's Continentals and militia destroyed Banastre Tarleton's British force with a skilful double envelopment. The victory was a turning point in the southern campaign.

01-17.title: Hawaii's Queen Liliuokalani overthrown
01-17.description: A committee of American and European businessmen, supported by US Marines from the USS Boston, deposed the Hawaiian queen and set up a provisional government. The United States annexed Hawaii in 1898.

01-17.title: Soviet and Polish troops enter the ruins of Warsaw
01-17.description: The Red Army and the Polish First Army took Warsaw, abandoned by the Germans. After the crushing of the 1944 Uprising, the Germans had systematically razed the city, destroying about 85 per cent of it.

01-17.title: UN Security Council meets for the first time
01-17.description: The United Nations Security Council held its first session at Church House, Westminster. Its five permanent members, each with a veto, were the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France and China.

01-17.title: Eisenhower warns of the 'military-industrial complex'
01-17.description: In his televised farewell address, the outgoing President cautioned that a permanent arms industry and huge defence establishment could acquire 'unwarranted influence' over American government.

01-17.title: Operation Desert Storm opens with air strikes on Iraq
01-17.description: A US-led coalition began a massive air campaign against Iraq, which had occupied Kuwait since August 1990. A ground offensive in late February expelled Iraqi forces within 100 hours.

01-17.title: Great Hanshin earthquake devastates Kobe
01-17.description: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Kobe region before dawn, killing 6,434 people and destroying over 100,000 buildings. The slow official response prompted reform of Japan's disaster planning.

01-18.title: Francisco Pizarro founds Lima
01-18.description: Pizarro founded the 'City of Kings' on the Rímac river near the Pacific coast. Lima became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru, created in 1542, and the centre of Spanish rule in South America.

01-18.title: Pereiaslav Council places the Cossack Hetmanate under the Tsar
01-18.description: Hetman Bohdan Khmelnytsky and his Cossack officers swore allegiance to Tsar Alexei in return for protection against Poland-Lithuania. The agreement's meaning remains disputed in Ukrainian and Russian history.

01-18.title: James Cook becomes the first European to sight Hawaii
01-18.description: On his third voyage, Cook sighted Oahu and then Kauai, where he landed two days later. He named the archipelago the Sandwich Islands and was killed there in February 1779.

01-18.title: Wilhelm I proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles
01-18.description: In the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, with Paris still under siege, Prussia's king was proclaimed Emperor of a united Germany. Bismarck's creation dominated continental Europe until 1918.

01-18.title: Japan presents its Twenty-One Demands to China
01-18.description: Japan secretly pressed Yuan Shikai's government for extensive rights in Shandong, Manchuria and beyond. China accepted a reduced version under ultimatum, fuelling Chinese nationalism against Japan.

01-18.title: Soviet forces open a land corridor into besieged Leningrad
01-18.description: In Operation Iskra, Soviet troops linked up south of Lake Ladoga, creating a narrow corridor into Leningrad after 16 months of siege. The blockade was finally lifted in January 1944.

01-18.title: Willie O'Ree breaks the NHL colour barrier
01-18.description: Playing for the Boston Bruins against the Montreal Canadiens, Willie O'Ree became the first Black player in the National Hockey League, despite being almost blind in one eye.

01-19.title: Rouen surrenders to Henry V
01-19.description: After a six-month siege that left thousands starving, Rouen yielded to Henry V of England, completing his conquest of Normandy. The Treaty of Troyes in 1420 made him heir to the French throne.

01-19.title: Verdi's 'Il trovatore' premieres in Rome
01-19.description: Giuseppe Verdi's opera of passion and revenge opened at the Teatro Apollo to great acclaim. With 'Rigoletto' and 'La traviata', it is one of the three popular masterpieces of his middle period.

01-19.title: Zeppelins bomb Britain for the first time
01-19.description: German airships dropped bombs on Great Yarmouth, Sheringham and King's Lynn in Norfolk, killing four civilians. It was the first air raid on Britain, opening a new front in the war.

01-19.title: Zimmermann Telegram is forwarded to Mexico
01-19.description: Germany's ambassador in Washington relayed Arthur Zimmermann's secret offer of an alliance to Mexico, promising Texas, New Mexico and Arizona. Decoded by British intelligence, its publication helped bring the US into the war.

01-19.title: Howard Hughes sets a transcontinental air speed record
01-19.description: Hughes flew his H-1 racer from Burbank, California, to Newark, New Jersey, in 7 hours, 28 minutes and 25 seconds. The record stood for seven years.

01-19.title: Indira Gandhi chosen to lead India
01-19.description: The Congress parliamentary party elected Indira Gandhi as its leader after the sudden death of Lal Bahadur Shastri. Sworn in five days later, she became India's first and only woman prime minister.

01-19.title: Apple announces the Lisa computer
01-19.description: Apple unveiled the Lisa, a personal computer with a graphical interface and a mouse. At nearly 10,000 dollars it sold poorly, but its ideas fed directly into the Macintosh a year later.

01-20.title: Simon de Montfort's Parliament meets at Westminster
01-20.description: Ruling in the name of the captive Henry III, Simon de Montfort summoned knights from the shires and, for the first time, burgesses from the towns. It is seen as a forerunner of the House of Commons.

01-20.title: Trial of Charles I opens in Westminster Hall
01-20.description: A High Court of Justice set up by the Rump Parliament tried the King for treason against his people. Charles refused to recognise its authority and was beheaded ten days later.

01-20.title: Britain agrees preliminary peace with France and Spain
01-20.description: Preliminary articles signed at Versailles ended hostilities between Britain and the Bourbon powers. With peace with the United States already agreed, the war that won American independence was over.

01-20.title: Convention of Chuenpi cedes Hong Kong Island to Britain
01-20.description: During the First Opium War, Charles Elliot and the Qing envoy Qishan agreed terms ceding Hong Kong Island. Neither government accepted the deal, but the 1842 Treaty of Nanking confirmed the cession.

01-20.title: George V dies and Edward VIII becomes king
01-20.description: King George V died at Sandringham, and his eldest son succeeded as Edward VIII. Edward abdicated before the end of the year to marry Wallis Simpson, the only voluntary abdication in British history.

01-20.title: Nazi officials meet at Wannsee to coordinate the Holocaust
01-20.description: Chaired by Reinhard Heydrich, senior officials met at a villa on the Wannsee in Berlin to organise the 'Final Solution', the deportation and murder of Europe's Jews. The minutes survived the war.

01-20.title: John F. Kennedy is inaugurated as US President
01-20.description: At 43, Kennedy became the youngest person elected President. His inaugural address urged Americans to 'ask what you can do for your country'. He was assassinated less than three years later.

01-20.title: Iran releases 52 American hostages after 444 days
01-20.description: Minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in, Iran freed the Americans held since the seizure of the US embassy in Tehran in 1979. The crisis had overshadowed Jimmy Carter's final year in office.

01-20.title: Barack Obama inaugurated as the first African American President
01-20.description: Before a crowd of some 1.8 million on the National Mall, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th President of the United States, taking office amid a deep financial crisis.

01-21.title: First adult baptisms in Zurich launch the Anabaptist movement
01-21.description: Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz and George Blaurock baptised one another as believing adults in Zurich. Fiercely persecuted, their movement gave rise to the Mennonites, Amish and Hutterites.

01-21.title: Louis XVI is guillotined in Paris
01-21.description: Convicted of conspiracy against the nation, the former king was executed in the Place de la Révolution. His death set revolutionary France against the crowned heads of Europe.

01-21.title: Jefferson Davis bids farewell to the US Senate
01-21.description: Following Mississippi's secession, Davis and four other Southern senators gave farewell speeches and resigned. Within weeks he was chosen as President of the Confederate States.

01-21.title: New York passes an ordinance banning women from smoking in public
01-21.description: The Sullivan Ordinance barred managers of public places from allowing women to smoke. Mayor George McClellan vetoed it two weeks later, but it reflected anxieties about women's changing roles.

01-21.title: Vladimir Lenin dies at Gorki
01-21.description: The founder of the Soviet state died aged 53 after a series of strokes. His body was embalmed and displayed in Red Square, and Stalin outmanoeuvred Trotsky and others to succeed him.

01-21.title: USS Nautilus, the first nuclear-powered submarine, is launched
01-21.description: First Lady Mamie Eisenhower christened Nautilus at Groton, Connecticut. Able to stay submerged for weeks, it sailed under the North Pole in 1958 and transformed undersea warfare.

01-21.title: Concorde begins commercial supersonic service
01-21.description: British Airways flew Concorde from London to Bahrain and Air France from Paris to Rio de Janeiro via Dakar. Flying at twice the speed of sound, Concorde served passengers until 2003.

01-22.title: Ottomans defeat the Mamluks at Ridaniya outside Cairo
01-22.description: Selim I's army, with superior artillery and firearms, crushed the Mamluk forces just outside Cairo. The victory ended the Mamluk Sultanate and brought Egypt, Syria and the Hejaz under Ottoman rule.

01-22.title: British defeat the French at Wandiwash
01-22.description: Sir Eyre Coote's East India Company army beat the Comte de Lally's French force in the Carnatic. The battle effectively ended French hopes of empire in India.

01-22.title: Zulu army destroys a British force at Isandlwana
01-22.description: Some 20,000 Zulu warriors overran a British camp at Isandlwana, killing over 1,300 soldiers and African auxiliaries. It was one of the worst defeats of the British army in the colonial era.

01-22.title: Queen Victoria dies at Osborne House
01-22.description: Victoria died on the Isle of Wight aged 81 after reigning for 63 years, then the longest reign in British history. Her son succeeded as Edward VII.

01-22.title: Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg sparks revolution
01-22.description: Imperial troops fired on unarmed workers led by Father Georgy Gapon marching to petition Tsar Nicholas II, killing many. The massacre set off the 1905 Revolution and badly damaged faith in the Tsar.

01-22.title: Allied troops land at Anzio
01-22.description: In Operation Shingle, Allied forces landed behind German lines south of Rome, hoping to outflank the Gustav Line. Quickly contained, they endured four months of hard fighting before breaking out.

01-22.title: US Supreme Court decides Roe v. Wade
01-22.description: By seven votes to two, the Court ruled that the constitutional right to privacy protected a woman's decision to have an abortion. The ruling was overturned in 2022.

01-23.title: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming dynasty
01-23.description: The former peasant and rebel leader declared himself the Hongwu Emperor at Nanjing. The Ming drove out the Mongol Yuan and ruled China for 276 years.

01-23.title: Shaanxi earthquake, the deadliest on record, strikes China
01-23.description: An earthquake centred in the Wei River valley killed an estimated 830,000 people. Many died when cave dwellings carved into soft loess cliffs collapsed.

01-23.title: Elizabeth Blackwell becomes the first woman to earn a US medical degree
01-23.description: Admitted to Geneva Medical College in New York almost as a joke, Blackwell graduated top of her class. She went on to found hospitals and a medical college for women.

01-23.title: Netherlands refuses to hand over Kaiser Wilhelm II
01-23.description: The Dutch government rejected Allied demands to extradite the former German Emperor for trial under the Treaty of Versailles. Wilhelm lived in exile at Doorn until his death in 1941.

01-23.title: British Eighth Army captures Tripoli
01-23.description: Montgomery's troops entered Tripoli, three months after El Alamein, as Rommel's forces retreated into Tunisia. It ended Italy's North African empire.

01-23.title: North Korea seizes the USS Pueblo
01-23.description: North Korean vessels captured the US Navy intelligence ship off Wonsan, killing one sailor. The 82 surviving crew were held for eleven months, and the ship is still held in Pyongyang.

01-24.title: Emperor Caligula assassinated by his guards
01-24.description: Praetorian officers led by Cassius Chaerea stabbed Caligula in a palace corridor during the Palatine games. The Guard then made his uncle Claudius emperor.

01-24.title: Gold found at Sutter's Mill sparks the California Gold Rush
01-24.description: James Marshall spotted flakes of gold in the tailrace of a sawmill at Coloma. Within a few years some 300,000 people had flooded into California, which became a state in 1850.

01-24.title: Baden-Powell publishes 'Scouting for Boys'
01-24.description: The first instalment of Robert Baden-Powell's handbook on outdoor skills and citizenship appeared in London. Boys began forming patrols of their own, and the Scout movement spread worldwide.

01-24.title: British battlecruisers defeat a German squadron at Dogger Bank
01-24.description: Forewarned by codebreakers, Admiral Beatty's battlecruisers intercepted a German raiding force in the North Sea and sank the armoured cruiser Blücher. Signalling errors let the rest escape.

01-24.title: Sir Winston Churchill dies aged 90
01-24.description: Britain's wartime Prime Minister died in London, seventy years to the day after his father. He received a state funeral, the first for a politician since Gladstone.

01-24.title: Apple Macintosh goes on sale
01-24.description: Apple's Macintosh brought the mouse and graphical interface to an affordable personal computer. Launched with a famous television advert, it shaped the design of computers for decades.

01-25.title: Henry VIII secretly marries Anne Boleyn
01-25.description: Henry married the pregnant Anne Boleyn in a private ceremony at Whitehall while still married to Catherine of Aragon. To make the marriage lawful he broke with Rome and headed his own Church of England.

01-25.title: Jesuit missionaries found São Paulo
01-25.description: Manuel da Nóbrega and José de Anchieta celebrated Mass at a new Jesuit mission on the Piratininga plateau. The settlement grew into São Paulo, now the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere.

01-25.title: Queen Victoria's eldest daughter marries Prince Frederick of Prussia
01-25.description: Victoria, the Princess Royal, married the future German Emperor Frederick III at St James's Palace. Mendelssohn's 'Wedding March' played as they left, starting a fashion for it at weddings.

01-25.title: Edison and Bell interests form the Oriental Telephone Company
01-25.description: Companies holding the telephone patents of Thomas Edison and Alexander Graham Bell combined to form the Oriental Telephone Company. It built early telephone exchanges in India and other parts of Asia.

01-25.title: First Winter Olympics open at Chamonix
01-25.description: An 'International Winter Sports Week' opened at Chamonix in the French Alps with athletes from 16 nations. The International Olympic Committee later recognised it as the first Winter Olympic Games.

01-25.title: Battle of the Bulge ends in Allied victory
01-25.description: Allied forces restored their line in the Ardennes, ending Germany's last major offensive in the west. Fought in bitter winter conditions, it was the costliest American battle of the Second World War.

01-25.title: Idi Amin seizes power in Uganda
01-25.description: While President Milton Obote was abroad, army commander Idi Amin took power in a coup. His eight-year rule saw the expulsion of Uganda's Asians and the killing of an estimated 100,000 to 500,000 people.

01-26.title: Vicente Yáñez Pinzón lands on the coast of Brazil
01-26.description: The Spanish navigator, who had captained the Niña under Columbus, landed near Cape Santo Agostinho in today's Pernambuco. He arrived three months before Cabral, but Brazil fell within Portugal's sphere.

01-26.title: First Fleet raises the British flag at Sydney Cove
01-26.description: Captain Arthur Phillip established a penal colony at Sydney Cove with some 1,300 convicts, marines and officials. The date is marked as Australia Day, and by many Indigenous Australians as a day of mourning.

01-26.title: Michigan becomes the 26th US state
01-26.description: Michigan joined the Union after giving up the disputed Toledo Strip to Ohio, the cause of the bloodless 'Toledo War'. In exchange it received most of the Upper Peninsula.

01-26.title: Cullinan diamond, the largest ever found, discovered
01-26.description: Mine manager Frederick Wells found a 3,106-carat rough diamond at the Premier Mine near Pretoria. Cut into nine major stones, it supplied the largest gems in the British Crown Jewels.

01-26.title: Germany and Poland sign a non-aggression pact
01-26.description: Hitler's Germany and Piłsudski's Poland agreed a ten-year declaration of non-aggression. It loosened Poland's ties with France; Hitler renounced it in April 1939 and invaded that September.

01-26.title: India becomes a republic under its new constitution
01-26.description: The Constitution of India came into force and Rajendra Prasad became the first President, replacing the British monarch as head of state. The day is celebrated as Republic Day.

01-26.title: Bill Clinton denies an affair with Monica Lewinsky
01-26.description: At the White House, President Clinton declared he 'did not have sexual relations with that woman'. He later admitted an inappropriate relationship and was impeached by the House in December 1998, then acquitted.

01-27.title: Trajan becomes Roman Emperor
01-27.description: On the death of Nerva, his adopted son Trajan, the first emperor born outside Italy, succeeded to the throne. His conquests of Dacia and Mesopotamia brought the empire to its greatest extent.

01-27.title: Dante Alighieri is sentenced to exile from Florence
01-27.description: Florence's victorious Black Guelphs convicted Dante of corruption in his absence. He never returned home, and wrote the 'Divine Comedy' during his exile.

01-27.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born in Salzburg
01-27.description: The son of the court musician Leopold Mozart, he toured Europe as a child prodigy. In a life of 35 years he wrote more than 600 works, including 'The Marriage of Figaro' and 'Don Giovanni'.

01-27.title: Thomas Edison patents his incandescent lamp
01-27.description: Edison received US patent 223,898 for a carbon-filament lamp. Others had made electric bulbs, but his long-lasting design and supply system made electric lighting practical.

01-27.title: Siege of Leningrad is lifted after 872 days
01-27.description: Soviet offensives drove German forces back from Leningrad, ending a blockade that began in September 1941. Some 800,000 or more civilians died, most from starvation.

01-27.title: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz
01-27.description: Red Army soldiers reached Auschwitz and found about 7,000 prisoners left behind. Around 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered there. The date is now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

01-27.title: Outer Space Treaty signed
01-27.description: The United States, the Soviet Union and Britain signed a treaty barring nuclear weapons from orbit and forbidding any nation from claiming the Moon or other celestial bodies. It remains the basis of space law.

01-27.title: Fire kills three Apollo 1 astronauts during a test
01-27.description: A flash fire in the pure-oxygen cabin of Apollo 1 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee during a launch rehearsal at Cape Kennedy. NASA redesigned the spacecraft before flying again.

01-28.title: Charlemagne dies at Aachen
01-28.description: The Frankish king, crowned emperor in 800, died after ruling much of western Europe. His empire was divided among his grandsons within thirty years, but its memory shaped the Holy Roman Empire.

01-28.title: Henry VIII dies at Whitehall
01-28.description: Henry VIII died aged 55 after a reign that broke with Rome, dissolved the monasteries and saw six marriages. His nine-year-old son succeeded him as Edward VI.

01-28.title: Galileo observes Neptune without recognising it
01-28.description: Galileo's notes record a 'star' near Jupiter that was in fact Neptune, and even note that it seemed to move. The planet was not identified until 1846.

01-28.title: Gas lamps light Pall Mall in London
01-28.description: Frederick Albert Winsor's demonstration lit part of Pall Mall with gas lamps, the first public street lighting by gas. Gas lighting spread rapidly through British cities over the next decades.

01-28.title: Paris capitulates and France signs an armistice with Germany
01-28.description: After a four-month siege, the French government agreed an armistice with the new German Empire. The peace that followed cost France Alsace and much of Lorraine.

01-28.title: Japanese forces attack Shanghai
01-28.description: Japanese marines clashed with China's 19th Route Army in Shanghai, and Japanese aircraft bombed the Zhabei district. The fighting lasted over a month before a ceasefire was brokered.

01-28.title: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart after launch
01-28.description: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after lift-off, killing its seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. A faulty seal in a booster rocket was to blame, and shuttle flights stopped for 32 months.

01-29.title: Feodor III becomes Tsar of Russia
01-29.description: On the death of Tsar Alexei, his sickly 14-year-old son Feodor succeeded him. In a short reign he abolished the system of ranking nobles by ancestry, paving the way for his half-brother Peter the Great.

01-29.title: George III dies at Windsor
01-29.description: Blind and suffering from mental illness, George III died after a reign of almost 60 years, which had seen the loss of America and victory over Napoleon. His son the Prince Regent became George IV.

01-29.title: Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Raven' is published
01-29.description: Poe's poem of a grieving lover and a talking bird appeared in the New York Evening Mirror. It made him famous almost overnight, though it earned him little money.

01-29.title: Karl Benz files a patent for his motor car
01-29.description: Benz applied for a German patent on a 'vehicle powered by a gas engine', his three-wheeled Motorwagen. It is generally regarded as the first practical petrol-driven automobile.

01-29.title: The American League of baseball is organised
01-29.description: Ban Johnson reorganised a minor league as the American League, with eight teams. It declared itself a major league in 1901 and met the National League in the first World Series in 1903.

01-29.title: Zeppelin raid kills civilians in Paris
01-29.description: A German airship bombed eastern Paris, killing more than twenty people in the Ménilmontant area. It was the last Zeppelin raid on the city, which strengthened its air defences.

01-30.title: Charles I is beheaded in Whitehall
01-30.description: Convicted of treason, Charles I was executed on a scaffold outside the Banqueting House. England became a republic, and the monarchy was not restored until 1660.

01-30.title: Andrew Jackson survives an assassination attempt
01-30.description: At the US Capitol, the house painter Richard Lawrence fired two pistols at Jackson, but both misfired. It was the first known attempt to kill a sitting American president.

01-30.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt is born at Hyde Park, New York
01-30.description: Roosevelt led the United States through the Great Depression and most of the Second World War. He is the only president elected four times.

01-30.title: Hitler appointed Chancellor of Germany
01-30.description: President Hindenburg made the Nazi leader Chancellor, with conservatives expecting to control him. Within months Hitler had suspended civil liberties and established a one-party dictatorship.

01-30.title: Soviet submarine sinks the Wilhelm Gustloff
01-30.description: Torpedoes from submarine S-13 sank the overcrowded German liner in the Baltic as it evacuated refugees and military personnel. An estimated 9,000 died, the greatest loss of life in a single sinking.

01-30.title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated in New Delhi
01-30.description: The Hindu nationalist Nathuram Godse shot Gandhi at a prayer meeting at Birla House. The death of the leader of India's non-violent independence struggle was mourned across the world.

01-30.title: Tet Offensive begins in South Vietnam
01-30.description: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces attacked towns and bases across South Vietnam during the lunar new year truce. Though repelled, the offensive undermined American confidence in the war.

01-31.title: London Lock Hospital opens for venereal disease patients
01-31.description: The Lock Hospital at Hyde Park Corner opened as the first hospital in Britain dedicated to treating venereal disease. It later added a chapel and an asylum for women.

01-31.title: US House passes the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery
01-31.description: After intense lobbying by President Lincoln, the House of Representatives approved the amendment by 119 votes to 56. Ratified in December 1865, it ended slavery throughout the United States.

01-31.title: Germany announces unrestricted submarine warfare
01-31.description: Germany told the United States its U-boats would sink without warning any ship in the war zone from the next day. The decision led to the break in relations and, in April, to America's declaration of war.

01-31.title: Police clash with strikers in Glasgow's George Square
01-31.description: A rally for a 40-hour week ended in violence between police and workers in George Square. Fearing revolution, the government sent troops and tanks into Glasgow.

01-31.title: First monthly Social Security cheque is issued
01-31.description: Ida May Fuller, a retired legal secretary from Vermont, received cheque number 00-000-001 for 22.54 dollars. She lived to 100 and collected about 22,000 dollars in benefits.

01-31.title: Private Eddie Slovik executed for desertion
01-31.description: Slovik was shot by firing squad in eastern France, the only American soldier executed for desertion since the Civil War. Of many soldiers sentenced to death for the offence, he alone was put to death.

01-31.title: Explorer 1, America's first satellite, is launched
01-31.description: A Jupiter-C rocket put Explorer 1 into orbit from Cape Canaveral, four months after Sputnik. Its Geiger counter detected the Van Allen radiation belts around the Earth.

01-31.title: Ham the chimpanzee flies into space
01-31.description: Ham flew a suborbital flight on Mercury-Redstone 2, performing simple tasks in response to lights. His safe return cleared the way for Alan Shepard's flight that May.

01-31.title: Apollo 14 launches for the Moon
01-31.description: Alan Shepard, Stuart Roosa and Edgar Mitchell lifted off from Kennedy Space Center. Landing at Fra Mauro on 5 February, Shepard famously hit two golf balls on the lunar surface.

01-31.title: McDonald's opens in Moscow
01-31.description: The first McDonald's in the Soviet Union opened on Pushkin Square, serving about 30,000 people on its first day. Queues stretched for hours as the Cold War drew to a close.

02-01.title: Edward III crowned after his father's deposition
02-01.description: Fourteen-year-old Edward III was crowned at Westminster Abbey after Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer forced Edward II from the throne. His later claim to the French crown began the Hundred Years' War.

02-01.title: US Supreme Court gathers for its first session
02-01.description: The Supreme Court convened at the Merchants' Exchange in New York, though too few justices had arrived to begin business until the next day. It heard no cases in its first year.

02-01.title: Revolutionary France declares war on Britain and the Dutch Republic
02-01.description: Days after executing Louis XVI, the National Convention declared war on Britain and the Netherlands. The conflict that followed lasted, with brief pauses, until Waterloo in 1815.

02-01.title: Texas votes to secede from the Union
02-01.description: A Texas convention voted 166 to 8 for secession, a decision confirmed by referendum later that month. Governor Sam Houston refused to swear loyalty to the Confederacy and was removed from office.

02-01.title: Lincoln signs the resolution for the Thirteenth Amendment
02-01.description: Abraham Lincoln added his signature to the congressional resolution sending the amendment to abolish slavery to the states, though presidents play no formal role in amendments. Illinois ratified it that day.

02-01.title: Puccini's 'La bohème' premieres in Turin
02-01.description: Conducted by the young Arturo Toscanini at the Teatro Regio, Puccini's opera of struggling artists in Paris received a cool critical welcome. Audiences loved it, and it became one of the most performed operas.

02-01.title: Royal Canadian Mounted Police is formed
