02-01.description: The Royal North-West Mounted Police merged with the Dominion Police to form the RCMP, Canada's national police force. Its scarlet tunics became one of the country's best-known symbols.

02-01.title: Trygve Lie becomes the first UN Secretary-General
02-01.description: The General Assembly appointed Norway's foreign minister Trygve Lie as the first Secretary-General of the United Nations. He served until 1952, resigning after Soviet opposition over the Korean War.

02-01.title: Greensboro sit-in begins at a Woolworth's lunch counter
02-01.description: Four Black students sat at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina, and stayed after being refused service. Sit-ins spread across the South, and Woolworth's desegregated the counter that July.

02-01.title: Space Shuttle Columbia breaks up on re-entry
02-01.description: Columbia disintegrated over Texas minutes before landing, killing all seven astronauts. Hot gases had entered a wing damaged by foam at launch; shuttle flights were suspended for two and a half years.

02-02.title: Alaric II issues the Breviary of Alaric
02-02.description: The Visigothic king promulgated a digest of Roman law for the Roman population of his kingdom in Gaul and Spain. It became one of the main channels through which Roman law reached early medieval western Europe.

02-02.title: Pedro de Mendoza founds Buenos Aires
02-02.description: The Spanish expedition founded a settlement on the Río de la Plata. Hunger and attacks forced its abandonment in 1541, and Juan de Garay refounded Buenos Aires in 1580.

02-02.title: New Amsterdam receives municipal government
02-02.description: The Dutch settlement on Manhattan was granted its own city government under Director-General Peter Stuyvesant. The English seized it in 1664 and renamed it New York.

02-02.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends the Mexican-American War
02-02.description: Mexico ceded about half its territory, including California, Nevada, Utah and most of Arizona and New Mexico, to the United States for 15 million dollars, and recognised Texas as American.

02-02.title: German Sixth Army's last units surrender at Stalingrad
02-02.description: The final German forces in Stalingrad's northern pocket laid down their arms. Some 91,000 were taken prisoner, and the defeat marked a turning point of the war on the Eastern Front.

02-02.title: Idi Amin proclaims himself President of Uganda
02-02.description: A week after his coup, Amin declared himself head of state and suspended parts of the constitution. His rule became one of the most brutal in post-colonial Africa until his overthrow in 1979.

02-02.title: F. W. de Klerk lifts the ban on the ANC
02-02.description: Opening parliament in Cape Town, South Africa's President legalised the African National Congress and other banned groups and announced Nelson Mandela's release. Negotiations to end apartheid followed.

02-02.title: IPCC finds global warming is 'very likely' caused by humans
02-02.description: Released in Paris, the summary of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's fourth assessment called warming 'unequivocal' and very likely due to human emissions. The panel shared that year's Nobel Peace Prize.

02-03.title: Murad II dies, and Mehmed II takes the Ottoman throne for good
02-03.description: The death of Sultan Murad II brought his 18-year-old son Mehmed II back to power. Two years later Mehmed captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

02-03.title: Bartolomeu Dias lands at Mossel Bay after rounding the Cape
02-03.description: Having been driven round the southern tip of Africa by storms, Dias landed on the South African coast east of the Cape. His voyage showed that ships could sail from the Atlantic into the Indian Ocean.

02-03.title: Dutch tulip prices collapse
02-03.description: At a bulb auction in Haarlem, buyers failed to appear and prices for tulip contracts crashed. 'Tulip mania' is often cited as the first recorded speculative bubble, though its damage is now thought modest.

02-03.title: Massachusetts Bay Colony issues paper money
02-03.description: To pay soldiers back from a failed expedition against Quebec, Massachusetts issued bills of credit, the first government paper money in the Americas (dated 1690 under the Old Style calendar).

02-03.title: London Protocol recognises an independent Greece
02-03.description: Britain, France and Russia agreed that Greece should be a fully independent kingdom, after nearly a decade of revolution against the Ottomans. It was the first new state to emerge in the Balkans.

02-03.title: Fifteenth Amendment ratified, barring racial bars to voting
02-03.description: The amendment forbade denying citizens the vote on grounds of race, colour or previous servitude. Southern states later evaded it with poll taxes, literacy tests and intimidation for almost a century.

02-03.title: Sixteenth Amendment allows a US federal income tax
02-03.description: Ratification of the Sixteenth Amendment gave Congress power to tax incomes without dividing the tax among states by population. Income tax became the main source of federal revenue.

02-03.title: Battle of Manila begins
02-03.description: American and Filipino forces entered Manila to retake it from the Japanese. The month-long battle destroyed much of the city, and around 100,000 Filipino civilians died, many in Japanese massacres.

02-03.title: Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens and the Big Bopper die in a plane crash
02-03.description: Their light aircraft crashed in snow near Clear Lake, Iowa, shortly after take-off, killing all aboard. Don McLean later called it 'the day the music died' in his song 'American Pie'.

02-04.title: Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song dynasty
02-04.description: Proclaimed emperor by his troops at Chenqiao, the general became Emperor Taizu of Song. The dynasty reunited most of China and presided over remarkable advances in commerce, printing and technology.

02-04.title: Electors unanimously choose George Washington as President
02-04.description: Presidential electors cast their votes and every one named George Washington. He remains the only President to win every electoral vote, which he did again in 1792.

02-04.title: French National Convention abolishes slavery
02-04.description: Inspired by the slave revolt in Saint-Domingue, the Convention abolished slavery in all French colonies. Napoleon restored it in 1802, and France did not abolish it finally until 1848.

02-04.title: John Marshall becomes Chief Justice of the United States
02-04.description: Marshall began 34 years as Chief Justice, the longest in the Court's history. His rulings, beginning with Marbury v. Madison, established judicial review and a strong federal government.

02-04.title: Seceded states meet at Montgomery to form the Confederacy
02-04.description: Delegates from six seceded states opened a convention in Montgomery, Alabama. Within days they adopted a provisional constitution and chose Jefferson Davis as provisional President.

02-04.title: Philippine-American War breaks out in Manila
02-04.description: Shots exchanged between American and Filipino troops sparked war between the United States and the Philippine Republic. Officially ended in 1902, the conflict killed some 200,000 or more Filipino civilians.

02-04.title: Hitler takes personal command of the German armed forces
02-04.description: After forcing out War Minister Blomberg and army chief Fritsch on trumped-up charges, Hitler abolished the War Ministry and assumed direct command. Ribbentrop became Foreign Minister the same day.

02-04.title: Yalta Conference opens in Crimea
02-04.description: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin met at the Livadia Palace to plan the end of the war. They agreed on the occupation of Germany, elections in Poland, Soviet entry into the Pacific war and the United Nations.

02-04.title: Ceylon becomes independent from Britain
02-04.description: Ceylon became a self-governing dominion in the Commonwealth, ending about 150 years of British rule. It became a republic and took the name Sri Lanka in 1972.

02-04.title: Mark Zuckerberg launches 'TheFacebook' at Harvard
02-04.description: The Harvard student launched a social network for fellow students. Opened to the public in 2006, Facebook grew to billions of users and transformed how people share news and personal life.

02-05.title: Earthquake strikes Pompeii and Herculaneum
02-05.description: A strong earthquake badly damaged towns around the Bay of Naples. Pompeii was still being repaired seventeen years later when Vesuvius buried it in 79.

02-05.title: Twenty-six Christians crucified at Nagasaki
02-05.description: On the orders of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, six Franciscan missionaries, Japanese Jesuits and lay converts were crucified on a hill at Nagasaki. They are honoured as the Twenty-Six Martyrs of Japan.

02-05.title: Calabrian earthquakes begin in southern Italy
02-05.description: The first of five major shocks struck Calabria and Sicily, beginning a sequence that lasted weeks. Around 30,000 to 50,000 people died, and the disaster prompted early scientific study of earthquakes.

02-05.title: New Hermitage museum opens to the public in St Petersburg
02-05.description: Nicholas I opened the purpose-built New Hermitage to display the imperial art collections. The Hermitage is now one of the largest museums in the world.

02-05.title: Britain and the United States sign the first Hay-Pauncefote Treaty
02-05.description: The agreement gave the United States the right to build a canal across Central America. Rejected by the Senate, it was renegotiated in 1901, opening the way for the Panama Canal.

02-05.title: BBC broadcasts the Greenwich time signal for the first time
02-05.description: The six short 'pips', generated by the Royal Observatory at Greenwich, were broadcast to mark the hour. The signal is still heard on BBC radio today.

02-05.title: Apollo 14 lands at Fra Mauro
02-05.description: Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell landed in the lunar highlands, the target of the aborted Apollo 13. Shepard, America's first astronaut in space, became the fifth person to walk on the Moon.

02-06.title: Spanish Inquisition holds its first auto-da-fé in Seville
02-06.description: Six people convicted of secretly practising Judaism were burned at the stake after a public ceremony in Seville. Autos-da-fé became the Inquisition's most notorious public ritual.

02-06.title: James II becomes king on the death of Charles II
02-06.description: Charles II died at Whitehall and his Catholic brother succeeded as James II of England and VII of Scotland. Fears of a Catholic dynasty led to his overthrow in the Glorious Revolution of 1688.

02-06.title: France signs an alliance with the United States
02-06.description: In Paris, Benjamin Franklin and his fellow commissioners signed treaties of alliance and commerce with France. French troops, money and naval power proved decisive in the war for independence.

02-06.title: First American Colonization Society settlers sail for Africa
02-06.description: The ship Elizabeth left New York carrying 86 free Black Americans bound for West Africa. Their settlement efforts led to the founding of Liberia.

02-06.title: Treaty of Waitangi signed in New Zealand
02-06.description: British officials and more than 40 Māori chiefs signed the treaty at Waitangi. Differences between its English and Māori texts over sovereignty remain central to New Zealand law and politics.

02-06.title: British women over thirty win the vote
02-06.description: The Representation of the People Act gave the vote to women over 30 who met property qualifications, about 8.4 million women. Equal voting rights with men followed in 1928.

02-06.title: Elizabeth II becomes Queen on the death of George VI
02-06.description: The 25-year-old princess learned of her father's death while in Kenya. She reigned for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch, until her death in 2022.

02-07.title: Leo I crowned Eastern Roman Emperor
02-07.description: Backed by the powerful general Aspar, Leo I became emperor in Constantinople. He is often said to be the first emperor crowned by the Patriarch, and he reigned until 474.

02-07.title: Edward of Caernarfon becomes the first English Prince of Wales
02-07.description: Edward I invested his son, the future Edward II, with the title Prince of Wales after his conquest of Wales. The title has been given to the heir to the English and British throne ever since.

02-07.title: Austria and Prussia ally against Revolutionary France
02-07.description: The two German powers signed a defensive alliance amid fears of the French Revolution. War broke out that April, beginning more than two decades of conflict across Europe.

02-07.title: Strongest of the New Madrid earthquakes strikes the Mississippi valley
02-07.description: The last and largest of a series of great earthquakes hit near New Madrid, Missouri. It created waterfalls and made the Mississippi briefly run backwards near the epicentre.

02-07.title: Great Baltimore Fire begins
02-07.description: A fire broke out in a dry-goods warehouse and burned for some 30 hours, destroying more than 1,500 buildings in central Baltimore. Fire crews from other cities could not connect hoses to local hydrants.

02-07.title: US embargo on trade with Cuba takes effect
02-07.description: A proclamation by John F. Kennedy banning almost all imports from Cuba came into force. Extended since, it is one of the longest-lasting trade embargoes in modern history.

02-07.title: Bruce McCandless makes the first untethered spacewalk
02-07.description: Using a nitrogen-jet backpack, the Manned Maneuvering Unit, McCandless flew about 100 metres from the shuttle Challenger. The photograph of him alone above Earth became famous.

02-07.title: Soviet Communist Party agrees to give up its monopoly on power
02-07.description: The Central Committee accepted Mikhail Gorbachev's proposal to end the party's constitutional leading role. The change opened the way to multi-party politics in the Soviet Union.

02-08.title: Mongols sack Vladimir in north-eastern Rus
02-08.description: Batu Khan's army stormed and burned Vladimir, the capital of the leading Russian principality. The Mongol conquest brought the Russian lands under the Golden Horde for some two centuries.

02-08.title: Mary, Queen of Scots is executed at Fotheringhay
02-08.description: After nineteen years in English captivity, Mary was beheaded for plotting against Elizabeth I. Her execution removed the Catholic claimant to the English throne and helped provoke the Spanish Armada.

02-08.title: Royal charter founds the College of William and Mary
02-08.description: William III and Mary II granted a charter for a college in Virginia, later sited at Williamsburg. It is the second-oldest college in the United States; Thomas Jefferson studied there.

02-08.title: Delaware rejects the Thirteenth Amendment
02-08.description: Delaware's legislature voted against the amendment abolishing slavery, although the state had remained in the Union. It ratified the amendment only symbolically, in 1901.

02-08.title: Japan attacks the Russian fleet at Port Arthur
02-08.description: Japanese torpedo boats struck the Russian Pacific squadron at night, opening the Russo-Japanese War. Japan's victory in 1905 was the first by an Asian power over a European one in modern times.

02-08.title: 'The Birth of a Nation' premieres in Los Angeles
02-08.description: D. W. Griffith's Civil War epic pioneered techniques of film storytelling but glorified the Ku Klux Klan. It drew protests from the NAACP and helped inspire the Klan's revival that year.

02-08.title: Skylab 4 crew return after 84 days in space
02-08.description: Gerald Carr, Edward Gibson and William Pogue splashed down after the longest crewed mission yet. Their experience of long-duration flight informed later space stations.

02-09.title: Child emperor Leo II crowns his father Zeno co-emperor
02-09.description: Seven-year-old Leo II, sole emperor since his grandfather's death in January, crowned his father Zeno as co-ruler. Leo died that November, leaving Zeno to rule alone.

02-09.title: Earliest recorded race is run at Chester
02-09.description: A Shrove Tuesday race on the Roodee at Chester is the first recorded at what is now Britain's oldest racecourse still in use. It replaced a violent football match as the city's holiday sport.

02-09.title: Parliament declares Massachusetts in rebellion
02-09.description: Both Houses of Parliament declared Massachusetts in a state of rebellion and asked the King to enforce the law. Fighting broke out at Lexington and Concord two months later.

02-09.title: Jefferson Davis elected provisional President of the Confederacy
02-09.description: Meeting in Montgomery, the Confederate provisional Congress chose Davis, a former Mississippi senator and US Secretary of War. He led the Confederacy throughout the Civil War.

02-09.title: Joseph McCarthy claims to have a list of communists in the State Department
02-09.description: In a speech at Wheeling, West Virginia, the Wisconsin senator said he held a list of 205 communists in the State Department. The charge launched years of anti-communist investigations.

02-09.title: Soviet R-7 becomes the first operational ICBM
02-09.description: The R-7 Semyorka, the rocket that had launched Sputnik, entered service as the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile. Its descendants still launch Soyuz spacecraft.

02-09.title: The Beatles appear on 'The Ed Sullivan Show'
02-09.description: An estimated 73 million Americans watched the Beatles' first live US television appearance. The broadcast launched the 'British Invasion' of American popular music.

02-10.title: Baghdad surrenders to the Mongols
02-10.description: After a short siege, the Abbasid Caliph al-Musta'sim surrendered Baghdad to Hulagu Khan. The city was sacked and the Caliph executed days later, ending five centuries of Abbasid rule from Baghdad.

02-10.title: Robert the Bruce kills John Comyn at Dumfries
02-10.description: Bruce stabbed his rival for the Scottish crown before the altar of Greyfriars church. Committed to rebellion, he was crowned King of Scots weeks later and defeated the English at Bannockburn in 1314.

02-10.title: Treaty of Paris ends the Seven Years' War
02-10.description: France ceded Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain gave up Florida. Britain emerged as the leading colonial power, though France kept its trading posts in India.

02-10.title: Queen Victoria marries Prince Albert
02-10.description: Victoria married her cousin Albert of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace. Her white wedding dress set a lasting fashion; Albert became her closest adviser.

02-10.title: HMS Dreadnought is launched
02-10.description: King Edward VII launched the battleship at Portsmouth. With ten 12-inch guns and steam turbines, she made existing battleships obsolete and intensified the naval race with Germany.

02-10.title: Soviet Union begins mass deportations from eastern Poland
02-10.description: The NKVD deported some 140,000 Polish citizens, many of them families of settlers and foresters, to Siberia and Kazakhstan. It was the first of four mass deportations in 1940-41.

02-10.title: U-2 pilot Gary Powers exchanged for Soviet spy Rudolf Abel
02-10.description: On the Glienicke Bridge between West Berlin and Potsdam, the US pilot shot down in 1960 was swapped for the KGB colonel Rudolf Abel. The bridge became known for Cold War exchanges.

02-10.title: Ron Brown becomes the first Black chairman of a major US party
02-10.description: Ron Brown was elected chairman of the Democratic National Committee. He helped Bill Clinton win in 1992 and became Secretary of Commerce before dying in a plane crash in 1996.

02-11.title: Legendary founding of Japan by Emperor Jimmu
02-11.description: According to the 8th-century chronicles, Jimmu, said to descend from the sun goddess Amaterasu, became Japan's first emperor on this day. The legend is commemorated as National Foundation Day.

02-11.title: English clergy recognise Henry VIII as head of the Church
02-11.description: Under threat of prosecution, the Convocation of Canterbury acknowledged Henry as Supreme Head of the Church in England 'as far as the law of Christ allows'. The full break with Rome followed by 1534.

02-11.title: Pennsylvania Hospital, the first in the American colonies, opens
02-11.description: Founded by Benjamin Franklin and Dr Thomas Bond, the Pennsylvania Hospital admitted its first patients in Philadelphia. It was the first hospital in what became the United States.

02-11.title: Thomas Edison is born in Milan, Ohio
02-11.description: Edison patented more than 1,000 inventions, including the phonograph and a practical incandescent lamp. His laboratory at Menlo Park pioneered organised industrial research.

02-11.title: Bernadette Soubirous sees her first vision at Lourdes
02-11.description: The 14-year-old miller's daughter reported seeing a lady in white in the grotto of Massabielle. Lourdes grew into one of the most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.

02-11.title: Lateran Treaty creates Vatican City
02-11.description: Mussolini's government and the Holy See agreed to recognise Vatican City as an independent state. The treaty ended the 'Roman Question' that had divided Church and Italian state since 1870.

02-11.title: Nelson Mandela walks free after 27 years in prison
02-11.description: Mandela left Victor Verster Prison near Paarl hand in hand with his wife Winnie, watched by millions on television. Four years later he was elected South Africa's first Black president.

02-12.title: Castile orders its Muslims to convert or leave
02-12.description: A decree of Isabella I gave the Muslims of Castile a choice between baptism and exile. Most converted, becoming Moriscos, whose descendants were expelled from Spain in 1609-14.

02-12.title: Lady Jane Grey is executed at the Tower
02-12.description: The teenage Protestant queen, deposed after nine days in 1553, was beheaded on Mary I's orders following Wyatt's Rebellion. Her husband Guildford Dudley was executed the same morning.

02-12.title: Charles Darwin is born in Shrewsbury
02-12.description: Born on the same day as Lincoln, Darwin sailed on HMS Beagle and developed the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859.

02-12.title: Abraham Lincoln is born in Kentucky
02-12.description: Born in a one-room log cabin near Hodgenville, Lincoln was largely self-taught. As the 16th President he led the Union through the Civil War and helped bring about the end of slavery.

02-12.title: Chile proclaims its independence from Spain
02-12.description: Bernardo O'Higgins formally proclaimed Chile's independence on the first anniversary of the victory at Chacabuco. Spanish forces were decisively beaten at Maipú that April.

02-12.title: Puyi, the last Emperor of China, abdicates
02-12.description: The Empress Dowager Longyu issued the edict of abdication for the six-year-old Puyi. The fall of the Qing ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

02-12.title: Soviet authorities arrest Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
02-12.description: Weeks after 'The Gulag Archipelago' appeared in Paris, the Nobel laureate was arrested in Moscow and charged with treason. The next day he was stripped of citizenship and deported to West Germany.

02-13.title: Mongols begin the sack of Baghdad
02-13.description: Hulagu's troops entered Baghdad and began a week of killing and plunder. Libraries and the city's great institutions of learning were destroyed, and tens of thousands of inhabitants died.

02-13.title: Catherine Howard is executed at the Tower of London
02-13.description: Henry VIII's fifth wife, still a teenager, was beheaded for adultery and treason. She was the second of his queens to be executed, after her cousin Anne Boleyn.

02-13.title: Galileo arrives in Rome to face the Inquisition
02-13.description: Summoned over his 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems', Galileo reached Rome. Tried that spring, he was forced to abjure the view that the Earth moves and spent his last years under house arrest.

02-13.title: William III and Mary II offered the English crown
02-13.description: At the Banqueting House, the Convention Parliament presented the Declaration of Rights and offered the throne jointly to William and Mary. The settlement limited royal power and confirmed Parliament's role.

02-13.title: Fortress of Gaeta surrenders, ending the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
02-13.description: After a three-month siege by Piedmontese forces, King Francis II surrendered Gaeta and went into exile. Weeks later the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed under Victor Emmanuel II.

02-13.title: Allied bombers begin the destruction of Dresden
02-13.description: British and then American raids over two days created a firestorm that killed about 25,000 people and destroyed the historic centre. The attack's justification has been debated ever since.

02-13.title: Kevin Rudd apologises to the Stolen Generations
02-13.description: Australia's Prime Minister delivered a formal apology in Parliament to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people taken from their families under past government policies.

02-14.title: Traditional date of the martyrdom of Saint Valentine
02-14.description: Tradition holds that Valentine, a priest or bishop of Terni, was beheaded on the Via Flaminia outside Rome. His link with romantic love dates only from the Middle Ages, notably the poetry of Chaucer.

02-14.title: Oaths of Strasbourg sworn by Charlemagne's grandsons
02-14.description: Louis the German and Charles the Bald pledged alliance against their brother Lothair, each swearing in the other's language. The oaths are the earliest surviving text in a form of French.

02-14.title: Deposed Richard II dies at Pontefract Castle
02-14.description: Richard II, overthrown by his cousin Henry Bolingbroke in 1399, died in captivity around this date, probably starved to death. His fall sowed the dynastic rivalry behind the Wars of the Roses.

02-14.title: Captain James Cook is killed in Hawaii
02-14.description: Cook died in a clash with Hawaiians at Kealakekua Bay after trying to take a chief hostage over a stolen boat. His three voyages had charted much of the Pacific.

02-14.title: Alexander Graham Bell files his telephone patent
02-14.description: Bell's lawyer filed his application at the US Patent Office on the same day that Elisha Gray filed a caveat for a similar device. Bell's patent was granted in March and upheld in long litigation.

02-14.title: Saint Valentine's Day Massacre in Chicago
02-14.description: Gunmen, some dressed as police, shot dead seven men linked to Bugs Moran's gang in a garage. The killings, widely blamed on Al Capone, turned public opinion against gangland violence.

02-14.title: ENIAC is unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania
02-14.description: The US Army publicly revealed ENIAC, the first programmable general-purpose electronic computer. With nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, it could perform 5,000 additions a second.

02-14.title: Ayatollah Khomeini issues a fatwa against Salman Rushdie
02-14.description: Iran's leader called on Muslims to kill the author of 'The Satanic Verses' and his publishers. Rushdie spent years in hiding; translators and publishers were attacked, and he was stabbed in 2022.

02-15.title: Pope Paschal II recognises the Knights Hospitaller
02-15.description: The bull Pie postulatio voluntatis placed the hospital of St John in Jerusalem under papal protection. The order later took on a military role and survives today as the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.

02-15.title: Galileo Galilei is born in Pisa
02-15.description: Galileo's telescopic discoveries, including Jupiter's moons, and his studies of motion made him a founder of modern physics. His defence of Copernicus brought his trial by the Inquisition in 1633.

02-15.title: USS Maine explodes in Havana harbour
02-15.description: An explosion sank the American battleship, killing some 260 men. The cause is still debated, but US newspapers blamed Spain, and the cry 'Remember the Maine' helped bring war in April.

02-15.title: Singapore surrenders to Japan
02-15.description: General Arthur Percival surrendered Singapore, and some 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops became prisoners. Churchill called it the worst disaster and largest capitulation in British history.

02-15.title: US figure skating team killed in the Sabena air crash
02-15.description: Sabena Flight 548 crashed on approach to Brussels, killing all 72 aboard and a man on the ground. Among the dead was the entire US figure skating team, en route to the world championships in Prague.

02-15.title: Canada raises its Maple Leaf flag
02-15.description: The red and white Maple Leaf flag was raised on Parliament Hill in Ottawa, replacing the Canadian Red Ensign. 15 February is now marked as National Flag of Canada Day.

02-16.title: Earliest surviving English cheque is written
02-16.description: Nicholas Vanacker wrote a cheque for 400 pounds drawn on his London goldsmith-bankers, Morris and Clayton. It is the oldest known surviving handwritten cheque in Britain.

02-16.title: Stephen Decatur burns the captured USS Philadelphia at Tripoli
02-16.description: Lieutenant Decatur and a small crew slipped into Tripoli harbour and set fire to the frigate, captured by the Barbary state. Nelson is said to have called it the most daring act of the age.

02-16.title: Howard Carter opens Tutankhamun's burial chamber
02-16.description: Before invited officials, Carter broke through the sealed wall to reveal a gilded shrine filling the chamber. The king's sarcophagus and gold coffins lay within, untouched for over 3,000 years.

02-16.title: Wallace Carothers's nylon is patented
02-16.description: DuPont received the patent for nylon, invented by a team led by Wallace Carothers. The first fully synthetic fibre, it was used for stockings and then wartime parachutes.

02-16.title: American paratroopers and infantry assault Corregidor
02-16.description: US forces landed by parachute and sea on the island fortress at the mouth of Manila Bay, lost in 1942. After two weeks of fighting most of its Japanese defenders were dead.

02-16.title: First 911 emergency call made in Alabama
02-16.description: In Haleyville, Alabama, Senator Rankin Fite made the first call on the new 911 emergency number. A single, easily remembered number spread across the United States over the following decades.

02-17.title: Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome
02-17.description: Condemned by the Inquisition for heresy, the Dominican philosopher was burned in the Campo de' Fiori. His views included an infinite universe with countless worlds; a statue of him now stands there.

02-17.title: House elects Thomas Jefferson President after an electoral tie
02-17.description: On the 36th ballot, the House of Representatives broke the tie between Jefferson and his running mate Aaron Burr. The crisis led to the Twelfth Amendment, separating votes for President and Vice-President.

02-17.title: Committee that became the Red Cross meets in Geneva
02-17.description: Five Genevans, including Henri Dunant, founded a committee to aid wounded soldiers, inspired by Dunant's account of Solferino. It became the International Committee of the Red Cross.

02-17.title: H. L. Hunley sinks USS Housatonic
02-17.description: The Confederate submarine rammed a torpedo into the Union warship off Charleston, the first sinking of an enemy ship by a submarine. The Hunley was lost with all eight crew that night.

02-17.title: First issue of News-Week is published
02-17.description: The weekly news magazine, later Newsweek, was launched in New York as a rival to Time. It became one of the leading American news weeklies of the 20th century.

02-17.title: China invades Vietnam
02-17.description: Chinese troops crossed Vietnam's northern border to punish Hanoi for invading Cambodia. Both sides claimed victory after a month of fighting that cost tens of thousands of lives.

02-18.title: Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty
02-18.description: In the Sixth Crusade, Emperor Frederick II agreed a ten-year truce with the Ayyubid Sultan al-Kamil that returned Jerusalem to Christian control without a battle. The deal angered many on both sides.

02-18.title: Michelangelo dies in Rome
02-18.description: The sculptor, painter and architect died aged 88, still working as chief architect of St Peter's. His works include the David, the Sistine Chapel ceiling and the Last Judgement.

02-18.title: John Bunyan's 'The Pilgrim's Progress' is published
02-18.description: Partly written in Bedford gaol, Bunyan's allegory of Christian's journey to the Celestial City was an immediate success. It has been translated into more than 200 languages.

02-18.title: Mark Twain's 'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn' published in the US
02-18.description: Twain's novel of a boy and an escaped slave on the Mississippi was published in America. Written in vernacular speech, it has been called the source of all modern American literature.

02-18.title: Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto
02-18.description: Comparing photographic plates at Lowell Observatory, Tombaugh found a faint moving object. Named Pluto at the suggestion of 11-year-old Venetia Burney, it was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

02-18.title: Hans and Sophie Scholl arrested in Munich
02-18.description: The siblings of the White Rose resistance group were caught distributing anti-Nazi leaflets at Munich University. They were tried and guillotined four days later.

02-19.title: Septimius Severus defeats Clodius Albinus at Lugdunum
02-19.description: Near modern Lyon, Severus won a hard-fought battle against his rival for the throne, said to have involved some 300,000 men. Albinus died, leaving Severus sole emperor.

02-19.title: Nicolaus Copernicus is born in Toruń
02-19.description: Copernicus's 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres', published as he died in 1543, placed the Sun rather than the Earth at the centre. It became a starting point of the Scientific Revolution.

02-19.title: Aaron Burr arrested for treason in Alabama
02-19.description: The former Vice-President was seized near Wakefield, accused of plotting to found an independent nation in the West. He was acquitted that September, but his political career was over.

02-19.title: Edison receives a patent for the phonograph
02-19.description: Edison's tinfoil phonograph was the first machine able to record sound and play it back. Its first words were 'Mary had a little lamb'.

02-19.title: Allied fleet begins bombarding the Dardanelles forts
02-19.description: British and French warships opened fire on Ottoman forts guarding the straits, hoping to force a way to Constantinople. The naval effort failed in March, leading to the Gallipoli landings.

02-19.title: Roosevelt signs Executive Order 9066
02-19.description: The order allowed the military to exclude people from designated areas, leading to the internment of about 120,000 Japanese Americans. Congress apologised and paid reparations in 1988.

02-19.title: US Marines land on Iwo Jima
02-19.description: The 36-day battle killed nearly 7,000 Americans and almost all of the 21,000 Japanese defenders. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the flag raising on Mount Suribachi became an icon.

02-20.title: Orkney and Shetland annexed to the Scottish crown
02-20.description: Pledged by Christian I of Denmark-Norway as security for his daughter's dowry when she married James III, the unredeemed islands were formally annexed by the Scottish Parliament.

02-20.title: Nine-year-old Edward VI is crowned
02-20.description: Henry VIII's only son was crowned at Westminster Abbey. Under his regents England became firmly Protestant, but Edward died aged fifteen in 1553.

02-20.title: Washington signs the Postal Service Act
02-20.description: The act established the US Post Office on a permanent footing and allowed newspapers to be mailed cheaply. It helped bind together a scattered young republic.

02-20.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art opens in New York
02-20.description: The museum opened in a former dance academy on Fifth Avenue with a modest collection. It moved to Central Park in 1880 and grew into one of the world's largest art museums.

02-20.title: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit Earth
02-20.description: Aboard Friendship 7, Glenn circled the Earth three times in under five hours. Ten months after Yuri Gagarin's flight, it restored American confidence in the space race.

02-20.title: Soviet Union launches the core of the Mir space station
02-20.description: Mir's first module was launched from Baikonur. Expanded over ten years, the station hosted crews from many nations and was continuously occupied for almost a decade before its re-entry in 2001.

02-21.title: Mikhail Romanov elected Tsar of Russia
02-21.description: An assembly of the land chose sixteen-year-old Mikhail Romanov as tsar (21 February Old Style), ending the Time of Troubles. His dynasty ruled Russia until the revolution of 1917.

02-21.title: Trevithick's steam locomotive makes the first railway journey
02-21.description: Richard Trevithick's locomotive hauled ten tons of iron and some 70 men along the Penydarren tramway in South Wales. It was the first working railway journey by a steam locomotive.

02-21.title: Marx and Engels publish 'The Communist Manifesto'
02-21.description: Commissioned by the Communist League, the pamphlet appeared in German in London just as revolution swept Europe. Its call 'Workers of the world, unite!' inspired socialist movements for generations.

02-21.title: Battle of Verdun begins
02-21.description: After a massive bombardment, the German army attacked the French fortress city of Verdun. The battle lasted ten months and caused some 700,000 casualties, becoming a symbol of French endurance.

02-21.title: Malcolm X assassinated in Harlem
02-21.description: Malcolm X was shot dead as he began speaking at the Audubon Ballroom in New York. A year after leaving the Nation of Islam, he had been moving towards a broader vision of human rights.

02-21.title: Richard Nixon arrives in Beijing
02-21.description: Nixon became the first US President to visit the People's Republic of China, meeting Mao Zedong. His week-long trip ended more than two decades of hostility and reshaped Cold War diplomacy.

02-22.title: Charles VIII of France enters Naples
02-22.description: After a rapid march through Italy, the French king took Naples almost without a fight. A coalition of Italian states, Spain and the Emperor soon forced him out, but the Italian Wars had begun.

02-22.title: George Washington is born in Virginia
02-22.description: Born at Popes Creek in Westmoreland County, Washington commanded the Continental Army in the Revolutionary War and became the first President of the United States.

02-22.title: Spain cedes Florida in the Adams-Onís Treaty
02-22.description: Spain gave Florida to the United States and agreed a boundary running to the Pacific. In return the US assumed claims of its citizens against Spain and gave up its claim to Texas.

02-22.title: Battle of Buena Vista begins in northern Mexico
02-22.description: Zachary Taylor's outnumbered army held off Santa Anna's attacks over two days near Saltillo. Santa Anna withdrew, and Taylor's fame carried him to the presidency in 1848.

02-22.title: US amateurs beat the Soviet Union in the 'Miracle on Ice'
02-22.description: A team of American college players defeated the Soviet Union, four-time Olympic champions, 4-3 at the Lake Placid Winter Olympics. The US went on to win the gold medal.

02-22.title: Scientists announce Dolly the sheep, the first clone of an adult mammal
02-22.description: Researchers at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh revealed they had cloned a sheep from an adult cell. Dolly, born in July 1996, sparked worldwide debate on the ethics of cloning.

02-23.title: Traditional date for the completion of the Gutenberg Bible
02-23.description: By tradition, Johannes Gutenberg's Bible was completed in Mainz around this date. It was the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type, and print spread rapidly across the continent.

02-23.title: George Frideric Handel is born in Halle
02-23.description: Handel trained in Germany and Italy before settling in London, where he wrote operas, the 'Water Music' and the oratorio 'Messiah'. He became a naturalised British subject in 1727.

02-23.title: Siege of the Alamo begins
02-23.description: Santa Anna's Mexican army surrounded the Texian garrison in the Alamo mission at San Antonio. After thirteen days the defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett, were killed in the final assault.

02-23.title: Lincoln arrives secretly in Washington
02-23.description: Warned of a plot to kill him in Baltimore, President-elect Lincoln travelled through the city overnight in secret. He was mocked for the manner of his arrival, ten days before his inauguration.

02-23.title: Rotary Club founded in Chicago
02-23.description: Lawyer Paul Harris and three business acquaintances met to found the first Rotary Club. Rotary International now has some 1.4 million members and led the campaign to eradicate polio.

02-23.title: US Marines raise the flag on Mount Suribachi
02-23.description: Marines planted the US flag on the summit of Iwo Jima's volcano. Joe Rosenthal's photograph of the second, larger flag won the Pulitzer Prize, though the fighting went on for another month.

02-24.title: Imperial army captures Francis I at the Battle of Pavia
02-24.description: Charles V's troops routed the French outside Pavia, and King Francis I was taken prisoner. He was released in 1526 only after signing away claims in Italy and Burgundy.

02-24.title: Pope Gregory XIII issues the bull reforming the calendar
02-24.description: The bull Inter gravissimas introduced the Gregorian calendar, dropping ten days that October to realign the calendar with the equinox. It is now the world's standard civil calendar.

02-24.title: Marbury v. Madison establishes judicial review
02-24.description: Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the Supreme Court could strike down acts of Congress that conflicted with the Constitution. The decision became a cornerstone of American constitutional law.

02-24.title: Plan of Iguala sets out Mexican independence
02-24.description: Agustín de Iturbide and Vicente Guerrero proclaimed a plan for an independent Mexican monarchy guaranteeing Catholicism and equality. Mexico's independence was declared that September.

02-24.title: Hitler presents the Nazi Party's 25-point programme
02-24.description: At the Hofbräuhaus in Munich, Hitler read out the programme of the German Workers' Party, which renamed itself the National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP) around this time.

02-24.title: Juan Perón elected President of Argentina
02-24.description: The former labour minister won the presidency with strong support from trade unions. With his wife Eva, he built the populist Peronist movement that still shapes Argentine politics.

02-25.title: Hadrian adopts Antoninus Pius as his heir
02-25.description: Hadrian made Antoninus his successor on condition that he adopt Marcus Aurelius and Lucius Verus. The arrangement secured more than four decades of stable rule.

02-25.title: Pope Pius V excommunicates Elizabeth I
02-25.description: The bull Regnans in Excelsis declared Elizabeth a heretic and released her subjects from obedience. English Catholics came to be seen as potential traitors, and persecution intensified.

02-25.title: Samuel Colt patents his revolver
02-25.description: Colt received a US patent for a revolving-cylinder pistol. His first company failed, but orders during the Mexican-American War made Colt revolvers famous worldwide.

02-25.title: Hiram Revels becomes the first African American US Senator
02-25.description: The Mississippi minister was sworn in after a fierce debate over his eligibility. He filled the seat Jefferson Davis had left when the South seceded.

02-25.title: Adolf Hitler acquires German citizenship
02-25.description: Stateless since renouncing his Austrian citizenship in 1925, Hitler was given a nominal post in the state of Brunswick, making him a German citizen. He could now stand for President.

02-25.title: People Power Revolution forces Marcos from the Philippines
02-25.description: After days of peaceful mass protest, Ferdinand Marcos fled Manila for Hawaii and Corazon Aquino was sworn in as president. His two decades of rule had included years of martial law.

02-26.title: Valentinian I proclaimed Roman Emperor
02-26.description: Army officers chose Valentinian, a Pannonian general, as emperor at Nicaea. A month later he made his brother Valens co-emperor in the East, while he ruled the West.

02-26.title: Galileo is warned to abandon Copernican theory
02-26.description: Cardinal Bellarmine instructed Galileo, on the Pope's orders, not to hold or defend the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. His 1632 'Dialogue' led to his trial for breaching the order.

02-26.title: Napoleon escapes from Elba
02-26.description: With about a thousand men, Napoleon slipped away from his island exile and sailed for France. He regained power without a shot, beginning the Hundred Days that ended at Waterloo.

02-26.title: Grand Canyon becomes a US national park
02-26.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed the act creating Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona. The gorge, carved by the Colorado River, is over 1.6 km deep in places.

02-26.title: Robert Watson-Watt's team demonstrates radar
02-26.description: At Daventry, radio waves from a BBC transmitter bounced off an RAF bomber and were detected on a screen. The test led to the Chain Home network, vital in the Battle of Britain.

02-26.title: Truck bomb explodes beneath the World Trade Center
02-26.description: Islamist militants detonated a bomb in the North Tower's underground car park, killing six people and injuring more than 1,000. The towers survived but were destroyed in the attacks of 2001.

02-27.title: Edict of Thessalonica makes Nicene Christianity Rome's state faith
02-27.description: Emperors Theodosius I, Gratian and Valentinian II decreed that all subjects should follow the Christianity of the bishops of Rome and Alexandria. Other Christians were branded heretics.

02-27.title: Henry IV crowned King of France at Chartres
02-27.description: A former Protestant who had converted to Catholicism, Henry was crowned at Chartres because Reims was held by the Catholic League. His Edict of Nantes in 1598 ended the Wars of Religion.

02-27.title: Lord Byron's maiden speech defends the Luddites
02-27.description: In the House of Lords, the young poet spoke against the Frame-Breaking Bill, which made wrecking machinery a capital crime. He blamed the desperation of the weavers on poverty, but the bill passed.

02-27.title: Labour Representation Committee founded in London
02-27.description: Trade unionists and socialist societies formed a committee to elect working-class MPs. Renamed the Labour Party in 1906, it formed governments from 1924 and created the NHS in 1948.

02-27.title: Fire destroys the Reichstag in Berlin
02-27.description: The German parliament building burned and a young Dutch communist, Marinus van der Lubbe, was arrested. Next day Hitler secured a decree suspending civil liberties, a key step to dictatorship.

02-27.title: Britain and France recognise Franco's government
02-27.description: With Barcelona fallen, Britain and France recognised the Nationalist regime as Spain's government a month before the Civil War ended. Franco ruled Spain until his death in 1975.

02-28.title: Hernán Cortés executes Cuauhtémoc, the last Aztec emperor
02-28.description: Held captive since the fall of Tenochtitlan, Cuauhtémoc was hanged during Cortés's expedition to Honduras on a charge of conspiracy. He is honoured in Mexico as a symbol of resistance.

02-28.title: John Wesley gives Methodism legal standing
02-28.description: Wesley's Deed of Declaration made a conference of 100 preachers the legal governing body of the Methodist societies. It ensured the movement could survive him, though it formally left the Church of England only later.

02-28.title: Congress votes to annex Texas
02-28.description: The House agreed to a Senate joint resolution offering annexation to the Republic of Texas, signed by President Tyler on 1 March. Mexico broke off relations, and war followed in 1846.

02-28.title: Watson and Crick work out the structure of DNA
02-28.description: At the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge, Francis Crick and James Watson arrived at the double-helix model of DNA, drawing on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data. They published it in April.

02-28.title: Gulf War ceasefire takes effect
02-28.description: One hundred hours after the ground offensive began, coalition forces halted operations, Kuwait having been liberated. Saddam Hussein remained in power in Baghdad.

02-28.title: Federal raid on the Branch Davidians begins the Waco siege
02-28.description: A gun battle at the compound near Waco, Texas, killed four federal agents and six Branch Davidians. The 51-day siege ended on 19 April in a fire that killed 76 people, including children.

03-01.title: Massacre of Huguenots at Wassy sparks the French Wars of Religion
03-01.description: Troops escorting the Duke of Guise attacked Protestants worshipping in a barn at Wassy, killing some 50 to 60. The killings set off more than three decades of religious civil war in France.

03-01.title: Salem witch trial examinations begin
03-01.description: Magistrates questioned Sarah Good, Sarah Osborne and the enslaved woman Tituba in Salem Village, Massachusetts. Accusations spread, and by autumn twenty people had been executed.

03-01.title: Articles of Confederation come into force
03-01.description: Maryland's ratification brought into effect the first constitution of the United States. The weak confederation lacked powers to tax and was replaced by the Constitution in 1789.

03-01.title: Napoleon lands in France after escaping Elba
03-01.description: Napoleon came ashore at Golfe-Juan near Cannes with about a thousand men. Troops sent to stop him joined him instead, and he entered Paris on 20 March to begin the Hundred Days.

03-01.title: Texas convention assembles at Washington-on-the-Brazos
03-01.description: Delegates from across Texas met in a half-built hall to decide the province's future while the Alamo was under siege. The next day they declared independence from Mexico.

03-01.title: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park
03-01.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the act setting aside Yellowstone's geysers and canyons 'for the benefit and enjoyment of the people'. The national park idea spread around the world.

03-01.title: Henri Becquerel discovers radioactivity
03-01.description: Becquerel found that uranium salts left in a drawer had fogged a photographic plate without any sunlight. He had discovered radioactivity, soon investigated by Marie and Pierre Curie.

03-01.title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at the Battle of Adwa
03-01.description: Emperor Menelik II's army routed an Italian invasion force in northern Ethiopia. The victory forced Italy to recognise Ethiopian independence and became a lasting symbol of African resistance.

03-01.title: Koreans rise against Japanese rule in the March 1st Movement
03-01.description: A declaration of independence was read in Seoul, and peaceful demonstrations spread across Korea. Japanese forces suppressed them, killing thousands, but the movement inspired Korean nationalism.

03-01.title: International Monetary Fund begins operations
03-01.description: Created at the Bretton Woods conference of 1944, the IMF opened for business in Washington. It was designed to stabilise exchange rates and lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulties.

03-01.title: Castle Bravo, the largest US nuclear test, contaminates the Pacific
03-01.description: The hydrogen bomb tested at Bikini Atoll yielded 15 megatons, far more than predicted. Fallout sickened Marshall Islanders and the crew of the Japanese fishing boat Lucky Dragon No. 5.

03-01.title: US Supreme Court bans the execution of juvenile offenders
03-01.description: In Roper v. Simmons the Court ruled five to four that executing people for crimes committed under 18 was cruel and unusual punishment. The decision spared some 70 people on death row.

03-02.title: Louis V becomes the last Carolingian King of the Franks
03-02.description: On the death of his father Lothair, Louis V became sole king. He died a year later without an heir, and the nobles elected Hugh Capet, founder of the Capetian dynasty.

03-02.title: Swiss defeat Charles the Bold at Grandson
03-02.description: The Swiss Confederates routed the Burgundian army near Lake Neuchâtel and seized Charles the Bold's rich baggage train. Further defeats at Morat and Nancy destroyed Burgundian power.

03-02.title: Jefferson signs the act banning the importation of slaves
03-02.description: The law prohibited bringing enslaved people into the United States from 1 January 1808, the earliest date the Constitution allowed. Smuggling and the domestic slave trade continued.

03-02.title: Texas declares independence from Mexico
03-02.description: Delegates at Washington-on-the-Brazos adopted a declaration of independence, creating the Republic of Texas. Victory at San Jacinto in April secured it, and Texas joined the United States in 1845.

03-02.title: Congress creates the Nevada and Dakota territories
03-02.description: Two days before leaving office, President James Buchanan signed acts organising the Nevada and Dakota territories. Nevada's silver helped finance the Union, and it became a state in 1864.

03-02.title: Rutherford B. Hayes declared winner of the disputed 1876 election
03-02.description: Congress confirmed the Electoral Commission's award of all disputed votes to Hayes, giving him victory by one electoral vote. Under the Compromise of 1877, federal troops left the South.

03-02.title: D. H. Lawrence dies in the south of France
03-02.description: The author of 'Sons and Lovers' and 'Lady Chatterley's Lover' died of tuberculosis at Vence, aged 44. 'Lady Chatterley' was not published openly in Britain until the 1960 obscenity trial.

03-02.title: Battle of the Bismarck Sea begins
03-02.description: American and Australian aircraft attacked a Japanese convoy bound for New Guinea, sinking all eight transports and four destroyers over three days. About 3,000 Japanese troops died.

03-02.title: Concorde makes its first flight
03-02.description: Test pilot André Turcat flew the Anglo-French supersonic airliner prototype from Toulouse. Concorde entered passenger service in 1976 and flew until 2003.

03-03.title: Glycerius proclaimed Western Roman Emperor
03-03.description: Backed by the Burgundian general Gundobad, the court official Glycerius was proclaimed emperor at Ravenna. Deposed the next year, he was one of the short-lived final rulers of the Western Empire.

03-03.title: Teatro Olimpico opens in Vicenza
03-03.description: Andrea Palladio's theatre opened with a performance of Sophocles's 'Oedipus Rex'. Its permanent painted street scenes survive, making it the oldest surviving enclosed theatre in the world.

03-03.title: Continental Marines land at Nassau in the Bahamas
03-03.description: In their first amphibious operation, American marines and sailors captured two British forts on New Providence island, seizing cannon and military stores.

03-03.title: Florida becomes the 27th US state
03-03.description: Florida, acquired from Spain in 1819, was admitted to the Union as a slave state. It seceded in 1861 and is now the third most populous state.

03-03.title: Lajos Kossuth demands constitutional reform for Hungary
03-03.description: In the Hungarian Diet at Pressburg, Kossuth called for a responsible government and constitutional rule. His speech, made as revolution swept Europe, helped launch the Hungarian revolution of 1848.

03-03.title: Treaty of San Stefano creates a 'Greater Bulgaria'
03-03.description: Ending the Russo-Turkish War, the treaty created a large autonomous Bulgaria. The other great powers revised it at the Congress of Berlin that summer, leaving lasting Balkan grievances.

03-03.title: Soviet Russia signs the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
03-03.description: The Bolsheviks made peace with the Central Powers, giving up Poland, the Baltic lands and Ukraine, with about a third of the old empire's population. Germany's defeat later voided the treaty.

03-03.title: Time magazine publishes its first issue
03-03.description: Founded by Henry Luce and Briton Hadden, Time summarised the week's news in a brisk, distinctive style. It became one of the most influential magazines in the world.

03-03.title: Rodney King's beating by Los Angeles police is filmed
03-03.description: A bystander videotaped officers beating Rodney King after a car chase. The officers' acquittal in April 1992 sparked riots in Los Angeles in which more than 60 people died.

03-04.title: Frederick Barbarossa elected King of Germany
03-04.description: The German princes chose Frederick of Hohenstaufen as king at Frankfurt. Crowned emperor in 1155, he fought repeated campaigns in Italy and clashed with the papacy until his death on crusade in 1190.

03-04.title: Edward IV proclaimed King of England
03-04.description: The Yorkist Edward, Earl of March, was proclaimed king in London, deposing the Lancastrian Henry VI. Weeks later he won the bloody Battle of Towton, securing his throne.

03-04.title: US Constitution takes effect as the first Congress meets
03-04.description: The new federal government began operation as Congress gathered at Federal Hall in New York, though it took weeks to reach a quorum. The Constitution is the oldest written national constitution still in force.

03-04.title: Abraham Lincoln inaugurated as 16th President
03-04.description: With seven states already seceded, Lincoln appealed to 'the better angels of our nature' in his inaugural address. War began at Fort Sumter five weeks later.

03-04.title: Tchaikovsky's 'Swan Lake' premieres at the Bolshoi
03-04.description: The first production in Moscow was poorly received. Revived in St Petersburg in 1895 with choreography by Petipa and Ivanov, it became the most famous of all ballets.

03-04.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt inaugurated in the depths of the Depression
03-04.description: With banks failing nationwide, Roosevelt told Americans 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself'. In his first hundred days Congress passed a wave of New Deal legislation.

03-04.title: John Lennon says the Beatles are 'more popular than Jesus'
03-04.description: The remark appeared in an interview in London's Evening Standard and passed unnoticed in Britain. Reprinted in the US months later, it led to record burnings and radio bans.

03-05.title: Emperor Julian sets out to invade Persia
03-05.description: Julian left Antioch with a large army to attack the Sasanian Empire. He reached Ctesiphon but was killed during the retreat in June, and with him ended the last attempt to restore paganism.

03-05.title: Henry VII commissions John Cabot to seek new lands
03-05.description: Letters patent authorised the Venetian navigator to sail under the English flag in search of unknown lands. His 1497 voyage reached North America and later underpinned English claims there.

03-05.title: British soldiers kill five in the Boston Massacre
03-05.description: Soldiers fired into a crowd taunting them in King Street, killing five men, including Crispus Attucks. Paul Revere's engraving of the scene became powerful propaganda against British rule.

03-05.title: Churchill warns of an 'iron curtain' across Europe
03-05.description: Speaking at Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill declared that an iron curtain had descended across the continent from the Baltic to the Adriatic. The speech popularised the phrase and the Cold War divide.

03-05.title: Joseph Stalin dies
03-05.description: The Soviet dictator died four days after a stroke at his dacha near Moscow. His rule had brought rapid industrialisation and victory over Germany, but also famine, purges and millions of deaths.

03-05.title: Alberto Korda photographs Che Guevara
03-05.description: At a Havana memorial for victims of a ship explosion, Korda captured Guevara's gaze in a photograph later titled 'Guerrillero Heroico'. It became one of the most reproduced images in the world.

03-05.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty enters into force
03-05.description: The treaty committed nuclear powers not to spread weapons and others not to acquire them, while promoting peaceful nuclear energy. With 191 parties, it is the most widely joined arms control agreement.

03-06.title: Philip II of France takes Château Gaillard
03-06.description: French troops captured Richard the Lionheart's great castle above the Seine after a six-month siege, some climbing in through a latrine chute. Normandy fell to France within months.

03-06.title: President Monroe signs the Missouri Compromise
03-06.description: Missouri was to enter the Union as a slave state and Maine as a free one, with slavery barred from the rest of the Louisiana Purchase north of 36°30'. The balance held for three decades.

03-06.title: The Alamo falls to Santa Anna
03-06.description: Mexican troops stormed the mission at dawn after a 13-day siege, killing nearly all of its roughly 200 defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. 'Remember the Alamo' became the Texan battle cry.

03-06.title: US Supreme Court decides Dred Scott v. Sandford
03-06.description: Chief Justice Roger Taney ruled that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories. The decision deepened the crisis that led to civil war.

03-06.title: Clarence Birdseye's frozen foods go on sale
03-06.description: Shops in Springfield, Massachusetts, began selling quick-frozen vegetables, fruit, fish and meat using Birdseye's process. Frozen food went on to transform shopping and diets.

03-06.title: Ghana becomes independent
03-06.description: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence from a European power after the war. It inspired independence movements across Africa.

03-07.title: Marcus Aurelius becomes Roman Emperor
03-07.description: On the death of Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius succeeded and made his adoptive brother Lucius Verus co-emperor. A Stoic philosopher, he wrote his 'Meditations' while campaigning on the Danube.

03-07.title: Napoleon storms Jaffa
03-07.description: French troops took the port of Jaffa during Napoleon's Syrian campaign. Thousands of prisoners were then executed, and plague broke out in the army, which was halted at Acre.

03-07.title: Daniel Webster's 'Seventh of March' speech backs compromise
03-07.description: The Massachusetts senator supported Henry Clay's compromise proposals, including a tougher fugitive slave law, to preserve the Union. Many Northern abolitionists denounced him.

03-07.title: Alexander Graham Bell is granted his telephone patent
03-07.description: US Patent 174,465 covered a method of transmitting speech electrically. It became one of the most valuable patents ever issued and was defended in hundreds of lawsuits.

03-07.title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
03-07.description: Hitler sent soldiers into the demilitarised Rhineland in breach of the Versailles and Locarno treaties. France and Britain did not respond with force, encouraging further German expansion.

03-07.title: US troops seize the Remagen bridge over the Rhine
03-07.description: American soldiers captured the Ludendorff railway bridge at Remagen before German demolition charges could destroy it. It gave the Allies their first crossing of the Rhine.

03-07.title: 'Bloody Sunday' on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma
03-07.description: Alabama state troopers attacked about 600 civil rights marchers with clubs and tear gas. Televised images shocked the nation and helped secure the Voting Rights Act that August.

03-08.title: Ferdowsi completes the 'Shahnameh'
03-08.description: After some thirty years' work, the poet Ferdowsi finished his epic of the kings of Iran, around 50,000 couplets long. Written in Persian with few Arabic words, it is Iran's national epic.

03-08.title: Anne becomes queen on the death of William III
03-08.description: William III died after a fall from his horse, and his sister-in-law Anne succeeded. During her reign England and Scotland united as Great Britain in 1707.

03-08.title: New York brokers form the New York Stock and Exchange Board
03-08.description: Brokers adopted a constitution and rented rooms on Wall Street, building on the Buttonwood Agreement of 1792. Their exchange became the New York Stock Exchange.

03-08.title: Raymonde de Laroche becomes the first licensed woman pilot
03-08.description: The Aéro-Club de France issued licence no. 36 to the French aviator. She set altitude records before dying in a crash in 1919.

03-08.title: Protests in Petrograd begin the February Revolution
03-08.description: On International Women's Day (23 February Old Style), women textile workers protesting about bread shortages began strikes that spread across the city. Within a week Tsar Nicholas II had abdicated.

03-08.title: Japanese forces occupy Rangoon
03-08.description: Japanese troops entered Burma's capital, abandoned by the British. The loss cut the Burma Road supply route to China, and by May Japan controlled most of Burma.

03-08.title: Joe Frazier beats Muhammad Ali in the 'Fight of the Century'
03-08.description: At Madison Square Garden, Frazier won a unanimous decision after knocking Ali down in the 15th round. It was Ali's first professional defeat.

03-09.title: Gregory VII's synod condemns married and simoniac priests
03-09.description: At his Lenten synod in Rome, Pope Gregory VII barred married priests and those who had bought office from ministering. The reforms helped impose clerical celibacy in the Western Church.

03-09.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral sails from Lisbon
03-09.description: Cabral's fleet of 13 ships left for India, swinging far west into the Atlantic. On 22 April it sighted the coast of Brazil, which Cabral claimed for Portugal.

03-09.title: Napoleon Bonaparte marries Joséphine de Beauharnais
03-09.description: The civil wedding in Paris took place two days before Napoleon left to command the Army of Italy. Joséphine became empress in 1804, but he divorced her in 1810 for lack of an heir.

03-09.title: Supreme Court frees the Amistad Africans
03-09.description: The Court ruled that the Mende captives who had seized the slave ship Amistad had been illegally enslaved. Argued by John Quincy Adams, the case became a cause for abolitionists.

03-09.title: Monitor and Virginia fight the first battle between ironclads
03-09.description: At Hampton Roads, Virginia, USS Monitor and the Confederate CSS Virginia fought for hours without decisive damage. The duel showed that wooden warships were obsolete.

03-09.title: Pancho Villa raids Columbus, New Mexico
03-09.description: Some 500 of Villa's fighters attacked the border town, killing 18 Americans. The US sent General John Pershing on a punitive expedition into Mexico, which failed to catch Villa.

03-09.title: US firebombing raid devastates Tokyo
03-09.description: In the night of 9-10 March, some 300 B-29 bombers dropped incendiaries on Tokyo, burning about 41 square kilometres. Around 100,000 people died, the deadliest air raid in history.

03-10.title: Rome defeats Carthage at the Aegates Islands
03-10.description: A new Roman fleet destroyed a Carthaginian relief fleet off western Sicily. Carthage sued for peace, ending the First Punic War and ceding Sicily, Rome's first overseas province.

03-10.title: Charles I dissolves Parliament and begins his Personal Rule
03-10.description: After clashes over taxation and religion, Charles dissolved Parliament and governed without one for eleven years. Financial need forced him to recall it in 1640, leading to civil war.

03-10.title: Upper Louisiana formally passes to the United States
03-10.description: In a ceremony at St Louis, the Spanish flag was lowered and the French tricolour raised, then the next day replaced by the Stars and Stripes. It completed the transfer of the Louisiana Purchase.

03-10.title: US Senate ratifies the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
03-10.description: The Senate approved the peace with Mexico, which ceded California and much of the Southwest. The United States paid 15 million dollars and assumed its citizens' claims against Mexico.

03-10.title: Bell makes the first telephone call
03-10.description: In his Boston laboratory Alexander Graham Bell spoke into his transmitter: 'Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you.' His assistant Thomas Watson heard him in the next room.

03-10.title: James Earl Ray pleads guilty to killing Martin Luther King Jr.
03-10.description: Ray was sentenced to 99 years in prison. Days later he recanted his plea and sought a trial for the rest of his life, fuelling persistent claims of a conspiracy.

03-10.title: Nasdaq peaks at the height of the dot-com bubble
03-10.description: The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite index closed at 5,048, more than double its level a year earlier. It then fell by nearly 80 per cent by October 2002 as internet stocks collapsed.

03-11.title: Giovanni de' Medici proclaimed Pope Leo X
03-11.description: The son of Lorenzo the Magnificent was announced as pope at 37. A lavish patron of Raphael and others, he promoted the indulgence campaign for St Peter's that provoked Martin Luther in 1517.

03-11.title: The Daily Courant, Britain's first daily newspaper, appears
03-11.description: Published by Elizabeth Mallet near Fleet Street, the single-sheet Courant carried foreign news translated from continental papers. It ran until 1735, founding the British daily press.

03-11.title: Luddite machine-breaking begins in Nottinghamshire
03-11.description: After a protest in Nottingham was dispersed, framework knitters broke dozens of stocking frames at Arnold. Attacks on machinery spread across the Midlands and North under the name of 'Ned Ludd'.

03-11.title: Verdi's 'Rigoletto' premieres in Venice
03-11.description: The opera of a hunchbacked jester was a triumph at La Fenice. Verdi reportedly kept the aria 'La donna è mobile' secret until the final rehearsals, and it was soon sung in the streets.

03-11.title: British and Indian troops capture Baghdad
03-11.description: General Stanley Maude's army entered Baghdad after the Ottoman garrison withdrew, avenging the surrender at Kut a year earlier. Britain went on to rule Mesopotamia, later Iraq, under a League mandate.

03-11.title: Roosevelt signs the Lend-Lease Act
03-11.description: The act allowed the United States to lend or lease war supplies to nations whose defence was vital to America. Britain, the Soviet Union and China received some 50 billion dollars of aid.

03-11.title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes Soviet leader
03-11.description: The 54-year-old Gorbachev was chosen General Secretary the day after Konstantin Chernenko's death. His policies of glasnost and perestroika unleashed forces that ended the Soviet Union in 1991.

03-11.title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
03-11.description: The World Health Organization described the coronavirus outbreak as a pandemic, with cases in over 100 countries. Lockdowns followed worldwide, and millions died in the years that followed.

03-12.title: Odo of Châtillon elected Pope Urban II
03-12.description: Elected at Terracina while a rival pope held Rome, Urban II continued Gregory VII's reforms. In 1095 he preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont.

03-12.title: Charles II grants New Netherland to the Duke of York
03-12.description: The King granted his brother James lands between the Connecticut and Delaware rivers, then held by the Dutch. English ships seized New Amsterdam that August and renamed it New York.

03-12.title: Juliette Gordon Low founds the Girl Scouts in Savannah
03-12.description: Inspired by the Guide movement she had seen in Britain, Low gathered 18 girls for the first meeting of the American Girl Guides. Renamed the Girl Scouts in 1913, it has had tens of millions of members.

03-12.title: German troops march into Austria
03-12.description: The Wehrmacht crossed the border unopposed and was greeted by cheering crowds. The next day Austria was declared part of the German Reich, the Anschluss that Versailles had forbidden.

03-12.title: Truman announces the Truman Doctrine
03-12.description: Asking Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey, Harry Truman pledged to support 'free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation'. The doctrine framed US Cold War policy of containment.

03-12.title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
03-12.description: At CERN in Geneva, Berners-Lee circulated 'Information Management: A Proposal' for a hypertext system linking documents across computers. His supervisor called it 'vague but exciting'.

03-13.title: Hernán Cortés lands on the Mexican coast
03-13.description: Cortés's expedition of about 500 men reached the Tabasco coast. Within two and a half years, with Indigenous allies, he overthrew the Aztec Empire and captured Tenochtitlan.

03-13.title: New College in Massachusetts is named after John Harvard
03-13.description: The college at Cambridge took the name of John Harvard, a young minister who left it his library and half his estate. Founded in 1636, Harvard is the oldest university in the United States.

03-13.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
03-13.description: From his garden in Bath, Herschel spotted an object he first took for a comet. It proved to be a new planet, the first discovered with a telescope, doubling the known size of the solar system.

03-13.title: Tsar Alexander II assassinated in St Petersburg
03-13.description: Members of the revolutionary group People's Will threw bombs at the Tsar's carriage. Alexander, who had freed the serfs, died within hours, and his son's reign brought harsh reaction.

03-13.title: Winter War ends as the Moscow Peace Treaty takes effect
03-13.description: Finland ceded about a tenth of its territory, including Karelia, to the Soviet Union. Its stubborn defence had cost the Red Army heavily and preserved Finnish independence.

03-13.title: Gunman kills 16 children and their teacher at Dunblane
03-13.description: Thomas Hamilton opened fire in the gym of Dunblane Primary School in Scotland before killing himself. Public campaigning led to a near-total ban on private handgun ownership in Britain.

03-14.title: Admiral John Byng executed by firing squad
03-14.description: Convicted of failing to do his utmost to relieve Minorca, Byng was shot on the deck of HMS Monarch at Portsmouth. Voltaire mocked the English for killing an admiral 'to encourage the others'.

03-14.title: Eli Whitney patents the cotton gin
03-14.description: Whitney's machine separated cotton fibre from seeds far faster than by hand. It made short-staple cotton highly profitable and fuelled a vast expansion of slavery in the American South.

03-14.title: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm
03-14.description: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity transformed ideas of space, time and gravity. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

03-14.title: Gold Standard Act puts the dollar on gold
03-14.description: President McKinley signed the act fixing the dollar's value in gold and ending the long political fight over free silver. The US left the gold standard domestically in 1933.

03-14.title: Penicillin saves its first American patient
03-14.description: Anne Miller, dying of streptococcal blood poisoning after a miscarriage, was treated at a New Haven hospital with a scarce supply of penicillin. She recovered and lived to the age of 90.

03-14.title: Jack Ruby convicted of murdering Lee Harvey Oswald
03-14.description: A Dallas jury found the nightclub owner guilty of shooting Kennedy's accused assassin on live television and sentenced him to death. The verdict was overturned, and Ruby died before a retrial.

03-15.title: Julius Caesar assassinated on the Ides of March
03-15.description: A group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed Caesar to death in the Curia of Pompey. Meant to save the Republic, the murder led to civil war and the rule of Augustus.

03-15.title: Theoderic the Great kills Odoacer at Ravenna
03-15.description: After a long siege ended in a power-sharing agreement, Theoderic murdered Odoacer at a banquet. The Ostrogothic king then ruled Italy for over thirty years.

03-15.title: Columbus returns to Spain from his first voyage
03-15.description: Columbus sailed into Palos, the port from which he had departed seven months earlier, with news of islands across the Atlantic. His voyages began lasting European contact with the Americas.

03-15.title: Akbar abolishes the jizya tax on non-Muslims
03-15.description: The Mughal emperor ended the poll tax on non-Muslim subjects, part of a policy of conciliating the Hindu majority of his empire. Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679.

03-15.title: Maine becomes the 23rd US state
03-15.description: Separated from Massachusetts, Maine entered the Union as a free state under the Missouri Compromise. Its admission balanced that of Missouri as a slave state.

03-15.title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
03-15.description: Facing revolution in Petrograd and mutiny in the army, Nicholas II gave up the throne for himself and his son. Over three centuries of Romanov rule ended, and a Provisional Government took power.

03-15.title: Gunman kills 51 at two Christchurch mosques
03-15.description: A white supremacist attacked worshippers at Friday prayers and livestreamed the killings. Within a month New Zealand's parliament banned most semi-automatic weapons.

03-16.title: Nebuchadnezzar II captures Jerusalem
03-16.description: The Babylonian Chronicle records that Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem, carried King Jehoiachin into exile and installed Zedekiah. A revolt led to the city's destruction in 587 BCE.

03-16.title: Magellan's expedition reaches the Philippines
03-16.description: After crossing the Pacific, Ferdinand Magellan's ships sighted Samar and landed at Homonhon. Magellan was killed on Mactan in April, but one ship completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.

03-16.title: Long Parliament dissolves itself
03-16.description: First summoned in 1640, the Long Parliament voted its own dissolution and called new elections. The Convention Parliament that followed invited Charles II to return as king.

03-16.title: Congress establishes the US Military Academy at West Point
03-16.description: President Jefferson signed the act founding a military academy at West Point, New York. Its graduates included Grant, Lee and Eisenhower.

03-16.title: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fuelled rocket
03-16.description: At Auburn, Massachusetts, Goddard's petrol and liquid-oxygen rocket flew for 2.5 seconds and rose about 12 metres. The principle underlies most modern space launch vehicles.

03-16.title: Hitler announces German rearmament and conscription
