03-16.description: Defying the Treaty of Versailles, Hitler reintroduced conscription and announced an army of 36 divisions. Britain, France and Italy protested, but took no effective action.

03-16.title: US soldiers massacre villagers at My Lai
03-16.description: American troops killed some 350 to 500 unarmed civilians, mostly women, children and old men, in a South Vietnamese hamlet. Exposed in 1969, the massacre deepened opposition to the war.

03-17.title: Traditional date of the death of Saint Patrick
03-17.description: By tradition Patrick, the Romano-British missionary to Ireland, died on 17 March, though the year is uncertain. His feast became Ireland's national day, celebrated by the Irish diaspora worldwide.

03-17.title: British troops evacuate Boston
03-17.description: After Washington fortified Dorchester Heights with cannon hauled from Fort Ticonderoga, General Howe's army sailed for Halifax. The siege of Boston ended in an American success.

03-17.title: Stephen Perry patents the rubber band
03-17.description: Stephen Perry of the London firm Messrs Perry and Co patented bands made of vulcanised rubber for holding papers together. The humble invention became universal.

03-17.title: Einstein completes his paper on light quanta
03-17.description: Einstein finished a paper proposing that light comes in discrete packets of energy, explaining the photoelectric effect. It helped found quantum theory and earned him the Nobel Prize.

03-17.title: Brussels Treaty creates a Western European defence pact
03-17.description: Britain, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg agreed to defend one another against attack. The pact paved the way for NATO in 1949 and later became the Western European Union.

03-17.title: US launches Vanguard 1 satellite
03-17.description: The grapefruit-sized satellite, mocked by Khrushchev, showed that the Earth is slightly pear-shaped. Long silent, it is the oldest human-made object still in orbit.

03-18.title: Frederick II crowns himself King of Jerusalem
03-18.description: Having regained Jerusalem by treaty while excommunicated, the Emperor took the crown from the altar of the Holy Sepulchre and placed it on his own head. No cleric would crown him.

03-18.title: Street fighting erupts in Berlin
03-18.description: Troops fired on a crowd outside the royal palace and barricade fighting spread through the city, leaving hundreds dead. King Frederick William IV withdrew the army and promised a constitution.

03-18.title: Parisians rise up and begin the Paris Commune
03-18.description: Attempts by the government to remove the National Guard's cannon from Montmartre provoked an uprising. The Commune ruled Paris until it was crushed in the 'Bloody Week' of May.

03-18.title: Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk
03-18.description: The Soviet cosmonaut spent about 12 minutes outside Voskhod 2. His suit ballooned in the vacuum, and he had to let out air to squeeze back into the airlock.

03-18.title: East Germany holds its first free elections
03-18.description: East Germans voted in their first free parliamentary elections. The conservative Alliance for Germany won, opening the way to rapid reunification with West Germany in October.

03-18.title: Russia signs a treaty annexing Crimea
03-18.description: Two days after a referendum held under Russian military control, Vladimir Putin signed a treaty absorbing Crimea. Most UN members regard the annexation as illegal.

03-19.title: Mongol fleet destroys the last Song forces at Yamen
03-19.description: In a sea battle off the Pearl River delta, Yuan forces crushed the Song navy. The minister Lu Xiufu jumped into the sea with the child emperor, completing Kublai Khan's conquest of China.

03-19.title: Edict of Amboise ends the first French War of Religion
03-19.description: Catherine de' Medici's peace allowed Huguenot nobles to worship freely and others in limited places. Neither side was satisfied, and war resumed in 1567.

03-19.title: René-Robert de La Salle killed by his own men
03-19.description: The explorer who had claimed the Mississippi basin for France was shot by mutineers in east Texas after his colony went astray. His Fort Saint Louis was soon destroyed.

03-19.title: Gounod's 'Faust' premieres in Paris
03-19.description: Charles Gounod's opera, based on Goethe, opened at the Théâtre Lyrique. Revised with recitatives and a ballet, it became one of the most performed operas of the 19th century.

03-19.title: US adopts standard time zones and daylight saving time
03-19.description: The Standard Time Act gave legal force to time zones first used by the railways and introduced daylight saving time to save fuel. Daylight saving proved unpopular and was repealed in 1919.

03-19.title: Hitler issues the 'Nero Decree'
03-19.description: Hitler ordered the destruction of German industry, transport and supplies before they fell to the Allies. Armaments Minister Albert Speer worked to ensure it was largely not carried out.

03-20.title: Dutch East India Company is founded
03-20.description: The States General granted the VOC a monopoly on Dutch trade in Asia. Financed by publicly traded shares, it could wage war, make treaties and found colonies, and dominated the spice trade.

03-20.title: Napoleon returns to Paris
03-20.description: The day after Louis XVIII fled, Napoleon entered the Tuileries to cheering crowds. His restored rule, the Hundred Days, ended with defeat at Waterloo in June.

03-20.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe publishes 'Uncle Tom's Cabin'
03-20.description: Stowe's novel of slavery sold some 300,000 copies in America in its first year and stirred anti-slavery feeling in the North. Lincoln is said to have greeted her as the author who started the war.

03-20.title: Opponents of slavery meet at Ripon to form a new party
03-20.description: Meeting in a schoolhouse in Ripon, Wisconsin, opponents of the Kansas-Nebraska Act called for a new party. The Republican Party was organised that summer and won the presidency in 1860.

03-20.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II dismisses Bismarck
03-20.description: After disputes with the young Emperor, Otto von Bismarck's resignation as Chancellor was accepted. Without him, Germany's alliances shifted, as Britain's Punch caricatured in 'Dropping the Pilot'.

03-20.title: Einstein submits his general theory of relativity
03-20.description: 'The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity' reached the journal Annalen der Physik. It described gravity as the curvature of spacetime and predicted the bending of light, confirmed in 1919.

03-20.title: Himmler announces the Dachau concentration camp
03-20.description: Munich's police chief Heinrich Himmler announced a camp for political prisoners near Dachau, opened two days later. It became the model for the Nazi camp system; over 40,000 died there.

03-21.title: Heraclius restores the True Cross to Jerusalem
03-21.description: By tradition on this day, Emperor Heraclius returned the relic of the cross, captured by the Persians in 614, to Jerusalem. Within a decade the city fell to the Arab armies.

03-21.title: Thomas Cranmer burned at the stake in Oxford
03-21.description: The former Archbishop of Canterbury, author of the Book of Common Prayer, withdrew his recantations before Mary I's officials. He thrust the hand that had signed them into the flames first.

03-21.title: Great fire destroys much of New Orleans
03-21.description: A Good Friday fire burned 856 buildings in the Spanish colonial city. With a second fire in 1794, it led to the rebuilding of the French Quarter in brick and tile.

03-21.title: Pius VII crowned pope in Venice
03-21.description: With Rome occupied by the French, the cardinals met in Venice, where Barnaba Chiaramonti was crowned Pope Pius VII. He later signed a concordat with Napoleon and was held captive by him.

03-21.title: Germany launches its Spring Offensive
03-21.description: Operation Michael struck British lines on the Somme after a five-hour bombardment, gaining more ground in days than any attack since 1914. It ran out of steam, and the Allies counter-attacked that summer.

03-21.title: Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville
03-21.description: South African police fired on an unarmed crowd protesting against the pass laws, killing 69 people. The government banned the ANC and PAC, and 21 March is now Human Rights Day in South Africa.

03-22.title: Pope Clement V suppresses the Knights Templar
03-22.description: Under pressure from Philip IV of France, Clement V issued the bull Vox in excelso at the Council of Vienne abolishing the Templars. Their property passed largely to the Hospitallers.

03-22.title: Powhatan attack kills 347 Virginia colonists
03-22.description: Warriors under Opechancanough struck English settlements along the James River, killing about a quarter of the colony's population. The English responded with years of retaliatory war.

03-22.title: Parliament passes the Stamp Act
03-22.description: The act taxed printed papers in the American colonies, from newspapers to playing cards. Colonists protested 'no taxation without representation', and Parliament repealed it the next year.

03-22.title: Stephen Decatur killed in a duel
03-22.description: The naval hero of the Barbary Wars was mortally wounded by Commodore James Barron at Bladensburg, Maryland. His death strengthened public feeling against duelling.

03-22.title: Lumière brothers show their first film
03-22.description: At a meeting in Paris, Louis and Auguste Lumière projected 'Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory' with their Cinématographe. Their first paying public screening followed in December.

03-22.title: Arab League founded in Cairo
03-22.description: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria signed the pact founding the League of Arab States, with Yemen joining soon after. It now has 22 members.

03-23.title: Waltham Abbey surrenders, the last English monastery to close
03-23.description: The Augustinian abbey at Waltham in Essex was surrendered to Henry VIII's commissioners. It completed the Dissolution of the Monasteries, which transferred vast church lands to the Crown.

03-23.title: Patrick Henry declares 'Give me liberty, or give me death!'
03-23.description: At the Second Virginia Convention in Richmond, Henry urged the colony to raise a militia against Britain. The convention agreed, and fighting began at Lexington four weeks later.

03-23.title: Tsar Paul I murdered in St Michael's Castle
03-23.description: Conspiring officers killed the erratic Tsar in his bedroom in St Petersburg. His son Alexander I, aware of the plot, succeeded him and later led Russia against Napoleon.

03-23.title: Mussolini founds the Fasci di Combattimento in Milan
03-23.description: Benito Mussolini gathered veterans and nationalists in Piazza San Sepolcro to found a new movement. Its blackshirts helped him take power in 1922, and Fascism became a model for Hitler.

03-23.title: Reichstag passes the Enabling Act
03-23.description: With communists barred and others intimidated, the German parliament allowed Hitler's cabinet to make laws without it. Only the Social Democrats voted against, and the dictatorship had a legal basis.

03-23.title: Gemini 3 makes the first crewed Gemini flight
03-23.description: Gus Grissom and John Young flew three orbits and became the first astronauts to change their spacecraft's orbit. The Gemini programme prepared the techniques for Apollo.

03-24.title: Timur sacks Damascus
03-24.description: The Central Asian conqueror's army plundered and burned Damascus after its surrender, and its craftsmen were carried off to Samarkand. The Mamluk Sultanate survived, but Syria was devastated.

03-24.title: Elizabeth I dies and James VI of Scotland inherits England
03-24.description: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace, and her cousin James VI became James I of England and Ireland. The crowns were united, though the kingdoms stayed separate until 1707.

03-24.title: Parliament passes the Quartering Act
03-24.description: The act required American colonies to provide barracks and supplies for British troops. Resentment of it was later listed among the grievances in the Declaration of Independence.

03-24.title: Robert Koch identifies the tuberculosis bacterium
03-24.description: In a lecture in Berlin, Koch showed that tuberculosis, then causing about one in seven deaths in Europe, was caused by a bacterium. 24 March is now World Tuberculosis Day.

03-24.title: Allied prisoners break out in the 'Great Escape'
03-24.description: That night 76 airmen crawled through a tunnel out of Stalag Luft III in Sagan. Only three reached safety; on Hitler's orders, 50 of those recaptured were shot.

03-24.title: Military coup overthrows Isabel Perón in Argentina
03-24.description: A junta led by General Jorge Videla took power and began the 'Dirty War'. Thousands of people, estimated at up to 30,000, were 'disappeared' before military rule ended in 1983.

03-25.title: Robert the Bruce crowned King of Scots at Scone
03-25.description: Weeks after killing his rival John Comyn, Bruce was crowned in defiance of Edward I. Defeated and hunted that year, he fought back to win at Bannockburn in 1314.

03-25.title: Christiaan Huygens discovers Titan
03-25.description: Using a telescope he had built with his brother, Huygens found Saturn's largest moon. Titan is now known to have a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.

03-25.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
03-25.description: The Slave Trade Act received royal assent, banning British participation in the Atlantic slave trade. Slavery itself continued in British colonies until the Abolition Act of 1833.

03-25.title: Traditional start of the Greek War of Independence
03-25.description: Tradition holds that Bishop Germanos of Patras raised the banner of revolt on this day. After years of war and great-power intervention, Greece became independent in 1830.

03-25.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire kills 146 in New York
03-25.description: Fire swept through a garment factory near Washington Square, and locked doors trapped workers, mostly young immigrant women. The disaster led to new fire safety and labour laws.

03-25.title: Treaty of Rome signed
03-25.description: France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg signed treaties creating the European Economic Community and Euratom. The EEC grew into today's European Union.

03-26.title: William Caxton prints his English translation of Aesop's Fables
03-26.description: England's first printer completed his edition of the 'Fables of Esope' at Westminster, illustrated with woodcuts. Caxton's books helped standardise written English.

03-26.title: Earthquake devastates Caracas and Venezuela
03-26.description: On Holy Thursday a powerful earthquake destroyed Caracas and other towns held by the young republic, killing thousands. Royalist clergy called it divine punishment, and the First Republic soon fell.

03-26.title: Ludwig van Beethoven dies in Vienna
03-26.description: Beethoven died aged 56 during a thunderstorm. Despite growing deafness he composed nine symphonies and late string quartets that changed Western music, and some 20,000 people attended his funeral.

03-26.title: Bangladesh declares independence from Pakistan
03-26.description: After the Pakistani army's crackdown in Dhaka, independence was proclaimed in the name of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Nine months of war followed, and Bangladesh won its freedom in December 1971.

03-26.title: Egypt and Israel sign a peace treaty
03-26.description: At the White House, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed the first peace treaty between Israel and an Arab state, building on the Camp David Accords. Israel returned the Sinai by 1982.

03-26.title: Schengen Agreement abolishes border checks in Europe
03-26.description: Seven European countries, including France and Germany, removed passport controls at their common borders. The Schengen Area now covers most of the European Union and several other states.

03-27.title: Juan Ponce de León sights Florida
03-27.description: Sailing north from Puerto Rico, Ponce de León sighted the coast he named La Florida, as it was the Easter season. He landed days later, beginning Spanish claims to the region.

03-27.title: Charles I becomes king on the death of James I
03-27.description: James I died at Theobalds and his son succeeded him. Charles's clashes with Parliament over money and religion led to civil war and his execution in 1649.

03-27.title: Congress passes the Naval Act, founding the US Navy
03-27.description: Prompted by Barbary corsairs seizing American ships, Congress authorised six frigates. Among them was USS Constitution, still in commission today.

03-27.title: Scotland and England play the first rugby international
03-27.description: At Raeburn Place in Edinburgh, Scotland beat England by a goal and a try to a try before about 4,000 spectators. It was the first international rugby match.

03-27.title: Two jumbo jets collide at Tenerife
03-27.description: A KLM 747 began its take-off in fog and struck a Pan Am 747 on the runway at Los Rodeos airport, killing 583 people. It remains the deadliest accident in aviation history.

03-27.title: Mount St Helens erupts for the first time in 123 years
03-27.description: A steam explosion blasted a crater in the summit of the Washington volcano after a week of earthquakes. On 18 May a massive eruption tore away its north face and killed 57 people.

03-28.title: Praetorians murder Pertinax and auction the empire
03-28.description: After killing Emperor Pertinax, the Praetorian Guard sold the throne to the senator Didius Julianus, who outbid his rival. He lasted 66 days before Septimius Severus took power.

03-28.title: Britain and France declare war on Russia
03-28.description: The two powers joined the Ottoman Empire against Russia, beginning their part in the Crimean War. Battlefield reporting and Florence Nightingale's nursing made it a turning point in public views of war.

03-28.title: Henri Fabre makes the first seaplane flight
03-28.description: The French engineer took off from the Étang de Berre near Marseille in his float-equipped Hydravion. It was the first powered aircraft to take off from water.

03-28.title: Virginia Woolf drowns herself in the River Ouse
03-28.description: Fearing a return of mental illness, the novelist filled her pockets with stones and walked into the river near her Sussex home. Her novels include 'Mrs Dalloway' and 'To the Lighthouse'.

03-28.title: Partial meltdown at Three Mile Island
03-28.description: A cooling failure caused part of a reactor core to melt at the Pennsylvania nuclear plant. Little radiation escaped, but it was the worst US nuclear accident and stalled new reactor orders.

03-29.title: Yorkists win the Battle of Towton
03-29.description: Fought in a snowstorm on Palm Sunday in Yorkshire, Towton is often called the bloodiest battle on English soil, with traditional estimates of 28,000 dead. It secured the throne for Edward IV.

03-29.title: Swedish settlers found New Sweden on the Delaware
03-29.description: Colonists from the Kalmar Nyckel and Fogel Grip landed at the site of Wilmington and built Fort Christina. The Dutch took New Sweden in 1655, but its log cabins became an American tradition.

03-29.title: Ice jam stops Niagara Falls
03-29.description: Ice blocking the Niagara River at Lake Erie reduced the falls to a trickle for over a day. Sightseers walked on the riverbed; it is the only time the falls are known to have stopped naturally.

03-29.title: Queen Victoria signs the British North America Act
03-29.description: The act united the Province of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as the Dominion of Canada. Confederation took effect on 1 July, now Canada Day.

03-29.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg convicted of espionage
03-29.description: A New York jury found the couple guilty of conspiring to pass atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Their execution in 1953 remained controversial, especially over Ethel's role.

03-29.title: Last US combat troops leave South Vietnam
03-29.description: The final American combat units departed under the Paris Peace Accords, and the last prisoners of war were released. Some 58,000 Americans and millions of Vietnamese had died in the war.

03-30.title: Sicilian Vespers uprising begins in Palermo
03-30.description: At the hour of vespers outside the church of Santo Spirito, Sicilians rose against Charles of Anjou's French rule, killing thousands. The island passed to Peter III of Aragon.

03-30.title: Allied armies win the Battle of Paris
03-30.description: Russian, Prussian and Austrian forces stormed the heights around Paris, and the city capitulated that night. Coalition troops entered the next day, and Napoleon abdicated within a week.

03-30.title: Crawford Long uses ether to anaesthetise a patient
03-30.description: In Jefferson, Georgia, Dr Crawford Long removed a tumour from James Venable's neck after giving him ether. He did not publish until 1849, after William Morton's public demonstration.

03-30.title: Treaty of Paris ends the Crimean War
03-30.description: Russia accepted the neutralisation of the Black Sea, barring warships from its waters, and gave up southern Bessarabia. The powers guaranteed the integrity of the Ottoman Empire.

03-30.title: United States agrees to buy Alaska from Russia
03-30.description: William Seward signed a treaty to buy Alaska for 7.2 million dollars, about two cents an acre. Mocked as 'Seward's Folly', it proved rich in gold, fish and oil.

03-30.title: Ronald Reagan shot outside the Washington Hilton
03-30.description: John Hinckley Jr. wounded the President and three others, including press secretary James Brady. Reagan, hit in the chest, recovered quickly, and his humour in hospital boosted his popularity.

03-31.title: Bernard of Clairvaux preaches the Second Crusade at Vézelay
03-31.description: Bernard's sermon on a hillside at Vézelay moved Louis VII and crowds of nobles to take the cross after the fall of Edessa. The crusade ended in failure before Damascus in 1148.

03-31.title: Ferdinand and Isabella order the expulsion of Spain's Jews
03-31.description: The Alhambra Decree gave Jews four months to convert or leave. Tens of thousands left, and Sephardic communities took root in the Ottoman Empire, North Africa and the Low Countries.

03-31.title: René Descartes is born in Touraine
03-31.description: The philosopher and mathematician sought certainty through doubt, concluding 'I think, therefore I am'. He also devised the coordinate geometry that links algebra and geometry.

03-31.title: Gustave Eiffel inaugurates his tower in Paris
03-31.description: Eiffel climbed the stairs of his newly completed tower to raise the French flag for the Exposition Universelle. At 300 metres it was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.

03-31.title: United States takes possession of the Danish West Indies
03-31.description: Denmark transferred St Thomas, St John and St Croix, sold for 25 million dollars in gold. The US wanted to deny the islands to Germany and guard the approaches to the Panama Canal.

03-31.title: Lyndon B. Johnson says he will not seek re-election
03-31.description: In a televised address on Vietnam, Johnson announced a partial bombing halt and said he would not run again. Richard Nixon won the presidency that November.

04-01.title: Justin I makes his nephew Justinian co-emperor
04-01.description: The ageing Justin I raised Justinian to co-emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire. Within months he ruled alone, and his reign would reconquer Italy, codify Roman law and raise the Hagia Sophia.

04-01.title: Sea Beggars capture Brielle from Spain
04-01.description: Dutch rebel privateers known as the Sea Beggars seized the port of Brielle. It was the revolt's first secure foothold on land and set off a wave of risings across Holland and Zeeland against Spanish rule.

04-01.title: Sheridan breaks the Confederate line at Five Forks
04-01.description: Union troops under Philip Sheridan routed Confederates at Five Forks, Virginia, cutting Lee's last supply railway into Petersburg. Lee abandoned Petersburg and Richmond the next day.

04-01.title: Royal Air Force formed as the first independent air force
04-01.description: Britain merged the Royal Flying Corps and the Royal Naval Air Service into the Royal Air Force, the world's first air arm independent of army and navy control.

04-01.title: Munich court sentences Hitler to five years for the Beer Hall Putsch
04-01.description: Adolf Hitler received five years' detention for his failed coup of November 1923. He served barely nine months at Landsberg, where he dictated Mein Kampf.

04-01.title: Nazi regime stages a nationwide boycott of Jewish businesses
04-01.description: SA men stood outside Jewish-owned shops, offices and surgeries across Germany to turn customers away. The one-day boycott was the first nationally coordinated anti-Jewish action of the new regime.

04-01.title: Franco declares the Spanish Civil War over
04-01.description: With the last Republican forces surrendered, Francisco Franco announced the end of the war. His victory began a dictatorship that would last until his death in 1975.

04-01.title: US forces land on Okinawa
04-01.description: American troops came ashore on Okinawa in Operation Iceberg, the largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War. The 82-day battle that followed cost the lives of well over 100,000 soldiers and civilians.

04-01.title: Jobs, Wozniak and Wayne found Apple Computer
04-01.description: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne signed the partnership that created Apple Computer in California. Its first product was the hand-built Apple I; Wayne sold his share within days.

04-02.title: Charlemagne is born, by tradition on this day
04-02.description: Charlemagne, future King of the Franks and emperor in the West, was traditionally born on 2 April; the year may have been as late as 748. His empire united much of Western Europe for the first time since Rome.

04-02.title: Ponce de León sights the coast he names La Florida
04-02.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León sighted the Florida coast during the Easter season, Pascua Florida, which gave the land its name. His was the first recorded European landing in what is now the United States.

04-02.title: US Coinage Act creates the dollar and the Mint
04-02.description: Congress passed the Coinage Act, establishing the United States Mint in Philadelphia and defining the dollar in silver and gold. It laid the foundations of American currency.

04-02.title: Jefferson Davis abandons Richmond as Petersburg falls
04-02.description: As Union troops broke through the Petersburg lines, Confederate President Jefferson Davis and his government fled Richmond by train. Lee surrendered at Appomattox a week later.

04-02.title: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands
04-02.description: Argentine forces seized the British-held Falklands, which Argentina claims as the Malvinas. Britain sent a naval task force; the ten-week war ended in Argentine surrender and hastened the fall of the junta.

04-02.title: Pope John Paul II dies after a 26-year pontificate
04-02.description: John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, died in the Vatican. His papacy, one of the longest in history, was closely tied to the fall of communism in his native Poland.

04-03.title: Black Prince defeats Henry of Trastámara at Nájera
04-03.description: Edward the Black Prince routed the Castilian and French army of Henry of Trastámara at Nájera, restoring Peter of Castile. The victory proved short-lived: Henry killed Peter and took the throne two years later.

04-03.title: Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis ends the Italian Wars
04-03.description: France and Spain signed the treaty that closed more than sixty years of war over Italy, a day after a separate Anglo-French peace. Spanish dominance in Italy was confirmed for over a century.

04-03.title: Sweden signs a treaty of amity with the United States
04-03.description: Benjamin Franklin and the Swedish envoy Gustaf Philip Creutz signed a treaty of amity and commerce in Paris. Sweden became the first state not at war with Britain to recognise American independence by treaty.

04-03.title: Pony Express sets off on its first run
04-03.description: Riders left St Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California, carrying mail across some 3,000 km in about ten days. The relay lasted only 18 months before the transcontinental telegraph made it obsolete.

04-03.title: Robert Ford shoots outlaw Jesse James in Missouri
04-03.description: Jesse James was shot dead at his home in St Joseph by Robert Ford, a member of his own gang hoping for a reward. The killing turned the train and bank robber into an enduring figure of American folklore.

04-03.title: British biplanes make the first flight over Everest
04-03.description: Two Westland aircraft of the Houston expedition flew over the summit of Mount Everest, crews breathing bottled oxygen in open cockpits. They brought back the first aerial photographs of the peak.

04-03.title: Martin Luther King gives his 'Mountaintop' speech
04-03.description: In Memphis, Martin Luther King Jr. told supporters he had 'seen the Promised Land' but might not get there with them. It was his last speech; he was assassinated the following evening.

04-04.title: Alexios I Komnenos is crowned Byzantine emperor
04-04.description: Days after his troops took Constantinople from Nikephoros III, Alexios Komnenos was crowned emperor. His dynasty steadied Byzantium for a century, and his appeal to the Pope helped prompt the First Crusade.

04-04.title: US Congress fixes the flag at thirteen stripes
04-04.description: The Flag Act of 1818 set the American flag at thirteen stripes for the original colonies, with a star for every state added on the following 4 July. The rule still governs the flag today.

04-04.title: William Henry Harrison dies a month into his presidency
04-04.description: President William Henry Harrison died 31 days after taking office, the shortest presidency in US history. His death raised the first test of presidential succession, settled when John Tyler took full office.

04-04.title: Lincoln walks through the fallen Confederate capital
04-04.description: Abraham Lincoln toured Richmond, Virginia, two days after its evacuation, greeted by crowds of newly freed Black residents. He sat briefly at Jefferson Davis's desk in the Confederate White House.

04-04.title: Twelve nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty
04-04.description: Foreign ministers meeting in Washington signed the treaty that created NATO, committing members to treat an attack on one as an attack on all. The alliance anchored Western defence through the Cold War.

04-04.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated in Memphis
04-04.description: Martin Luther King Jr. was shot dead on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel, where he had come to support striking sanitation workers. Riots broke out in more than a hundred American cities.

04-04.title: Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft
04-04.description: Gates and Allen formed a partnership in Albuquerque, New Mexico, to sell a BASIC interpreter for the Altair 8800. Their company went on to dominate personal computer software.

04-05.title: Pope Paschal I crowns Lothar co-emperor in Rome
04-05.description: On Easter Sunday Pope Paschal I crowned Lothar, son of Louis the Pious, as co-emperor in St Peter's. The ceremony reinforced the idea that imperial legitimacy came through papal coronation in Rome.

04-05.title: Alexander Nevsky defeats the Teutonic Order on frozen Lake Peipus
04-05.description: Novgorod's forces under Prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order in the Battle on the Ice, halting the Order's eastward expansion into Russian lands.

04-05.title: Jacob Roggeveen reaches Easter Island
04-05.description: Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen became the first known European to reach Rapa Nui, naming it after the day of his arrival, Easter Sunday. His crew recorded the island's great stone moai.

04-05.title: George Washington issues the first presidential veto
04-05.description: Washington vetoed a bill apportioning seats in the House of Representatives, judging it unconstitutional. It was the first use of a power that later presidents would wield thousands of times.

04-05.title: Chile declares war on Peru and Bolivia
04-05.description: Chile's declaration opened the War of the Pacific, fought over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Victory gave Chile the coastal provinces and left Bolivia without access to the sea.

04-05.title: Winston Churchill resigns as Prime Minister
04-05.description: Aged 80 and in failing health, Winston Churchill stepped down as Prime Minister and was succeeded by Anthony Eden. It closed a career at the top of British politics spanning more than half a century.

04-05.title: Nirvana's Kurt Cobain dies in Seattle
04-05.description: Kurt Cobain, singer and guitarist of Nirvana, died at his Seattle home aged 27; his body was found three days later. His death closed the band that had carried grunge into the mainstream.

04-06.title: Scottish barons date the Declaration of Arbroath
04-06.description: Scotland's nobles sent Pope John XXII a letter asserting the kingdom's independence from England and their right to depose any king who submitted to it. It is one of the most celebrated statements of medieval national identity.

04-06.title: Jan van Riebeeck arrives at the Cape of Good Hope
04-06.description: Jan van Riebeeck reached Table Bay to set up a supply station for the Dutch East India Company. The outpost grew into Cape Town and began European settlement in southern Africa.

04-06.title: Rama I takes the throne and founds the Chakri dynasty
04-06.description: The general Chao Phraya Chakri became king of Siam as Rama I and soon moved the capital across the river to Bangkok. His Chakri dynasty still reigns in Thailand today.

04-06.title: First modern Olympic Games open in Athens
04-06.description: King George I of Greece opened the first modern Olympics at the Panathenaic Stadium. Revived by Pierre de Coubertin, the Games drew some 240 athletes from 14 nations.

04-06.title: Peary and Henson claim to reach the North Pole
04-06.description: Robert Peary, Matthew Henson and four Inuit companions reported reaching the North Pole. Doubts over Peary's navigation mean historians still debate how close they actually came.

04-06.title: United States declares war on Germany
04-06.description: Congress approved President Wilson's request for war, provoked by unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram. American troops and resources helped tip the balance on the Western Front.

04-06.title: Gandhi breaks the salt law at Dandi
04-06.description: At the end of his 24-day march to the sea, Mohandas Gandhi picked up a lump of natural salt at Dandi, defying the British monopoly. The gesture launched a mass campaign of civil disobedience across India.

04-07.title: Justinian promulgates the first Code of Roman law
04-07.description: Emperor Justinian issued the Codex Justinianus, gathering imperial constitutions into a single authoritative collection. Revised in 534, it became the core of the Corpus Juris Civilis that shaped European law.

04-07.title: Charles IV founds the university in Prague
04-07.description: Charles IV, King of Bohemia, issued the charter founding a university in Prague, the first in Central Europe. Now Charles University, it later became a centre of the Hussite reform movement.

04-07.title: Highwayman Dick Turpin is hanged at York
04-07.description: Dick Turpin, convicted of horse theft, was hanged on the Knavesmire at York. The violent robber was later romanticised in fiction as a dashing gentleman of the road.

04-07.title: Congress creates the Mississippi Territory
04-07.description: The US Congress organised the Mississippi Territory on land ceded by Spain in 1795. It was later enlarged and divided into the states of Mississippi and Alabama.

04-07.title: John Walker records the first sale of friction matches
04-07.description: Stockton-on-Tees chemist John Walker sold his newly invented 'friction lights', matches struck against sandpaper. He never patented them, and others soon copied the idea.

04-07.title: Italy invades Albania
04-07.description: Mussolini's forces landed at Durrës and other ports, and within days King Zog had fled. Albania was joined to the Italian crown, and the invasion later served as a base for Italy's attack on Greece.

04-07.title: Genocide against the Tutsi begins in Rwanda
04-07.description: Hours after President Habyarimana's aircraft was shot down, extremists began killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu. In about 100 days an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people were murdered.

04-08.title: Emperor Caracalla is murdered near Carrhae
04-08.description: Caracalla was stabbed to death by a soldier while travelling to a temple near Carrhae in Mesopotamia. His praetorian prefect Macrinus, who had arranged the killing, became the first emperor not of senatorial rank.

04-08.title: New Norman cathedral at Winchester is consecrated
04-08.description: Bishop Walkelin's Romanesque cathedral at Winchester was consecrated in the presence of bishops and abbots. Later extended, it is now the longest medieval cathedral in Europe.

04-08.title: Farmer unearths the Venus de Milo on Milos
04-08.description: A peasant named Yorgos Kentrotas found the marble statue in the ruins of ancient Milos. Bought by the French and taken to the Louvre, the armless Aphrodite became one of the most famous sculptures in the world.

04-08.title: Britain and France sign the Entente Cordiale
04-08.description: A set of agreements settled colonial disputes, with Britain recognised in Egypt and France in Morocco. The understanding ended centuries of rivalry and drew the two powers together before 1914.

04-08.title: Seventeenth Amendment introduces direct election of US senators
04-08.description: Connecticut's ratification completed the Seventeenth Amendment, transferring the choice of senators from state legislatures to voters. Secretary of State Bryan certified it at the end of May.

04-08.title: Jomo Kenyatta is convicted at the Kapenguria trial
04-08.description: A colonial court in Kenya sentenced Jomo Kenyatta and five others to seven years' hard labour for allegedly managing Mau Mau. The widely criticised verdict made him a national symbol; he became Kenya's first president.

04-08.title: Pablo Picasso dies at Mougins aged 91
04-08.description: Pablo Picasso died at his home in the south of France. Co-founder of Cubism and creator of Guernica, he had reshaped modern art over a career lasting more than seventy years.

04-09.title: Danube legions proclaim Septimius Severus emperor
04-09.description: After the murder of Pertinax, the legions at Carnuntum hailed their governor Septimius Severus as emperor. He marched on Rome, defeated his rivals and founded the Severan dynasty.

04-09.title: Mongols defeat a Polish and German army at Legnica
04-09.description: A Mongol force under Baidar and Kadan crushed the army of Duke Henry II the Pious, who was killed. Two days later the main Mongol army destroyed the Hungarians at Mohi.

04-09.title: La Salle claims the Mississippi basin for France
04-09.description: Reaching the mouth of the Mississippi, René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle claimed its whole drainage basin for Louis XIV and named it Louisiana. France sold the territory to the United States in 1803.

04-09.title: Lee surrenders to Grant at Appomattox Court House
04-09.description: Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia to Ulysses S. Grant. Other Confederate forces followed in the weeks after, bringing the American Civil War to an end.

04-09.title: Germany invades Denmark and Norway
04-09.description: German forces struck both neutral states in Operation Weserübung. Denmark yielded within hours, while Norway, aided by Britain and France, fought on for two months, giving Germany vital North Sea and Atlantic bases.

04-09.title: Dietrich Bonhoeffer is executed at Flossenbürg
04-09.description: Lutheran pastor and theologian Dietrich Bonhoeffer was hanged on Hitler's orders for his links to the resistance. He died a month before Germany's surrender.

04-09.title: Baghdad falls and Saddam's statue is pulled down
04-09.description: As US troops entered central Baghdad, a statue of Saddam Hussein in Firdos Square was toppled with the help of a Marine vehicle. The images marked the regime's collapse, though years of insurgency followed.

04-10.title: Nestorius becomes Archbishop of Constantinople
04-10.description: Nestorius was consecrated archbishop of the eastern capital. His teaching on the two natures of Christ was condemned at Ephesus in 431, and the Church of the East that kept his name spread as far as China.

04-10.title: James I charters the Virginia Company
04-10.description: King James I granted a charter to the Virginia Company's London and Plymouth branches to settle the North American coast. The London company founded Jamestown the following year.

04-10.title: Statute of Anne, the first copyright law, takes effect
04-10.description: Britain's Statute of Anne came into force, vesting copyright in authors rather than printers for a term of 14 years, renewable once. It set the principle on which modern copyright law is built.

04-10.title: Mount Tambora reaches its cataclysmic climax
04-10.description: The Indonesian volcano produced the largest eruption in recorded history, killing tens of thousands on Sumbawa and Lombok. Its ash cooled the globe, making 1816 the 'Year Without a Summer'.

04-10.title: Titanic leaves Southampton on her maiden voyage
04-10.description: RMS Titanic, the largest ship afloat, sailed from Southampton for New York via Cherbourg and Queenstown. Five days later she struck an iceberg and sank with the loss of more than 1,500 lives.

04-10.title: Good Friday Agreement is signed in Belfast
04-10.description: The British and Irish governments and most Northern Ireland parties agreed a settlement creating a power-sharing assembly and cross-border bodies. It largely brought three decades of the Troubles to a close.

04-11.title: Mongols destroy the Hungarian army at Mohi
04-11.description: Mongol forces under Batu and Subutai encircled and annihilated King Béla IV's army by the Sajó river. Hungary was laid open to a year of devastating occupation.

04-11.title: William III and Mary II are crowned joint monarchs
04-11.description: William and Mary were crowned together in Westminster Abbey after accepting the Declaration of Rights. The settlement confirmed the Glorious Revolution and the limits Parliament had placed on the Crown.

04-11.title: Treaty of Fontainebleau sends Napoleon to Elba
04-11.description: The allied powers signed the treaty confirming Napoleon's abdication and granting him the island of Elba as a sovereign principality. He escaped less than a year later for the Hundred Days.

04-11.title: US troops reach Buchenwald concentration camp
04-11.description: American soldiers arrived at Buchenwald near Weimar, where prisoners had already taken control of the camp. Some 56,000 people had died there; Eisenhower later had local Germans brought to see it.

04-11.title: Adolf Eichmann's trial opens in Jerusalem
04-11.description: Adolf Eichmann, a principal organiser of the deportation of Europe's Jews, went on trial in Jerusalem. Survivor testimony broadcast worldwide shaped public understanding of the Holocaust; he was hanged in 1962.

04-11.title: Apollo 13 lifts off for the Moon
04-11.description: Apollo 13 launched from Kennedy Space Center. Two days out an oxygen tank exploded, the lunar landing was abandoned, and the crew used the lunar module as a lifeboat to return safely.

04-12.title: Anthemius is proclaimed Western Roman emperor
04-12.description: Backed by the eastern emperor Leo I, Anthemius was raised to the western throne near Rome. A joint expedition against the Vandals failed, and he was killed in 472.

04-12.title: Fourth Crusade storms Constantinople
04-12.description: Crusaders and Venetians broke into Constantinople and began three days of pillage. They set up a Latin Empire, and Byzantium never recovered its former strength.

04-12.title: First Union Flag is adopted for English and Scottish ships
04-12.description: A royal proclamation of James I ordered ships of England and Scotland to fly a new flag combining the crosses of St George and St Andrew. St Patrick's saltire was added in 1801.

04-12.title: Confederate guns open fire on Fort Sumter
04-12.description: Confederate batteries bombarded the federal fort in Charleston harbour, forcing its surrender the next day. The attack began the American Civil War.

04-12.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt dies at Warm Springs
04-12.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt died of a cerebral haemorrhage in Georgia early in his fourth term. Harry Truman became president and presided over the end of the war in Europe and the Pacific.

04-12.title: Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
04-12.description: Results of a nationwide trial involving more than a million children showed Jonas Salk's vaccine worked. Mass vaccination soon cut polio cases dramatically.

04-12.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
04-12.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once aboard Vostok 1 in a flight of 108 minutes. The achievement gave the Soviet Union a major lead in the space race.

04-13.title: Pope Paschal II crowns Henry V emperor under duress
04-13.description: Having held the Pope captive for two months, Henry V forced him to concede the right of investiture and crown him in Rome. The concession was soon revoked, and the dispute lasted until 1122.

04-13.title: Henry IV signs the Edict of Nantes
04-13.description: Henry IV granted French Protestants freedom of worship in specified places, civil rights and fortified towns. The edict ended the Wars of Religion until Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.

04-13.title: Handel's Messiah has its premiere in Dublin
04-13.description: Handel's oratorio was first performed at the New Music Hall in Fishamble Street, Dublin, in aid of charity. It became one of the most performed choral works in the Western tradition.

04-13.title: Catholic Relief Act receives royal assent
04-13.description: The Roman Catholic Relief Act allowed Catholics to sit in Parliament and hold most public offices. It was forced through by Wellington and Peel after Daniel O'Connell's election in County Clare.

04-13.title: Troops fire on a crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar
04-13.description: Soldiers under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired without warning into an unarmed crowd in an enclosed garden. At least 379 were killed by official count; the massacre hardened Indian opposition to British rule.

04-13.title: Germany announces discovery of the Katyń graves
04-13.description: Berlin radio reported mass graves of Polish officers in the Katyń Forest near Smolensk. They had been shot by the Soviet NKVD in 1940, a crime Moscow denied until 1990.

04-14.title: Vitellius's army defeats Otho at Bedriacum
04-14.description: Troops loyal to Vitellius beat Emperor Otho's forces near Cremona in northern Italy. Otho took his own life two days later, but Vitellius himself fell before the year was out.

04-14.title: Warwick the Kingmaker is killed at the Battle of Barnet
04-14.description: Edward IV defeated the Lancastrian army in fog at Barnet, and Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, was killed in the rout. Victory at Tewkesbury weeks later secured Edward's throne.

04-14.title: Noah Webster registers his American Dictionary
04-14.description: Noah Webster's American Dictionary of the English Language, with some 70,000 entries, was published. It promoted American spellings such as 'color' and 'center'.

04-14.title: John Wilkes Booth shoots Lincoln at Ford's Theatre
04-14.description: Five days after Lee's surrender, the actor John Wilkes Booth shot President Lincoln during a play in Washington. Lincoln died the next morning, the first US president to be assassinated.

04-14.title: Titanic strikes an iceberg in the North Atlantic
04-14.description: At 11.40 pm the liner struck an iceberg south of Newfoundland, opening several forward compartments to the sea. She sank less than three hours later, early on 15 April.

04-14.title: Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed
04-14.description: After republicans swept the cities in municipal elections, the Republic was declared and Alfonso XIII left Spain. The new democracy was overthrown by the civil war that began in 1936.

04-15.title: French victory at Formigny seals the loss of English Normandy
04-15.description: French cannon and cavalry destroyed an English relief army at Formigny. Normandy fell within months; the Hundred Years' War itself ended after Castillon in 1453.

04-15.title: Samuel Johnson publishes his Dictionary
04-15.description: Samuel Johnson's Dictionary of the English Language appeared after nine years' work, defining some 42,000 words with literary quotations. It remained the leading English dictionary for over a century.

04-15.title: First American school for the deaf opens in Hartford
04-15.description: Thomas Hopkins Gallaudet and the French deaf teacher Laurent Clerc opened what is now the American School for the Deaf in Connecticut. Its signing community helped give rise to American Sign Language.

04-15.title: Abraham Lincoln dies of his wound
04-15.description: Lincoln died at 7.22 am in a boarding house opposite Ford's Theatre. Andrew Johnson was sworn in as president hours later, inheriting the task of Reconstruction.

04-15.title: Titanic sinks with the loss of more than 1,500 lives
04-15.description: The liner went down at 2.20 am with lifeboat places for barely half of the 2,224 aboard. The disaster led to the first International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea in 1914.

04-15.title: Fatal crush at Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield
04-15.description: A crush on the terraces at an FA Cup semi-final killed 97 Liverpool supporters. Fresh inquests in 2016 found they were unlawfully killed and that fans bore no blame.

04-16.title: Thutmose III defeats a Canaanite coalition at Megiddo
04-16.description: Pharaoh Thutmose III routed a coalition led by the king of Kadesh at Megiddo, on a date traditionally reckoned to 16 April. His annals give the first detailed account of a battle in recorded history.

04-16.title: Jacobite army is crushed at Culloden
04-16.description: Government troops under the Duke of Cumberland routed Charles Edward Stuart's army near Inverness in under an hour. It was the last pitched battle on British soil and was followed by harsh repression in the Highlands.

04-16.title: Powers sign the Paris Declaration on maritime law
04-16.description: Meeting at the Congress of Paris, the great powers agreed to abolish privateering and protect neutral goods at sea. It was the first multilateral treaty codifying the laws of naval warfare.

04-16.title: Lenin arrives at Petrograd's Finland Station
04-16.description: Returning from Swiss exile with German help, Vladimir Lenin was greeted by crowds in Petrograd. His call to oppose the Provisional Government set the Bolsheviks on the road to the October Revolution.

04-16.title: Albert Hofmann experiences the effects of LSD by accident
04-16.description: Working at Sandoz in Basel, chemist Albert Hofmann absorbed a trace of LSD and felt its effects. Three days later, on 19 April, he took a deliberate dose to test it.

04-16.title: Gunman kills 32 people at Virginia Tech
04-16.description: A student shot dead 32 people on the campus in Blacksburg, Virginia, before killing himself. It was then the deadliest shooting by a lone gunman in US history and led to reforms of background checks.

04-17.title: Columbus and the Spanish Crown agree the Capitulations of Santa Fe
04-17.description: Ferdinand and Isabella agreed terms with Christopher Columbus for a westward voyage, promising him the title of admiral and a tenth of the wealth from any lands he found.

04-17.title: Luther is summoned to recant before the Diet of Worms
04-17.description: Before Emperor Charles V, Martin Luther acknowledged his books but asked for time to answer whether he would retract them. The next day he refused, defying both emperor and Pope.

04-17.title: Treaty of Shimonoseki ends the First Sino-Japanese War
04-17.description: China recognised Korean independence, ceded Taiwan and the Pescadores to Japan and paid a large indemnity. Defeat exposed the weakness of the Qing and announced Japan as a regional power.

04-17.title: Last French troops leave Syria
04-17.description: The withdrawal of the final French forces completed Syria's independence after a quarter-century of mandate rule. The day is still marked in Syria as Evacuation Day.

04-17.title: Cuban exiles land at the Bay of Pigs
04-17.description: A CIA-trained brigade of some 1,400 Cuban exiles landed in southern Cuba to overthrow Fidel Castro. They were defeated within three days, a grave embarrassment for the new Kennedy administration.

04-17.title: Khmer Rouge take Phnom Penh
04-17.description: Khmer Rouge forces entered the Cambodian capital and immediately drove its population into the countryside. Their rule until 1979 led to the deaths of an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people.

04-18.title: King Æthelred I of Northumbria is murdered
04-18.description: Æthelred I was killed at Corbridge by his own nobles. His death, typical of Northumbria's violent politics, came three years after Viking raiders had sacked the monastery at Lindisfarne.

04-18.title: Julius II lays the foundation stone of the new St Peter's
04-18.description: Pope Julius II laid the first stone of Bramante's new basilica in Rome. Building took 120 years and drew on Michelangelo, Maderno and Bernini.

04-18.title: Paul Revere rides to warn of British troops
04-18.description: Paul Revere and William Dawes rode from Boston to warn that British regulars were marching to seize colonial arms. The first shots of the Revolutionary War were fired at dawn the next day.

04-18.title: Earthquake and fire devastate San Francisco
04-18.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck before dawn, and fires burned for three days. Some 3,000 people died and more than half the city's population was left homeless.

04-18.title: Yankee Stadium opens with a Babe Ruth home run
04-18.description: Babe Ruth hit a three-run home run in the first game at the new Bronx ballpark, quickly nicknamed 'The House That Ruth Built'. It was home to the Yankees until 2008.

04-18.title: Albert Einstein dies in Princeton
04-18.description: Albert Einstein died aged 76. His theories of special and general relativity and his work on light quanta transformed physics in the twentieth century.

04-19.title: Lutheran princes protest at the Diet of Speyer
04-19.description: Six princes and fourteen imperial cities formally protested against the Diet's move to curb the Reformation. Their Protestation gave the movement the name 'Protestant'.

04-19.title: Shots at Lexington and Concord begin the American Revolution
04-19.description: Militiamen clashed with British regulars at Lexington and Concord in Massachusetts, and harried them all the way back to Boston. The skirmishes began the War of Independence.

04-19.title: First Boston Marathon is run
04-19.description: Fifteen runners set out on the first Boston race, inspired by the marathon at the 1896 Athens Olympics. It is now the world's oldest annual marathon.

04-19.title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising begins
04-19.description: Jewish fighters resisted German troops sent to deport the ghetto's remaining inhabitants to Treblinka. They held out for nearly a month in the largest Jewish revolt of the war.

04-19.title: Truck bomb kills 168 in Oklahoma City
04-19.description: Timothy McVeigh detonated a truck bomb outside the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building, killing 168 people, including 19 children. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in US history.

04-20.title: Jacques Cartier sails from Saint-Malo for North America
04-20.description: Jacques Cartier left Brittany on the first of three voyages that explored the Gulf of St Lawrence. His expeditions laid the basis for France's later claim to Canada.

04-20.title: Oliver Cromwell dissolves the Rump Parliament
04-20.description: Cromwell entered the Commons with musketeers and expelled the remaining members. The act paved the way for his rule as Lord Protector later that year.

04-20.title: Robert Blake destroys a Spanish fleet at Santa Cruz de Tenerife
04-20.description: Admiral Robert Blake sailed into the defended harbour and burned the Spanish ships sheltering there without losing a vessel of his own. It was one of the boldest naval actions of the age.

04-20.title: France declares war on Austria
04-20.description: The Legislative Assembly voted for war against the Habsburg monarch, opening the French Revolutionary Wars. Conflict between France and the European powers would last, almost unbroken, until 1815.

04-20.title: Two students kill 13 people at Columbine High School
04-20.description: Two students at the Colorado school shot dead twelve classmates and a teacher before killing themselves. The attack transformed school security and police response tactics across the United States.

04-21.title: Romulus founds Rome, according to Roman tradition
04-21.description: Roman writers placed the city's foundation by Romulus on the Palatine on 21 April 753 BCE, a date fixed by the scholar Varro. Romans celebrated it each year as the Parilia.

04-21.title: Three days of massacre in Lisbon come to an end
04-21.description: Rioting stirred up by Dominican friars killed between 1,000 and 4,000 New Christians, Jews forcibly converted in 1497. King Manuel I punished the city and had two of the friars executed.

04-21.title: Rama I founds Bangkok as Siam's new capital
04-21.description: The city pillar of Bangkok was erected on the east bank of the Chao Phraya, marking the official founding of the new royal capital. It replaced Thonburi across the river.

04-21.title: Texans defeat Santa Anna at San Jacinto
04-21.description: Sam Houston's army surprised the Mexican camp and won in about eighteen minutes. Santa Anna was captured the next day and forced to order his troops out of Texas, securing its independence.

04-21.title: The Red Baron is shot down and killed near Amiens
04-21.description: Manfred von Richthofen, credited with 80 victories, was killed while pursuing an enemy aircraft over the Somme. Whether a Canadian pilot or Australian ground gunners fired the fatal shot is still debated.

04-21.title: Brasília is inaugurated as Brazil's capital
04-21.description: Built in under four years to plans by Lúcio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer, Brasília replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital. It was meant to draw development into Brazil's interior.

04-22.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral reaches the coast of Brazil
04-22.description: A Portuguese fleet bound for India sighted land in South America and claimed it for Portugal. The landfall began Portuguese colonisation of what became Brazil, long inhabited by Indigenous peoples.

04-22.title: Hernán Cortés lands at Veracruz
04-22.description: Cortés landed on the Gulf coast of Mexico and soon founded Villa Rica de la Vera Cruz. The settlement served as his base for the conquest of the Aztec Empire.

04-22.title: Coinage Act puts 'In God We Trust' on US coins
04-22.description: Congress authorised a new two-cent coin, the first to bear the motto 'In God We Trust'. It spread to other coins and became the official US national motto in 1956.

04-22.title: Germany releases chlorine gas at Ypres
04-22.description: German troops released chlorine from cylinders against French and Algerian positions near Ypres. It was the first large-scale use of lethal gas on the Western Front and opened a chemical arms race.

04-22.title: Millions mark the first Earth Day
04-22.description: Some 20 million Americans joined rallies and teach-ins for the first Earth Day. Its momentum helped create the Environmental Protection Agency later that year.

04-23.title: Brian Boru wins at Clontarf but is killed
04-23.description: The Irish high king Brian Boru defeated the forces of Leinster and their Norse allies from Dublin and beyond. He was slain in his tent during the battle, and his hard-won supremacy collapsed.

04-23.title: Order of the Garter is founded, by tradition on St George's Day
04-23.description: Edward III created the Order of the Garter, England's senior order of chivalry, around this time, traditionally marked on St George's Day. Its 24 knights still meet at Windsor.

04-23.title: William Shakespeare is born, by tradition, in Stratford
04-23.description: Shakespeare's birth is traditionally dated to 23 April; only his baptism on 26 April is recorded. He went on to write some 38 plays and 154 sonnets.

04-23.title: William Shakespeare dies in Stratford-upon-Avon
04-23.description: Shakespeare died at his home of New Place, aged 52. Seven years later his fellow actors gathered 36 of his plays in the First Folio, preserving many that might otherwise have been lost.

04-23.title: Future president James Buchanan is born
04-23.description: James Buchanan was born in a log cabin in Pennsylvania. The 15th US president, and the only one never to marry, failed to halt the secession of Southern states in 1860 and 1861.

04-23.title: Coca-Cola launches New Coke
04-23.description: Coca-Cola replaced its 99-year-old formula with a sweeter recipe. Public protest was so strong that the original returned as Coca-Cola Classic 79 days later.

04-24.title: Troy falls, according to ancient Greek reckoning
04-24.description: Greek chronographers, notably Eratosthenes, dated the fall of Troy to 1184 BCE, and later writers placed it in late April. The legend, told in Homer and Virgil, shaped European literature for millennia.

04-24.title: Congress establishes the Library of Congress
04-24.description: President John Adams signed the act moving the government to Washington and setting aside $5,000 for books for Congress. The collection became one of the largest libraries in the world.

04-24.title: Russia declares war on the Ottoman Empire
04-24.description: Russia went to war in support of the Balkan Christians. The peace that followed made Romania, Serbia and Montenegro fully independent and created an autonomous Bulgaria.

04-24.title: Ottoman authorities arrest Armenian leaders in Constantinople
04-24.description: Hundreds of Armenian intellectuals and community leaders were rounded up and deported, most later killed. The date marks the start of the Armenian genocide, in which around a million people died.

04-24.title: Irish rebels launch the Easter Rising in Dublin
04-24.description: Irish Volunteers and the Citizen Army seized the General Post Office and proclaimed an Irish Republic. The Rising was crushed within a week, but the executions that followed turned opinion towards independence.

04-24.title: Space shuttle Discovery launches the Hubble Space Telescope
04-24.description: Hubble was carried into orbit by Discovery and deployed the next day. A flaw in its mirror was corrected in 1993, after which it transformed astronomy.

04-25.title: Saint-Dié scholars publish the book that names America
04-25.description: The Cosmographiae Introductio, issued with Martin Waldseemüller's world map, proposed naming the New World 'America' after Amerigo Vespucci. The only surviving copy of the map is in the Library of Congress.

04-25.title: Last Ming emperor takes his own life as Beijing falls
04-25.description: As Li Zicheng's rebels entered Beijing, the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on Coal Hill behind the Forbidden City. Within weeks the Manchus seized the capital and founded Qing rule.

04-25.title: Work begins on the Suez Canal
04-25.description: Ferdinand de Lesseps struck the first blow at the site of Port Said. The canal opened in 1869, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and shortening the sea route from Europe to Asia.

04-25.title: Allied troops land at Gallipoli
04-25.description: British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula. The campaign failed after eight months and around 100,000 deaths on both sides; 25 April is now Anzac Day.

04-25.title: Watson and Crick publish the double helix
04-25.description: Nature published James Watson and Francis Crick's paper on the structure of DNA, alongside papers by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin's group. It explained how genetic information is copied.

04-25.title: Carnation Revolution topples Portugal's dictatorship
04-25.description: A largely bloodless coup by army officers ended the Estado Novo regime. Democracy followed, and Portugal's African colonies gained independence within two years.

04-26.title: Petrarch climbs Mont Ventoux for the view
04-26.description: The poet Petrarch climbed Mont Ventoux in Provence, by his own account simply to see the view from the summit. His letter describing it is often cited as an early sign of a new attitude to nature.

04-26.title: William Shakespeare is baptised in Stratford-upon-Avon
04-26.description: The parish register of Holy Trinity Church records the baptism of 'Gulielmus filius Johannes Shakspere'. It is the earliest documentary record of the playwright.

04-26.title: John Wilkes Booth is cornered and killed in Virginia
04-26.description: Union troops trapped Lincoln's assassin in a tobacco barn and set it alight; Booth was shot by Sergeant Boston Corbett and died within hours. It ended a twelve-day manhunt.

04-26.title: German and Italian aircraft bomb Guernica
04-26.description: The Condor Legion, with Italian support, bombed the Basque town on market day, killing hundreds of civilians. The attack inspired Picasso's painting Guernica.

04-26.title: Reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear plant
04-26.description: A safety test went wrong at reactor No. 4 in Soviet Ukraine, causing an explosion and fire that spread radioactive fallout across Europe. Over 100,000 people were evacuated.

04-27.title: Ferdinand Magellan is killed on Mactan
04-27.description: Magellan died fighting the forces of the chief Lapulapu in the Philippines. Under Juan Sebastián Elcano, one ship of his fleet returned to Spain in 1522, completing the first circumnavigation.

04-27.title: Montrose's royalists are routed at Carbisdale
04-27.description: The Marquess of Montrose, landing in Scotland for the exiled Charles II, was defeated by Covenanter forces. He was captured and hanged in Edinburgh a month later.

04-27.title: Samuel Morse is born in Massachusetts
04-27.description: Samuel Morse, painter turned inventor, was born in Charlestown. He developed an electric telegraph and, with Alfred Vail, the code that bears his name.

04-27.title: Beethoven dates the manuscript of Für Elise
04-27.description: Beethoven's autograph of the Bagatelle in A minor carried the date 27 April 1810. Unpublished in his lifetime, it appeared in 1867 and became one of the best-known piano pieces.

04-27.title: Partisans capture Mussolini at Dongo
04-27.description: Disguised in a German greatcoat in a convoy heading north, Benito Mussolini was recognised and seized by Italian partisans near Lake Como. He was shot the next day.

04-27.title: South Africa holds its first all-race elections
04-27.description: Millions of Black South Africans voted for the first time. The ANC won decisively and Nelson Mandela became president, ending the apartheid order. The date is now Freedom Day.

04-28.title: Constantius II makes his only visit to Rome
04-28.description: Emperor Constantius II entered Rome in triumph for the first time. The historian Ammianus Marcellinus described his astonishment at the Forum of Trajan and other monuments.

04-28.title: Fletcher Christian leads the mutiny on the Bounty
04-28.description: Mutineers seized HMS Bounty and set Captain William Bligh adrift with 18 men in an open launch. Bligh navigated some 6,700 km to Timor with the loss of only one man.

04-28.title: Rush-Bagot Agreement is proclaimed
04-28.description: President Monroe proclaimed the Anglo-American agreement limiting warships on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain. It helped demilitarise the border between the United States and British North America.

04-28.title: Partisans shoot Mussolini near Lake Como
04-28.description: Benito Mussolini and Clara Petacci were shot by partisans at Giulino di Mezzegra. The next day their bodies were hung upside down in Milan's Piazzale Loreto.

04-28.title: Japan regains its sovereignty as the Allied occupation ends
04-28.description: The Treaty of San Francisco came into force, ending the Allied occupation of Japan that had begun in 1945. A US-Japan security treaty took effect the same day.

04-28.title: Charles de Gaulle resigns as President of France
04-28.description: After voters rejected his referendum on regional and Senate reform, de Gaulle stepped down at noon. He had led the Fifth Republic since its foundation in 1958.

04-29.title: Joan of Arc enters besieged Orléans
04-29.description: Joan of Arc entered Orléans with supplies and reinforcements. Within ten days the English abandoned the siege, a turning point in the Hundred Years' War.

04-29.title: James Cook lands at Botany Bay
04-29.description: The crew of HMS Endeavour made the first recorded European landing on Australia's east coast, meeting resistance from Gweagal men. The bay was named for the plants collected by Joseph Banks.

04-29.title: British garrison surrenders to the Ottomans at Kut
04-29.description: After a siege of nearly five months, General Charles Townshend surrendered some 13,000 British and Indian troops at Kut al-Amara in Mesopotamia. Thousands died in captivity.

04-29.title: US troops liberate Dachau
04-29.description: American soldiers entered Dachau, the first concentration camp, opened in 1933. They found more than 30,000 prisoners and thousands of bodies.

04-29.title: Cyclone strikes the coast of Bangladesh
04-29.description: A severe tropical cyclone drove a storm surge of up to six metres onto the Chittagong coast, killing some 138,000 people. It led to wider investment in cyclone shelters and warnings.

04-29.title: Rioting erupts in Los Angeles after the Rodney King verdict
04-29.description: Riots began after four police officers were acquitted of beating Rodney King. Over six days more than 60 people died and damage reached about $1 billion.

04-30.title: Galerius issues an edict ending the persecution of Christians
04-30.description: Gravely ill, Emperor Galerius granted Christians the right to worship, ending the Great Persecution in his territories. He died days later; Constantine's Edict of Milan followed in 313.

04-30.title: Ferdinand and Isabella confirm Columbus's titles
04-30.description: At Granada the monarchs granted Columbus the titles of admiral, viceroy and governor of any lands he found, and ordered Palos to provide ships. He sailed in August.

04-30.title: George Washington is inaugurated as first US president
04-30.description: Washington took the oath of office on the balcony of Federal Hall in New York. His conduct in office set precedents, such as the two-term tradition, that shaped the presidency.

04-30.title: Louisiana Purchase treaty doubles the size of the United States
04-30.description: American envoys in Paris agreed to buy France's Louisiana territory for $15 million. The deal, dated this day, gave the young republic the vast basin west of the Mississippi.

04-30.title: Adolf Hitler takes his own life in Berlin
04-30.description: With Soviet troops closing in, Hitler shot himself in his bunker beneath the Reich Chancellery. Germany surrendered unconditionally a week later.

04-30.title: Saigon falls to North Vietnamese forces
04-30.description: Tanks broke through the gates of the presidential palace hours after the last Americans were lifted out by helicopter. The war ended and Vietnam was reunified under communist rule in 1976.

05-01.title: Diocletian and Maximian abdicate together
05-01.description: In ceremonies at Nicomedia and Milan, the two senior emperors stepped down in favour of Galerius and Constantius. The planned handover soon broke down into civil war among their successors.

05-01.title: England ratifies the Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton
05-01.description: Meeting at Northampton, the English Parliament ratified the treaty recognising Robert the Bruce as king of an independent Scotland. It ended the First War of Scottish Independence, though peace did not last.

05-01.title: Acts of Union create the Kingdom of Great Britain
05-01.description: The union of England and Scotland took effect, creating a single kingdom and a single Parliament at Westminster. Scotland kept its own legal system and established church.

05-01.title: Adam Weishaupt founds the Bavarian Illuminati
05-01.description: Law professor Adam Weishaupt founded a secret society to spread Enlightenment ideas in Catholic Bavaria. It was banned in the 1780s but has lived on in conspiracy theories ever since.

05-01.title: Britain issues the Penny Black, the first adhesive stamp
05-01.description: The Penny Black went on sale, valid for postage from 6 May. Prepaid at a flat rate under Rowland Hill's reforms, it made letters affordable for ordinary people.

05-01.title: American workers strike for an eight-hour day
05-01.description: Hundreds of thousands of workers across the United States walked out to demand an eight-hour day. Events in Chicago that week, culminating at Haymarket, led to 1 May becoming International Workers' Day.

05-01.title: Empire State Building opens in New York
05-01.description: President Hoover pressed a button in Washington to switch on the lights of the newly finished skyscraper. At 381 metres it remained the world's tallest building for nearly forty years.

05-01.title: Soviet missile downs a US U-2 spy plane
05-01.description: A U-2 piloted by Francis Gary Powers was shot down near Sverdlovsk. Washington's initial cover story collapsed when Moscow produced the pilot, wrecking the Paris summit two weeks later.

05-01.title: George W. Bush declares major combat in Iraq over
05-01.description: Speaking aboard USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a 'Mission Accomplished' banner, the president announced the end of major combat operations. The insurgency that followed made the moment notorious.

05-01.title: US special forces kill Osama bin Laden in Pakistan
05-01.description: Navy SEALs raided a compound in Abbottabad and killed the al-Qaeda leader behind the 11 September attacks. President Obama announced it that night, US time; in Pakistan it was early on 2 May.

05-02.title: Leonardo da Vinci dies at Amboise
05-02.description: Leonardo died at Clos Lucé, the manor near Amboise given to him by Francis I. Painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, he also left thousands of pages of notes on anatomy, engineering and nature.

05-02.title: Anne Boleyn is arrested and taken to the Tower
05-02.description: Queen Anne Boleyn was arrested at Greenwich on charges of adultery, incest and treason. She was beheaded at the Tower seventeen days later, and Henry VIII married Jane Seymour within days.

05-02.title: Charles II charters the Hudson's Bay Company
05-02.description: The company received a monopoly of trade across the lands draining into Hudson Bay, a vast territory named Rupert's Land. It remains one of the oldest commercial enterprises in the world.

05-02.title: Madrid rises against French occupation
05-02.description: Crowds in Madrid attacked French troops in the Dos de Mayo uprising, which was suppressed with mass executions painted by Goya. Revolt spread across Spain and began the Peninsular War.

05-02.title: Stonewall Jackson is shot by his own men at Chancellorsville
05-02.description: Returning from a night reconnaissance, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson was hit by fire from Confederate pickets. He died of pneumonia eight days later, a grave loss to Lee.

05-02.title: Berlin garrison surrenders to the Red Army
05-02.description: General Helmuth Weidling surrendered the German forces in Berlin to the Soviets two days after Hitler's suicide. Germany's unconditional surrender followed within a week.

05-02.title: J. Edgar Hoover dies after 48 years leading the FBI
05-02.description: J. Edgar Hoover died in Washington, having led the Bureau and its predecessor since 1924. He built a modern federal police force but also used it to spy on activists and politicians.

05-03.title: Niccolò Machiavelli is born in Florence
05-03.description: Machiavelli, diplomat of the Florentine republic and author of The Prince, was born. His unsentimental analysis of power made him a founder of modern political thought.

05-03.title: Columbus sights Jamaica on his second voyage
05-03.description: Christopher Columbus reached Jamaica, which the Taíno called Xaymaca, and named it Santiago. The island remained under Spanish rule until England captured it in 1655.

05-03.title: Treaty of Oliva makes peace between Sweden and Poland
05-03.description: Signed near Danzig, the treaty ended the war between Sweden and Poland-Lithuania. Poland's king renounced his claim to the Swedish throne and recognised Swedish rule in Livonia.

05-03.title: Poland-Lithuania adopts the Constitution of 3 May
05-03.description: The Sejm passed Europe's first modern codified national constitution, strengthening the monarchy and ending the liberum veto. Russia and Prussia responded with war and the second partition.

05-03.title: Napoleon arrives off Elba to begin his exile
05-03.description: HMS Undaunted brought the deposed emperor to Portoferraio, where he landed the next morning to rule his tiny island principality. He escaped in February 1815.

05-03.title: Northern Ireland comes into being
05-03.description: The Government of Ireland Act took effect, partitioning Ireland and creating Northern Ireland from six north-eastern counties with its own parliament. Partition remains in place today.

05-03.title: Margaret Mitchell wins the Pulitzer for Gone with the Wind
05-03.description: Margaret Mitchell's novel of the Civil War and Reconstruction won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. A huge bestseller, it was filmed in 1939, though its portrayal of slavery is now widely criticised.

05-04.title: Pope Alexander VI divides the Atlantic world
05-04.description: The bull Inter caetera drew a line west of the Azores, granting Spain lands beyond it. Portugal objected, and the line was moved further west by the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494.

05-04.title: Peter Minuit arrives in New Netherland
05-04.description: Peter Minuit reached Manhattan as director of the Dutch colony. He soon bought the island from the Lenape for goods worth 60 guilders, and New Amsterdam became its capital.

05-04.title: Rhode Island renounces allegiance to George III
05-04.description: Rhode Island's assembly became the first colonial legislature to formally renounce allegiance to the Crown, two months before the Declaration of Independence.

05-04.title: Tipu Sultan is killed as the British storm Seringapatam
05-04.description: British and allied troops breached the walls of Mysore's capital, and Tipu Sultan died fighting at a gate. His defeat removed the strongest opponent of the East India Company in southern India.

05-04.title: Bomb explodes at a labour rally in Haymarket Square
