05-04.description: A bomb thrown at police in Chicago, and the gunfire that followed, killed seven officers and several civilians. Eight anarchists were convicted on thin evidence and four were hanged.

05-04.title: United States takes over the Panama Canal works
05-04.description: The US formally took possession of the abandoned French canal project. Completed in 1914, the canal spared ships the long voyage around South America.

05-04.title: National Guard kills four students at Kent State
05-04.description: Ohio National Guardsmen fired on students protesting the US invasion of Cambodia, killing four and wounding nine. The shootings set off a nationwide student strike.

05-04.title: Margaret Thatcher becomes Britain's first woman Prime Minister
05-04.description: After the Conservatives won the general election, Margaret Thatcher took office. In eleven years in power she privatised industries, curbed trade unions and fought the Falklands War.

05-05.title: Rebel barons renounce their allegiance to King John
05-05.description: A group of English barons formally withdrew their fealty from John and took up arms. Their capture of London weeks later forced the king to agree to Magna Carta in June.

05-05.title: Estates-General opens at Versailles
05-05.description: Louis XVI convened the Estates-General for the first time since 1614 to resolve a financial crisis. Disputes over voting led the Third Estate to declare itself the National Assembly in June.

05-05.title: Napoleon dies in exile on St Helena
05-05.description: Napoleon Bonaparte died aged 51 on the remote Atlantic island where the British had held him since 1815. His legal code and the states he redrew outlived his empire.

05-05.title: Continental Europe's first passenger railway opens in Belgium
05-05.description: Trains began running between Brussels and Mechelen on the first state-built passenger line on the European mainland. Newly independent Belgium soon had a national rail network.

05-05.title: Mexican army defeats the French at Puebla
05-05.description: General Ignacio Zaragoza's outnumbered troops repulsed a French assault on Puebla. The victory, marked as Cinco de Mayo, delayed but did not prevent the French occupation of Mexico.

05-05.title: Tchaikovsky helps open New York's Music Hall, later Carnegie Hall
05-05.description: Andrew Carnegie's new concert hall opened with a festival at which Tchaikovsky conducted. Renamed Carnegie Hall in 1893, it became America's most famous concert venue.

05-05.title: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space
05-05.description: Alan Shepard made a 15-minute suborbital flight in Freedom 7, three weeks after Gagarin's orbit. Twenty days later President Kennedy committed the US to landing a man on the Moon.

05-06.title: Imperial troops sack Rome
05-06.description: Unpaid troops of Emperor Charles V stormed Rome, killing thousands and looting churches while Pope Clement VII sheltered in Castel Sant'Angelo. The sack scattered Rome's artists and humbled the papacy.

05-06.title: Penny Black becomes valid for postage
05-06.description: Britain's prepaid adhesive stamps could now be used on letters. Paying a flat penny in advance, rather than charging recipients by distance, made post cheap and predictable.

05-06.title: Chester Arthur signs the Chinese Exclusion Act
05-06.description: The law suspended the immigration of Chinese labourers and barred Chinese immigrants from citizenship. It was the first major US law to exclude a group by nationality and was repealed only in 1943.

05-06.title: Paris Exposition Universelle opens beneath the Eiffel Tower
05-06.description: The world's fair marking the centenary of the French Revolution opened in Paris. Its entrance arch, Gustave Eiffel's iron tower, was then the tallest structure in the world.

05-06.title: Edward VII dies and George V becomes king
05-06.description: Edward VII died at Buckingham Palace after a nine-year reign. Known for his diplomacy and support for the Entente Cordiale, he gave his name to the Edwardian era.

05-06.title: Hindenburg airship bursts into flames at Lakehurst
05-06.description: The German airship Hindenburg caught fire while mooring in New Jersey, killing 36 people. Newsreel film and radio coverage of the disaster ended public faith in passenger airships.

05-06.title: Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile
05-06.description: On a windy evening at Oxford's Iffley Road track, the medical student Roger Bannister ran the mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds, helped by pacemakers Chris Brasher and Chris Chataway.

05-06.title: Channel Tunnel is formally opened
05-06.description: Queen Elizabeth II and President François Mitterrand opened the 50 km rail tunnel under the Channel. It gave Britain its first fixed link to the Continent since the Ice Age.

05-07.title: Main dome of Hagia Sophia collapses
05-07.description: Weakened by earthquakes, the great dome of Justinian's cathedral fell. It was rebuilt taller and steeper by Isidore the Younger, and that dome, though repaired, still stands.

05-07.title: Louis XIV opens a grand festival at Versailles
05-07.description: Louis XIV began 'The Pleasures of the Enchanted Island', a week of spectacles and plays including Molière's first Tartuffe. Versailles became the seat of court and government in 1682.

05-07.title: Bienville founds New Orleans, by tradition on this day
05-07.description: Jean-Baptiste Le Moyne de Bienville chose a crescent of high ground on the Mississippi for a new French post. The city became a meeting point of French, Spanish, African and American cultures.

05-07.title: HMS Victory is launched at Chatham
05-07.description: The 100-gun first-rate HMS Victory was floated out of dry dock at Chatham. Forty years later she was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, and she survives at Portsmouth as the oldest commissioned warship.

05-07.title: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is first performed in Vienna
05-07.description: Beethoven's Ninth, with its choral setting of Schiller's 'Ode to Joy', premiered at the Kärntnertortheater. The composer, almost entirely deaf, had to be turned to see the audience's applause.

05-07.title: German U-boat sinks the liner Lusitania
05-07.description: U-20 torpedoed the Cunard liner off southern Ireland, sinking her in 18 minutes with the loss of 1,198 lives, 128 of them American. Outrage in the US turned opinion sharply against Germany.

05-07.title: Germany signs its unconditional surrender at Reims
05-07.description: General Alfred Jodl signed the surrender at Eisenhower's headquarters, to take effect the next night. A second signing in Berlin followed at Soviet insistence.

05-08.title: Elizabeth I's Act of Supremacy receives royal assent
05-08.description: The Act restored the Church of England's independence from Rome and made Elizabeth its Supreme Governor. With the Act of Uniformity it formed the basis of the Elizabethan religious settlement.

05-08.title: Chemist Antoine Lavoisier is guillotined in Paris
05-08.description: Lavoisier, executed as a former tax farmer during the Terror, had named oxygen and hydrogen and set chemistry on modern foundations. 'It took them only an instant to cut off that head,' said Lagrange.

05-08.title: US and Mexican armies clash at Palo Alto
05-08.description: Zachary Taylor's artillery won the first major battle of the Mexican-American War near the Rio Grande. By 1848 Mexico had lost about half its territory, including California.

05-08.title: Coca-Cola goes on sale at an Atlanta pharmacy
05-08.description: Pharmacist John Pemberton's new syrup, mixed with carbonated water, was sold at Jacobs' Pharmacy for five cents a glass. It became one of the most widely recognised brands in the world.

05-08.title: Allies celebrate Victory in Europe Day
05-08.description: Germany's surrender took effect and crowds filled the streets of London, Paris and New York. In Moscow, where the surrender came after midnight, victory is marked on 9 May.

05-08.title: Troops fire on Buddhist protesters in Huế
05-08.description: South Vietnamese forces fired on crowds protesting a ban on Buddhist flags, killing nine. The Buddhist crisis that followed undermined President Ngo Dinh Diem, who was overthrown in November.

05-09.title: England and Portugal seal their alliance at Windsor
05-09.description: The Treaty of Windsor pledged perpetual friendship between the two kingdoms. The Anglo-Portuguese alliance is the oldest diplomatic alliance in the world still in force.

05-09.title: Thomas Blood tries to steal the Crown Jewels
05-09.description: Disguised as a parson, Thomas Blood and his accomplices overpowered the keeper of the Jewel House and fled with the crown and orb, but were caught. Charles II surprisingly pardoned him.

05-09.title: Sniper kills Union general John Sedgwick at Spotsylvania
05-09.description: Moments after telling his men that Confederate sharpshooters 'couldn't hit an elephant at this distance', General Sedgwick was shot dead. He was the highest-ranking Union officer killed in the war.

05-09.title: Byrd and Bennett claim to fly over the North Pole
05-09.description: Richard Byrd and Floyd Bennett flew a Fokker trimotor from Spitsbergen and reported reaching the Pole. Doubts about their speed and navigation have kept the claim in dispute.

05-09.title: Robert Schuman proposes pooling Europe's coal and steel
05-09.description: France's foreign minister proposed placing French and German coal and steel under a common authority, making war between them 'materially impossible'. It led to the European Coal and Steel Community.

05-09.title: FDA says it will approve the first contraceptive pill
05-09.description: The US Food and Drug Administration announced it would license Enovid for contraception. The pill gave women far greater control over fertility and transformed family life.

05-10.title: Columbus sights the Cayman Islands
05-10.description: On his fourth voyage, Christopher Columbus sighted two small islands teeming with turtles, which he named Las Tortugas. They later became known as the Cayman Islands.

05-10.title: Parliament passes the Tea Act
05-10.description: The Act let the East India Company ship tea directly to America, undercutting smugglers while keeping the Townshend duty. Colonists saw it as a ploy to make them accept taxation, leading to the Boston Tea Party.

05-10.title: Second Continental Congress meets in Philadelphia
05-10.description: Delegates from the colonies gathered weeks after Lexington and Concord. The Congress created the Continental Army, appointed George Washington to command it and declared independence in 1776.

05-10.title: Stonewall Jackson dies of pneumonia
05-10.description: Eight days after being wounded by his own men at Chancellorsville, General Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson died. Lee said he had lost his right arm.

05-10.title: Union cavalry capture Jefferson Davis in Georgia
05-10.description: The fleeing Confederate president was seized near Irwinville, Georgia. He was held for two years at Fort Monroe but never brought to trial.

05-10.title: Golden spike completes the first transcontinental railroad
05-10.description: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines met at Promontory Summit, Utah. Coast-to-coast travel fell from months to about a week, at great cost to Native American lands.

05-10.title: Churchill becomes Prime Minister as Germany attacks in the West
05-10.description: As German forces invaded the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, Neville Chamberlain resigned and Winston Churchill formed a coalition government to lead Britain's war.

05-11.title: Diamond Sutra is printed in Tang China
05-11.description: A block-printed copy of the Diamond Sutra was made on this date, according to its colophon. Found in a cave at Dunhuang, it is the oldest dated printed book known.

05-11.title: Columbus sails from Cádiz on his fourth voyage
05-11.description: Christopher Columbus set out on his last voyage, exploring the coast of Central America from Honduras to Panama. Shipwrecked on Jamaica for a year, he returned to Spain in 1504.

05-11.title: Marshal Saxe defeats the allied army at Fontenoy
05-11.description: French forces under Maurice de Saxe beat British, Dutch and Hanoverian troops led by the Duke of Cumberland. The victory opened the way to the French conquest of the Austrian Netherlands.

05-11.title: Prime Minister Spencer Perceval is shot in the Commons lobby
05-11.description: John Bellingham, a merchant with a grievance against the government, shot Perceval dead. He remains the only British prime minister to be assassinated.

05-11.title: Mutinous sepoys from Meerut seize Delhi
05-11.description: Rebel soldiers rode into Delhi and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II their leader. The Indian Rebellion that spread from here led to the end of East India Company rule in 1858.

05-11.title: India conducts nuclear tests at Pokhran
05-11.description: India detonated three nuclear devices in the Rajasthan desert, followed by two more on 13 May, and declared itself a nuclear weapons state. Pakistan responded with its own tests within weeks.

05-12.title: Richard the Lionheart marries Berengaria in Cyprus
05-12.description: During his conquest of Byzantine-ruled Cyprus on the way to the Third Crusade, Richard I married Berengaria of Navarre at Limassol. The island became a long-lasting crusader kingdom.

05-12.title: Casimir the Great founds a university in Kraków
05-12.description: King Casimir III founded the Kraków Academy, now the Jagiellonian University. It is the oldest university in Poland, where Nicolaus Copernicus later studied.

05-12.title: Florence Nightingale is born in Florence
05-12.description: Florence Nightingale, named after her birthplace, was born to a wealthy English family. Her work in the Crimean War and her use of statistics reshaped nursing and hospital care.

05-12.title: Airship Norge crosses the North Pole
05-12.description: Roald Amundsen, Umberto Nobile and Lincoln Ellsworth flew over the Pole in the airship Norge on a flight from Svalbard to Alaska. It is the first undisputed arrival at the North Pole.

05-12.title: Red Army opens its offensive at Kharkov
05-12.description: Soviet forces attacked around Kharkov in Ukraine to regain the initiative. German forces encircled the attackers within days, and the disaster cost the Red Army more than 200,000 men.

05-12.title: Soviet Union lifts the Berlin Blockade
05-12.description: After almost eleven months, Soviet authorities reopened road and rail routes into West Berlin. The Allied airlift that had supplied the city became a defining episode of the early Cold War.

05-13.title: Mary, Queen of Scots is defeated at Langside
05-13.description: Mary's forces were routed near Glasgow by the regent Moray. Three days later she fled to England, where Elizabeth I kept her captive for nineteen years before her execution.

05-13.title: The First Fleet sails from Portsmouth for Australia
05-13.description: Eleven ships under Captain Arthur Phillip left England carrying some 1,400 people, about half of them convicts. They reached Botany Bay in January 1788 and founded Sydney.

05-13.title: US Congress declares war on Mexico
05-13.description: Congress approved President Polk's request for war after clashes near the Rio Grande. By the 1848 peace, Mexico had ceded California and most of the present American Southwest.

05-13.title: Churchill offers 'blood, toil, tears and sweat'
05-13.description: In his first speech to the Commons as Prime Minister, Winston Churchill promised a long struggle and declared his aim to be 'victory at all costs'.

05-13.title: Pope John Paul II is shot in St Peter's Square
05-13.description: Mehmet Ali Ağca shot and seriously wounded the Pope as he greeted crowds in Rome. John Paul II recovered and later visited his attacker in prison to forgive him.

05-14.title: English colonists land at Jamestown
05-14.description: Settlers of the Virginia Company came ashore on a peninsula in the James River and built a fort. Despite famine and disease, Jamestown became the first permanent English settlement in America.

05-14.title: Henry IV of France is assassinated in Paris
05-14.description: François Ravaillac stabbed the king when his carriage was halted in the rue de la Ferronnerie. Henry, who had ended the Wars of Religion, was succeeded by his eight-year-old son Louis XIII.

05-14.title: Edward Jenner performs the first vaccination
05-14.description: Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox and later showed the boy was immune to smallpox. Vaccination spread worldwide, and smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980.

05-14.title: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel
05-14.description: As the British Mandate ended, Ben-Gurion declared Israel's independence in Tel Aviv. Neighbouring Arab states invaded the next day, and hundreds of thousands of Palestinians were displaced in the war.

05-14.title: Soviet bloc signs the Warsaw Pact
05-14.description: The USSR and seven Eastern European states formed a military alliance days after West Germany joined NATO. The pact lasted until 1991.

05-14.title: NASA launches Skylab, America's first space station
05-14.description: Skylab was launched on the last Saturn V flown. Damaged on ascent, it was repaired by its first crew, and three crews lived aboard for a total of 171 days.

05-15.title: Emperor Valentinian II is found hanged at Vienne
05-15.description: The young western emperor was found dead in his residence in Gaul. Whether he was murdered by his general Arbogast or took his own life is still debated; civil war followed.

05-15.title: Pope Innocent IV authorises torture by inquisitors
05-15.description: The bull Ad extirpanda permitted secular authorities to use torture to extract confessions from suspected heretics. It set a precedent for inquisitorial practice for centuries.

05-15.title: Bartholomew Gosnold names Cape Cod
05-15.description: English navigator Bartholomew Gosnold reached the Massachusetts peninsula and named it for the abundant cod his crew caught there. His voyage was an early English exploration of New England.

05-15.title: Johannes Kepler confirms his third law of planetary motion
05-15.description: Kepler found that the square of a planet's orbital period is proportional to the cube of its distance from the Sun. Published in Harmonices Mundi, the law later underpinned Newton's theory of gravitation.

05-15.title: Nylon stockings go on sale across the United States
05-15.description: Shoppers bought some four million pairs of DuPont nylon stockings on the first day of nationwide sales. The synthetic fibre transformed fashion and was soon diverted to wartime parachutes.

05-15.title: Britain tests its first thermonuclear weapon design
05-15.description: Operation Grapple saw a British bomb dropped near Malden Island in the Pacific. Its yield fell short of a true hydrogen bomb, but later tests that year succeeded and secured US nuclear cooperation.

05-16.title: Thomas More resigns as Lord Chancellor
05-16.description: A day after the clergy submitted to Henry VIII's authority, Sir Thomas More gave up the Great Seal. His refusal to accept the king's supremacy over the Church led to his execution in 1535.

05-16.title: Marie Antoinette marries the future Louis XVI
05-16.description: The fourteen-year-old Austrian archduchess married the French dauphin at Versailles, sealing an alliance between Habsburgs and Bourbons. Both were guillotined during the Revolution.

05-16.title: Andrew Johnson escapes conviction by one vote
05-16.description: The Senate voted 35 to 19 to convict President Johnson on the first article tried, one vote short of the two-thirds needed. Johnson was the first US president to be impeached.

05-16.title: First Academy Awards are presented in Hollywood
05-16.description: About 270 guests attended a dinner at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel where the first Oscars were handed out in around fifteen minutes. Wings won the top prize.

05-16.title: Theodore Maiman operates the first laser
05-16.description: At Hughes Research Laboratories in California, Maiman produced a pulse of red laser light from a ruby crystal. Lasers went on to transform medicine, communications and industry.

05-17.title: Duke of Buckingham is executed for treason
05-17.description: Edward Stafford, Duke of Buckingham, was beheaded on Tower Hill after a trial for allegedly plotting against Henry VIII. His fall showed how dangerous royal blood had become under the Tudors.

05-17.title: Jolliet and Marquette set out to explore the Mississippi
05-17.description: Louis Jolliet and the Jesuit Jacques Marquette left St Ignace with five companions in two canoes. They travelled down the Mississippi as far as the Arkansas River, mapping it for France.

05-17.title: Brokers sign the Buttonwood Agreement on Wall Street
05-17.description: Twenty-four brokers agreed to trade securities among themselves at a fixed commission. Their pact, traditionally signed under a buttonwood tree, is the origin of the New York Stock Exchange.

05-17.title: Supreme Court strikes down school segregation
05-17.description: In Brown v. Board of Education the US Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racially segregated public schools were unconstitutional, overturning the 'separate but equal' doctrine in education.

05-17.title: Senate Watergate hearings open on television
05-17.description: The Senate committee began televised hearings into the Watergate break-in and cover-up. Testimony revealed the White House taping system, which led to Nixon's resignation in August 1974.

05-18.title: Mamluks capture Acre, the last great crusader city
05-18.description: Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil's army stormed Acre after a six-week siege. The remaining crusader towns on the coast were abandoned within months, ending the crusader states in the Levant.

05-18.title: French Senate proclaims Napoleon Emperor of the French
05-18.description: A decree of the Senate made First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte hereditary emperor. He crowned himself in Notre-Dame in December, in the presence of Pope Pius VII.

05-18.title: Republicans nominate Abraham Lincoln for president
05-18.description: At the Chicago convention Lincoln overtook the favourite, William Seward, on the third ballot. His election in November prompted Southern states to secede.

05-18.title: Plessy v. Ferguson upholds 'separate but equal'
05-18.description: The US Supreme Court ruled that racial segregation on Louisiana railways did not violate the Constitution. The decision underpinned Jim Crow laws until Brown v. Board of Education in 1954.

05-18.title: Mount St Helens erupts in Washington State
05-18.description: An earthquake triggered a vast landslide and lateral blast that tore away the mountain's north face. Fifty-seven people died in the deadliest eruption in US history.

05-19.title: Anne Boleyn is beheaded at the Tower of London
05-19.description: Henry VIII's second queen, mother of the future Elizabeth I, was executed by a French swordsman on charges widely seen as fabricated. Henry was betrothed to Jane Seymour the next day.

05-19.title: French victory at Rocroi breaks Spain's military reputation
05-19.description: The young Duke of Enghien, later the Great Condé, defeated the Spanish army at Rocroi in northern France. The defeat of the famed tercios signalled the decline of Spanish power on land.

05-19.title: England is declared a Commonwealth
05-19.description: Four months after the execution of Charles I, the Rump Parliament declared England a 'Commonwealth and Free State' without king or House of Lords. It gave way to Cromwell's Protectorate in 1653.

05-19.title: T. E. Lawrence dies after a motorcycle crash
05-19.description: T. E. Lawrence, 'Lawrence of Arabia', died six days after crashing near his Dorset cottage. He had served with the Arab Revolt and wrote Seven Pillars of Wisdom.

05-19.title: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis dies in New York
05-19.description: The former First Lady died aged 64. Her composure after her husband's assassination in 1963 made her an enduring public figure, and she later worked as a book editor.

05-20.title: Council of Nicaea opens under Constantine
05-20.description: Bishops from across the empire gathered at Nicaea in the first ecumenical council of the Church. It condemned Arianism and produced the first version of the Nicene Creed.

05-20.title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut in India
05-20.description: Da Gama's fleet arrived on India's Malabar coast after sailing around Africa. The sea route he opened allowed Portugal to bypass the overland spice trade and build an Asian empire.

05-20.title: Ortelius publishes the first modern atlas
05-20.description: Abraham Ortelius issued the Theatrum Orbis Terrarum in Antwerp, a bound collection of uniform maps covering the known world. It became a bestseller and went through many editions.

05-20.title: Napoleon restores slavery in French colonies
05-20.description: A law of the Consulate maintained slavery where it had not been abolished and paved the way for its return elsewhere, reversing the Revolution's abolition of 1794. Resistance helped drive Haiti to independence.

05-20.title: Levi Strauss and Jacob Davis patent riveted denim trousers
05-20.description: The patent for copper rivets at the stress points of work trousers marked the birth of blue jeans. Made for labourers in the American West, they became a global garment.

05-20.title: Charles Lindbergh takes off for Paris
05-20.description: Lindbergh left Roosevelt Field, New York, in the Spirit of St Louis. He landed at Le Bourget 33.5 hours later, completing the first solo non-stop transatlantic flight.

05-20.title: Amelia Earhart sets off on her solo Atlantic flight
05-20.description: Earhart took off from Harbour Grace, Newfoundland, and landed in a field near Derry the next day. She became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

05-20.title: First prisoners are brought to Auschwitz
05-20.description: Thirty German criminal prisoners arrived from Sachsenhausen to act as camp functionaries. Auschwitz grew into the largest Nazi death camp, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered.

05-21.title: Portuguese navigator João da Nova sights St Helena
05-21.description: Returning from India, João da Nova's fleet found an uninhabited island in the South Atlantic, traditionally on St Helena's feast day. It became a vital supply stop and later Napoleon's place of exile.

05-21.title: John Sobieski is elected King of Poland
05-21.description: The nobility of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth elected the victorious commander Jan Sobieski as John III. In 1683 he led the relief army that broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

05-21.title: William Hobson proclaims British sovereignty over New Zealand
05-21.description: Following the Treaty of Waitangi, Lieutenant-Governor Hobson declared British sovereignty over the North Island by cession and the South Island by discovery. The treaty's meaning is still central to New Zealand law.

05-21.title: Clara Barton founds the American Red Cross
05-21.description: Clara Barton, a nurse in the Civil War, set up the American Association of the Red Cross in Washington. It became the country's main organisation for disaster relief and blood donation.

05-21.title: Lindbergh lands in Paris after flying the Atlantic alone
05-21.description: Charles Lindbergh touched down at Le Bourget after 33.5 hours in the air, greeted by a crowd of some 100,000. He won the $25,000 Orteig Prize and instant worldwide fame.

05-21.title: Rajiv Gandhi is assassinated in Tamil Nadu
05-21.description: A suicide bomber from the Tamil Tigers killed the former Indian prime minister at an election rally in Sriperumbudur. His mother, Indira Gandhi, had been assassinated in 1984.

05-22.title: Constantine the Great dies near Nicomedia
05-22.description: The first Christian Roman emperor died after being baptised on his deathbed. He had founded Constantinople, and the empire was divided among his three sons.

05-22.title: Yorkists win the First Battle of St Albans
05-22.description: Richard, Duke of York, defeated royal forces in the streets of St Albans and took Henry VI into his custody. The clash is usually seen as the opening battle of the Wars of the Roses.

05-22.title: Treaty of Hamburg takes Sweden out of the Seven Years' War
05-22.description: Sweden made peace with Prussia, restoring the pre-war borders. With Russia's withdrawal that same month, the treaty relieved Frederick the Great of two enemies.

05-22.title: Senator Charles Sumner is beaten on the floor of the Senate
05-22.description: Congressman Preston Brooks attacked the anti-slavery senator with a cane after Sumner's speech against slavery in Kansas. The assault deepened the bitterness between North and South.

05-22.title: Wright brothers receive their patent for a flying machine
05-22.description: The US Patent Office granted Orville and Wilbur Wright patent 821,393 for their method of controlling an aircraft. They spent years defending it in the courts.

05-22.title: Ceylon becomes the Republic of Sri Lanka
05-22.description: A new constitution made Ceylon a republic, ending the British monarch's role as head of state, and adopted the name Sri Lanka. The island had become independent in 1948.

05-23.title: Joan of Arc is captured at Compiègne
05-23.description: Leading a sortie from the besieged town, Joan was pulled from her horse by Burgundian troops. They sold her to the English, who had her tried for heresy and burned at Rouen a year later.

05-23.title: Defenestration of Prague sparks the Thirty Years' War
05-23.description: Protestant nobles threw two Catholic regents and their secretary from a window of Prague Castle; all three survived. The Bohemian revolt that followed grew into the Thirty Years' War.

05-23.title: Captain William Kidd is hanged for piracy
05-23.description: Kidd, commissioned as a privateer by English backers, was hanged at Execution Dock in Wapping. Many historians think he was made a scapegoat to protect his powerful sponsors.

05-23.title: South Carolina ratifies the US Constitution
05-23.description: South Carolina became the eighth state to ratify. New Hampshire's ratification a month later made nine, the number needed for the Constitution to take effect.

05-23.title: Bonnie and Clyde are killed in a police ambush
05-23.description: Texas and Louisiana lawmen shot Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow in their car near Gibsland, Louisiana. The pair's gang had killed at least nine police officers.

05-23.title: Ben-Gurion announces the capture of Adolf Eichmann
05-23.description: Israel's prime minister told the Knesset that Eichmann, a principal organiser of the Holocaust, had been found and was in Israeli custody. Mossad agents had seized him in Argentina.

05-24.title: Nicolaus Copernicus dies in Frombork
05-24.description: Copernicus died weeks after his On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres was printed; tradition says he saw a copy on his deathbed. His Sun-centred model began a revolution in astronomy.

05-24.title: Toleration Act grants freedom of worship to Dissenters
05-24.description: The Act allowed Protestant Nonconformists in England to worship in their own licensed meeting houses. Catholics and anti-Trinitarians were excluded.

05-24.title: John Wesley feels his heart 'strangely warmed'
05-24.description: At a meeting in Aldersgate Street, London, John Wesley experienced an assurance of faith while hearing Luther's preface to Romans read. The experience energised the Methodist movement.

05-24.title: Samuel Morse sends 'What hath God wrought'
05-24.description: Morse tapped out the biblical phrase from the Capitol in Washington to Alfred Vail in Baltimore. The line opened the age of the electric telegraph in the United States.

05-24.title: Brooklyn Bridge opens across the East River
05-24.description: After fourteen years of construction, the bridge linking Manhattan and Brooklyn opened. It was then the longest suspension bridge in the world, the first to use steel wire cables.

05-24.title: Bismarck sinks HMS Hood in the Denmark Strait
05-24.description: A shell from the German battleship detonated Hood's magazine, and she sank in minutes; only three of her 1,418 crew survived. The Royal Navy hunted Bismarck down three days later.

05-25.title: Alfonso VI of Castile takes Toledo
05-25.description: Alfonso VI entered Toledo after its Muslim ruler surrendered. The old Visigothic capital became a centre where Christian, Jewish and Muslim scholars translated Arabic learning into Latin.

05-25.title: Charles V issues the Edict of Worms against Luther
05-25.description: The emperor declared Martin Luther an outlaw and banned his writings. Protected by Frederick the Wise at the Wartburg, Luther began translating the New Testament into German.

05-25.title: Constitutional Convention opens in Philadelphia
05-25.description: Delegates reached a quorum at the Pennsylvania State House and chose George Washington to preside. Over the summer they drafted the US Constitution.

05-25.title: Ralph Waldo Emerson is born in Boston
05-25.description: Emerson became the leading voice of Transcendentalism. Essays such as 'Self-Reliance' shaped American thought and influenced Thoreau and Whitman.

05-25.title: Kennedy commits America to landing on the Moon
05-25.description: Addressing Congress, President Kennedy called for a man to be landed on the Moon and returned safely before the decade was out. Apollo 11 met the goal in July 1969.

05-25.title: Star Wars opens in American cinemas
05-25.description: George Lucas's space adventure opened in a few dozen cinemas and became the highest-grossing film to that date. It reshaped Hollywood around the blockbuster and merchandising.

05-26.title: English colonists destroy the Pequot fort at Mystic
05-26.description: Connecticut forces and their Mohegan and Narragansett allies set fire to the fortified village, killing some 400 to 700 Pequot, many of them women and children. The Pequot War ended months later.

05-26.title: Last public hanging takes place in England
05-26.description: Michael Barrett, convicted of the Clerkenwell bombing, was hanged before a crowd outside Newgate Prison. Three days later a new Act moved executions inside prison walls.

05-26.title: Nicholas II is crowned Tsar of Russia
05-26.description: Nicholas II and Alexandra were crowned in the Kremlin's Dormition Cathedral. Days later more than a thousand people died in a crush at the celebrations on Khodynka Field, a grim omen for the reign.

05-26.title: Evacuation of Allied troops from Dunkirk begins
05-26.description: Operation Dynamo began. By 4 June more than 338,000 British and French soldiers had been carried to England by warships and hundreds of civilian 'little ships'.

05-26.title: Apollo 10 splashes down after the Moon landing rehearsal
05-26.description: Apollo 10 returned safely after its lunar module descended to about 15 km above the Moon. The mission tested every step of a landing except the touchdown itself.

05-27.title: John Calvin dies in Geneva
05-27.description: The French reformer died aged 54 in the city he had shaped into a Protestant model. His Institutes of the Christian Religion influenced Reformed churches from Scotland to the Netherlands.

05-27.title: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
05-27.description: Construction began on the Peter and Paul Fortress on an island in the Neva, on land newly taken from Sweden. Peter made the city his capital, Russia's 'window on Europe'.

05-27.title: Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrians
05-27.description: Some 200,000 people walked across the new bridge on its opening day before cars were allowed the next. Its main span was then the longest of any suspension bridge.

05-27.title: Royal Navy sinks the battleship Bismarck
05-27.description: Crippled by a torpedo hit to her rudder, Bismarck was pounded by British battleships and sank in the Atlantic. Only about 114 of her crew of over 2,000 survived.

05-27.title: Australians vote to include Aboriginal people in the census
05-27.description: Over 90 per cent voted to count Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the population and to let the Commonwealth make laws for them. It remains Australia's most successful referendum.

05-28.title: Solar eclipse halts a battle between Lydia and Media
05-28.description: According to Herodotus, day turned to night during a battle on the Halys river, and the armies made peace. Astronomers date the eclipse to 28 May 585 BCE, one of the earliest precisely dated events.

05-28.title: Andrew Jackson signs the Indian Removal Act
05-28.description: The law authorised the president to exchange lands west of the Mississippi for Native territory in the East. It led to the forced removals known as the Trail of Tears, in which thousands died.

05-28.title: Paris Commune falls after the 'Bloody Week'
05-28.description: The last Communard defenders were overcome around the Père Lachaise cemetery. Government troops killed thousands during the week, and the Commune became a lasting symbol for the left.

05-28.title: Azerbaijan and Armenia declare independence
05-28.description: As the short-lived Transcaucasian federation broke up, the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the Republic of Armenia proclaimed independence. Both were absorbed by Soviet Russia in 1920.

05-28.title: King Leopold III surrenders the Belgian army
05-28.description: After eighteen days of fighting, Leopold III capitulated to Germany against his government's wishes. The surrender exposed the Allied flank as the Dunkirk evacuation gathered pace.

05-28.title: Pakistan carries out nuclear tests in Balochistan
05-28.description: Pakistan detonated nuclear devices in the Chagai Hills, responding to India's tests earlier that month. Both countries now stood as declared nuclear powers.

05-29.title: Constantinople falls to the Ottoman Turks
05-29.description: After a 53-day siege, Mehmed II's army broke through the city walls; Constantine XI died in the fighting. The Byzantine Empire ended, and Constantinople became the Ottoman capital.

05-29.title: Charles II enters London as the monarchy is restored
05-29.description: On his 30th birthday, Charles II rode into London to cheering crowds after years of exile. The Restoration ended the republican experiment that had followed his father's execution.

05-29.title: Patrick Henry is born in Virginia
05-29.description: Patrick Henry became one of the most powerful orators of the American Revolution. His 1775 speech ending 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' rallied Virginia to arm.

05-29.title: Wisconsin becomes the 30th US state
05-29.description: Wisconsin joined the Union from the old Northwest Territory. It later became known for dairy farming and as a centre of the Progressive movement.

05-29.title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Everest
05-29.description: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa from Nepal, became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of the world's highest mountain.

05-29.title: Nigeria returns to civilian rule
05-29.description: Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as president, ending fifteen years of military government. The date was kept as Nigeria's Democracy Day until 2019, when it moved to 12 June.

05-30.title: Joan of Arc is burned at the stake in Rouen
05-30.description: Condemned as a relapsed heretic by a church court under English control, Joan died aged about 19. Her conviction was annulled in 1456, and she was canonised in 1920.

05-30.title: Columbus sails on his third voyage
05-30.description: Columbus left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with six ships. He reached Trinidad and the Paria peninsula of Venezuela, his first sight of the South American mainland.

05-30.title: Christopher Marlowe is killed in Deptford
05-30.description: The playwright of Doctor Faustus was stabbed by Ingram Frizer during a dispute over a bill. His links to government espionage have fuelled theories about his death ever since.

05-30.title: America's first daily newspaper appears in Philadelphia
05-30.description: Benjamin Towne's Pennsylvania Evening Post began publishing daily, the first newspaper in the United States to do so. It folded the following year.

05-30.title: Biafra declares independence from Nigeria
05-30.description: Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu proclaimed the Republic of Biafra in Nigeria's south-east. The civil war that followed lasted until 1970, and up to two million people died, many from famine.

05-30.title: Students unveil the Goddess of Democracy in Tiananmen Square
05-30.description: Art students erected a ten-metre statue facing Mao's portrait as a symbol of the pro-democracy movement. Troops destroyed it when they cleared the square on 4 June.

05-31.title: Mongols rout the Rus and Cumans at the Kalka River
05-31.description: A Mongol expedition under Jebe and Subutai crushed the armies of several Rus princes and their Cuman allies. The full Mongol conquest of the Rus lands came fourteen years later.

05-31.title: Martin Frobisher sails on his third Arctic voyage
05-31.description: Frobisher left Harwich with fifteen ships to mine what he believed was gold ore on Baffin Island. The ore proved worthless, and the Northwest Passage stayed unfound.

05-31.title: George Washington signs the first US copyright law
05-31.description: The Copyright Act protected books, maps and charts for 14 years, renewable once. It drew on Britain's Statute of Anne and founded American copyright law.

05-31.title: The Great Clock of Westminster starts keeping time
05-31.description: The clock in the new tower of the Houses of Parliament began running. Its great bell, Big Ben, struck the hours for the first time that July.

05-31.title: Treaty of Vereeniging ends the South African War
05-31.description: Boer leaders accepted British sovereignty over the Transvaal and Orange Free State in return for promises of self-government. The war had cost tens of thousands of lives, many in British camps.

05-31.title: British and German fleets clash at Jutland
05-31.description: The largest naval battle of the First World War saw the Royal Navy lose more ships and men, but the German High Seas Fleet withdrew to port and rarely ventured out again.

05-31.title: Earthquake and avalanche devastate northern Peru
05-31.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake set off an avalanche from Huascarán that buried the town of Yungay. About 70,000 people died, making it Peru's worst natural disaster.

06-01.title: Emperor Didius Julianus is killed as Severus nears Rome
06-01.description: Abandoned by the Senate and the Praetorian Guard, Didius Julianus was killed in the palace after a reign of 66 days. Septimius Severus entered Rome soon afterwards and founded a new dynasty.

06-01.title: Scottish exchequer records malt for 'aqua vitae'
06-01.description: An entry in the Exchequer Rolls records malt given to Friar John Cor 'to make aqua vitae' for King James IV. It is the earliest known written reference to whisky distilling in Scotland.

06-01.title: Anne Boleyn is crowned Queen of England
06-01.description: Six months pregnant with the future Elizabeth I, Anne Boleyn was crowned in Westminster Abbey. Her marriage to Henry VIII had required England's break with the papacy.

06-01.title: Howe defeats the French fleet on the Glorious First of June
06-01.description: Lord Howe's Channel Fleet captured six French ships of the line far out in the Atlantic. Yet the grain convoy the French were protecting reached France safely.

06-01.title: Tennessee becomes the 16th US state
06-01.description: Tennessee was the first state created from a federal territory, the Territory South of the River Ohio. It later produced three presidents: Andrew Jackson, James Polk and Andrew Johnson.

06-01.title: Madison asks Congress for war with Britain
06-01.description: President Madison's message cited the impressment of American sailors and British restrictions on neutral trade. Congress declared war on 18 June, beginning the War of 1812.

06-01.title: HMS Shannon captures USS Chesapeake off Boston
06-01.description: In a fight lasting about fifteen minutes, HMS Shannon took the American frigate Chesapeake. The dying American captain James Lawrence's words, 'Don't give up the ship', became a US Navy motto.

06-01.title: CNN launches as the first 24-hour news channel
06-01.description: Ted Turner's Cable News Network began broadcasting from Atlanta. Its round-the-clock coverage created the modern continuous news cycle.

06-02.title: Vandals begin a two-week sack of Rome
06-02.description: King Gaiseric's Vandals entered Rome and plundered it for fourteen days, carrying off treasure and captives to Carthage. The episode later gave the word 'vandalism' to European languages.

06-02.title: Crusaders are let into Antioch by night
06-02.description: On the night of 2 to 3 June, a tower commander named Firouz let Bohemond's men over the walls, ending a seven-month siege. The crusaders were themselves besieged in the city days later.

06-02.title: Ojibwe warriors seize Fort Michilimackinac
06-02.description: During a game of baaga'adowe, a form of lacrosse, Ojibwe players chased the ball into the fort and took it by surprise. The attack was part of the wider uprising known as Pontiac's War.

06-02.title: Guglielmo Marconi applies for a wireless telegraphy patent
06-02.description: The young Italian inventor filed his application in London for a system of telegraphy without wires. Within five years his signals had crossed the Atlantic.

06-02.title: Coolidge signs the Indian Citizenship Act
06-02.description: The law granted US citizenship to all Native Americans born in the United States. Some states still kept Native people from voting for decades afterwards.

06-02.title: Elizabeth II is crowned at Westminster Abbey
06-02.description: The coronation was the first to be televised in full; some 27 million people in Britain watched, many on newly bought sets. It was a landmark in the spread of television.

06-03.title: Dutch West India Company receives its charter
06-03.description: The States General granted the company a trade monopoly in the Americas and West Africa. It founded New Netherland, seized part of Brazil and became a major Atlantic slave trader.

06-03.title: Lin Zexu begins destroying confiscated opium at Humen
06-03.description: The Chinese commissioner had over a thousand tonnes of British-traded opium mixed with lime and salt and flushed into the sea. Britain's response led to the First Opium War.

06-03.title: Luftwaffe bombs Paris
06-03.description: In Operation Paula, German aircraft struck airfields and factories around Paris, killing some 250 people. Eleven days later German troops entered the city.

06-03.title: Battle of Midway opens with US air attacks
06-03.description: Bombers from Midway Atoll attacked the approaching Japanese invasion force. The next day US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese carriers, turning the tide of the Pacific war.

06-03.title: Ayatollah Khomeini dies in Tehran
06-03.description: Ruhollah Khomeini, leader of the 1979 Iranian Revolution and the Islamic Republic's first Supreme Leader, died aged 86. Ali Khamenei succeeded him the next day.

06-03.title: Chinese troops move on Tiananmen Square
06-03.description: On the night of 3 to 4 June, the army forced its way into central Beijing, firing on crowds. Hundreds, possibly thousands, were killed, ending seven weeks of pro-democracy protest.

06-04.title: Osaka Castle falls and the Toyotomi line ends
06-04.description: As Tokugawa forces took Osaka Castle, Toyotomi Hideyori and his mother took their own lives. The Tokugawa shogunate faced no serious rival for the next 250 years.

06-04.title: Montgolfier brothers fly a hot-air balloon in public
06-04.description: In the market square at Annonay, Joseph and Étienne Montgolfier launched an unmanned linen balloon that rose some 2,000 metres. Human flights followed before the year was out.

06-04.title: Suffragette Emily Davison is struck by the King's horse at Epsom
06-04.description: During the Derby, Emily Wilding Davison stepped onto the course and was knocked down by Anmer, George V's horse. She died four days later and became a martyr of the suffrage movement.

06-04.title: Churchill vows 'we shall fight on the beaches'
06-04.description: As the Dunkirk evacuation ended, Churchill told the Commons it was not a victory but promised that Britain would 'never surrender'.

06-04.title: US dive-bombers wreck Japan's carrier force at Midway
06-04.description: Within minutes American dive-bombers set three Japanese carriers ablaze; a fourth was hit that afternoon. Japan lost its best carriers and many experienced aircrew.

06-04.title: Solidarity sweeps Poland's semi-free elections
06-04.description: Solidarity won all but one of the freely contested seats. The result led to the first non-communist-led government in the Soviet bloc and began the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.

06-05.title: Bertrand de Got is elected Pope Clement V
06-05.description: The archbishop of Bordeaux was elected after a long deadlock. Clement V never went to Rome; his move to Avignon began nearly seventy years of papal residence in France.

06-05.title: June Rebellion breaks out in Paris
06-05.description: Republicans raised barricades after the funeral of General Lamarque. The rising was crushed the next day, and Victor Hugo later set the climax of Les Misérables on its barricades.

06-05.title: Express d'Orient makes its first run from Paris
06-05.description: Georges Nagelmackers's luxury train service left Paris for Vienna. That October it was extended towards Constantinople, and as the Orient Express it became a legend of rail travel.

06-05.title: Arab Revolt against Ottoman rule begins
06-05.description: Forces of Sharif Hussein of Mecca, led by his sons, attacked the Ottoman garrison at Medina. Backed by Britain, the revolt helped drive the Ottomans from Arabia and Syria.

06-05.title: George Marshall proposes a plan to rebuild Europe
06-05.description: In a speech at Harvard, the US Secretary of State offered aid to European recovery. The Marshall Plan provided some $13 billion and deepened the divide between East and West.

06-05.title: Israel launches the Six-Day War
06-05.description: Israeli air strikes destroyed most of Egypt's air force on the ground. In six days Israel took Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights.

06-05.title: Robert F. Kennedy is shot in Los Angeles
06-05.description: Minutes after winning the California primary, Senator Kennedy was shot by Sirhan Sirhan at the Ambassador Hotel. He died the next day, two months after Martin Luther King's assassination.

06-06.title: Gustav Vasa is elected King of Sweden
06-06.description: At Strängnäs the Swedish estates chose Gustav Eriksson Vasa, leader of the revolt against Danish rule, as king. He broke with Rome and laid the foundations of the Swedish state. The day is now Sweden's National Day.

06-06.title: George Williams founds the YMCA in London
06-06.description: A draper's assistant, George Williams, and eleven friends founded the Young Men's Christian Association to support young workers in the city. It spread worldwide.

06-06.title: US Marines attack at Belleau Wood
06-06.description: American Marines launched costly assaults on German positions west of Château-Thierry. Three weeks of fighting helped halt the German drive on Paris.

06-06.title: First drive-in cinema opens in New Jersey
06-06.description: Richard Hollingshead opened his 'Automobile Movie Theatre' at Pennsauken, near Camden. Drive-ins became a fixture of post-war American suburban life.

06-06.title: Allied armies land in Normandy on D-Day
06-06.description: About 156,000 Allied troops landed by sea and air on the Normandy coast. The invasion opened the long-awaited second front against Germany in Western Europe.

06-06.title: Alexey Pajitnov completes the first version of Tetris
06-06.description: Working at a Soviet Academy of Sciences computing centre in Moscow, Pajitnov finished his falling-block puzzle game. It became one of the best-selling video games in history.

06-07.title: First Crusade begins the siege of Jerusalem
06-07.description: The crusader armies reached Jerusalem and invested the city. They stormed it on 15 July and massacred many of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants.

06-07.title: Spain and Portugal sign the Treaty of Tordesillas
06-07.description: The two kingdoms divided newly found lands along a meridian 370 leagues west of Cape Verde. The line later gave Portugal its claim to Brazil.

06-07.title: Earthquake sinks much of Port Royal, Jamaica
06-07.description: A violent earthquake plunged two-thirds of the buccaneer town into the sea, killing some 2,000 people at once. Many saw it as divine judgement on 'the wickedest city on Earth'.

06-07.title: Richard Henry Lee moves for American independence
06-07.description: Lee proposed that 'these United Colonies are, and of right ought to be, free and independent States'. Congress adopted the resolution on 2 July.

06-07.title: Norway dissolves its union with Sweden
06-07.description: The Norwegian parliament declared that King Oscar II had ceased to rule as King of Norway. Sweden accepted the separation peacefully after a referendum, and Norway chose a Danish prince as king.

06-07.title: Battle of Midway ends with the sinking of Yorktown
06-07.description: The damaged carrier USS Yorktown finally sank as the battle closed. Japan's loss of four fleet carriers ended its naval superiority in the Pacific.

06-08.title: Prophet Muhammad dies in Medina
06-08.description: Muhammad died in Medina, by most traditions on this day. Within a generation his successors, the caliphs, had carried Islam from Arabia to Persia and North Africa.

06-08.title: Vikings raid the monastery of Lindisfarne
06-08.description: Norse raiders attacked the island monastery off Northumbria, killing monks and seizing treasure. The shock across Christian Europe has made the raid a symbolic start of the Viking Age.

06-08.title: Richard the Lionheart arrives at the siege of Acre
06-08.description: Richard I joined the crusaders besieging Acre, which surrendered five weeks later. He went on to win at Arsuf but never retook Jerusalem.

06-08.title: Andrew Jackson dies at the Hermitage
06-08.description: The seventh US president died at his Tennessee plantation aged 78. Victor at New Orleans and champion of the 'common man', he also drove the forced removal of Native Americans.

06-08.title: Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published
06-08.description: Secker and Warburg published George Orwell's novel of a totalitarian surveillance state. Terms such as 'Big Brother' and 'doublethink' passed into everyday language.

06-08.title: James Earl Ray is arrested at Heathrow
06-08.description: Martin Luther King's killer was caught at London Heathrow travelling on a false Canadian passport. He pleaded guilty in 1969 and was sentenced to 99 years.

06-09.title: Emperor Nero takes his own life
06-09.description: Declared a public enemy by the Senate, Nero died at a freedman's villa outside Rome. His death ended the Julio-Claudian dynasty and opened the Year of the Four Emperors.

06-09.title: Congress of Vienna signs its Final Act
06-09.description: Days before Waterloo, the great powers signed the treaty redrawing Europe's map after Napoleon. Its settlement shaped European borders and diplomacy for decades.

06-09.title: Charles Dickens dies at Gad's Hill
06-09.description: Dickens died at his Kent home aged 58, leaving The Mystery of Edwin Drood unfinished. His novels of poverty and injustice had made him the most popular author of his age.

06-09.title: Donald Duck makes his screen debut
06-09.description: Donald Duck first appeared in the Disney short The Wise Little Hen. His temper and garbled voice made him one of the studio's most popular characters.

06-09.title: Secretariat wins the Belmont by 31 lengths
06-09.description: Secretariat set a world record for the distance and became the first US Triple Crown winner in 25 years. His Belmont time still stands as the race record.

06-10.title: Frederick Barbarossa drowns on the Third Crusade
06-10.description: The Holy Roman Emperor drowned in the Saleph river in Anatolia while leading his army to the Holy Land. Much of the German crusading force broke up after his death.

06-10.title: Bridget Bishop is hanged in the Salem witch trials
06-10.description: Bridget Bishop was the first person executed in the Salem witch trials. By September eighteen more had been hanged, and one man had been pressed to death.

06-10.title: National Museum of Natural History is founded in Paris
06-10.description: The Convention reorganised the royal botanical garden as the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle. Scientists there, including Lamarck and Cuvier, transformed biology and palaeontology.

06-10.title: SS troops massacre the village of Oradour-sur-Glane
06-10.description: A Waffen-SS unit killed 643 people in the French village, shooting the men and burning women and children in the church. The ruins are preserved as a memorial.

06-10.title: Six-Day War ends in a ceasefire
06-10.description: Fighting ended with Israel holding Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights. The status of these territories has remained central to the conflict ever since.

06-11.title: Henry VIII marries Catherine of Aragon
06-11.description: Weeks after his accession, Henry married his brother Arthur's widow at Greenwich. Their failure to produce a surviving son later led Henry to break with Rome.

06-11.title: Congress appoints a committee to draft a declaration of independence
06-11.description: Thomas Jefferson, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Roger Sherman and Robert Livingston formed the Committee of Five. Jefferson wrote the first draft.

06-11.title: George Wallace stands in the schoolhouse door
06-11.description: Alabama's governor blocked the entrance to the University of Alabama to stop two Black students enrolling, then stood aside when federalised Guard troops arrived. Kennedy addressed the nation on civil rights that night.

06-11.title: Thích Quảng Đức burns himself to death in Saigon
06-11.description: The Buddhist monk set himself alight at a busy junction to protest the Diem government's treatment of Buddhists. Malcolm Browne's photograph shocked the world.

06-11.title: Timothy McVeigh is executed for the Oklahoma City bombing
06-11.description: McVeigh was put to death by lethal injection in Terre Haute, Indiana. It was the first federal execution in the United States since 1963.

06-12.title: New York is incorporated as an English city
06-12.description: Governor Richard Nicolls replaced New Amsterdam's Dutch government with an English mayor, aldermen and sheriff. The English had taken the colony from the Dutch the previous year.

06-12.title: Virginia adopts its Declaration of Rights
06-12.description: Drafted mainly by George Mason, the Declaration set out rights such as freedom of the press and trial by jury. It influenced the US Bill of Rights and the French Declaration of 1789.

06-12.title: Emilio Aguinaldo declares Philippine independence
06-12.description: At Kawit, Cavite, revolutionaries proclaimed independence from Spain. The United States annexed the islands instead, and full independence came only in 1946.

06-12.title: Nelson Mandela is sentenced to life imprisonment
06-12.description: Mandela and seven co-accused in the Rivonia Trial were sentenced to life for sabotage. He spent 27 years in prison before his release in 1990.

06-12.title: Reagan urges Gorbachev to 'tear down this wall'
06-12.description: Speaking at the Brandenburg Gate, President Reagan challenged the Soviet leader to open the Berlin Wall. It fell two and a half years later.

06-13.title: Licinius publishes the agreement known as the Edict of Milan
06-13.description: At Nicomedia, Emperor Licinius issued the letter agreed with Constantine granting freedom of worship to Christians and all others. Confiscated church property was ordered returned.

06-13.title: Peasants' Revolt rebels enter London
06-13.description: Wat Tyler's rebels crossed London Bridge and burned John of Gaunt's Savoy Palace. The next day they stormed the Tower and beheaded the Archbishop of Canterbury.

06-13.title: Martin Luther marries Katharina von Bora
06-13.description: The former monk married a former nun in Wittenberg. Their marriage became a model for the Protestant clerical household.

06-13.title: Ludwig II of Bavaria is found drowned
06-13.description: Days after being declared insane and deposed, the builder of Neuschwanstein was found dead in Lake Starnberg with his psychiatrist. The circumstances have never been explained.

06-13.title: Supreme Court decides Miranda v. Arizona
06-13.description: The Court ruled that suspects must be told of their right to remain silent and to have a lawyer before police questioning. The 'Miranda warning' became standard practice.

06-14.title: New Model Army defeats Charles I at Naseby
06-14.description: Fairfax and Cromwell's New Model Army destroyed the main royalist army in Northamptonshire. Captured royal letters damaged the king's cause, and the First Civil War was effectively decided.

06-14.title: Congress adopts the Stars and Stripes
06-14.description: The Flag Resolution called for thirteen stripes, red and white, and thirteen white stars on a blue field. The anniversary is celebrated in the US as Flag Day.

06-14.title: Napoleon wins at Marengo
06-14.description: Near defeat by the Austrians, Napoleon was saved by Desaix's arriving division, and the battle turned. The victory secured northern Italy and his position as First Consul.

06-14.title: German troops enter Paris
06-14.description: The Wehrmacht marched into the French capital, which had been declared an open city. France signed an armistice eight days later.

06-14.title: Argentine forces surrender at Port Stanley
06-14.description: The surrender ended the 74-day Falklands War, in which 649 Argentine and 255 British service personnel died. Argentina's military junta fell soon after.

06-15.title: Robert I of West Francia is killed at Soissons
06-15.description: King Robert I fell in battle against the deposed Carolingian Charles the Simple, though his side won the field. His grandson Hugh Capet later founded the Capetian dynasty.

06-15.title: King John agrees to Magna Carta at Runnymede
06-15.description: Facing rebel barons, John accepted a charter limiting royal power and promising justice under law. Though soon annulled, it was reissued and became a lasting symbol of constitutional government.

06-15.title: Serbs and Ottomans fight the Battle of Kosovo
06-15.description: Prince Lazar's Serbian army met Sultan Murad I's forces on the Field of Blackbirds; both rulers were killed. The battle weakened Serbia and became central to Serbian national memory.

06-15.title: Charles Goodyear patents vulcanised rubber
06-15.description: Goodyear patented his process of heating rubber with sulphur so that it stayed firm and elastic in heat and cold. Vulcanised rubber made possible tyres, seals and hoses.

06-15.title: Hitler and Mussolini hold talks in Venice
06-15.description: At their first meeting, Mussolini was unimpressed by the German leader, and the two clashed over Austria. Within a few years they had drawn together in the Rome-Berlin Axis.

06-15.title: Mount Pinatubo erupts in the Philippines
06-15.description: The second-largest eruption of the twentieth century sent ash 35 km into the sky. Its aerosols cooled global temperatures by about 0.5°C, and timely evacuations saved thousands of lives.

06-16.title: Henry VII defeats the Yorkist rebels at Stoke Field
06-16.description: Henry VII crushed a rebel army supporting the pretender Lambert Simnel. It is often counted as the last battle of the Wars of the Roses.

06-16.title: Spain declares war on Britain
06-16.description: Spain joined France in the American War of Independence, aiming to recover Gibraltar and Minorca. The Great Siege of Gibraltar that followed lasted more than three years.

06-16.title: Lincoln delivers his 'House Divided' speech
06-16.description: Accepting the Illinois Republican nomination for the Senate, Abraham Lincoln warned that the nation could not endure 'permanently half slave and half free'. The speech raised his national profile.

06-16.title: Ford Motor Company is incorporated
06-16.description: Henry Ford and eleven investors founded the company in Detroit. Its Model T and moving assembly line made cars affordable to millions.

06-16.title: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space
06-16.description: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and orbited Earth 48 times in nearly three days. No other woman flew in space for 19 years.

06-16.title: Police fire on students in Soweto
06-16.description: Police shot at schoolchildren marching against compulsory Afrikaans teaching, killing 13-year-old Hector Pieterson among others. The uprising spread, and hundreds died in the months that followed.

06-17.title: Vlad the Impaler attacks the Ottoman camp by night
06-17.description: Vlad III of Wallachia led a night raid on Sultan Mehmed II's camp near Târgovişte, failing to kill the sultan. His reputation for cruelty later fed the legend behind Bram Stoker's Dracula.

06-17.title: Francis Drake claims Nova Albion for Elizabeth I
06-17.description: During his circumnavigation, Drake landed on the coast of what is now northern California and claimed it for England as Nova Albion. England made no attempt to settle it.

06-17.title: British take Breed's Hill at heavy cost in the Battle of Bunker Hill
06-17.description: After two failed assaults, British troops drove colonial militia from the heights near Boston. They suffered more than 1,000 casualties, proving the Americans could stand against regulars.

06-17.title: Iceland becomes a republic
06-17.description: At Þingvellir, the site of its ancient assembly, Iceland ended its union with the Danish crown and proclaimed a republic. Denmark was then under German occupation.

06-17.title: Five men are arrested in the Watergate building
06-17.description: Burglars linked to President Nixon's re-election committee were caught inside the Democratic National Committee offices in Washington. The cover-up led to Nixon's resignation in 1974.

06-17.title: O. J. Simpson leads police on a televised chase
06-17.description: About 95 million viewers watched police follow a white Ford Bronco carrying the former football star along Los Angeles freeways. Simpson was later acquitted of murdering his ex-wife and her friend.

06-18.title: Li Yuan proclaims himself emperor, founding the Tang dynasty
06-18.description: After the fall of the Sui, Li Yuan took the throne at Chang'an as Emperor Gaozu. The Tang dynasty presided over one of the most brilliant periods of Chinese culture.

06-18.title: United States declares war on Britain
06-18.description: Madison signed the declaration after Congress narrowly voted for war. The War of 1812 ended in stalemate in 1815, but gave Americans 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

06-18.title: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon at Waterloo
06-18.description: The arrival of Blücher's Prussians broke Napoleon's final assault on Wellington's army near Brussels. Napoleon abdicated four days later and was exiled to St Helena.

06-18.title: De Gaulle calls on the French to fight on
06-18.description: Speaking on the BBC from London, General Charles de Gaulle rejected the coming armistice and urged French forces to continue resistance. The appeal founded the Free French movement.

06-18.title: Carter and Brezhnev sign the SALT II treaty
06-18.description: The treaty capped each side's strategic nuclear launchers. The US Senate never ratified it after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, though both sides largely observed its limits.

06-19.title: Louis IX orders Jews in France to wear a badge
06-19.description: An ordinance of Louis IX required Jews to wear a coloured circle of cloth, the rouelle, on their clothing. It enforced a rule of the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215 and marked Jews out for discrimination.

06-19.title: Union troops proclaim emancipation in Galveston, Texas
06-19.description: General Gordon Granger announced that all enslaved people in Texas were free, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. The day is celebrated as Juneteenth, a US federal holiday since 2021.

06-19.title: Emperor Maximilian of Mexico is executed
06-19.description: Maximilian, the Austrian archduke installed by France as Emperor of Mexico, was shot by firing squad at Querétaro with two of his generals. Benito Juárez's republic was restored.

06-19.title: First Father's Day is held in Spokane
06-19.description: Sonora Smart Dodd organised the celebration to honour her father, a widower who raised six children. Father's Day became a permanent US national holiday in 1972.

06-19.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed
06-19.description: The couple were electrocuted at Sing Sing for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Ethel's role, in particular, remains disputed.

06-19.title: Kuwait gains independence from Britain
06-19.description: An exchange of notes ended the 1899 agreement that made Kuwait a British protectorate. Iraq claimed the new state, and invaded it in 1990.

06-20.title: Aetius checks Attila at the Catalaunian Plains
06-20.description: A coalition of Romans and Visigoths under Aetius fought Attila's Huns to a halt in Gaul, on a date traditionally given as 20 June. Attila withdrew, and invaded Italy the following year.

06-20.title: British captives are confined in the 'Black Hole of Calcutta'
06-20.description: After the Nawab of Bengal took Calcutta, British prisoners were held overnight in a tiny guardroom, where many died. The numbers are disputed, but the story fuelled British retaliation.

06-20.title: Third Estate swears the Tennis Court Oath
06-20.description: Locked out of their hall, deputies of the National Assembly met in a royal tennis court at Versailles and vowed not to separate until France had a constitution.

06-20.title: Victoria becomes queen at the age of 18
06-20.description: Victoria was woken at Kensington Palace with news that William IV had died. Her 63-year reign saw industrial growth and the expansion of the British Empire.

06-20.title: US and Soviet Union agree to set up a hotline
06-20.description: Signed in Geneva after the Cuban Missile Crisis, the agreement created a direct teletype link between Washington and Moscow. Popularly called the 'red telephone', it was never a telephone.

06-20.title: Bundestag votes to move Germany's government to Berlin
06-20.description: By 338 votes to 320, the parliament of reunified Germany chose Berlin over Bonn as the seat of government. The move was completed in 1999.

06-21.title: Hannibal ambushes a Roman army at Lake Trasimene
06-21.description: In morning mist on the lake shore, Hannibal trapped the consul Flaminius's army, killing about 15,000 Romans. The disaster led Rome to appoint Fabius Maximus as dictator.

06-21.title: Edward Cornwallis founds Halifax, Nova Scotia
06-21.description: British settlers arrived to build a fortified town as a counterweight to French Louisbourg. Halifax became a key naval base for Britain and later for Canada.

06-21.title: New Hampshire's ratification puts the US Constitution into effect
06-21.description: New Hampshire became the ninth state to ratify, the number required for the Constitution to take effect. The new federal government began work in 1789.

06-21.title: Wellington routs Joseph Bonaparte at Vitoria
06-21.description: Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese and Spanish army broke the French in northern Spain, capturing their baggage train. Joseph fled, and French rule in Spain collapsed.

06-21.title: Three civil rights workers are murdered in Mississippi
06-21.description: James Chaney, Andrew Goodman and Michael Schwerner were killed by Klansmen, with the involvement of local law officers, during Freedom Summer. Their deaths spurred support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

06-22.title: Rome defeats Macedon at Pydna
06-22.description: Lucius Aemilius Paullus's legions broke the Macedonian phalanx of King Perseus. The Antigonid kingdom was abolished, and Rome became the dominant power in the Greek world.

06-22.title: Galileo is made to abjure before the Inquisition
06-22.description: Found 'vehemently suspect of heresy', Galileo formally abjured the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. He spent the rest of his life under house arrest.

06-22.title: Lord Mansfield rules in the Somerset case
06-22.description: The judge held that James Somerset, an enslaved man brought to England, could not be forcibly removed abroad. The ruling was widely taken to mean slavery had no basis in English law.

06-22.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
06-22.description: Operation Barbarossa sent some three million Axis troops across a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The war in the east became the largest and deadliest land conflict in history.

06-22.title: Roosevelt signs the G.I. Bill
06-22.description: The Servicemen's Readjustment Act gave veterans college tuition, low-cost home loans and unemployment pay. Millions took up its benefits, expanding higher education and home ownership.

06-23.title: Battle of Bannockburn begins
06-23.description: On the first day, Robert the Bruce killed the English knight Henry de Bohun in single combat before the armies. Edward II's larger army was routed the next day.

06-23.title: Robert Clive defeats the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey
06-23.description: Helped by the defection of Mir Jafar, Clive's East India Company troops defeated Siraj ud-Daulah. The victory gave the Company control of Bengal and launched British territorial rule in India.

06-23.title: June Days uprising erupts in Paris
06-23.description: Workers rose after the government closed the National Workshops. General Cavaignac crushed them in four days; thousands were killed and many more deported.

06-23.title: Christopher Latham Sholes patents a typewriter
06-23.description: Sholes and his partners received a patent for a 'Type-Writer'. Developed further and sold by Remington, it popularised the QWERTY keyboard and transformed office work.

06-23.title: Nixon approves using the CIA to block the Watergate inquiry
06-23.description: In a taped conversation, Nixon agreed that the CIA should ask the FBI to halt its investigation. The release of this 'smoking gun' tape in August 1974 forced his resignation.

06-23.title: United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union
06-23.description: In a referendum, 52 per cent voted to leave the EU. Prime Minister David Cameron resigned, and Britain formally left in January 2020.

06-24.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Bannockburn
06-24.description: On the second day, Scottish spearmen drove the English army into the burns and marshes near Stirling. Edward II fled, and Scotland's independence was secured until England recognised it in 1328.

06-24.title: John Cabot makes landfall in North America
06-24.description: Sailing for Henry VII, the Venetian navigator John Cabot landed on the coast, probably of Newfoundland or Cape Breton. His voyage became the basis of later English claims in North America.

06-24.title: Premier Grand Lodge of England is founded
06-24.description: Four London lodges met at the Goose and Gridiron alehouse to form a Grand Lodge. It marks the beginning of organised modern Freemasonry.

06-24.title: Napoleon's Grande Armée crosses the Niemen into Russia
06-24.description: Some 450,000 troops in the first wave crossed into Russian territory. By December only a fraction had survived the retreat from Moscow.

06-24.title: Soviet Union begins the Berlin Blockade
06-24.description: Soviet forces cut road, rail and canal links to West Berlin. The Western Allies responded with an airlift that supplied the city's two million people for eleven months.

06-25.title: Elena Cornaro Piscopia becomes the first woman to earn a doctorate
06-25.description: The Venetian scholar was awarded a doctorate in philosophy by the University of Padua. She is the first woman known to have received a university doctoral degree.

06-25.title: Virginia ratifies the US Constitution
06-25.description: Despite Patrick Henry's opposition, Virginia narrowly ratified, the tenth state to do so. Without the largest state, the new union could hardly have worked.

06-25.title: Lakota and Cheyenne defeat Custer at the Little Bighorn
06-25.description: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors killed Lieutenant Colonel George Custer and some 268 soldiers in Montana Territory. The US Army responded with campaigns that ended Plains resistance.

06-25.title: North Korea invades South Korea
06-25.description: North Korean troops crossed the 38th parallel in force. The Korean War drew in UN forces and China and ended in a 1953 armistice near the original line.

06-25.title: Croatia and Slovenia declare independence
06-25.description: The two republics broke away from Yugoslavia on the same day. A brief war in Slovenia was followed by much longer conflicts in Croatia and Bosnia.

06-26.title: Mongols crush the Seljuks of Rûm at Köse Dağ
06-26.description: A Mongol army under Baiju defeated Sultan Kaykhusraw II in north-eastern Anatolia. The Seljuk sultanate became a Mongol vassal and broke into the principalities from which the Ottomans emerged.

06-26.title: George IV dies at Windsor
06-26.description: The former Prince Regent, known for extravagance and his patronage of architecture, died at 67. His brother William IV succeeded him, and the Great Reform Act followed in 1832.

06-26.title: Queen Victoria presents the first Victoria Crosses
06-26.description: In Hyde Park, Queen Victoria decorated 62 servicemen for valour in the Crimean War. The Victoria Cross remains Britain's highest award for gallantry.

06-26.title: United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco
06-26.description: Delegates of 50 nations signed the Charter creating the United Nations to maintain peace and security. It came into force in October 1945.

06-26.title: Kennedy tells West Berlin 'Ich bin ein Berliner'
06-26.description: Speaking at Rathaus Schöneberg to a crowd of about 450,000, President Kennedy declared solidarity with the people of the walled city two years after the Berlin Wall went up.

06-27.title: George II leads his army to victory at Dettingen
06-27.description: In the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army under George II beat the French in Bavaria. It was the last time a reigning British monarch commanded troops in battle.

06-27.title: Mormon founder Joseph Smith is killed by a mob
06-27.description: Militiamen stormed the jail in Carthage, Illinois, where Smith and his brother Hyrum were held, and shot them dead. Brigham Young later led most of his followers west to Utah.

06-27.title: Sailors mutiny aboard the battleship Potemkin
06-27.description: Crew of the Russian Black Sea Fleet battleship rose against their officers after a dispute over rotten meat. The mutiny became a symbol of the 1905 Revolution, later immortalised by Eisenstein.

06-27.title: UN Security Council calls on members to defend South Korea
