06-27.description: Resolution 83 recommended that members help South Korea repel the North's attack. The Soviet Union was boycotting the Council and could not veto it.

06-27.title: Gordon Brown succeeds Tony Blair as Prime Minister
06-27.description: After ten years as Chancellor, Gordon Brown became Prime Minister. His premiership was dominated by the global financial crisis of 2008.

06-28.title: Crusaders break out of Antioch and rout Kerbogha
06-28.description: Besieged in the city they had just taken, and inspired by the supposed discovery of the Holy Lance, the crusaders defeated the army of Kerbogha of Mosul. The road to Jerusalem lay open.

06-28.title: Charles of Spain is elected Holy Roman Emperor
06-28.description: The electors chose Charles I of Spain over Francis I of France. As Charles V he ruled Spain, the Low Countries, Austria and much of Italy and the Americas.

06-28.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau is born in Geneva
06-28.description: Rousseau's The Social Contract and Émile shaped political thought and education, and his Confessions helped create modern autobiography. His ideas inspired French revolutionaries.

06-28.title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo
06-28.description: Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne and his wife Sophie. Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia set off the July Crisis and the First World War.

06-28.title: Treaty of Versailles is signed
06-28.description: Germany signed the peace in the Hall of Mirrors, five years to the day after Sarajevo. It accepted territorial losses, disarmament and reparations, which fuelled lasting resentment.

06-29.title: Globe Theatre burns down during Henry VIII
06-29.description: A cannon fired for a stage effect set the thatched roof alight, and Shakespeare's playhouse burned to the ground within an hour. No one was killed, and it was rebuilt the next year.

06-29.title: Spanish found Mission San Francisco de Asís
06-29.description: Franciscan friars celebrated the first Mass at the mission later known as Mission Dolores, as Spain expanded northward in California. The settlement grew into San Francisco.

06-29.title: The Daily Telegraph is first published
06-29.description: The Daily Telegraph and Courier appeared in London. Under new owners it soon became a penny paper and for a time had the largest circulation in the world.

06-29.title: Roger Casement is sentenced to death for treason
06-29.description: The Irish nationalist and former British diplomat was condemned for seeking German help for the Easter Rising. Despite pleas for clemency he was hanged in August.

06-29.title: Sampoong Department Store collapses in Seoul
06-29.description: The five-storey store fell in seconds, killing 502 people. Investigators found illegal alterations and ignored warnings, prompting reforms of South Korean building safety.

06-30.title: Cortés flees Tenochtitlan on the Noche Triste
06-30.description: Under attack by the Mexica, Cortés's forces fought their way out of the city along the causeways at night, losing hundreds of Spaniards and many more Tlaxcalan allies. He returned to besiege it in 1521.

06-30.title: Henry II of France is mortally wounded in a joust
06-30.description: A splinter from the lance of the Count of Montgomery pierced the king's eye at a tournament in Paris. His death ten days later left France to weak young sons on the eve of the Wars of Religion.

06-30.title: Einstein's paper on special relativity reaches the journal
06-30.description: Annalen der Physik received 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', which showed that measurements of time and space depend on motion. E = mc² followed in a short sequel that autumn.

06-30.title: Tunguska explosion flattens Siberian forest
06-30.description: An asteroid or comet fragment exploded above the Tunguska river, levelling some 2,000 square km of forest. It is the largest impact event in recorded history.

06-30.title: Hitler purges the SA in the Night of the Long Knives
06-30.description: SS squads killed SA chief Ernst Röhm and other rivals, including the former chancellor Kurt von Schleicher. The army welcomed the purge, and Hitler's grip on power tightened.

06-30.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
06-30.description: At midnight, at a ceremony attended by the Prince of Wales and President Jiang Zemin, sovereignty passed to China after 156 years of British rule. Hong Kong became a Special Administrative Region.

07-01.title: Crusaders defeat the Seljuk Turks at Dorylaeum
07-01.description: The First Crusade routed the army of Kilij Arslan I at Dorylaeum in Anatolia. The victory opened the road across Asia Minor and showed that the crusaders could beat the Seljuks in open battle.

07-01.title: William III defeats James II at the Battle of the Boyne
07-01.description: William of Orange defeated the deposed James II on the River Boyne in Ireland (1 July Old Style). The victory secured the Protestant succession and is still commemorated by the Orange Order each July.

07-01.title: Continental Congress debates independence in a decisive test vote
07-01.description: Meeting as a committee of the whole, Congress debated Richard Henry Lee's resolution for independence; nine colonies backed it in a test vote. The formal vote followed the next day with twelve in favour.

07-01.title: Union guns repel Lee's assaults at Malvern Hill
07-01.description: Massed Union artillery shattered Confederate attacks at Malvern Hill near Richmond, the last of the Seven Days Battles. Though McClellan withdrew afterwards, Lee's costly assaults ended the campaign.

07-01.title: The Battle of Gettysburg begins in Pennsylvania
07-01.description: Confederate and Union forces collided at Gettysburg, opening the largest battle ever fought in North America. Three days later Lee's army withdrew, having suffered some 23,000 of the roughly 50,000 casualties.

07-01.title: British army suffers 57,470 casualties on the first day of the Somme
07-01.description: After a week-long bombardment, British and French infantry attacked along the Somme. Britain lost 57,470 men killed, wounded or missing, the heaviest single-day toll in the British Army's history.

07-01.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
07-01.description: At midnight sovereignty over Hong Kong passed from Britain to China, ending 156 years of British rule. The territory became a Special Administrative Region under the 'one country, two systems' principle.

07-02.title: Li Shimin kills his brothers in the Xuanwu Gate Incident
07-02.description: Prince Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji at the Xuanwu Gate of Chang'an. Within two months his father abdicated, and as Emperor Taizong he presided over a golden age of Tang China.

07-02.title: Continental Congress votes for independence from Britain
07-02.description: Congress adopted the Lee Resolution declaring the colonies free and independent states, with twelve in favour and New York abstaining. John Adams predicted that 2 July would be celebrated for ever; posterity chose the 4th.

07-02.title: Union troops hold Little Round Top on Gettysburg's second day
07-02.description: Confederate assaults struck the Union left at Little Round Top, the Wheatfield and the Peach Orchard. The Union line held its high ground by a narrow margin, setting the stage for Pickett's Charge the next day.

07-02.title: First Zeppelin airship flies over Lake Constance
07-02.description: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's LZ 1 made its maiden flight from a floating hangar on Lake Constance. It was the first flight of a rigid airship, beginning an era that ended with the Hindenburg disaster of 1937.

07-02.title: Amelia Earhart disappears over the Pacific
07-02.description: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished while searching for tiny Howland Island on the last long legs of their round-the-world flight. Despite a vast search, their fate has never been conclusively established.

07-02.title: Lyndon Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act
07-02.description: President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, outlawing discrimination on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex or national origin. It ended legal segregation in public places and was the most sweeping civil rights law since Reconstruction.

07-03.title: Hugh Capet is crowned King of the Franks
07-03.description: Hugh Capet was crowned, replacing the Carolingian line with his own family. The Capetians and their cadet branches would rule France almost without a break until 1848.

07-03.title: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec
07-03.description: Samuel de Champlain established a fortified trading post at Quebec on the St Lawrence. It became the capital of New France and the heart of French-speaking North America, a culture that endures in Canada today.

07-03.title: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to the French
07-03.description: Outnumbered and rain-soaked, the 22-year-old Washington surrendered Fort Necessity in western Pennsylvania. It was the only surrender of his military career and an opening clash of the French and Indian War.

07-03.title: Pickett's Charge fails on the final day of Gettysburg
07-03.description: Some 12,500 Confederates advanced across open fields against the Union centre on Cemetery Ridge and were cut down. The repulse ended Lee's invasion of the North and is often called the high-water mark of the Confederacy.

07-03.title: Karl Benz drives his Motorwagen in public in Mannheim
07-03.description: Karl Benz made the first public drive of his three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen on the Ringstrasse in Mannheim. Patented that January, it is widely regarded as the first practical petrol-powered motor car.

07-03.title: USS Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Flight 655
07-03.description: The US cruiser Vincennes, mistaking the Airbus for an attacking fighter, shot down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 on board. The tragedy deepened hostility between Washington and Tehran.

07-04.title: Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence
07-04.description: Congress approved the final text of the Declaration, drafted chiefly by Thomas Jefferson. Its assertion that all men are created equal, with unalienable rights, became the founding statement of the United States.

07-04.title: US Military Academy opens at West Point
07-04.description: The United States Military Academy formally opened at West Point, New York. It went on to train generations of officers, among them Grant, Lee, Eisenhower and MacArthur.

07-04.title: John Adams and Thomas Jefferson die on the same day
07-04.description: Former presidents John Adams and Thomas Jefferson died within hours of each other on the 50th anniversary of the Declaration. Adams's reported last words were 'Thomas Jefferson survives', unaware his rival had died first.

07-04.title: Vicksburg surrenders to Ulysses S. Grant
07-04.description: After a 47-day siege, John Pemberton surrendered Vicksburg and nearly 30,000 men. With Port Hudson falling days later, the Union controlled the Mississippi and split the Confederacy in two.

07-04.title: Polish leader Władysław Sikorski dies in a crash at Gibraltar
07-04.description: General Sikorski, prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile, was killed when his aircraft crashed seconds after take-off from Gibraltar. His death removed the Allies' most respected Polish voice at a critical moment.

07-04.title: The Philippines gains independence from the United States
07-04.description: The Philippines became a sovereign republic after nearly half a century of American rule, as promised by the 1934 Tydings-McDuffie Act. For decades 4 July was celebrated as its Independence Day.

07-04.title: Mars Pathfinder lands on Mars
07-04.description: NASA's Pathfinder bounced to a landing on airbags in Ares Vallis and soon deployed Sojourner, the first rover on another planet. The mission returned thousands of images and revived public interest in Mars.

07-05.title: Isaac Newton publishes the Principia
07-05.description: Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was published in London. It set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation, giving physics the framework that dominated science for more than two centuries.

07-05.title: French forces capture Algiers
07-05.description: The Dey of Algiers surrendered to a French expeditionary force, beginning 132 years of French rule in Algeria. The colonisation ended only after a long and bloody war of independence.

07-05.title: William Booth begins the mission that becomes the Salvation Army
07-05.description: Methodist preacher William Booth began evangelising in London's East End, founding the Christian Mission. Renamed the Salvation Army in 1878, it grew into a worldwide church and charity.

07-05.title: Louis Réard unveils the bikini at a Paris swimming pool
07-05.description: Engineer and designer Louis Réard presented his two-piece swimsuit at the Piscine Molitor, modelled by dancer Micheline Bernardini. He named it after Bikini Atoll, where atomic tests had just begun.

07-05.title: The National Health Service launches in Britain
07-05.description: Aneurin Bevan's National Health Service began, offering comprehensive care free at the point of use to everyone in Britain. It became one of the defining institutions of the post-war welfare state.

07-05.title: Algeria becomes independent from France
07-05.description: Algeria proclaimed independence, 132 years to the day after French troops took Algiers. It followed an eight-year war of liberation and a referendum in which Algerians voted overwhelmingly for independence.

07-06.title: Richard the Lionheart becomes King of England
07-06.description: Henry II died at Chinon, and his son Richard succeeded him. Famed as a crusader against Saladin, Richard spent barely six months of his ten-year reign in England.

07-06.title: Jan Hus is burned at the stake in Constance
07-06.description: The Czech reformer Jan Hus, condemned as a heretic by the Council of Constance despite a promise of safe conduct, was burned. His death provoked the Hussite revolt in Bohemia a century before Luther.

07-06.title: Richard III is crowned at Westminster Abbey
07-06.description: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, was crowned after his nephew Edward V was declared illegitimate. Two years later his death at Bosworth ended Plantagenet rule and brought the Tudors to the throne.

07-06.title: Monmouth's rebellion is crushed at Sedgemoor
07-06.description: Royal troops routed the Duke of Monmouth's rebel army at Sedgemoor in Somerset, often called the last pitched battle on English soil. Judge Jeffreys's 'Bloody Assizes' followed.

07-06.title: German ambassador Mirbach is assassinated in Moscow
07-06.description: Left Socialist Revolutionaries shot Count Wilhelm von Mirbach in the German embassy, hoping to wreck the Brest-Litovsk peace. Their uprising was crushed and the Bolsheviks became Russia's sole ruling party.

07-06.title: Fire sweeps a circus big top in Hartford, killing 167
07-06.description: The Ringling Bros. tent, waterproofed with paraffin and petrol, caught fire during a matinee in Hartford, Connecticut. At least 167 people died, many of them children, prompting tighter fire-safety rules.

07-07.title: Joan of Arc is cleared of heresy 25 years after her death
07-07.description: A retrial authorised by Pope Callixtus III quashed Joan of Arc's 1431 conviction and declared her innocent. She was canonised as a saint in 1920.

07-07.title: American rearguard fights the British at Hubbardton
07-07.description: Retreating from Fort Ticonderoga, an American rearguard fought pursuing British and German troops at Hubbardton, Vermont. Though defeated, they slowed Burgoyne's advance towards eventual surrender at Saratoga.

07-07.title: President McKinley signs the resolution annexing Hawaii
07-07.description: McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution, annexing the Republic of Hawaii five years after American businessmen had overthrown Queen Liliuokalani. Hawaii became a US territory and, in 1959, the 50th state.

07-07.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident sparks war between China and Japan
07-07.description: A night-time clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beijing escalated into full-scale war. The Second Sino-Japanese War merged into the Second World War and cost millions of Chinese lives.

07-07.title: Boris Becker, 17, becomes Wimbledon's youngest men's champion
07-07.description: Unseeded West German Boris Becker beat Kevin Curren in four sets to win Wimbledon at 17. He remains the youngest men's singles champion in the tournament's history.

07-07.title: Suicide bombers kill 52 on London's transport network
07-07.description: Four bombers struck three Underground trains and a bus during the morning rush hour, killing 52 people. It was Britain's deadliest terrorist attack since Lockerbie, a day after London won the 2012 Olympics.

07-08.title: Crusaders process barefoot around the walls of Jerusalem
07-08.description: Weakened by thirst and heat, the crusaders fasted and walked barefoot around besieged Jerusalem, ending on the Mount of Olives. A week later their final assault took the city.

07-08.title: Vasco da Gama sails from Lisbon for India
07-08.description: Vasco da Gama left Lisbon with four ships on a voyage that rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut in 1498. The sea route to India launched Portugal's maritime empire in Asia.

07-08.title: Peter the Great crushes the Swedish army at Poltava
07-08.description: Russian forces destroyed the army of Charles XII at Poltava in Ukraine. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and announced Russia as the dominant force in northern Europe.

07-08.title: The Declaration of Independence is first read in public in Philadelphia
07-08.description: Colonel John Nixon read the Declaration to a crowd in the State House yard, now Independence Square. Tradition holds that the Liberty Bell rang out, though this story dates from the nineteenth century.

07-08.title: Commodore Perry's 'Black Ships' arrive in Edo Bay
07-08.description: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored four warships off Uraga and demanded that Japan open its ports. The visit ended two centuries of restricted contact and set Japan on the path to rapid modernisation.

07-08.title: The Wall Street Journal publishes its first issue
07-08.description: Dow Jones and Company, founded by Charles Dow, Edward Jones and Charles Bergstresser, launched the Wall Street Journal. It became one of the world's most influential financial newspapers.

07-09.title: Avitus is acclaimed Western Roman Emperor near Arles
07-09.description: Backed by the Visigoths and the Gallo-Roman nobility, the senator Avitus was acclaimed emperor near Arles. His reign lasted barely a year, a sign of how weak the Western Empire had become.

07-09.title: New Yorkers topple George III's statue after the Declaration is read
07-09.description: Washington had the Declaration read to his troops in New York. That evening a crowd pulled down the gilded lead statue of George III on Bowling Green; much of the lead was later cast into musket balls.

07-09.title: Napoleon annexes the Kingdom of Holland to France
07-09.description: Days after his brother Louis abdicated rather than enforce the blockade of British trade, Napoleon decreed Holland's annexation to the French Empire. Dutch independence was restored only in 1813.

07-09.title: The 14th Amendment wins enough states for ratification
07-09.description: South Carolina's and Louisiana's approval gave the 14th Amendment the three-quarters of states it needed. It guaranteed citizenship to all born in the US and equal protection of the laws.

07-09.title: The first Wimbledon Championships begin
07-09.description: The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club opened its first lawn tennis championship, with 22 men competing. Spencer Gore won the title ten days later, launching the world's oldest tennis tournament.

07-09.title: South Sudan becomes independent
07-09.description: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan after a referendum, becoming the world's newest internationally recognised state. Independence followed decades of civil war, but a new conflict erupted in 2013.

07-10.title: Lady Jane Grey is proclaimed Queen of England
07-10.description: Days after Edward VI's death, the Duke of Northumberland had his Protestant daughter-in-law proclaimed queen to bar the Catholic Mary Tudor. Jane's reign lasted nine days; she was executed the following year.

07-10.title: William the Silent is assassinated in Delft
07-10.description: Balthasar Gérard shot William of Orange, leader of the Dutch revolt against Spain, at his home in Delft. He is often cited as the first head of state killed with a handgun.

07-10.title: Wyoming becomes the 44th US state
07-10.description: Wyoming joined the Union with women's suffrage intact; as a territory it had given women the vote in 1869. Congress accepted the state despite opposition to its equal-suffrage clause.

07-10.title: The Scopes 'Monkey Trial' opens in Tennessee
07-10.description: Teacher John Scopes went on trial in Dayton for teaching human evolution. The clash between Clarence Darrow and William Jennings Bryan turned a local case into a national debate on science and faith.

07-10.title: The Battle of Britain begins
07-10.description: The Luftwaffe began attacking Channel convoys and coastal targets, the date Britain uses for the start of the Battle of Britain. The RAF's survival over four months forced Hitler to postpone his invasion.

07-10.title: Telstar is launched, the first satellite to relay live TV
07-10.description: NASA launched AT&T's Telstar 1 from Cape Canaveral. Within hours it relayed the first television pictures across the Atlantic, opening the age of satellite communications.

07-11.title: Flemish militia defeat French knights at the Battle of the Golden Spurs
07-11.description: Flemish townsmen on foot routed the French cavalry at Courtrai, collecting hundreds of golden spurs from the dead. The battle showed that disciplined infantry could beat mounted knights.

07-11.title: Charles of Luxembourg is elected King of the Romans
07-11.description: Five prince-electors meeting at Rhens chose Charles of Luxembourg as rival king to Louis IV. Later crowned emperor as Charles IV, he issued the Golden Bull of 1356 that fixed imperial elections for centuries.

07-11.title: Congress re-establishes the US Marine Corps
07-11.description: An Act of Congress created the US Marine Corps as a permanent service, reviving the Continental Marines of the Revolution. It grew into one of America's most celebrated fighting forces.

07-11.title: Aaron Burr mortally wounds Alexander Hamilton in a duel
07-11.description: Vice President Aaron Burr shot Alexander Hamilton at Weehawken, New Jersey; Hamilton died the next day. The death of the first Treasury Secretary ended Burr's political career.

07-11.title: Babe Ruth makes his major league debut for the Red Sox
07-11.description: Nineteen-year-old Babe Ruth pitched for the Boston Red Sox against Cleveland, winning his first major league game. He went on to become baseball's greatest slugger and a symbol of the 1920s.

07-11.title: Skylab falls to Earth over Western Australia
07-11.description: NASA's Skylab space station broke up on re-entry, scattering debris near Esperance in Western Australia. The local shire jokingly fined NASA for littering; an American radio host paid the fine in 2009.

07-12.title: Acre surrenders to the armies of the Third Crusade
07-12.description: After a siege of almost two years, the garrison of Acre surrendered to Richard I and Philip II. The port became the crusaders' main base and later capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

07-12.title: Henry VIII marries Catherine Parr, his sixth wife
07-12.description: Henry VIII married the twice-widowed Catherine Parr at Hampton Court. She outlived him, helped reconcile the king with his daughters and became the first English queen to publish a book in her own name.

07-12.title: Williamite army wins the Battle of Aughrim
07-12.description: William III's forces under Godert de Ginkel defeated the Jacobite army at Aughrim in County Galway (12 July Old Style). The bloodiest battle in Irish history effectively decided the Williamite war.

07-12.title: Lincoln signs the act creating the Army Medal of Honor
07-12.description: President Lincoln signed a resolution authorising the Medal of Honor for army soldiers who distinguished themselves by gallantry. It remains the highest US military decoration.

07-12.title: Soviet and German tanks clash at Prokhorovka
07-12.description: Soviet tank armies counter-attacked the SS Panzer Corps at Prokhorovka, one of the largest tank battles in history. The Soviets lost heavily, but the German offensive at Kursk was halted.

07-12.title: Malala Yousafzai is born in Pakistan's Swat Valley
07-12.description: Malala Yousafzai was born in Mingora. Shot by the Taliban in 2012 for campaigning for girls' education, she survived and in 2014 became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

07-13.title: Kalbid army defeats Emperor Otto II at Stilo
07-13.description: The forces of the Kalbid emir of Sicily routed Otto II's army near Stilo in Calabria, though the emir himself was killed. Otto barely escaped by swimming to a ship, and his plans to conquer southern Italy collapsed.

07-13.title: William the Lion of Scotland is captured at Alnwick
07-13.description: English knights surprised King William I of Scotland in fog outside Alnwick and took him prisoner. To win his release he accepted the Treaty of Falaise, submitting Scotland to Henry II's overlordship.

07-13.title: Congress passes the Northwest Ordinance
07-13.description: The Confederation Congress set out how lands north-west of the Ohio River would be governed and admitted as new states. It also banned slavery there, shaping the pattern of American westward expansion.

07-13.title: Queen Victoria moves into Buckingham Palace
07-13.description: Three weeks after her accession, 18-year-old Victoria became the first monarch to live at Buckingham Palace. It has been the sovereign's principal London residence ever since.

07-13.title: The Treaty of Berlin redraws the map of the Balkans
07-13.description: The Congress of Berlin recognised the independence of Serbia, Montenegro and Romania and cut back the large Bulgaria created by Russia. Its compromises left grievances that fed later Balkan wars.

07-13.title: The Hollywoodland sign is dedicated in Los Angeles
07-13.description: A giant sign reading 'Hollywoodland' was unveiled in the hills above Los Angeles to advertise a housing development. Shortened to 'Hollywood' in 1949, it became a global symbol of the film industry.

07-14.title: Louis VIII becomes King of France on Philip Augustus's death
07-14.description: Philip II died at Mantes and his son Louis VIII succeeded him. In a reign of just three years Louis took Poitou from the English and led a royal crusade against the Cathars of the south.

07-14.title: Parisians storm the Bastille
07-14.description: Crowds seeking gunpowder stormed the Bastille fortress, which held just seven prisoners. Its fall became the symbol of the French Revolution, and 14 July is France's national day.

07-14.title: John Adams signs the Sedition Act
07-14.description: The Sedition Act made it a crime to publish 'false, scandalous and malicious' writing against the US government. It was used to prosecute Republican editors and helped Jefferson win the 1800 election.

07-14.title: Edward Whymper's party makes the first ascent of the Matterhorn
07-14.description: A seven-man team led by Edward Whymper reached the summit of the Matterhorn. On the descent a rope broke and four men fell to their deaths, a tragedy that shocked Victorian Britain.

07-14.title: Nazi Germany becomes a one-party state
07-14.description: The Law against the Formation of New Parties declared the Nazi Party the only legal party in Germany. Less than six months after Hitler became chancellor, organised political opposition had been outlawed.

07-14.title: Iraqi army officers overthrow the Hashemite monarchy
07-14.description: Officers led by Brigadier Abd al-Karim Qasim seized Baghdad and killed King Faisal II and members of the royal family. The coup ended the British-backed monarchy and made Iraq a republic.

07-15.title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
07-15.description: Crusaders broke into Jerusalem and slaughtered many of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants. The capture fulfilled the First Crusade's goal and led to the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

07-15.title: Poland and Lithuania crush the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald
07-15.description: King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas destroyed the army of the Teutonic Order at Grunwald, killing its grand master. One of medieval Europe's largest battles, it broke the order's power.

07-15.title: Napoleon surrenders aboard HMS Bellerophon
07-15.description: Unable to escape to America, Napoleon gave himself up to Captain Frederick Maitland of HMS Bellerophon off Rochefort. The British exiled him to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

07-15.title: William Boeing founds his aircraft company in Seattle
07-15.description: Timber merchant William Boeing incorporated the Pacific Aero Products Company, renamed Boeing Airplane Company the next year. It grew into a leading aerospace maker, builder of the 707 and 747.

07-15.title: Gianni Versace is shot dead outside his Miami Beach home
07-15.description: Fashion designer Gianni Versace was murdered on the steps of his villa by Andrew Cunanan, who had already killed four men. Cunanan killed himself eight days later as police closed in.

07-16.title: The Islamic calendar begins its first year
07-16.description: The first day of the year of the Hijra, 1 Muharram AH 1, corresponds to 16 July 622. Caliph Umar later chose the year of Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina as the starting point of the Islamic era.

07-16.title: Christian kings defeat the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa
07-16.description: The kings of Castile, Aragon and Navarre routed the Almohad caliph's army in the Sierra Morena. The battle broke Almohad power in Iberia and opened Andalusia to Christian conquest.

07-16.title: Stockholms Banco issues Europe's first banknotes
07-16.description: Sweden's Stockholms Banco began issuing paper credit notes, the first banknotes in Europe. The bank over-issued and collapsed within a few years, but paper money was here to stay.

07-16.title: The first atomic bomb is detonated in New Mexico
07-16.description: The Trinity test at 5.29 am in the Jornada del Muerto desert proved the plutonium bomb worked. Oppenheimer later recalled the Bhagavad Gita: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'

07-16.title: Apollo 11 launches for the Moon
07-16.description: A Saturn V rocket lifted Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins from Kennedy Space Center. Four days later Armstrong and Aldrin became the first people to land on the Moon.

07-16.title: Fragments of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 begin hitting Jupiter
07-16.description: Over six days some 21 fragments of the comet slammed into Jupiter, the first collision between solar system bodies ever observed. They left dark scars in the atmosphere larger than Earth.

07-17.title: French artillery wins the Battle of Castillon
07-17.description: French cannon cut down an English army under John Talbot at Castillon in Gascony. It was the last battle of the Hundred Years' War, leaving Calais as England's only possession in France.

07-17.title: Deposed Tsar Peter III dies in captivity
07-17.description: Days after his wife Catherine seized the throne in a coup, Peter III died at Ropsha, almost certainly murdered by her supporters. Catherine the Great went on to rule Russia for 34 years.

07-17.title: Bolsheviks execute the Romanov family in Yekaterinburg
07-17.description: In the early hours, Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and four retainers were shot in the cellar of the Ipatiev House. Their remains were found decades later; the Orthodox Church canonised the family in 2000.

07-17.title: The Potsdam Conference opens
07-17.description: Truman, Stalin and Churchill, later replaced by Attlee, met at Cecilienhof near Berlin. They settled the occupation of Germany and issued the Potsdam Declaration demanding Japan's unconditional surrender.

07-17.title: American and Soviet spacecraft dock in orbit
07-17.description: An Apollo capsule docked with Soyuz 19, and Thomas Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the hatch. The first international crewed space mission was a landmark of Cold War détente.

07-17.title: TWA Flight 800 explodes off Long Island
07-17.description: A Boeing 747 bound for Paris exploded minutes after take-off from New York, killing all 230 on board. Investigators concluded that a spark had ignited fuel vapour in the centre wing tank.

07-18.title: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out
07-18.description: Fire broke out near the Circus Maximus and raged for days, gutting ten of Rome's fourteen districts. Rumour blamed Nero; Tacitus records that he blamed the Christians, beginning their first persecution.

07-18.title: Edward I orders the expulsion of the Jews from England
07-18.description: Edward I issued the Edict of Expulsion, ordering all Jews to leave England by 1 November. Several thousand were forced out, and Jews were not readmitted until the Cromwellian era of the 1650s.

07-18.title: The 54th Massachusetts leads the assault on Fort Wagner
07-18.description: The 54th Massachusetts, one of the first Black regiments in the Union army, led a night attack on Fort Wagner near Charleston. The assault failed with heavy losses, but the regiment's courage changed Northern opinion.

07-18.title: The First Vatican Council defines papal infallibility
07-18.description: The council adopted Pastor aeternus, declaring the Pope free from error when he defines doctrine on faith or morals ex cathedra. The decree strengthened papal authority and caused a schism with the Old Catholics.

07-18.title: The first volume of Hitler's Mein Kampf is published
07-18.description: Hitler's autobiography and manifesto, written partly in prison, set out his antisemitism and his aim of conquering 'living space' in the east. Its ideas foreshadowed the policies of the Third Reich.

07-18.title: Military uprising launches the Spanish Civil War
07-18.description: Following the army revolt in Morocco the day before, garrisons across Spain rose against the Republic. The war lasted nearly three years and ended in General Franco's dictatorship.

07-19.title: Tariq ibn Ziyad defeats King Roderic at Guadalete
07-19.description: Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated and killed the Visigothic king Roderic, by the traditional date. Within a few years most of Iberia was under Muslim rule, the beginning of al-Andalus.

07-19.title: Mary Tudor is proclaimed Queen of England in London
07-19.description: As support for Lady Jane Grey collapsed, the Privy Council proclaimed Mary queen to cheering crowds. England's first undisputed queen regnant restored Catholicism and burned some 280 Protestants.

07-19.title: The Seneca Falls Convention opens
07-19.description: Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott opened the first women's rights convention in the United States. Its Declaration of Sentiments, stating that 'all men and women are created equal', launched the suffrage movement.

07-19.title: France declares war on Prussia
07-19.description: Provoked by Bismarck's edited Ems Dispatch, Napoleon III's government declared war on Prussia. Within months France was defeated, the Second Empire fell and the German Empire was proclaimed at Versailles.

07-19.title: Sandinista rebels take power in Nicaragua
07-19.description: Two days after Anastasio Somoza Debayle fled, Sandinista forces entered Managua, ending the Somoza family's 43-year rule. The revolution soon drew the US into backing the Contra insurgency.

07-20.title: Bogotá rises against Spanish rule
07-20.description: A quarrel over a borrowed flower vase sparked an uprising in Bogotá that created a governing junta. Colombia celebrates 20 July as its Independence Day; full independence came after Bolívar's victory in 1819.

07-20.title: Austria defeats Italy at Lissa, the first great ironclad battle
07-20.description: Admiral Tegetthoff's Austrian fleet defeated a larger Italian force off the island of Lissa in the Adriatic. The ramming of the Italian flagship convinced navies to fit rams to warships for decades.

07-20.title: Stauffenberg's bomb fails to kill Hitler
07-20.description: Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg left a briefcase bomb at Hitler's Wolf's Lair headquarters, but Hitler survived. The plotters were executed and thousands more were arrested in the reprisals that followed.

07-20.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
07-20.description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquillity. Hours later, at 10.56 pm US Eastern time, Armstrong stepped onto the surface, watched by some 600 million people.

07-20.title: Viking 1 makes the first successful landing on Mars
07-20.description: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down on Chryse Planitia and sent back the first photographs from the Martian surface. It operated for more than six years.

07-21.title: Alexander the Great is born in Pella
07-21.description: Alexander, son of Philip II of Macedon, was born by the traditional dating around 20 or 21 July. By his death at 32 he had conquered an empire stretching from Greece and Egypt to north-west India.

07-21.title: English ships first engage the Spanish Armada off Plymouth
07-21.description: The English fleet under Lord Howard and Drake attacked the Armada off Plymouth (21 July Old Style). The running fight up the Channel ended at Gravelines and in the Armada's disastrous voyage home.

07-21.title: Pope Clement XIV suppresses the Jesuits
07-21.description: Under pressure from the Catholic monarchies of France, Spain and Portugal, Clement XIV dissolved the Society of Jesus. The order survived in Russia and was restored worldwide in 1814.

07-21.title: Napoleon defeats the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids
07-21.description: French infantry squares broke the charges of the Mamluk cavalry near Cairo. The victory gave Napoleon control of Egypt, where his expedition's scholars laid the foundations of modern Egyptology.

07-21.title: John Scopes is found guilty of teaching evolution
07-21.description: A Dayton jury convicted teacher John Scopes of breaking Tennessee's ban on teaching human evolution, and he was fined 100 dollars. The verdict was later overturned on a technicality.

07-21.title: Armstrong and Aldrin lift off from the Moon
07-21.description: After about 21 hours on the lunar surface, Armstrong and Aldrin fired the ascent stage of Eagle to rejoin Michael Collins in lunar orbit. They left a plaque reading 'We came in peace for all mankind'.

07-22.title: Crusaders sack Béziers and massacre its people
07-22.description: The army of the Albigensian Crusade stormed Béziers and killed much of its population. A chronicler later attributed to the papal legate the words 'Kill them all; God will know his own'.

07-22.title: Edward I defeats William Wallace at Falkirk
07-22.description: English longbowmen broke the Scottish spear formations at Falkirk, ending Wallace's career as a field commander. He was captured and executed in 1305.

07-22.title: John White's colonists arrive at Roanoke Island
07-22.description: More than 100 English settlers led by John White landed at Roanoke, intending to found the 'City of Ralegh'. When White returned in 1590 they had vanished, becoming the 'Lost Colony'.

07-22.title: Hood attacks Sherman in the Battle of Atlanta
07-22.description: Confederate General John Bell Hood struck Sherman's armies east of Atlanta, killing Union General James McPherson. The attack failed, and Atlanta's fall in September boosted Lincoln's re-election.

07-22.title: Wiley Post completes the first solo flight around the world
07-22.description: Wiley Post landed at Floyd Bennett Field, New York, after circling the globe alone in 7 days, 18 hours and 49 minutes. An autopilot and radio direction-finder made the feat possible.

07-23.title: Riot greets Charles I's new prayer book in Edinburgh
07-23.description: Worshippers in St Giles' Cathedral protested violently when the new Scottish Book of Common Prayer was first read. The resistance led to the National Covenant, the Bishops' Wars and the British civil wars.

07-23.title: Bonnie Prince Charlie lands on Eriskay
07-23.description: Charles Edward Stuart landed on the Hebridean island of Eriskay to reclaim the throne for his father. The Jacobite rising he launched ended in defeat at Culloden in April 1746.

07-23.title: William Austin Burt patents his 'typographer'
07-23.description: Michigan surveyor William Austin Burt received a US patent for the typographer, a hand-operated printing machine. Slow and never sold commercially, it is often called the first American typewriter.

07-23.title: Egypt's Free Officers overthrow King Farouk
07-23.description: Army officers led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser seized power in a bloodless coup, forcing King Farouk to abdicate days later. Egypt became a republic in 1953.

07-23.title: Greece's military junta collapses after the Cyprus crisis
07-23.description: Discredited by its coup in Cyprus and the Turkish invasion that followed, the Greek junta handed power to civilians. Konstantinos Karamanlis returned from exile the next day to restore democracy.

07-24.title: Jacques Cartier plants a cross at Gaspé and claims it for France
07-24.description: Jacques Cartier raised a nine-metre wooden cross at Gaspé Bay bearing the arms of the King of France. The gesture began French claims to the St Lawrence region that became New France.

07-24.title: Mary, Queen of Scots is forced to abdicate
07-24.description: Imprisoned at Lochleven, Mary was compelled to abdicate in favour of her one-year-old son, crowned James VI five days later. She fled to England in 1568 and was executed in 1587.

07-24.title: Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founds Detroit
07-24.description: French officer Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac established Fort Pontchartrain du Détroit on the strait between Lakes Erie and Huron. The trading post grew into Detroit, later the heart of the US car industry.

07-24.title: Brigham Young's Mormon pioneers enter the Salt Lake Valley
07-24.description: After a long trek from Illinois, Brigham Young's vanguard company entered the Great Salt Lake Valley; he reportedly declared 'This is the right place'. Salt Lake City became the centre of the Latter-day Saints.

07-24.title: Hiram Bingham reaches the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu
07-24.description: Guided by local farmer Melchor Arteaga, Yale lecturer Hiram Bingham climbed to Machu Picchu, already known to local families. His photographs made the Inca site world-famous.

07-24.title: Supreme Court orders Nixon to hand over the Watergate tapes
07-24.description: In United States v. Nixon the Supreme Court ruled 8-0 that the president must surrender the tapes. Their contents destroyed his remaining support, and he resigned 16 days later.

07-25.title: Afonso Henriques wins the Battle of Ourique
07-25.description: Afonso Henriques defeated an Almoravid army at Ourique and was soon styling himself King of Portugal. The victory became a founding legend of Portuguese independence from León.

07-25.title: Henry IV of France converts to Catholicism
07-25.description: The Protestant Henry IV abjured his faith at the basilica of Saint-Denis to win acceptance from Catholic France. The words 'Paris is well worth a Mass' are attributed to him, and he entered Paris the next year.

07-25.title: Cooke and Wheatstone demonstrate the electric telegraph
07-25.description: William Cooke and Charles Wheatstone sent messages along a telegraph line between Euston and Camden Town in London. Its success led to the first commercial telegraph on the Great Western Railway.

07-25.title: Louise Brown, the first 'test-tube baby', is born
07-25.description: Louise Brown was born in Oldham, the first person conceived by in vitro fertilisation, pioneered by Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe. Millions of people have since been born through IVF.

07-25.title: Svetlana Savitskaya becomes the first woman to walk in space
07-25.description: Soviet cosmonaut Svetlana Savitskaya spent three and a half hours outside the Salyut 7 space station. She tested a hand-held tool for cutting and welding metal in space.

07-26.title: Dutch provinces renounce Philip II in the Act of Abjuration
07-26.description: The States General of the rebel provinces declared that Philip II had forfeited his rule by tyranny. The Act of Abjuration was in effect a declaration of independence for what became the Dutch Republic.

07-26.title: First recorded women's cricket match is played in Surrey
07-26.description: Eleven women of Bramley played eleven of Hambledon on Gosden Common near Guildford, reported in the Reading Mercury. It is the earliest recorded women's cricket match.

07-26.title: Liberia declares independence
07-26.description: Liberia, founded by the American Colonization Society as a home for freed Black Americans, declared itself an independent republic. It became Africa's oldest modern republic, though settler rule marginalised indigenous peoples.

07-26.title: The Bureau of Investigation, forerunner of the FBI, is created
07-26.description: Attorney General Charles Bonaparte set up a force of special agents in the US Justice Department. Renamed the FBI in 1935, it grew under J. Edgar Hoover into America's main federal police agency.

07-26.title: Fidel Castro leads the attack on the Moncada Barracks
07-26.description: Fidel Castro led some 160 rebels against the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba. The attack failed, but his trial speech 'History Will Absolve Me' made him a national figure, and 26 July named his movement.

07-26.title: Nasser nationalises the Suez Canal
07-26.description: Egypt's President Nasser announced the nationalisation of the Suez Canal Company to fund the Aswan Dam. Britain, France and Israel invaded in October, but US pressure forced a humiliating withdrawal.

07-27.title: Philip II of France wins the Battle of Bouvines
07-27.description: Philip Augustus defeated Emperor Otto IV and his allies, backed by King John of England, at Bouvines. The defeat wrecked John's hopes of recovering Normandy and weakened him before Magna Carta.

07-27.title: The Bank of England receives its royal charter
07-27.description: The Bank of England was founded to lend 1.2 million pounds to William III's government for war with France. It became the model for central banks around the world.

07-27.title: Armistice ends the fighting in the Korean War
07-27.description: The armistice signed at Panmunjom halted three years of war that had cost millions of lives. It created a demilitarised zone roughly along the 38th parallel, but no peace treaty has ever been signed.

07-27.title: Bomb explodes in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park
07-27.description: A pipe bomb exploded during a concert at the Atlanta Olympics, killing one woman and injuring 111. Security guard Richard Jewell was wrongly suspected; Eric Rudolph later confessed.

07-27.title: Danny Boyle's ceremony opens the London Olympics
07-27.description: The London 2012 Olympics opened with 'Isles of Wonder', a ceremony tracing Britain from rural idyll through the Industrial Revolution to the NHS and pop culture. It was watched by hundreds of millions.

07-28.title: Thomas Cromwell is beheaded on Tower Hill
07-28.description: Henry VIII's chief minister, architect of the break with Rome and the Dissolution of the Monasteries, was executed for treason and heresy. His fall followed the king's disastrous marriage to Anne of Cleves.

07-28.title: Johann Sebastian Bach dies in Leipzig
07-28.description: Bach died aged 65 after failed eye operations. Little valued by his immediate successors, his music was revived in the nineteenth century, and he is now ranked among the greatest composers.

07-28.title: The 14th Amendment is certified as part of the US Constitution
07-28.description: Secretary of State William Seward certified the 14th Amendment, guaranteeing citizenship and equal protection of the laws. It became the basis for many landmark civil rights rulings.

07-28.title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
07-28.description: One month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. Within a week Russia, Germany, France and Britain were drawn in, and the First World War had begun.

07-28.title: US troops drive the Bonus Army out of Washington
07-28.description: On Hoover's orders, troops under Douglas MacArthur used tear gas and bayonets to clear camps of First World War veterans demanding early payment of bonuses. The scenes damaged Hoover's re-election hopes.

07-29.title: The English fleet defeats the Spanish Armada at Gravelines
07-29.description: Scattered by fire-ships the night before, the Armada was attacked at close range off Gravelines (29 July Old Style). Driven north by wind, its ships fled around Scotland and Ireland, where many were wrecked.

07-29.title: The Arc de Triomphe is inaugurated in Paris
07-29.description: Commissioned by Napoleon in 1806 to honour his armies, the Arc de Triomphe was finally inaugurated under King Louis-Philippe. Since 1921 it has sheltered France's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

07-29.title: King Umberto I of Italy is assassinated at Monza
07-29.description: The anarchist Gaetano Bresci shot Umberto I to avenge the killing of protesters in Milan in 1898. It was one of a wave of anarchist assassinations that also claimed US President McKinley in 1901.

07-29.title: Eisenhower signs the act creating NASA
07-29.description: Spurred by Sputnik, President Eisenhower signed the National Aeronautics and Space Act, creating a civilian space agency. NASA opened that October and within 11 years landed astronauts on the Moon.

07-29.title: Prince Charles marries Lady Diana Spencer
07-29.description: The Prince of Wales married Lady Diana Spencer at St Paul's Cathedral before a global television audience estimated at 750 million. The couple separated in 1992 and divorced in 1996.

07-30.title: Caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad
07-30.description: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur laid the foundations of his Round City on the Tigris, naming it Madinat al-Salam, the City of Peace. Baghdad became a great centre of learning and trade.

07-30.title: Virginia's General Assembly meets for the first time
07-30.description: Elected burgesses met with the governor and council in the church at Jamestown. It was the first representative legislature in English America, the root of later colonial assemblies.

07-30.title: Baltimore is founded in Maryland
07-30.description: The Maryland legislature authorised a new town on the Patapsco River. Baltimore grew into a major Atlantic port; its defence in 1814 inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

07-30.title: German saboteurs blow up the Black Tom munitions depot
07-30.description: German agents set off explosions at the Black Tom depot in New York Harbor, destroying munitions bound for the Allies. The blast shattered windows across Manhattan and damaged the Statue of Liberty.

07-30.title: Lyndon Johnson signs Medicare and Medicaid into law
07-30.description: Johnson signed the Social Security Amendments in Independence, Missouri, with Harry Truman beside him. Medicare and Medicaid brought health insurance to millions of older and poorer Americans.

07-31.title: Deadline passes for Jews to leave Spain under the Alhambra Decree
07-31.description: The last day allowed by Ferdinand and Isabella's expulsion edict passed, and Spain's Jewish communities left or converted. Tens of thousands went into exile, founding the Sephardic diaspora.

07-31.title: Ignatius of Loyola dies in Rome
07-31.description: Ignatius of Loyola, the Basque soldier turned founder of the Society of Jesus, died in Rome. His Spiritual Exercises and the Jesuits' schools and missions reshaped Catholicism worldwide.

07-31.title: Daniel Defoe stands in the pillory for seditious libel
07-31.description: Daniel Defoe began three days in the pillory for a satirical pamphlet mocking Tory hostility to Dissenters. By tradition the crowd threw flowers instead of filth. He later wrote Robinson Crusoe.

07-31.title: The first US patent is issued to Samuel Hopkins
07-31.description: Samuel Hopkins received the first patent under the new US Patent Act, for an improved way of making potash. It was signed by George Washington and Thomas Jefferson.

07-31.title: The Battle of Passchendaele begins
07-31.description: British and French forces opened the Third Battle of Ypres in Flanders. Heavy rain turned the battlefield into a swamp, and months of fighting won a few miles for hundreds of thousands of casualties.

07-31.title: Apollo 15 astronauts drive the first rover on the Moon
07-31.description: David Scott and James Irwin took the battery-powered Lunar Roving Vehicle on its first drive near Hadley Rille. The rover let astronauts range much farther from their lander to collect samples.

08-01.title: Octavian takes Alexandria and Mark Antony takes his own life
08-01.description: Octavian's army entered Alexandria and Mark Antony, defeated and deserted, killed himself. Cleopatra's suicide days later ended the Ptolemaic dynasty and Egypt became a Roman province.

08-01.title: Swiss cantons swear the alliance celebrated as Switzerland's birth
08-01.description: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden concluded a perpetual defensive alliance, recorded in the Federal Charter dated early August 1291. 1 August is now Swiss National Day.

08-01.title: Queen Anne dies, ending the Stuart line
08-01.description: Queen Anne died without surviving children, the last Stuart monarch. Under the Act of Settlement the crown passed to George, Elector of Hanover, beginning the Hanoverian dynasty.

08-01.title: Joseph Priestley isolates oxygen
08-01.description: By heating mercuric oxide, Joseph Priestley produced a gas in which a candle burned with remarkable vigour. He called it 'dephlogisticated air'; Lavoisier later named it oxygen.

08-01.title: France's Convention adopts the metric system
08-01.description: The National Convention decreed a provisional metre, based on a fraction of the Earth's meridian, as France's unit of length. The decimal metric system has since been adopted almost worldwide.

08-01.title: Germany declares war on Russia
08-01.description: After Russia refused to halt mobilisation, Germany declared war on it. The declaration turned the Austro-Serbian conflict into a general European war within days.

08-01.title: The Warsaw Uprising begins
08-01.description: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers of Warsaw. After 63 days, with the Red Army halted across the Vistula, the uprising was crushed and the city systematically destroyed.

08-02.title: Hannibal annihilates a Roman army at Cannae
08-02.description: Hannibal's Carthaginians encircled and destroyed a much larger Roman army in southern Italy, killing perhaps 50,000 men. Cannae remains the classic model of a battle of encirclement.

08-02.title: Delegates sign the engrossed Declaration of Independence
08-02.description: Most members of the Continental Congress signed the parchment copy of the Declaration in Philadelphia. By signing, they put their names to an act of treason in British eyes.

08-02.title: The Tower Subway opens beneath the Thames
08-02.description: A cable-hauled railway carriage began carrying passengers through the Tower Subway in London. Bored with a tunnelling shield, it was the world's first tube railway, though it closed within months.

08-02.title: President Warren Harding dies in San Francisco
08-02.description: Warren Harding died suddenly during a western tour, and Vice President Calvin Coolidge was sworn in by his father by lamplight in Vermont. The Teapot Dome scandal soon tarnished Harding's memory.

08-02.title: Hitler becomes Führer on Hindenburg's death
08-02.description: President Paul von Hindenburg died, and a law passed the day before merged the presidency with the chancellorship. Hitler became head of state and the army swore an oath of loyalty to him personally.

08-02.title: Iraq invades Kuwait
08-02.description: Saddam Hussein's forces overran Kuwait in a matter of hours. A US-led coalition expelled them in early 1991, though Saddam remained in power.

08-03.title: Tiberius defeats the Pannonian rebels at the River Bathinus
08-03.description: Roman forces under Tiberius defeated the rebel Breuci at the River Bathinus, and their leader Bato surrendered. It was a turning point in the great Illyrian revolt against Roman rule.

08-03.title: Columbus sets sail from Palos on his first voyage
08-03.description: Christopher Columbus left Palos de la Frontera with the Niña, Pinta and Santa María, seeking a westward route to Asia. Ten weeks later he reached the Bahamas.

08-03.title: La Scala opera house opens in Milan
08-03.description: The Teatro alla Scala opened with Salieri's opera L'Europa riconosciuta. It became one of the world's leading opera houses, closely linked with Verdi, Puccini and Toscanini.

08-03.title: Germany declares war on France
08-03.description: Germany declared war on France and prepared to strike through neutral Belgium under the Schlieffen Plan. The invasion of Belgium the next day brought Britain into the war.

08-03.title: Jesse Owens wins the 100 metres at the Berlin Olympics
08-03.description: Jesse Owens won the 100 metres, the first of four gold medals at the Berlin Games. The success of a Black American athlete undercut Nazi propaganda about racial superiority.

08-03.title: US air traffic controllers go on strike
08-03.description: Nearly 13,000 members of the PATCO union walked out. President Reagan gave them 48 hours to return; he then fired more than 11,000, a defining moment for American labour relations.

08-04.title: Simon de Montfort is killed at the Battle of Evesham
08-04.description: The future Edward I defeated and killed Simon de Montfort at Evesham, ending the barons' rebellion against Henry III. Montfort's parliaments with elected burgesses outlived him.

08-04.title: Anglo-Dutch forces capture Gibraltar
08-04.description: A fleet under Admiral Sir George Rooke took Gibraltar during the War of the Spanish Succession. Ceded to Britain in 1713, it remains a British territory despite repeated Spanish claims.

08-04.title: France's National Assembly abolishes feudal privileges
08-04.description: In a night session, nobles and clergy renounced their seigneurial rights, tithes and exemptions one after another. The decrees swept away much of the legal framework of the Ancien Régime.

08-04.title: Britain declares war on Germany
08-04.description: When Germany ignored an ultimatum to respect Belgian neutrality, Britain declared war at 11 pm London time. The British Empire's entry turned a continental war into a global one.

08-04.title: Anne Frank and her family are arrested in Amsterdam
08-04.description: German police raided the secret annexe at Prinsengracht 263, arresting the Frank family and four others. Anne died in Bergen-Belsen in early 1945; her diary became a classic of Holocaust testimony.

08-04.title: US destroyers report a second attack in the Gulf of Tonkin
08-04.description: US warships reported an attack by North Vietnamese boats that probably never happened. Within days Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, authorising Johnson to escalate the Vietnam War.

08-05.title: Henry I is crowned King of England
08-05.description: Three days after William Rufus died in a hunting accident, his brother Henry was crowned at Westminster. His Charter of Liberties and administrative reforms made him one of England's ablest medieval kings.

08-05.title: Sir Humphrey Gilbert claims Newfoundland for England
08-05.description: At St John's harbour, Humphrey Gilbert claimed Newfoundland for Elizabeth I, an early step in English overseas expansion. No settlement followed, and Gilbert was lost at sea on the voyage home.

08-05.title: The first transatlantic telegraph cable is completed
08-05.description: Cable ships landed the ends of the first telegraph line across the Atlantic in Ireland and Newfoundland. It carried messages for just three weeks before failing, but proved the idea possible.

08-05.title: Cornerstone laid for the Statue of Liberty's pedestal
08-05.description: The cornerstone of the pedestal was laid on Bedloe's Island in New York Harbor. Americans had to raise the funds for the base, while France paid for the statue itself.

08-05.title: An electric traffic signal is installed in Cleveland
08-05.description: An electric traffic signal with red and green lights was installed at Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street in Cleveland, Ohio. It is often cited as the first of its kind in the world.

08-05.title: Marilyn Monroe is found dead in Los Angeles
08-05.description: Marilyn Monroe was found dead at her home in Brentwood, aged 36; the coroner ruled probable suicide from barbiturates. Her death cut short the career of Hollywood's most famous star.

08-06.title: Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet at Meloria
08-06.description: The Genoese navy crushed Pisa's fleet off the islet of Meloria, capturing thousands of prisoners. Pisa never recovered as a sea power, leaving Genoa dominant in the western Mediterranean.

08-06.title: Francis II dissolves the Holy Roman Empire
08-06.description: Under pressure from Napoleon, Francis II laid down the imperial crown and dissolved the Holy Roman Empire. A political order dating back to Charlemagne's coronation in 800 came to an end.

08-06.title: Bolivia declares independence
08-06.description: An assembly in Chuquisaca proclaimed the independence of Upper Peru, naming the new republic after Simón Bolívar. Antonio José de Sucre became its first president.

08-06.title: William Kemmler is the first person executed by electric chair
08-06.description: Convicted murderer William Kemmler was executed at Auburn Prison, New York. The botched execution took two shocks, and came amid the 'war of the currents' between Edison and Westinghouse.

08-06.title: US bomber drops the atomic bomb on Hiroshima
08-06.description: The B-29 Enola Gay dropped a uranium bomb on Hiroshima, the first nuclear weapon used in war. Some 70,000 people died at once and perhaps 140,000 by the end of 1945.

08-06.title: Tim Berners-Lee makes the World Wide Web public
08-06.description: Tim Berners-Lee posted a summary of his World Wide Web project to an internet newsgroup, inviting outside collaboration. The web, created at CERN, spread rapidly and transformed communication.

08-07.title: Western Emperor Majorian is executed on Ricimer's orders
08-07.description: Majorian, the last Western emperor to attempt a real recovery of the empire, was arrested and beheaded by his general Ricimer. Afterwards Ricimer ruled through puppet emperors.

08-07.title: George Washington creates the Badge of Military Merit
08-07.description: Washington established a purple cloth heart to honour enlisted soldiers for meritorious action. Revived in 1932 as the Purple Heart, it is now awarded to those wounded or killed in US service.

08-07.title: Simón Bolívar wins the Battle of Boyacá
08-07.description: After a daring march over the Andes, Bolívar's army defeated the royalists at Boyacá. Bogotá fell days later, securing the independence of New Granada, present-day Colombia.

08-07.title: US Marines land on Guadalcanal
08-07.description: US Marines landed on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands, the first major American offensive of the Pacific war. Six months of fighting ended in a Japanese withdrawal.

08-07.title: Thor Heyerdahl's Kon-Tiki raft reaches Polynesia
08-07.description: After 101 days and some 7,000 km from Peru, Thor Heyerdahl's balsa raft ran onto the reef at Raroia. The voyage showed that prehistoric people could have crossed the Pacific on such craft.

08-07.title: Al-Qaeda bombs US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
08-07.description: Truck bombs exploded almost simultaneously at the US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, killing 224 people, most of them Africans. The attacks brought Osama bin Laden to world attention.

08-08.title: Treaty of Meerssen partitions Lotharingia
08-08.description: Charles the Bald and Louis the German divided the lands of their late nephew Lothair II between West and East Francia. The partition helped shape the later frontier between France and Germany.

08-08.title: Foundation stone is laid for Tycho Brahe's Uraniborg
08-08.description: Work began on Tycho Brahe's observatory on the island of Hven, granted to him by Frederick II of Denmark. Its precise naked-eye observations later allowed Kepler to derive his laws of planetary motion.

08-08.title: Allied attack at Amiens breaks the German line
08-08.description: British, Australian, Canadian and French troops, with hundreds of tanks, broke through near Amiens. Ludendorff called it the 'black day of the German army'; the Hundred Days Offensive had begun.

08-08.title: The Soviet Union declares war on Japan
08-08.description: Moscow declared war on Japan and, within hours, launched a massive invasion of Manchuria. Coming between the atomic bombings, it helped persuade Japan's leaders to surrender.

08-08.title: Richard Nixon announces his resignation
08-08.description: In a televised address, Richard Nixon said he would resign the presidency at noon the next day. Released tapes had proved his role in the Watergate cover-up, leaving him facing certain impeachment.

08-09.title: Caesar defeats Pompey at Pharsalus
08-09.description: Julius Caesar's veterans routed Pompey's larger army in Thessaly. Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered, and Caesar became master of the Roman world.

08-09.title: Goths destroy a Roman army and kill Emperor Valens at Adrianople
08-09.description: Gothic cavalry and infantry overwhelmed the Eastern Roman army near Adrianople in Thrace, killing Emperor Valens and much of his force. Rome was never again able to expel the Goths from its territory.

08-09.title: Construction begins on the bell tower of Pisa
08-09.description: Work started on the campanile of Pisa Cathedral. Soft ground made it lean by the time the third storey was built, and it became famous as the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

08-09.title: US bomber drops an atomic bomb on Nagasaki
08-09.description: The plutonium bomb Fat Man exploded over Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people at once and many more later. Six days later Japan announced its surrender.

08-09.title: Manson Family members murder Sharon Tate and four others
08-09.description: Followers of Charles Manson killed actress Sharon Tate, who was heavily pregnant, and four others at her Los Angeles home. The murders horrified America and Manson became a byword for evil.

08-09.title: Gerald Ford becomes president after Nixon resigns
08-09.description: Gerald Ford was sworn in as the 38th president, telling Americans 'our long national nightmare is over'. His pardon of Nixon a month later probably cost him the 1976 election.

08-10.title: The Swedish warship Vasa sinks on her maiden voyage
08-10.description: Top-heavy and unstable, the warship Vasa heeled over in a gust and sank in Stockholm harbour less than a mile into her first voyage. Raised in 1961, she is now a celebrated museum ship.

08-10.title: Insurgents storm the Tuileries Palace in Paris
08-10.description: Armed Parisians and provincial volunteers attacked the Tuileries, killing hundreds of the Swiss Guards. Louis XVI was suspended and imprisoned, and the French monarchy fell weeks later.

08-10.title: The Louvre opens as a public museum
08-10.description: The revolutionary government opened the Muséum central des arts in the former royal palace, on the first anniversary of the monarchy's fall. The Louvre became one of the world's greatest museums.

08-10.title: Quito's patriots depose the Spanish authorities
08-10.description: Criollo leaders in Quito overthrew the royal president and formed a governing junta, one of the first such moves in Spanish South America. It was crushed, but Ecuador won independence in 1822.

08-10.title: Congress establishes the Smithsonian Institution
08-10.description: President Polk signed the act creating the Smithsonian, funded by the bequest of British chemist James Smithson. It grew into the world's largest museum, education and research complex.

08-10.title: Japan offers to surrender if the Emperor is preserved
08-10.description: After an imperial intervention, Japan told the Allies it would accept the Potsdam terms provided the Emperor's prerogatives were kept. The US reply left his status to the Allied commander and the Japanese people.

08-11.title: Hadrian is proclaimed Roman Emperor
08-11.description: Days after Trajan's death in Cilicia, the army in Syria hailed Hadrian as emperor. He abandoned Trajan's eastern conquests and consolidated the frontiers, building Hadrian's Wall in Britain.

08-11.title: Rodrigo Borgia is elected Pope Alexander VI
08-11.description: The Spanish cardinal Rodrigo Borgia was elected pope, amid accusations of bribery. His reign became notorious for nepotism and for advancing his children, among them Cesare and Lucrezia Borgia.

08-11.title: President Ebert signs the Weimar Constitution
08-11.description: Friedrich Ebert signed the constitution of the new German republic, with universal suffrage and a strong president. Its emergency powers were later exploited in Hitler's rise to power.

08-11.title: Chad becomes independent from France
08-11.description: Chad gained independence, with François Tombalbaye as its first president. It was one of 17 African countries to win independence in 1960, the 'Year of Africa'.

08-11.title: The Watts riots erupt in Los Angeles
08-11.description: A traffic stop in the Watts district sparked six days of unrest in which 34 people died. The riots exposed deep anger over poverty and policing in America's segregated cities.

08-12.title: Crusaders defeat a Fatimid army at Ascalon
08-12.description: A month after taking Jerusalem, the crusaders surprised and routed an Egyptian relief army near Ascalon. The victory, the last battle of the First Crusade, secured the new Latin kingdom.

08-12.title: Frederick the Great is crushed at Kunersdorf
08-12.description: A Russian and Austrian army destroyed Frederick II's Prussian force near Frankfurt an der Oder. Frederick wrote that all was lost, but his enemies failed to follow up and Prussia survived.

08-12.title: Isaac Singer patents his improved sewing machine
08-12.description: Isaac Singer received a US patent for a sewing machine with an up-and-down needle and foot treadle. Sold on instalment plans, Singer machines brought sewing machines into homes worldwide.

08-12.title: SS troops massacre villagers at Sant'Anna di Stazzema
08-12.description: Waffen-SS soldiers killed some 560 civilians, many of them women and children, in the Tuscan village of Sant'Anna di Stazzema. It was one of the worst atrocities of the German occupation of Italy.

08-12.title: IBM launches its Personal Computer
08-12.description: IBM unveiled the IBM PC model 5150, running Microsoft's MS-DOS. Its open design was widely copied, and 'PC compatible' machines came to dominate business and home computing.

08-12.title: Russian submarine Kursk sinks in the Barents Sea
08-12.description: Explosions in its torpedo compartment sent the nuclear submarine Kursk to the seabed, killing all 118 crew. Russia's slow response and refusal of early foreign help caused national anger.

08-13.title: Tenochtitlan falls to Cortés and his allies
08-13.description: After a siege of nearly three months, Spanish forces and their Tlaxcalan allies captured Cuauhtémoc and the Aztec capital. Mexico City, capital of New Spain, rose on its ruins.

08-13.title: Marlborough and Prince Eugene win the Battle of Blenheim
08-13.description: The Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy destroyed a Franco-Bavarian army at Blenheim. The victory saved Vienna and knocked Bavaria out of the War of the Spanish Succession.

08-13.title: The Netherlands cedes the Cape Colony to Britain
08-13.description: Under the Anglo-Dutch Convention of London, the Dutch formally ceded the Cape of Good Hope, which Britain had occupied since 1806. British rule shaped southern Africa for the following century.

08-13.title: US forces take Manila from Spain
08-13.description: American troops occupied Manila after a largely staged battle with the Spanish garrison, unaware that a peace protocol had been signed the day before. The US went on to annex the Philippines.

08-13.title: East Germany seals the border in Berlin
08-13.description: Overnight, East German forces closed the crossings and began building barriers that became the Berlin Wall. For 28 years it divided the city, and at least 140 people died trying to cross.

08-14.title: King Duncan I of Scotland is killed by Macbeth
08-14.description: Duncan I was killed in battle near Elgin by Macbeth, who took the throne. Macbeth ruled for 17 years, a far more capable king than the villain of Shakespeare's play written five centuries later.

08-14.title: The Mainz Psalter becomes the first dated printed book
08-14.description: Johann Fust and Peter Schöffer completed the Mainz Psalter, the first printed book to carry a date and printer's names. It also pioneered colour printing with its red and blue initials.

08-14.title: International forces relieve the besieged legations in Beijing
08-14.description: Troops of the Eight-Nation Alliance entered Beijing and lifted the 55-day siege of the foreign legations by Boxers and Qing troops. China was forced to pay a crushing indemnity.

08-14.title: Franklin Roosevelt signs the Social Security Act
08-14.description: Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act, creating old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid for dependent children. It became the cornerstone of the American welfare state.

08-14.title: Japan accepts the Allied terms of surrender
08-14.description: Japan's government notified the Allies that it accepted the Potsdam Declaration, and President Truman announced the news that evening. Emperor Hirohito recorded a broadcast to his people for the next day.

08-15.title: Basques destroy Charlemagne's rearguard at Roncevaux
08-15.description: Basque fighters ambushed Charlemagne's rearguard in the Pyrenees, killing the commander Roland. The Song of Roland later recast the skirmish as a heroic stand against Saracens.

08-15.title: Macbeth is killed at the Battle of Lumphanan
08-15.description: King Macbeth of Scotland was killed at Lumphanan in Aberdeenshire by forces of Malcolm Canmore, Duncan's son. He had ruled for 17 years and even made a pilgrimage to Rome.

08-15.title: Ignatius of Loyola and companions take vows at Montmartre
08-15.description: Ignatius and six companions vowed poverty and chastity in a chapel on Montmartre in Paris. The group became the Society of Jesus, approved by the Pope in 1540.

08-15.title: Napoleon Bonaparte is born in Corsica
08-15.description: Napoleone Buonaparte was born in Ajaccio, a year after France acquired Corsica from Genoa. He rose to become Emperor of the French and redrew the map and laws of Europe.

08-15.title: Emperor Hirohito broadcasts Japan's surrender
08-15.description: For the first time, ordinary Japanese heard their emperor's voice as he announced acceptance of the Allied terms. The day is marked as VJ Day in Britain; the formal surrender was signed on 2 September.

08-15.title: India becomes independent as British rule ends
08-15.description: At midnight India became independent, a day after Pakistan. Partition uprooted perhaps 15 million people and communal violence killed hundreds of thousands, possibly up to two million.

08-16.title: Henry VIII's army routs French cavalry at the Battle of the Spurs
08-16.description: English and imperial troops put French cavalry to flight near Guinegate, the speed of their retreat giving the battle its name. Thérouanne surrendered days later.

08-16.title: Cornwallis routs the Americans at Camden
08-16.description: British forces under Lord Cornwallis shattered Horatio Gates's army at Camden, South Carolina. The defeat led to Nathanael Greene taking command in the south.

08-16.title: Cavalry attack a reform meeting at Peterloo
08-16.description: Yeomanry and hussars charged a crowd of some 60,000 at St Peter's Field, Manchester, gathered to demand parliamentary reform. About 18 people died and hundreds were injured.

08-16.title: Gold is found on Bonanza Creek in the Klondike
08-16.description: George Carmack, Skookum Jim and Dawson Charlie struck gold on a tributary of the Klondike River in the Yukon. When news reached the south in 1897, some 100,000 people set out for the goldfields.

08-16.title: Elvis Presley dies at Graceland
08-16.description: Elvis Presley was found dead at his Memphis home, aged 42. The 'King of Rock and Roll' had sold hundreds of millions of records and transformed popular music.

08-17.title: English army defeats a Franco-Scottish force at Verneuil
08-17.description: The Duke of Bedford's army won a bloody victory over French and Scottish troops at Verneuil in Normandy. Hailed as a second Agincourt, it secured English control of northern France for years.

08-17.title: Robert Fulton's steamboat begins its voyage up the Hudson
08-17.description: Robert Fulton's North River Steamboat left New York and reached Albany in 32 hours of running. It launched the first commercially successful steamboat service, transforming river travel.

08-17.title: Bridget Driscoll becomes Britain's first pedestrian killed by a car
08-17.description: Bridget Driscoll was struck by a demonstration car in the grounds of the Crystal Palace in London. The coroner hoped such a thing would never happen again.

08-17.title: Sukarno proclaims Indonesian independence
08-17.description: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaimed independence in Jakarta. The Dutch fought to return, but transferred sovereignty in 1949.

08-17.title: Pakistan's President Zia ul-Haq dies in a plane crash
08-17.description: General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq, Pakistan's military ruler for eleven years, died when his C-130 crashed near Bahawalpur. The US ambassador also died; the cause has never been established.

08-18.title: Genghis Khan dies during his campaign against the Tangut
08-18.description: Genghis Khan died during the siege of the Western Xia, traditionally on this date. He had built the Mongol Empire, which under his heirs became the largest contiguous land empire in history.

08-18.title: Henry of Navarre marries Margaret of Valois in Paris
08-18.description: The Protestant Henry of Navarre married the Catholic princess Margaret, sister of Charles IX, a union meant to reconcile France's factions. Six days later the St Bartholomew's Day massacre began.

08-18.title: Solar eclipse observations reveal the element later named helium
08-18.description: Observing a total solar eclipse in India, Jules Janssen saw an unexplained yellow line in the Sun's spectrum. Norman Lockyer attributed it to a new element, helium, not found on Earth until 1895.

08-18.title: Tennessee ratifies the 19th Amendment, giving US women the vote
