08-18.description: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify, by one vote cast by a young legislator heeding his mother's letter. The amendment barred denial of the vote on account of sex.

08-18.title: James Meredith graduates from the University of Mississippi
08-18.description: James Meredith became the first Black graduate of Ole Miss. His enrolment in 1962 had provoked a deadly riot and required thousands of federal troops to enforce.

08-19.title: Emperor Augustus dies at Nola
08-19.description: Augustus, Rome's first emperor, died aged 75 after more than four decades in power. His stepson Tiberius succeeded him, confirming the hereditary principle of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

08-19.title: Mary, Queen of Scots returns to Scotland
08-19.description: Widowed by Francis II of France, Mary landed at Leith after 13 years in France. She returned as a Catholic queen to a kingdom that had just adopted the Protestant Reformation.

08-19.title: USS Constitution defeats HMS Guerriere
08-19.description: The American frigate Constitution dismasted and captured HMS Guerriere off Nova Scotia. Seeing shot rebound from her oak hull, sailors nicknamed her 'Old Ironsides'.

08-19.title: Coup backed by the CIA and MI6 topples Iran's Mosaddegh
08-19.description: Army units and paid crowds overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, who had nationalised Iran's oil industry. The Shah's power was restored, and resentment of foreign meddling fed the 1979 revolution.

08-19.title: Soviet hardliners launch a coup against Gorbachev
08-19.description: Communist hardliners placed Mikhail Gorbachev under house arrest in Crimea and declared a state of emergency. Boris Yeltsin led resistance in Moscow, the coup collapsed, and the USSR dissolved by December.

08-20.title: Arab armies defeat the Byzantines at the Yarmouk
08-20.description: After six days of fighting, the Muslim Arab army under Khalid ibn al-Walid destroyed the Byzantine forces near the River Yarmouk. Byzantium lost Syria and Palestine for good.

08-20.title: Richard I has 2,700 Muslim prisoners executed at Ayyadieh
08-20.description: When negotiations with Saladin over ransom and the True Cross stalled, Richard the Lionheart had the captured garrison of Acre killed outside the city. The massacre embittered the war.

08-20.title: Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture has its premiere in Moscow
08-20.description: Tchaikovsky's overture marking Russia's defeat of Napoleon was first performed in a tent near the unfinished Cathedral of Christ the Saviour. Its cannon and bells made it a perennial favourite.

08-20.title: Leon Trotsky is struck with an ice axe in Mexico City
08-20.description: Soviet agent Ramón Mercader attacked Leon Trotsky in his study in Coyoacán; Trotsky died the next day. Stalin had pursued his exiled rival for over a decade.

08-20.title: Warsaw Pact armies invade Czechoslovakia
08-20.description: Hundreds of thousands of Soviet-led troops crossed into Czechoslovakia overnight to end Alexander Dubček's Prague Spring reforms. Moscow soon claimed the right to intervene in any socialist state.

08-20.title: US strikes al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan and Sudan
08-20.description: In retaliation for the embassy bombings in East Africa, US cruise missiles hit camps in Afghanistan and the al-Shifa pharmaceutical factory in Khartoum, whose link to weapons was disputed.

08-21.title: Spanish colonists abandon Santa Fe during the Pueblo Revolt
08-21.description: Besieged by Pueblo fighters led by Popé, the Spanish governor and settlers retreated from Santa Fe towards El Paso. The Pueblo peoples kept New Mexico free of Spanish rule for twelve years.

08-21.title: Cameronians repel the Jacobites at Dunkeld
08-21.description: A small regiment of Cameronians held the town of Dunkeld against a much larger Jacobite force. The defeat broke the momentum of the rising that had followed Killiecrankie.

08-21.title: Lincoln and Douglas hold their first debate
08-21.description: Abraham Lincoln and Senator Stephen Douglas met in Ottawa, Illinois, for the first of seven debates on the spread of slavery. Lincoln lost the Senate race but won national attention.

08-21.title: The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre
08-21.description: Italian handyman Vincenzo Peruggia walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa under his smock. The theft made the painting world-famous; it was recovered in Florence in 1913.

08-21.title: Hawaii becomes the 50th US state
08-21.description: President Eisenhower proclaimed Hawaii's admission as the 50th state. It was the first state outside North America and the first with an Asian American plurality.

08-21.title: Total solar eclipse crosses the United States coast to coast
08-21.description: The Moon's shadow swept from Oregon to South Carolina, the first total eclipse to cross the whole country since 1918. Tens of millions watched along the path of totality.

08-22.title: English forces defeat David I of Scotland at the Battle of the Standard
08-22.description: Northern English levies rallied round a cart bearing a ship's mast and sacred banners near Northallerton and routed King David I's army. It was a key battle of the civil war period known as the Anarchy.

08-22.title: Henry Tudor defeats and kills Richard III at Bosworth
08-22.description: Richard III was killed fighting at Bosworth Field when Lord Stanley's forces turned against him. Henry Tudor took the crown as Henry VII, founding the Tudor dynasty.

08-22.title: The first Geneva Convention is signed
08-22.description: Twelve states signed the Geneva Convention protecting wounded soldiers and the medical staff caring for them. It grew out of Henry Dunant's campaign and founded modern humanitarian law.

08-22.title: The Cadillac Automobile Company is founded in Detroit
08-22.description: Investors reorganised Henry Ford's former company as Cadillac, named after the founder of Detroit. Engineer Henry Leland's precision manufacturing made it a byword for quality.

08-22.title: Joseph Walker flies the X-15 to the edge of space
08-22.description: NASA pilot Joseph Walker took the X-15 rocket plane to 107.8 km, beyond the 100 km boundary of space. The record for a winged aircraft stood until SpaceShipOne in 2004.

08-23.title: Stilicho executes the Gothic leader Radagaisus
08-23.description: Having trapped Radagaisus's invading army near Faesulae, the Roman general Stilicho had the Gothic king executed. Italy was saved for now, but Rome's frontiers were under mounting pressure.

08-23.title: William Wallace is executed in London
08-23.description: Betrayed and captured near Glasgow, William Wallace was hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield. The victor of Stirling Bridge became an enduring symbol of Scottish independence.

08-23.title: French court resolves to kill the Huguenot leaders
08-23.description: On the eve of St Bartholomew's Day, Charles IX and his council agreed to eliminate the Protestant leaders gathered in Paris. The killings began before dawn and spread across France.

08-23.title: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact
08-23.description: Ribbentrop and Molotov signed a pact in Moscow whose secret protocol divided eastern Europe into spheres of influence. It cleared the way for Germany's invasion of Poland a week later.

08-23.title: Two million people form the Baltic Way human chain
08-23.description: Some two million people joined hands across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania on the 50th anniversary of the Nazi-Soviet Pact. The 675 km chain demanded independence, regained in 1990-91.

08-24.title: Vesuvius erupts, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum
08-24.description: By the traditional date, Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and pumice, killing thousands. Some evidence suggests October; the ruins preserve a unique picture of Roman life.

08-24.title: Alaric's Visigoths sack Rome
08-24.description: The Visigoths under Alaric entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time the city had fallen to a foreign enemy in some 800 years. The shock prompted Augustine's City of God.

08-24.title: British troops burn Washington
08-24.description: After routing American militia at Bladensburg, British forces entered Washington and set fire to the Capitol and the President's House. It was partly revenge for the American burning of York.

08-24.title: Amelia Earhart flies non-stop across the United States
08-24.description: Amelia Earhart flew from Los Angeles to Newark in about 19 hours, the first woman to cross the continent non-stop. That May she had become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

08-24.title: Microsoft launches Windows 95
08-24.description: Microsoft released Windows 95 with a huge marketing campaign; customers queued at midnight. Its Start menu and taskbar set the pattern of the personal computer desktop for decades.

08-25.title: The First Council of Nicaea closes
08-25.description: By tradition the council summoned by Constantine ended on this date. It had condemned Arianism, adopted the Nicene Creed and set rules for dating Easter, shaping Christian doctrine for centuries.

08-25.title: Galileo demonstrates his telescope to Venice's rulers
08-25.description: Galileo showed the Venetian authorities his improved telescope, which made distant ships visible hours before they could be seen by eye. The Republic rewarded him with a lifetime post at Padua.

08-25.title: Uruguay declares independence from Brazil
08-25.description: A congress at Florida declared the Banda Oriental independent of the Empire of Brazil and united with the River Plate provinces. After a war, Uruguay became a sovereign state under the 1828 treaty.

08-25.title: First daily international scheduled air service begins
08-25.description: Aircraft Transport and Travel began daily flights between London's Hounslow Heath and Paris, carrying passengers, mail and goods. It was the start of scheduled international commercial aviation.

08-25.title: Paris is liberated from German occupation
08-25.description: French and American troops entered Paris and the German commander, General von Choltitz, surrendered, having ignored Hitler's order to destroy the city. De Gaulle led a victory march the next day.

08-25.title: Neil Armstrong dies aged 82
08-25.description: Neil Armstrong, the first person to walk on the Moon, died in Cincinnati after heart surgery. A modest engineer, he largely avoided the celebrity that followed Apollo 11.

08-26.title: Edward III's longbowmen defeat the French at Crécy
08-26.description: English archers and dismounted men-at-arms cut down repeated French cavalry charges at Crécy. The victory, with heavy losses among the French nobility, opened the way to the siege of Calais.

08-26.title: France adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
08-26.description: The National Assembly proclaimed that men are born free and equal in rights, and that sovereignty rests with the nation. The declaration became a founding text of modern human rights.

08-26.title: Krakatoa begins its cataclysmic eruption
08-26.description: The volcano of Krakatoa in the Sunda Strait began its climactic eruption, culminating in explosions the next day heard thousands of kilometres away. Tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people.

08-26.title: The 19th Amendment is certified, giving US women the vote
08-26.description: Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the 19th Amendment, barring denial of the vote on account of sex. It crowned a campaign launched at Seneca Falls in 1848.

08-26.title: Albino Luciani is elected Pope John Paul I
08-26.description: The Patriarch of Venice became the first pope to take a double name, honouring his two predecessors. Known as the 'smiling pope', he died after just 33 days.

08-27.title: Greeks defeat the Persian army at Plataea
08-27.description: A Greek alliance led by Sparta defeated the Persian army of Mardonius at Plataea, on a date traditionally placed in late August. The victory ended Persia's invasion of mainland Greece.

08-27.title: British forces defeat Washington at the Battle of Long Island
08-27.description: General William Howe outflanked and routed the Continental Army in Brooklyn, the largest battle of the war. Two nights later Washington's army escaped across the East River.

08-27.title: Edwin Drake strikes oil in Pennsylvania
08-27.description: Drilling near Titusville, Edwin Drake's well struck oil at about 21 metres. It was the first commercially successful oil well in the US and launched the modern petroleum industry.

08-27.title: Fifteen nations sign the Kellogg-Briand Pact
08-27.description: Signatories in Paris renounced war as an instrument of national policy. The pact had no means of enforcement, but it later underpinned charges of crimes against peace at Nuremberg.

08-27.title: The Heinkel He 178 makes the first jet-powered flight
08-27.description: Test pilot Erich Warsitz flew the Heinkel He 178 at Rostock-Marienehe, the first flight of an aircraft powered by a turbojet. Days later Germany invaded Poland.

08-28.title: Orestes drives Western Emperor Julius Nepos from Ravenna
08-28.description: The general Orestes seized Ravenna and Julius Nepos fled to Dalmatia. Orestes then made his young son Romulus Augustulus emperor; he would be the last to rule in the West.

08-28.title: Pedro Menéndez sights Florida and names it for St Augustine
08-28.description: Pedro Menéndez de Avilés sighted the Florida coast on the feast of St Augustine and gave the saint's name to the harbour. He founded the settlement on 8 September; it is the oldest continuously occupied European city in the US.

08-28.title: First issue of Scientific American is published
08-28.description: Inventor Rufus Porter launched Scientific American as a weekly in New York. It is the oldest continuously published monthly magazine in the United States.

08-28.title: Martin Luther King gives his 'I Have a Dream' speech
08-28.description: Speaking to some 250,000 people at the March on Washington, King described his dream of a nation free from racial injustice. The march helped build support for the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

08-28.title: New Orleans orders its first mandatory evacuation as Katrina nears
08-28.description: With Hurricane Katrina at Category 5 in the Gulf of Mexico, Mayor Ray Nagin ordered the city's first-ever mandatory evacuation. Tens of thousands without transport sheltered in the Superdome.

08-29.title: Suleiman the Magnificent crushes Hungary at Mohács
08-29.description: The Ottoman army destroyed the Hungarian forces at Mohács; King Louis II drowned while fleeing. Hungary was partitioned, and the Habsburgs inherited its crown.

08-29.title: The Treaty of Nanking ends the First Opium War
08-29.description: China ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain, opened five ports to foreign trade and paid a large indemnity. It was the first of the 'unequal treaties' China remembers as a century of humiliation.

08-29.title: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb
08-29.description: The USSR exploded its first atomic bomb at Semipalatinsk in Kazakhstan, years earlier than the West expected. The American nuclear monopoly was over and the arms race had begun.

08-29.title: The Beatles play their last concert for paying fans
08-29.description: The Beatles played a half-hour set at Candlestick Park in San Francisco. They then gave up touring to concentrate on studio albums such as Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band.

08-29.title: Hurricane Katrina strikes the US Gulf Coast
08-29.description: Katrina made landfall as a Category 3 hurricane; storm surge broke the levees of New Orleans and flooded some 80 per cent of the city. More than 1,300 people died and the government response was widely condemned.

08-30.title: The Battle of Lake Poyang begins
08-30.description: The fleets of Zhu Yuanzhang and Chen Youliang clashed on Lake Poyang in one of the largest naval battles in history. Zhu's victory weeks later opened his path to founding the Ming dynasty.

08-30.title: John Pascoe Fawkner's settlers land at the site of Melbourne
08-30.description: Settlers sent by John Pascoe Fawkner went ashore on the Yarra River, building the first houses of what became Melbourne. It grew into Australia's second-largest city.

08-30.title: Ty Cobb makes his major league debut
08-30.description: Eighteen-year-old Ty Cobb hit a double in his first game for the Detroit Tigers. His lifetime batting average of .366 remains the highest in major league history.

08-30.title: The Washington-Moscow hotline goes into service
08-30.description: A direct teleprinter link between the White House and the Kremlin began operating. Set up after the Cuban missile crisis, it aimed to prevent war by misunderstanding; it was never a red telephone.

08-30.title: East Timor votes for independence
08-30.description: In a UN-run referendum, 78.5 per cent of East Timorese voted for independence from Indonesia. Militia violence followed until an Australian-led force restored order; independence came in 2002.

08-31.title: Henry V of England dies at Vincennes
08-31.description: Henry V, victor of Agincourt and heir to the French throne, died of dysentery aged 35. His nine-month-old son Henry VI inherited a dual monarchy that soon unravelled.

08-31.title: An earthquake devastates Charleston, South Carolina
08-31.description: A powerful earthquake struck Charleston, damaging most of its buildings and killing about 60 people. It remains the strongest recorded earthquake in the south-eastern United States.

08-31.title: Mary Ann Nichols is murdered in Whitechapel
08-31.description: The body of Mary Ann Nichols was found in Buck's Row, the first of five victims generally attributed to 'Jack the Ripper'. The killer was never identified.

08-31.title: SS men stage a fake Polish attack at Gleiwitz
08-31.description: SS operatives seized the German radio station at Gleiwitz and broadcast an anti-German message, posing as Polish raiders. Hitler used such incidents to justify invading Poland the next morning.

08-31.title: Trinidad and Tobago becomes independent
08-31.description: Trinidad and Tobago gained independence from Britain, with Eric Williams as prime minister. Oil and gas wealth made it one of the most prosperous nations in the Caribbean.

08-31.title: Diana, Princess of Wales dies in a Paris car crash
08-31.description: Diana was fatally injured when her car crashed in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel while pursued by photographers. Her death provoked an extraordinary outpouring of public grief in Britain and beyond.

09-01.title: Adrian IV, the only English pope, dies at Anagni
09-01.description: Nicholas Breakspear, Pope Adrian IV, died after a stormy pontificate dominated by conflict with Frederick Barbarossa. His death led to a disputed election and an 18-year schism.

09-01.title: Louis XIV dies after 72 years on the throne
09-01.description: The Sun King died at Versailles days before his 77th birthday, having reigned for 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch. His five-year-old great-grandson succeeded as Louis XV.

09-01.title: Aaron Burr is acquitted of treason
09-01.description: A jury in Richmond acquitted former Vice President Aaron Burr of plotting to wage war in the West. Chief Justice John Marshall's strict reading of treason doomed Jefferson's prosecution.

09-01.title: Confederates evacuate Atlanta
09-01.description: General John Bell Hood abandoned Atlanta, blowing up ammunition trains as he left, and Sherman's troops entered the next day. The capture of the rail hub revived Lincoln's re-election hopes.

09-01.title: The Great Kantō earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama
09-01.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing more than 100,000 people. In the chaos, vigilantes murdered thousands of Koreans.

09-01.title: Germany invades Poland
09-01.description: German forces crossed into Poland at dawn without a declaration of war. Britain and France declared war two days later, and the Second World War had begun.

09-01.title: Muammar Gaddafi seizes power in Libya
09-01.description: Junior army officers led by 27-year-old Muammar Gaddafi overthrew King Idris in a bloodless coup. Gaddafi ruled Libya for 42 years until his overthrow and death in 2011.

09-02.title: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
09-02.description: Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra off Actium in western Greece. Their flight to Egypt left Octavian, soon to be Augustus, master of the Roman world.

09-02.title: The Great Fire of London breaks out in Pudding Lane
09-02.description: Fire broke out in Thomas Farriner's bakery and raged for four days, destroying some 13,200 houses, 87 churches and old St Paul's Cathedral. Wren's rebuilding transformed the City.

09-02.title: The September Massacres begin in Paris
09-02.description: Fearing a Prussian advance and a plot among prisoners, crowds broke into Paris prisons and killed some 1,100 to 1,400 inmates over five days. The massacres foreshadowed the Terror.

09-02.title: Japan signs the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri
09-02.description: Japanese envoys signed the formal surrender in Tokyo Bay before General MacArthur and Allied representatives. The ceremony officially ended the Second World War.

09-02.title: CBS Evening News becomes America's first half-hour network newscast
09-02.description: Walter Cronkite's evening news on CBS expanded from 15 to 30 minutes, opening with an interview with President Kennedy. NBC followed within a week, setting the format of US network news.

09-03.title: Gregory the Great is consecrated Pope
09-03.description: Gregory, a former prefect of Rome turned monk, was consecrated pope after months of reluctance. He reorganised the Church's estates, sent missionaries to England and shaped the medieval papacy.

09-03.title: Cromwell routs the Scottish army at Dunbar
09-03.description: Trapped against the coast, Oliver Cromwell attacked at dawn and shattered David Leslie's larger Scottish army. Dunbar opened the way to the English conquest of Scotland.

09-03.title: The Treaty of Paris recognises American independence
09-03.description: British and American envoys signed the Treaty of Paris, ending the Revolutionary War and fixing the new nation's borders at the Mississippi. Britain signed separate treaties with France and Spain the same day.

09-03.title: Britain and France declare war on Germany
09-03.description: When Germany ignored ultimatums to withdraw from Poland, Britain and France declared war. Neville Chamberlain announced it to the nation in a sombre radio broadcast.

09-03.title: Italy secretly signs an armistice with the Allies
09-03.description: Italian and Allied officers signed the Armistice of Cassibile in Sicily, the same day British troops landed in Calabria. When it was announced on 8 September, Germany occupied much of Italy.

09-03.title: Sweden switches to driving on the right
09-03.description: At 4.50 am all traffic in Sweden stopped, changed sides and restarted on the right. Dagen H, 'H Day', went remarkably smoothly after years of preparation.

09-04.title: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, the last Western emperor
09-04.description: The Germanic commander Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The date is conventionally taken as the end of the Western Roman Empire.

09-04.title: Spanish settlers found the pueblo of Los Angeles
09-04.description: Forty-four settlers of mixed Spanish, Native and African ancestry founded a farming town near the Porciúncula River. El Pueblo de la Reina de los Ángeles grew into the second-largest US city.

09-04.title: George Eastman patents the Kodak roll-film camera
09-04.description: George Eastman received a patent for his Kodak box camera. Sold pre-loaded with film under the slogan 'You press the button, we do the rest', it made photography a mass pastime.

09-04.title: Arkansas National Guard blocks Black students at Little Rock
09-04.description: Governor Orval Faubus used the National Guard to stop nine Black students entering Little Rock Central High School. Later in the month Eisenhower sent federal troops to enforce desegregation.

09-04.title: Larry Page and Sergey Brin incorporate Google
09-04.description: Two Stanford PhD students incorporated Google, working from a rented garage in Menlo Park. Its search engine became the gateway to the web and the company one of the world's most valuable.

09-05.title: Peter the Great shaves his nobles' beards
09-05.description: Back from his Grand Embassy to western Europe, Peter I personally cut off the beards of leading boyars. A tax on beards followed, part of his drive to westernise Russia's elite.

09-05.title: The First Continental Congress meets in Philadelphia
09-05.description: Delegates from twelve colonies gathered at Carpenters' Hall to coordinate resistance to Britain's Intolerable Acts. They agreed a boycott of British goods and planned to meet again.

09-05.title: Crazy Horse is killed at Camp Robinson
09-05.description: The Oglala Lakota leader Crazy Horse, a victor at Little Bighorn, was bayoneted by a soldier while resisting arrest at Camp Robinson, Nebraska. He died that night.

09-05.title: Palestinian gunmen seize Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympics
09-05.description: Black September militants killed two members of the Israeli team and took nine hostage. All nine and a West German policeman died in a failed rescue at Fürstenfeldbruck airbase.

09-05.title: Lynette Fromme tries to shoot President Ford
09-05.description: Manson Family follower Lynette 'Squeaky' Fromme aimed a pistol at Gerald Ford in Sacramento, but no round was chambered. A second attempt on Ford came 17 days later.

09-06.title: Theodosius I defeats Eugenius at the Frigidus
09-06.description: Emperor Theodosius defeated the usurper Eugenius, backed by the pagan senatorial aristocracy, in a two-day battle in the Julian Alps. Traditional Roman religion lost its last political champion.

09-06.title: The Victoria completes the first voyage around the world
09-06.description: The Victoria, last survivor of Magellan's five ships, reached Spain under Juan Sebastián Elcano with 18 men. The voyage revealed the vast size of the Pacific and the true scale of the globe.

09-06.title: John Endecott's Puritans arrive at Salem
09-06.description: John Endecott landed at Naumkeag with Puritan settlers, taking charge of the small settlement soon renamed Salem. It became the first town of the Massachusetts Bay Colony.

09-06.title: President McKinley is shot in Buffalo
09-06.description: Anarchist Leon Czolgosz shot William McKinley twice at the Pan-American Exposition. The president died eight days later, and Theodore Roosevelt succeeded him.

09-06.title: Hendrik Verwoerd is stabbed to death in parliament
09-06.description: South Africa's prime minister, chief architect of apartheid, was killed in the House of Assembly in Cape Town by parliamentary messenger Dimitri Tsafendas. Apartheid continued under his successors.

09-07.title: Richard the Lionheart defeats Saladin at Arsuf
09-07.description: Marching down the coast, Richard's army withstood harassing attacks before a crusader charge broke Saladin's forces at Arsuf. The victory let the crusaders take Jaffa.

09-07.title: The future Elizabeth I is born at Greenwich
09-07.description: Anne Boleyn gave birth to a daughter, Elizabeth, a disappointment to Henry VIII, who wanted a son. As queen for 44 years she defeated the Armada and presided over a golden age of English culture.

09-07.title: The submarine Turtle makes the first submarine attack
09-07.description: Sergeant Ezra Lee steered David Bushnell's one-man submarine Turtle towards HMS Eagle in New York Harbor. He failed to attach the charge to the hull, but it was the first submarine attack in war.

09-07.title: Napoleon and Kutuzov fight the Battle of Borodino
09-07.description: Some 70,000 men fell at Borodino, the bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars. The Russians withdrew, and a week later Napoleon entered an abandoned Moscow that was soon ablaze.

09-07.title: The Blitz begins with a massive raid on London
09-07.description: The Luftwaffe switched to bombing London, starting 57 consecutive nights of raids. The Blitz killed some 43,000 civilians by May 1941 but failed to break British morale.

09-08.title: Michelangelo's David is unveiled in Florence
09-08.description: Michelangelo's colossal marble David was unveiled outside the Palazzo Vecchio. Carved from a block other sculptors had abandoned, it became a symbol of the Florentine Republic.

09-08.title: The Ottomans abandon the Great Siege of Malta
09-08.description: After nearly four months, the Ottoman army withdrew from Malta, defeated by the Knights of St John under Jean de Valette. The new capital, Valletta, was named after him.

09-08.title: The Dutch hand New Amsterdam to the English
09-08.description: Facing English warships and an unwilling population, Peter Stuyvesant surrendered New Amsterdam without a fight. It was renamed New York after the Duke of York.

09-08.title: Italy's armistice with the Allies is announced
09-08.description: General Eisenhower broadcast news of Italy's surrender. German troops quickly disarmed the Italian army and occupied much of the country, which became a battleground for 20 months.

09-08.title: Gerald Ford pardons Richard Nixon
09-08.description: President Ford granted Nixon a full pardon for any crimes he 'committed or may have committed' in office. Ford said it would end the national ordeal; it damaged his own popularity.

09-09.title: Germanic tribes destroy three Roman legions in the Teutoburg Forest
09-09.description: Arminius led Germanic warriors in an ambush that wiped out three legions under Varus over several days, by tradition ending around this date. Rome never again tried to conquer Germany beyond the Rhine.

09-09.title: William the Conqueror dies in Rouen
09-09.description: William I died of injuries received at the burning of Mantes. Normandy went to his eldest son Robert and England to William Rufus, a division that set his heirs against each other.

09-09.title: Congress adopts the name 'United States of America'
09-09.description: The Continental Congress resolved that wherever 'United Colonies' had been used, the new nation should be styled the 'United States'. The name had appeared in the Declaration two months earlier.

09-09.title: California becomes the 31st US state
09-09.description: California entered the Union as a free state under the Compromise of 1850, two years after gold was found at Sutter's Mill. Its admission upset the balance between free and slave states.

09-09.title: North Korea is proclaimed under Kim Il-sung
09-09.description: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was proclaimed in the Soviet-occupied north, weeks after the Republic of Korea in the south. Kim Il-sung founded a dynasty that still rules.

09-09.title: Elvis Presley first appears on The Ed Sullivan Show
09-09.description: Some 60 million Americans, over 80 per cent of the TV audience, watched Elvis's first appearance on Sullivan's show. The 'waist up' camera shots came only on his third appearance in 1957.

09-10.title: Bishops of Visigothic Gaul meet at the Council of Agde
09-10.description: With the permission of the Arian king Alaric II, Catholic bishops met at Agde and issued canons on clerical discipline, marriage and church property. Many entered later collections of church law.

09-10.title: John the Fearless is murdered on the bridge at Montereau
09-10.description: The Duke of Burgundy was killed by followers of the Dauphin Charles during peace talks. Burgundy allied with England, leading to the Treaty of Troyes that made Henry V heir to France.

09-10.title: Oliver Hazard Perry wins the Battle of Lake Erie
09-10.description: Perry's American squadron captured the entire British force on Lake Erie. His message 'We have met the enemy and they are ours' heralded the recovery of Detroit and the American north-west.

09-10.title: Elias Howe patents the lockstitch sewing machine
09-10.description: Elias Howe received a US patent for a machine using an eye-pointed needle and a shuttle to form a lockstitch. He later won royalties from Singer and other makers who used his design.

09-10.title: Canada declares war on Germany
09-10.description: A week after Britain, Canada's parliament declared war on Germany in its own right. More than a million Canadians served in the Second World War.

09-11.title: Marlborough wins a costly victory at Malplaquet
09-11.description: Marlborough and Prince Eugene drove a French army from its positions at Malplaquet, but lost far more men than the enemy. The bloodiest battle of the century strengthened calls in Britain for peace.

09-11.title: Howe defeats Washington at Brandywine
09-11.description: General William Howe outflanked Washington's army at Brandywine Creek in Pennsylvania. Two weeks later the British occupied Philadelphia, and Congress fled to York.

09-11.title: Ground is broken for the Pentagon
09-11.description: Construction began on the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, to house the War Department. Finished in just 16 months, it remains one of the world's largest office buildings.

09-11.title: Military coup overthrows Chile's President Allende
09-11.description: Armed forces led by General Augusto Pinochet bombed the presidential palace, and Salvador Allende died inside. The US had worked to undermine Allende; Pinochet's dictatorship killed and disappeared thousands.

09-11.title: Al-Qaeda's September 11 attacks kill 2,977 people
09-11.description: Hijackers crashed airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; a fourth plane came down in Pennsylvania. The attacks killed 2,977 people and led to the US-led wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

09-12.title: Athenians defeat the Persians at Marathon
09-12.description: By the traditional date, the Athenians and Plataeans charged and routed the Persian landing force at Marathon. The legend of a runner carrying news to Athens inspired the modern marathon race.

09-12.title: Simon de Montfort defeats and kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret
09-12.description: Crusaders under Simon de Montfort routed a larger army of Aragon and Toulouse at Muret, killing King Peter II. The defeat ended Aragonese hopes in Languedoc and opened it to northern French rule.

09-12.title: John III Sobieski relieves the siege of Vienna
09-12.description: A relief army led by King John III Sobieski of Poland routed the Ottoman forces besieging Vienna, ending with a great charge of Polish hussars. The Ottoman advance into central Europe was halted for good.

09-12.title: Switzerland adopts its federal constitution
09-12.description: The Swiss Diet declared the new federal constitution accepted, turning a loose league of cantons into a federal state with a two-chamber parliament. Its framework still underpins Switzerland today.

09-12.title: Kennedy tells Rice University 'we choose to go to the Moon'
09-12.description: In a speech at Rice University in Houston, John F. Kennedy committed America to a Moon landing that decade, 'not because they are easy, but because they are hard'. Apollo 11 landed seven years later.

09-13.title: Wolfe defeats Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham
09-13.description: British troops under James Wolfe climbed the cliffs above Quebec and defeated the French in a brief battle. Wolfe was killed and Montcalm mortally wounded; Quebec fell, sealing Britain's conquest of Canada.

09-13.title: The British bombard Fort McHenry in Baltimore
09-13.description: British warships shelled Fort McHenry for some 25 hours. Seeing the flag still flying at dawn, Francis Scott Key wrote the poem that became 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

09-13.title: Rabin and Arafat shake hands on the Oslo Accords
09-13.description: Israel and the PLO signed the Declaration of Principles at the White House, with a historic handshake between Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat. The deal created Palestinian self-rule, but lasting peace proved elusive.

09-13.title: Tupac Shakur dies after a drive-by shooting
09-13.description: Rapper Tupac Shakur died in Las Vegas aged 25, six days after being shot. One of hip-hop's best-selling and most influential artists, his murder long went unsolved.

09-14.title: Harun al-Rashid becomes Abbasid caliph
09-14.description: On the night his brother al-Hadi died, Harun al-Rashid became caliph in Baghdad. His reign, remembered through the Thousand and One Nights, marked a high point of Abbasid power and culture.

09-14.title: Dante Alighieri dies in exile in Ravenna
09-14.description: Dante died in Ravenna, months after finishing the Divine Comedy. Written in Tuscan rather than Latin, his poem helped make that dialect the basis of the Italian language.

09-14.title: Napoleon's army enters Moscow
09-14.description: The Grande Armée entered a largely deserted Moscow, and fires soon destroyed much of the city. Napoleon waited five weeks for a peace offer that never came before beginning his disastrous retreat.

09-14.title: McKinley dies and Theodore Roosevelt becomes president
09-14.description: William McKinley died of gangrene from his gunshot wounds. Theodore Roosevelt, aged 42, became the youngest president in US history.

09-14.title: Princess Grace of Monaco dies after a car crash
09-14.description: Former film star Grace Kelly died a day after her car left a mountain road above Monaco. She had given up Hollywood to marry Prince Rainier III in 1956.

09-15.title: British troops land at Kip's Bay and take New York
09-15.description: After a heavy naval bombardment, British forces landed on Manhattan at Kip's Bay, sending American troops fleeing. New York stayed in British hands until 1783.

09-15.title: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens
09-15.description: The first inter-city railway relying wholly on steam locomotives opened with great ceremony. The day was marred when the MP William Huskisson was struck and killed by Stephenson's Rocket.

09-15.title: HMS Beagle reaches the Galápagos Islands
09-15.description: Charles Darwin spent five weeks studying the islands' finches, tortoises and mockingbirds. His observations later helped shape his theory of evolution by natural selection.

09-15.title: Tanks go into battle for the first time on the Somme
09-15.description: British Mark I tanks supported an attack at Flers-Courcelette. Many broke down, but those that advanced showed the potential of armoured warfare.

09-15.title: The RAF repels massed daylight raids on Battle of Britain Day
09-15.description: The Luftwaffe launched two huge raids on London and lost around 60 aircraft. Two days later Hitler postponed his planned invasion of Britain indefinitely.

09-15.title: UN forces land at Inchon
09-15.description: US Marines led General MacArthur's amphibious landing at Inchon, far behind North Korean lines. Seoul was retaken within two weeks and the North Korean army collapsed.

09-16.title: Owain Glyndŵr is proclaimed Prince of Wales
09-16.description: Supporters at Glyndyfrdwy proclaimed Owain Glyndŵr Prince of Wales, launching a revolt against English rule. For several years he controlled much of Wales and summoned Welsh parliaments.

09-16.title: The Mayflower sails from Plymouth
09-16.description: The Mayflower left Plymouth with 102 passengers, Separatist 'Pilgrims' and others (6 September Old Style). After a gruelling crossing they founded Plymouth Colony in Massachusetts.

09-16.title: Miguel Hidalgo's 'Grito de Dolores' launches Mexico's revolt
09-16.description: Priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell in Dolores and called his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule. Mexico celebrates the day as Independence Day, won in 1821.

09-16.title: William Durant incorporates General Motors
09-16.description: Buick head William Durant formed General Motors as a holding company, soon adding Oldsmobile, Cadillac and others. GM became for decades the world's largest car maker.

09-16.title: Phalangist militia begin the Sabra and Shatila massacre
09-16.description: Lebanese Christian militiamen entered Beirut's Sabra and Shatila refugee camps, in an area under Israeli control, and killed hundreds of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians over two days.

09-17.title: Charles VI orders the expulsion of the Jews from France
09-17.description: King Charles VI decreed that all Jews must leave the kingdom of France. The edict ended organised Jewish life in most of the kingdom for some four centuries.

09-17.title: Delegates sign the US Constitution in Philadelphia
09-17.description: Thirty-nine delegates signed the Constitution, creating a federal government with separated powers and checks and balances. The Bill of Rights was added by amendment in 1791.

09-17.title: The Battle of Antietam, America's bloodiest single day
09-17.description: Union and Confederate armies suffered about 23,000 casualties along Antietam Creek in Maryland. Lee's retreat gave Lincoln the victory he needed to announce the Emancipation Proclamation.

09-17.title: Operation Market Garden begins in the Netherlands
09-17.description: Some 35,000 Allied airborne troops landed to seize bridges leading to the Rhine. The operation failed at Arnhem, ending hopes of finishing the war by Christmas 1944.

09-17.title: Egypt and Israel sign the Camp David Accords
09-17.description: After 13 days of talks hosted by Jimmy Carter, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed two frameworks for peace. They led to the Egypt-Israel peace treaty of March 1979.

09-18.title: Domitian is murdered and Nerva becomes emperor
09-18.description: Emperor Domitian was stabbed to death in a palace conspiracy, and the Senate chose the elderly Nerva to succeed him. Nerva's adoption of Trajan began the era of the 'Five Good Emperors'.

09-18.title: Constantine defeats Licinius at Chrysopolis
09-18.description: Constantine's victory over his co-emperor Licinius at Chrysopolis, across the Bosporus from Byzantium, made him sole ruler of the Roman Empire. He soon refounded Byzantium as Constantinople.

09-18.title: George Washington lays the cornerstone of the US Capitol
09-18.description: President Washington laid the cornerstone of the Capitol in a Masonic ceremony. Congress first met in the unfinished building in November 1800.

09-18.title: President Fillmore signs the Fugitive Slave Act
09-18.description: Part of the Compromise of 1850, the act required citizens of free states to help return people who had escaped slavery, and denied them a jury trial. It turned many Northerners against slavery.

09-18.title: Jimi Hendrix dies in London aged 27
09-18.description: Guitarist Jimi Hendrix died in London after taking barbiturates. In four years of fame he had transformed the electric guitar with his use of feedback, distortion and virtuoso technique.

09-19.title: The Black Prince captures King John II at Poitiers
09-19.description: Edward the Black Prince's outnumbered army defeated the French at Poitiers and captured King John II. His huge ransom and the chaos that followed brought France to the brink of collapse.

09-19.title: Nathaniel Bacon's rebels burn Jamestown
09-19.description: Rebels led by Nathaniel Bacon burned Virginia's capital, Jamestown, in a revolt against Governor Berkeley. Their alliance of poor whites, servants and enslaved Africans alarmed the colony's elite.

09-19.title: George Washington's Farewell Address is published
09-19.description: Washington announced he would not seek a third term in an address printed in a Philadelphia newspaper. He warned against party faction and permanent foreign alliances.

09-19.title: President James Garfield dies 79 days after being shot
09-19.description: Garfield died of infection and complications from the wound inflicted by Charles Guiteau. His doctors' unsterile probing of the wound almost certainly contributed to his death.

09-19.title: Hikers find Ötzi the Iceman in the Alps
09-19.description: Two German hikers found a body in the ice on the Austrian-Italian border. Ötzi proved to be a man who died some 5,300 years ago, killed by an arrow, with his clothes and tools preserved.

09-20.title: Saladin begins the siege of Jerusalem
09-20.description: Saladin's army arrived before Jerusalem, held by the crusaders for 88 years. Balian of Ibelin surrendered the city twelve days later, and most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves.

09-20.title: Magellan sets sail to find a western route to the Spice Islands
09-20.description: Ferdinand Magellan left Sanlúcar de Barrameda with five ships and about 270 men. He was killed in the Philippines, but one ship returned in 1522, completing the first voyage round the world.

09-20.title: Italian troops breach the walls of Rome at Porta Pia
09-20.description: After French troops left Rome, Italian forces broke through the walls and took the city. The Papal States ended, and Rome became the capital of united Italy the following year.

09-20.title: Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the 'Battle of the Sexes'
09-20.description: Before some 30,000 spectators in Houston and a huge TV audience, Billie Jean King beat former champion Bobby Riggs in straight sets. The match became a landmark for women's sport.

09-21.title: Emperor Valentinian III murders his general Aetius
09-21.description: Valentinian III killed Flavius Aetius with his own hands during a meeting in Ravenna. The West lost the commander who had checked Attila; Valentinian was himself assassinated six months later.

09-21.title: Deposed Edward II dies at Berkeley Castle
09-21.description: Edward II was announced dead at Berkeley Castle, almost certainly murdered on the orders of Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer. The later tale of a red-hot poker is unsupported.

09-21.title: Jacobites rout a government army at Prestonpans
09-21.description: Bonnie Prince Charlie's Highlanders routed Sir John Cope's army in a few minutes near Edinburgh. The victory encouraged the Jacobite invasion of England, which turned back at Derby.

09-21.title: H. G. Wells is born in Bromley
09-21.description: Herbert George Wells was born in Kent to a shopkeeper's family. His novels The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds helped found modern science fiction.

09-21.title: Belize becomes independent
09-21.description: The former British Honduras became independent as Belize, with George Price as prime minister. British troops remained because Guatemala claimed the territory; it recognised Belize in 1991.

09-22.title: Treaty of Basel ends the Swabian War
09-22.description: Emperor Maximilian I made peace with the Swiss Confederation after its victories in the Swabian War. The Swiss became independent of the Empire in practice; formal recognition came in 1648.

09-22.title: The British hang Nathan Hale as a spy
09-22.description: Captured behind British lines on Long Island, 21-year-old Captain Nathan Hale was hanged in Manhattan. He is said to have regretted that he had 'but one life to lose for my country'.

09-22.title: Lincoln issues the preliminary Emancipation Proclamation
09-22.description: Lincoln announced that enslaved people in states still in rebellion on 1 January 1863 would be declared free. The war for the Union became also a war against slavery.

09-22.title: Iraq invades Iran
09-22.description: Saddam Hussein's forces invaded Iran, starting an eight-year war of trenches, missile attacks and poison gas. Hundreds of thousands died before a ceasefire in 1988 left borders unchanged.

09-23.title: The future Emperor Augustus is born in Rome
09-23.description: Gaius Octavius was born in Rome, great-nephew of Julius Caesar. As Augustus he ended the civil wars and turned the Republic into a monarchy that lasted for centuries.

09-23.title: John Paul Jones captures HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head
09-23.description: In a brutal moonlit battle, John Paul Jones's sinking Bonhomme Richard captured HMS Serapis off Yorkshire. His later-reported reply 'I have not yet begun to fight' became a naval legend.

09-23.title: Johann Galle discovers Neptune
09-23.description: At the Berlin Observatory, Johann Galle found Neptune within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier had calculated. It was the first planet found by mathematical prediction.

09-23.title: Sigmund Freud dies in London
09-23.description: Freud, who had fled Nazi-occupied Vienna the year before, died aged 83 after his doctor gave him lethal doses of morphine at his request. His theories of the unconscious reshaped twentieth-century thought.

09-24.title: Pepin the Short dies, leaving the Franks to Charlemagne and Carloman
09-24.description: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.

09-24.title: Washington signs the Judiciary Act
09-24.description: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.

09-24.title: Gold price collapses on 'Black Friday'
09-24.description: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.

09-24.title: B. R. Ambedkar and Hindu leaders sign the Poona Pact
09-24.description: Agreed with Gandhi during his fast, the Poona Pact was signed, replacing separate electorates for the 'depressed classes' with reserved seats. Gandhi ended his fast against separate electorates two days later.

09-24.title: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature
09-24.description: The CTBT, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN and was signed first by President Clinton. It has not entered into force, as key states have not ratified it.

09-25.title: Harold II defeats Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge
09-25.description: King Harold of England surprised and destroyed the Norwegian army near York, killing Harald Hardrada and Tostig. Three days later William of Normandy landed in the south, forcing Harold to march back.

09-25.title: Balboa becomes the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas
09-25.description: Vasco Núñez de Balboa climbed a peak on the Isthmus of Panama and sighted the 'South Sea'. Days later he waded into the water and claimed it and all its shores for Castile.

09-25.title: Congress proposes the amendments that become the Bill of Rights
09-25.description: The First Congress sent twelve proposed amendments to the states. Ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, protecting freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly.

09-25.title: Sonny Liston knocks out Floyd Patterson to win the world title
09-25.description: Sonny Liston took the world heavyweight title in Chicago by knocking out Floyd Patterson in 2 minutes 6 seconds of the first round. He lost the title to Cassius Clay in 1964.

09-26.title: Julius Caesar dedicates the Temple of Venus Genetrix
09-26.description: Amid the celebrations of his triumphs, Caesar dedicated a temple to Venus Genetrix, the mythical ancestress of his family, in his new forum. It proclaimed his divine lineage and unrivalled power.

09-26.title: Francis Drake returns from his voyage around the world
09-26.description: The Golden Hind sailed into Plymouth after nearly three years, laden with Spanish treasure. Drake was the first captain to complete a circumnavigation and was knighted aboard his ship the next April.

09-26.title: A Venetian shell blows apart the Parthenon
09-26.description: During the Venetian siege of the Acropolis, a mortar shell ignited Ottoman gunpowder stored in the Parthenon. The explosion destroyed the temple's centre and killed some 300 people.

09-26.title: Einstein's paper on special relativity is published
09-26.description: Annalen der Physik published Einstein's 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', which showed that measurements of time and space depend on the observer's motion. It transformed physics.

09-26.title: Stanislav Petrov judges a Soviet missile alert a false alarm
09-26.description: Duty officer Stanislav Petrov saw satellite warnings of US missile launches and reported them as a malfunction rather than an attack. He was right, and may have averted a nuclear war.

09-27.title: Pope Paul III approves the Society of Jesus
09-27.description: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's Jesuits. The order became a leading force of the Catholic Reformation, founding schools and missions worldwide.

09-27.title: Venice surrenders Candia to the Ottomans
09-27.description: The Venetians handed over Candia, modern Heraklion, ending a siege of more than 21 years, one of the longest in history. Crete passed to Ottoman rule.

09-27.title: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens
09-27.description: George Stephenson drove Locomotion No. 1, hauling coal wagons and hundreds of passengers, on the opening run. It was the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives.

09-27.title: Germany, Italy and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact
09-27.description: The three powers signed a ten-year military alliance in Berlin, pledging mutual aid if attacked by a power not yet at war, aimed chiefly at the United States. It formalised the Axis.

09-27.title: The Warren Commission report is made public
09-27.description: The commission's report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald alone had killed President Kennedy. Its findings have been widely debated ever since.

09-28.title: Pompey is murdered on landing in Egypt
09-28.description: Fleeing after Pharsalus, Pompey the Great was stabbed to death as he stepped ashore, on the orders of Ptolemy XIII's advisers. Caesar is said to have wept when shown his rival's head.

09-28.title: William of Normandy lands at Pevensey
09-28.description: William's invasion fleet landed unopposed on the Sussex coast while King Harold was in the north. Just over two weeks later William won the Battle of Hastings.

09-28.title: American and French armies begin the siege of Yorktown
09-28.description: Washington and Rochambeau's forces closed in on Cornwallis at Yorktown, Virginia, while a French fleet blocked escape by sea. Cornwallis surrendered on 19 October, effectively ending the war.

09-28.title: Alexander Fleming notices the mould that leads to penicillin
09-28.description: Back from holiday, Alexander Fleming found a mould killing bacteria on a culture plate in his London laboratory. Developed into a drug in the 1940s, penicillin opened the antibiotic era.

09-28.title: Ferdinand Marcos dies in exile in Hawaii
09-28.description: Former Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos died in Honolulu, three years after the People Power Revolution drove him from power. His regime was notorious for martial law and plunder.

09-29.title: Pope Gregory IX excommunicates Emperor Frederick II
09-29.description: Gregory IX excommunicated Frederick II for again delaying his promised crusade. Frederick went anyway, regaining Jerusalem by treaty in 1229 and crowning himself in the Holy Sepulchre.

09-29.title: Horatio Nelson is born in Norfolk
09-29.description: Horatio Nelson was born at Burnham Thorpe, the son of a rector. He won the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen and died at his greatest victory, Trafalgar, in 1805.

09-29.title: London's Metropolitan Police go on patrol for the first time
09-29.description: Constables of Robert Peel's new Metropolitan Police began patrolling London. Nicknamed 'Bobbies' or 'Peelers', they set a model of uniformed, civilian policing by consent.

09-29.title: Munich conference hands the Sudetenland to Germany
09-29.description: Chamberlain, Daladier, Hitler and Mussolini agreed at Munich that Czechoslovakia must cede the Sudetenland; the deal was signed after midnight. Czechoslovakia was not consulted.

09-30.title: St Jerome dies in Bethlehem
09-30.description: The scholar Jerome died in Bethlehem, where he had translated most of the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek. His Vulgate became the standard Bible of the Western Church for over a thousand years.

09-30.title: Parliament accepts Richard II's deposition and Henry IV's claim
09-30.description: Richard II's abdication was read to an assembly at Westminster, which then acclaimed Henry Bolingbroke as Henry IV. The Lancastrian usurpation sowed the seeds of the Wars of the Roses.

09-30.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute premieres in Vienna
09-30.description: Die Zauberflöte opened at the Theater auf der Wieden with Mozart conducting. It was a popular success, and he died nine weeks later at the age of 35.

09-30.title: Chamberlain returns from Munich promising 'peace for our time'
09-30.description: Neville Chamberlain landed at Heston waving the declaration signed with Hitler and later spoke of 'peace for our time'. Within six months Germany had seized the rest of Czechoslovakia.

09-30.title: James Dean dies in a car crash aged 24
09-30.description: Actor James Dean was killed when his Porsche collided with another car in California. Two of his three starring films were released after his death, making him a lasting icon of youth.

10-01.title: Alexander defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
10-01.description: Alexander the Great routed the far larger army of the Persian king Darius III near Gaugamela in northern Mesopotamia. The victory broke Achaemenid power and opened the road to Babylon, Susa and Persepolis.

10-01.title: The Congress of Vienna is due to open formally
10-01.description: Europe's statesmen had gathered in Vienna to redraw the continent after Napoleon's fall, and 1 October was fixed for the Congress's formal opening. Its settlement shaped a balance of power that endured for decades.

10-01.title: John Philip Sousa takes charge of the US Marine Band
10-01.description: The 25-year-old John Philip Sousa became leader of the United States Marine Band. Over the next twelve years he turned it into a celebrated ensemble and began the career that earned him the name 'The March King'.

10-01.title: Congress creates Yosemite National Park
10-01.description: An Act of Congress established Yosemite National Park in California's Sierra Nevada, protecting the high country around the Yosemite Valley. John Muir's campaigning had helped make the case for preservation.

10-01.title: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China
10-01.description: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China. Communist victory in the civil war placed the world's most populous country under a new regime.

10-01.title: 'In God We Trust' first appears on US paper money
10-01.description: The first US banknotes carrying 'In God We Trust', one-dollar silver certificates, entered circulation. Congress had made the phrase the national motto in 1956, at the height of Cold War anxieties about 'godless' communism.

10-01.title: Nigeria gains independence from Britain
10-01.description: Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, became independent from Britain with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as prime minister. It was one of seventeen African states to win independence in 1960, the 'Year of Africa'.

10-02.title: Saladin takes Jerusalem from the Crusaders
10-02.description: After a short siege, Saladin accepted the surrender of Jerusalem, ending 88 years of Crusader rule. Most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves, and the city's loss prompted the Third Crusade.

10-02.title: Major John André is hanged as a British spy
10-02.description: Major John André, captured carrying Benedict Arnold's plans to surrender West Point, was hanged at Tappan, New York. His composure won sympathy even among his captors, while Arnold's name became a byword for treason.

10-02.title: Texan settlers fire the first shots of the Texas Revolution
10-02.description: At Gonzales, Texan colonists refused to hand back a small cannon to Mexican troops and fired on them beneath a flag reading 'Come and Take It'. The skirmish opened the war that led to Texan independence in 1836.

10-02.title: Mohandas Gandhi is born in Porbandar
10-02.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in Porbandar, on India's western coast. His method of non-violent mass resistance, satyagraha, drove the Indian independence movement and inspired civil rights campaigns worldwide.

10-02.title: Mexican troops open fire on students at Tlatelolco
10-02.description: Soldiers and police fired on a student rally in Mexico City's Plaza de las Tres Culturas, ten days before the Olympic Games opened. Estimates of the dead range from about 30 to several hundred; the government long concealed the toll.

10-03.title: Theodosius I settles the Goths inside the Roman Empire
10-03.description: Emperor Theodosius I concluded a treaty allowing the Goths to settle south of the Danube as semi-autonomous allies. Giving a whole people land within the frontier set a precedent that reshaped the late Roman world.

10-03.title: Francis of Assisi dies at the Porziuncola
10-03.description: Francis of Assisi died at the Porziuncola chapel below Assisi. The merchant's son who embraced radical poverty had founded the Franciscan order, and he was canonised less than two years later.

10-03.title: Lincoln proclaims a national day of Thanksgiving
10-03.description: Amid the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln proclaimed the last Thursday of November a national day of thanksgiving. The proclamation answered years of campaigning by the editor Sarah Josepha Hale and began an annual federal holiday.

10-03.title: King Alexander renames his realm the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
10-03.description: Alexander I renamed the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as Yugoslavia, 'land of the South Slavs', as part of his royal dictatorship. The new name was meant to override the national rivalries dividing the state.

10-03.title: Germany is reunified
10-03.description: The German Democratic Republic acceded to the Federal Republic, reuniting Germany 45 years after its division. The peaceful merger, less than a year after the Berlin Wall opened, marked the close of the Cold War in Europe.

10-04.title: Heraclius reaches Constantinople to overthrow Phocas
10-04.description: Heraclius, son of the exarch of Africa, arrived at Constantinople with a fleet from Carthage and toppled the unpopular emperor Phocas. His reign saw triumph over Persia but also the loss of Syria and Egypt to the Arabs.

10-04.title: Catholic Europe switches to the Gregorian calendar
10-04.description: In Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed directly by Friday 15 October. Pope Gregory XIII's reform dropped ten days to realign the calendar with the solar year.

10-04.title: Belgium's provisional government declares independence
10-04.description: Following the September uprising in Brussels, Belgium's provisional government declared independence from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. The great powers recognised the new state, and later guaranteed its neutrality.

10-04.title: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1
10-04.description: The Soviet Union placed Sputnik 1, an 84-kilogram metal sphere, into orbit, the first artificial satellite. Its radio beeps, picked up worldwide, shocked the West and launched the Space Race.

10-04.title: Paul VI becomes the first pope to visit the United States
10-04.description: Pope Paul VI flew to New York for a one-day visit, the first by a reigning pope to the United States. He appealed for peace at the United Nations General Assembly and celebrated Mass at Yankee Stadium.

10-05.title: The Fourth Council of Constantinople opens
10-05.description: A church council opened in Constantinople that deposed the patriarch Photius. Counted by the Catholic Church as the eighth ecumenical council but rejected by the Orthodox, it foreshadowed the later schism between East and West.

10-05.title: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice premieres in Vienna
10-05.description: Christoph Willibald Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice was first performed at the Burgtheater in Vienna. Its simplicity and dramatic directness began Gluck's reform of opera away from showy vocal display.

10-05.title: Parisian women march on Versailles
10-05.description: Thousands of Parisians, led by market women angry at the price of bread, marched to Versailles. The next day they brought Louis XVI and his family back to Paris, placing the monarchy under the eye of the Revolution.

10-05.title: The Beatles release their first single, 'Love Me Do'
10-05.description: Parlophone released 'Love Me Do', the Beatles' debut single in Britain. It reached only number 17, but within a year the band from Liverpool had become a national sensation.

10-05.title: Dr. No premieres, launching the James Bond films
10-05.description: Dr. No, starring Sean Connery as Ian Fleming's secret agent, premiered at the London Pavilion. It began one of the longest-running series in cinema history.

10-06.title: Rebels kill Wang Mang as Chang'an falls
10-06.description: Rebel forces broke into Chang'an and killed Wang Mang, the usurper who had founded the Xin dynasty. His death cleared the way for the restoration of the Han dynasty under Emperor Guangwu.

10-06.title: Peri's Euridice, the oldest surviving opera, is performed
10-06.description: Jacopo Peri's Euridice was staged at the Pitti Palace in Florence during celebrations for the marriage of Maria de' Medici to Henry IV of France. It is the earliest opera whose music survives complete.

10-06.title: The Jazz Singer premieres in New York
10-06.description: Warner Bros released The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, the first feature film with synchronised dialogue and singing. Its success ended the silent era within a few years.

10-06.title: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on Yom Kippur
10-06.description: Egyptian and Syrian forces launched surprise attacks on Israeli positions in Sinai and the Golan Heights on the holiest day of the Jewish year. The war ended in Israeli counter-offensives and reshaped Middle Eastern diplomacy.

10-06.title: Egyptian president Anwar Sadat is assassinated
10-06.description: Islamist army officers shot Anwar Sadat during a military parade in Cairo marking the 1973 war. Sadat had signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1979 and shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Menachem Begin.

10-07.title: The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto
10-07.description: Galleys of the Holy League under Don John of Austria destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet off western Greece. Lepanto was the last great battle of oared galleys and ended the image of Ottoman naval invincibility.

10-07.title: A cyclone and storm surge devastate Calcutta and Bengal
10-07.description: A violent cyclone struck the Hooghly delta, wrecking ships and much of Calcutta. Contemporary reports put the dead at 300,000, a figure modern historians consider greatly exaggerated.

10-07.title: Luna 3 photographs the far side of the Moon
10-07.description: The Soviet probe Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which is never visible from Earth. The grainy images revealed a surface with far fewer dark lunar 'seas' than the near side.

10-07.title: The US and Britain begin air strikes on Afghanistan
10-07.description: American and British forces began bombing Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan, four weeks after the 11 September attacks. The war toppled the Taliban but lasted nearly twenty years.

10-07.title: The epoch of the Hebrew calendar
10-07.description: The Hebrew calendar counts its years from a date equivalent to 7 October 3761 BCE, the traditional date of creation calculated from biblical chronology. Year 1 of this reckoning is still used to number the Jewish year.

10-08.title: The Council of Chalcedon opens
10-08.description: Bishops summoned by Emperor Marcian met at Chalcedon, across the Bosporus from Constantinople. Its definition of Christ as one person in two natures became orthodoxy in the West and Byzantium but split the eastern churches.

10-08.title: Chinese officials board the Arrow at Canton
10-08.description: Qing officials boarded the Arrow, a Chinese-owned ship flying a British flag, and arrested its crew on suspicion of piracy. Britain used the incident as grounds for the Second Opium War.

10-08.title: The Great Chicago Fire breaks out
10-08.description: Fire broke out in a barn on DeKoven Street and, driven by strong winds, burned for two days across Chicago. About 300 people died and 100,000 lost their homes, but rebuilding made the city a centre of modern architecture.

10-08.title: Corporal Alvin York captures 132 German soldiers
10-08.description: In the Argonne Forest, Corporal Alvin York led a small patrol that silenced German machine guns, killing about 25 soldiers and taking 132 prisoners. He received the Medal of Honor and became a national hero.

10-08.title: Che Guevara is captured in Bolivia
10-08.description: Bolivian troops, aided by the CIA, wounded and captured Ernesto 'Che' Guevara in the Yuro ravine. He was executed the next day at La Higuera, and his image became an enduring icon of revolution.

10-09.title: King Sejong promulgates the Korean alphabet
10-09.description: Sejong the Great of Joseon published the Hunminjeongeum, introducing a new phonetic script now called Hangul. Designed so ordinary people could read and write, it is commemorated each year on Hangul Day.

10-09.title: Connecticut charters the school that became Yale
10-09.description: The Connecticut General Assembly chartered the Collegiate School to train ministers and public leaders. It later settled in New Haven and in 1718 was renamed Yale College after the benefactor Elihu Yale.

10-09.title: The Treaty of Bern founds the Universal Postal Union
10-09.description: Representatives of 22 countries signed the Treaty of Bern, creating a single postal territory for exchanging letters. Its anniversary is marked as World Post Day.

10-09.title: John Lennon is born in Liverpool
10-09.description: John Winston Lennon was born at Liverpool Maternity Hospital. As co-founder and songwriter of the Beatles, and later as a solo artist and peace campaigner, he became one of the defining figures of 20th-century popular culture.

10-09.title: Uganda gains independence from Britain
10-09.description: Uganda became independent with Milton Obote as prime minister and the Kabaka of Buganda later as president. Its early decades were marked by political upheaval, including the dictatorship of Idi Amin.

10-10.title: Charles Martel defeats an Umayyad army near Tours
10-10.description: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Arab and Berber army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi between Tours and Poitiers; the traditional date is 10 October. How decisive the battle was remains debated.

10-10.title: The US Naval School opens at Annapolis
10-10.description: The Naval School, renamed the United States Naval Academy in 1850, opened at Fort Severn in Annapolis, Maryland, with 50 midshipmen. It has trained American naval officers ever since; Jimmy Carter was among its graduates.

10-10.title: The Wuchang Uprising sparks the Chinese revolution
10-10.description: Revolutionary soldiers mutinied at Wuchang, beginning the Xinhai Revolution. Within months the Qing dynasty abdicated, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

10-10.title: Woodrow Wilson triggers the blast that floods the Panama Canal cut
10-10.description: From the White House, President Wilson sent a telegraph signal that detonated the Gamboa dike. Water flowed into the Culebra Cut, joining the canal's waters ten months before it opened to shipping.

10-10.title: The Outer Space Treaty enters into force
10-10.description: The Outer Space Treaty came into effect, forming the basis of international space law. It bars nuclear weapons from orbit and forbids any nation from claiming sovereignty over the Moon or other celestial bodies.

10-11.title: Pope Leo X names Henry VIII 'Defender of the Faith'
10-11.description: Pope Leo X granted Henry VIII the title Fidei Defensor for his treatise attacking Martin Luther. Henry later broke with Rome, yet British monarchs still use the title, abbreviated 'F.D.' on coins.

10-11.title: The Second Boer War begins in South Africa
10-11.description: War broke out when Britain let a Boer ultimatum expire. In the three-year conflict that followed, British concentration camps saw the deaths of about 26,000 Boer women and children and many thousands of black Africans.

10-11.title: Roosevelt receives Einstein's warning about atomic bombs
10-11.description: The economist Alexander Sachs delivered to Franklin Roosevelt a letter signed by Albert Einstein, warning that Germany might build a uranium bomb. Roosevelt set up an advisory committee that led eventually to the Manhattan Project.

10-11.title: Pope John XXIII opens the Second Vatican Council
10-11.description: More than 2,000 bishops gathered in St Peter's Basilica for the opening of the Second Vatican Council. Over three years it introduced vernacular liturgy, embraced ecumenism and affirmed religious freedom.

10-12.title: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas
10-12.description: After 33 days crossing the Atlantic, Christopher Columbus's expedition landed on an island its Taíno inhabitants called Guanahani. The encounter began sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, with vast consequences for both.

10-12.title: Crown Prince Ludwig's wedding gives rise to Oktoberfest
10-12.description: Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria married Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen, and Munich's citizens were invited to celebrate on the fields before the city gates. The festivities, crowned by a horse race, became the annual Oktoberfest.

10-12.title: Pedro I is acclaimed Emperor of Brazil
10-12.description: In Rio de Janeiro, Prince Pedro was acclaimed constitutional Emperor of Brazil, five weeks after declaring independence from Portugal. Brazil became the only lasting monarchy in independent Latin America.

10-12.title: Germans execute the British nurse Edith Cavell
10-12.description: A German firing squad in Brussels executed Edith Cavell, who had helped some 200 Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium. Her death caused international outrage and became a powerful theme of Allied propaganda.

10-12.title: Bombings in Bali kill 202 people
10-12.description: Militants of Jemaah Islamiyah bombed two nightclubs in the tourist district of Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people from 21 countries. It remains the deadliest terrorist attack in Indonesia's history.

10-13.title: Nero becomes Roman emperor at 16
10-13.description: On the death of Claudius, reputedly poisoned by his wife Agrippina, her 16-year-old son Nero was proclaimed emperor. His reign began promisingly but ended in tyranny, rebellion and his suicide in 68.

10-13.title: Philip IV of France orders the arrest of the Templars
10-13.description: In dawn raids across France, Philip IV's officers arrested hundreds of Knights Templar on charges of heresy and blasphemy. The heavily indebted king coveted their wealth, and the order was suppressed in 1312.

10-13.title: The cornerstone of the White House is laid
10-13.description: Freemasons laid the cornerstone of the President's House in the new federal city of Washington. Designed by James Hoban, it has housed every US president since John Adams.

10-13.title: Greenwich is chosen as the world's prime meridian
10-13.description: Delegates at the International Meridian Conference in Washington voted to adopt the meridian through Greenwich as the zero of longitude. The decision underpins maps, navigation and the world's time zones.

10-13.title: Italy declares war on Germany
10-13.description: Five weeks after its armistice with the Allies, Pietro Badoglio's Italian government declared war on its former Axis partner. German forces nonetheless occupied northern and central Italy until 1945.

10-14.title: William of Normandy defeats Harold II at Hastings
10-14.description: After a day-long battle near Hastings, Norman forces killed King Harold II and broke the English army. The conquest replaced England's ruling class and transformed its language, law and architecture.

10-14.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Old Byland
10-14.description: A Scottish army under Robert the Bruce defeated English forces at Old Byland in Yorkshire, and Edward II narrowly escaped capture. The defeat pushed England towards the truce of 1323.

10-14.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, goes on trial at Fotheringhay
10-14.description: Mary was tried before a commission of English peers and officials at Fotheringhay Castle, accused of plotting Elizabeth I's death in the Babington Plot. Found guilty, she was beheaded in February 1587.

10-14.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower is born in Texas
10-14.description: Dwight David Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas. He commanded the Allied invasion of Europe in 1944 and served two terms as the 34th US president, warning on leaving office of the 'military-industrial complex'.

10-14.title: Chuck Yeager flies faster than sound
10-14.description: Captain Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 past Mach 1 high over the Mojave Desert. It was the first confirmed supersonic flight in level flight, opening the age of supersonic aviation.

10-14.title: Soviet leaders oust Nikita Khrushchev
10-14.description: Recalled from holiday, Nikita Khrushchev was forced out by the Communist Party's Central Committee. Leonid Brezhnev succeeded him as party leader and steered the Soviet Union into two decades of stability and stagnation.

10-15.title: The Gregorian calendar takes effect
10-15.description: Friday 15 October 1582 was the first day of the Gregorian calendar in Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, following directly on Thursday 4 October. Protestant and Orthodox countries adopted it only over the following centuries.

10-15.title: Pilâtre de Rozier makes the first human balloon ascent
10-15.description: In Paris, Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier rose about 25 metres in a tethered Montgolfier hot-air balloon, the first human ascent. Five weeks later he made the first free flight.

10-15.title: Napoleon arrives in exile at Saint Helena
10-15.description: HMS Northumberland anchored off Jamestown, Saint Helena, carrying the defeated Napoleon. On this remote South Atlantic island he spent his last six years, dying there in 1821.

10-15.title: Cologne Cathedral is completed after 632 years
10-15.description: Kaiser Wilhelm I attended celebrations marking the completion of Cologne Cathedral. Begun in 1248 and left unfinished for centuries, the Gothic church was completed using its medieval plans.

10-15.title: Mata Hari is executed by a French firing squad
10-15.description: The Dutch-born dancer Margaretha Zelle, known as Mata Hari, was shot at Vincennes after conviction as a German spy. Historians still dispute how much, if any, useful intelligence she passed on.

10-16.title: Wu Zetian proclaims herself emperor of China
10-16.description: Wu Zetian, long the power behind the Tang throne, took the title of emperor and founded her own Zhou dynasty. She remains the only woman to rule China in her own name, and expanded recruitment by examination.

10-16.title: Marie Antoinette is guillotined in Paris
10-16.description: After a two-day trial before the Revolutionary Tribunal, the former queen Marie Antoinette was executed on the Place de la Révolution. She was 37, and her husband Louis XVI had been executed nine months earlier.
