10-16.title: The Battle of Leipzig begins
10-16.description: Austrian, Prussian, Russian and Swedish armies attacked Napoleon around Leipzig. With some 600,000 soldiers engaged over three days, the 'Battle of the Nations' was the largest in Europe before the First World War.

10-16.title: Margaret Sanger opens the first US birth control clinic
10-16.description: Margaret Sanger, her sister and a colleague opened a birth control clinic in Brownsville, Brooklyn. Police closed it nine days later, but Sanger's campaign led to the organisation that became Planned Parenthood.

10-16.title: Ten Nazi leaders are hanged at Nuremberg
10-16.description: Ten men sentenced by the International Military Tribunal, including Ribbentrop, Keitel and Streicher, were hanged in Nuremberg prison's gymnasium. Göring had taken poison the night before.

10-17.title: The English capture David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross
10-17.description: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.

10-17.title: Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga
10-17.description: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.

10-17.title: Edison files his first motion picture caveat
10-17.description: Thomas Edison filed a patent caveat describing an 'optical phonograph' to record and reproduce moving images. The idea, developed largely by his assistant William Dickson, became the Kinetoscope.

10-17.title: The Queen opens Calder Hall nuclear power station
10-17.description: Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumberland, the world's first nuclear power station to supply electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale. It also produced plutonium for Britain's weapons programme.

10-17.title: Mother Teresa is named winner of the Nobel Peace Prize
10-17.description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced its Peace Prize for Mother Teresa, founder of the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, for her work among the poorest and dying.

10-18.title: Caliph al-Hakim has the Holy Sepulchre demolished
10-18.description: On the orders of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem was torn down. Its destruction shocked Christendom and was remembered as a grievance when the First Crusade was preached.

10-18.title: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes
10-18.description: By the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship in France. Some 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad to England, the Dutch Republic and Prussia, taking valuable skills with them.

10-18.title: Mason and Dixon complete their boundary survey
10-18.description: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon finished surveying the boundary between Pennsylvania and Maryland. Their line later became the symbolic divide between free and slave states.

10-18.title: The United States takes possession of Alaska
10-18.description: At Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag raised, formally transferring Alaska, bought for 7.2 million dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' until gold and oil proved its value.

10-18.title: The British Broadcasting Company is founded
10-18.description: Wireless manufacturers formed the British Broadcasting Company to run Britain's first national radio service. Under John Reith it became the public British Broadcasting Corporation in 1927.

10-19.title: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama
10-19.description: Publius Cornelius Scipio defeated Hannibal near Zama in North Africa; 19 October is the traditional date. The victory ended the Second Punic War, leaving Rome dominant in the western Mediterranean.

10-19.title: King John dies at Newark Castle
10-19.description: King John died of dysentery at Newark during a civil war with his barons and a French invasion. His nine-year-old son became Henry III, and his regents reissued Magna Carta to win back support.

10-19.title: Cornwallis's army surrenders at Yorktown
10-19.description: Besieged by American and French forces, Lord Cornwallis's army of about 8,000 surrendered at Yorktown, Virginia. The defeat effectively ended major fighting in the American Revolutionary War.

10-19.title: Napoleon retreats after defeat at Leipzig
10-19.description: The Battle of the Nations ended with Napoleon's army in retreat from Leipzig, its rearguard trapped when a bridge was blown too early. He lost control of Germany, and the Allies invaded France within months.

10-19.title: Black Monday: stock markets crash worldwide
10-19.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 508 points, or 22.6 per cent, its largest one-day percentage fall. Markets crashed worldwide, though the wider economy recovered far faster than after 1929.

10-20.title: Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands
10-20.description: The death of Emperor Charles VI left his 23-year-old daughter Maria Theresa ruler of Austria, Hungary and Bohemia. She fought off Frederick the Great's challenge and reformed the state over a 40-year reign.

10-20.title: The US Senate ratifies the Louisiana Purchase
10-20.description: The Senate approved the treaty buying Louisiana from France by 24 votes to 7. For 15 million dollars, the United States gained some 828,000 square miles, roughly doubling its territory.

10-20.title: Allied fleets destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian navy at Navarino
10-20.description: British, French and Russian squadrons destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet in Navarino Bay, Greece. The last major battle fought entirely by sailing ships, it secured Greek independence.

10-20.title: US forces land on Leyte as MacArthur returns
10-20.description: American troops landed on Leyte, and General Douglas MacArthur waded ashore to fulfil his 1942 promise to return to the Philippines. Days later, the Battle of Leyte Gulf crippled the Japanese navy.

10-20.title: Muammar Gaddafi is captured and killed near Sirte
10-20.description: Rebel fighters captured Muammar Gaddafi near his hometown of Sirte and killed him shortly afterwards. His death ended 42 years of rule and the Libyan civil war.

10-21.title: Seljuk Turks destroy the People's Crusade at Civetot
10-21.description: The undisciplined People's Crusade, inspired by Peter the Hermit, was ambushed and annihilated by Seljuk forces near Civetot in Anatolia. On its way east, the movement had massacred Jewish communities in the Rhineland.

10-21.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the Battle of Sekigahara
10-21.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated a coalition of western lords at Sekigahara, helped by defections mid-battle. The victory led to the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled a largely peaceful Japan for more than 250 years.

10-21.title: Nelson defeats the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar
10-21.description: Admiral Horatio Nelson's fleet destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar, ending Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain. Nelson was mortally wounded by a musket ball during the battle.

10-21.title: Edison's carbon-filament lamp begins a 13-hour test
10-21.description: At Menlo Park, Thomas Edison's team lit a bulb with a carbonised cotton-thread filament that glowed for about 13.5 hours. The result made long-lasting electric lighting practical.

10-21.title: A colliery spoil tip engulfs a school at Aberfan
10-21.description: A coal waste tip slid down onto the Welsh village of Aberfan, burying Pantglas Junior School. The disaster killed 144 people, 116 of them children, and an inquiry blamed the National Coal Board.

10-22.title: Emperor Kanmu moves Japan's capital to Heian-kyō
10-22.description: On the 22nd day of the tenth month, Emperor Kanmu formally moved his court to the new capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial seat for over a thousand years; the Jidai Matsuri festival marks the date.

10-22.title: Peter the Great takes the title of emperor
10-22.description: After victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War, the Russian Senate conferred on Peter I the titles 'the Great' and Emperor of All Russia (22 October, Old Style). Russia was now formally an empire and a European great power.

10-22.title: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute descent from a balloon
10-22.description: Over the Parc Monceau in Paris, André-Jacques Garnerin cut his parachute free of a hydrogen balloon at about 1,000 metres. He landed safely despite violent swinging, the first frameless silk parachute jump.

10-22.title: Sam Houston becomes the first president of the Republic of Texas
10-22.description: Sam Houston, victor of San Jacinto, was inaugurated as the first elected president of the Republic of Texas at Columbia. Texas remained an independent republic until joining the United States in 1845.

10-22.title: Kennedy tells Americans of Soviet missiles in Cuba
10-22.description: In a televised address, John F. Kennedy revealed that Soviet nuclear missile sites were being built in Cuba and announced a naval 'quarantine' of the island. The crisis brought the superpowers closer to nuclear war than ever before.

10-23.title: Archbishop Ussher's date for the Creation
10-23.description: In his chronology of 1650, Archbishop James Ussher calculated from biblical genealogies that the world was created on the evening before Sunday 23 October 4004 BCE. The date was printed in many English Bibles for two centuries.

10-23.title: Royalists and Parliamentarians clash at Edgehill
10-23.description: Charles I's army fought Parliament's forces under the Earl of Essex at Edgehill in Warwickshire, the first pitched battle of the English Civil War. The indecisive result made clear the war would be long.

10-23.title: The Hungarian Revolution begins in Budapest
10-23.description: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a national uprising against the communist government and Soviet control. Soviet forces crushed it in November, leaving some 2,500 Hungarians dead and 200,000 in exile.

10-23.title: Truck bombs kill 241 US and 58 French troops in Beirut
10-23.description: Suicide bombers drove explosive-laden trucks into the US Marine barracks and a French paratroop building in Beirut. The attacks led to the withdrawal of the multinational peacekeeping force from Lebanon.

10-24.title: The Treaty of Brétigny is ratified at Calais
10-24.description: Edward III and John II of France ratified at Calais the peace agreed at Brétigny in May. England gained Aquitaine and Calais in full sovereignty and a huge ransom for the captured French king, pausing the Hundred Years' War.

10-24.title: The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War
10-24.description: Treaties signed at Münster and Osnabrück ended the Thirty Years' War, which had devastated central Europe. The settlement confirmed the autonomy of the German princes and recognised Dutch and Swiss independence.

10-24.title: Black Thursday: panic selling hits Wall Street
10-24.description: Nearly 13 million shares changed hands as panic swept the New York Stock Exchange. Bankers briefly steadied prices, but the crash that followed the next week opened the way to the Great Depression.

10-24.title: The United Nations comes into being
10-24.description: The United Nations Charter entered into force once a majority of signatories, including the five permanent Security Council members, had ratified it. The date is celebrated annually as United Nations Day.

10-24.title: Concorde makes its last commercial flight
10-24.description: British Airways Concorde flight BA002 from New York landed at Heathrow, ending 27 years of supersonic passenger travel. The aircraft could cross the Atlantic in about three and a half hours.

10-25.title: Geoffrey Chaucer dies in London
10-25.description: Geoffrey Chaucer died, according to the date on his tomb in Westminster Abbey. His Canterbury Tales, written in English rather than French or Latin, helped establish English as a literary language.

10-25.title: Henry V defeats a larger French army at Agincourt
10-25.description: Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army, largely archers, defeated the French at Agincourt as heavily armoured knights struggled across muddy ground. Many French nobles were killed or captured.

10-25.title: George III becomes king of Great Britain
10-25.description: George II died suddenly at Kensington Palace, and his 22-year-old grandson succeeded as George III. His 60-year reign saw the loss of the American colonies and victory over Napoleonic France.

10-25.title: The Light Brigade charges at Balaclava
10-25.description: A misunderstood order sent British light cavalry charging down a valley ringed by Russian guns. About 270 of some 670 riders were killed or wounded, and Tennyson's poem made the charge a byword for courage and blunder.

10-25.title: Japan launches its first organised kamikaze attacks
10-25.description: During the Battle of Leyte Gulf, Japanese pilots deliberately crashed their aircraft into American ships, sinking the escort carrier St. Lo. Suicide attacks became a central Japanese tactic for the rest of the war.

10-26.title: Alfred the Great dies
10-26.description: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.

10-26.title: The Erie Canal opens
10-26.description: Governor DeWitt Clinton set off from Buffalo on the newly completed Erie Canal, which linked Lake Erie to the Hudson River over 363 miles. Cheap transport to the Midwest made New York City the nation's leading port.

10-26.title: The gunfight near the O.K. Corral erupts in Tombstone
10-26.description: Wyatt, Virgil and Morgan Earp and Doc Holliday shot dead Billy Clanton and Tom and Frank McLaury in about 30 seconds in Tombstone, Arizona. The fight became the Wild West's most famous legend.

10-26.title: Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims the Republic of Vietnam
10-26.description: After a heavily rigged referendum deposed the former emperor Bảo Đại, Ngô Đình Diệm proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam in the south. US support for the regime drew America into the Vietnam War.

10-26.title: Russian forces end the Moscow theatre siege with gas
10-26.description: Special forces pumped an incapacitating chemical into a Moscow theatre where Chechen militants held some 850 hostages. The attackers were killed, but about 130 hostages died, mostly from the gas's effects.

10-27.title: Amsterdam is first mentioned in a charter
10-27.description: Count Floris V of Holland granted toll exemption to the people living near the dam on the Amstel. The charter is the earliest document to mention Amsterdam, then a small fishing settlement.

10-27.title: Michael Servetus is burned for heresy in Geneva
10-27.description: Geneva's council, with John Calvin's backing, had the Spanish physician and theologian Michael Servetus burned for denying the Trinity. His death became a landmark in arguments for religious toleration.

10-27.title: William Penn arrives to found Pennsylvania
10-27.description: William Penn reached the Delaware River aboard the Welcome to take possession of his new colony. He laid out Philadelphia as a planned 'greene Countrie Towne' that later hosted the Declaration of Independence.

10-27.title: The first Federalist essay is published
10-27.description: Writing as 'Publius', Alexander Hamilton published the first of 85 essays urging New Yorkers to ratify the new US Constitution. With Madison and Jay he produced the most influential commentary on the Constitution.

10-27.title: The New York City Subway opens
10-27.description: The Interborough Rapid Transit Company opened New York's first underground line, from City Hall to 145th Street. Around 150,000 people rode on the first day of a network that grew into one of the world's largest.

10-28.title: Constantine defeats Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge
10-28.description: Constantine's army defeated his rival Maxentius outside Rome, and Maxentius drowned in the Tiber. Constantine credited the Christian God with his victory and went on to legalise and favour Christianity.

10-28.title: Columbus reaches Cuba
10-28.description: On his first voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the north-east coast of Cuba. Convinced he was near Asia, he sent envoys inland in search of the court of the Great Khan.

10-28.title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated in New York Harbor
10-28.description: President Grover Cleveland dedicated Liberty Enlightening the World, a gift from the people of France, on Bedloe's Island. The statue became a symbol of welcome for millions of immigrants.

10-28.title: Italy invades Greece from Albania
10-28.description: Mussolini's forces invaded Greece after Prime Minister Metaxas rejected an ultimatum. The Greeks drove the Italians back into Albania, and Germany invaded the following spring to rescue its ally.

10-28.title: Angelo Roncalli is elected Pope John XXIII
10-28.description: The 76-year-old patriarch of Venice was elected pope, widely seen as a caretaker. Within three months he announced the Second Vatican Council, which transformed the Catholic Church.

10-29.title: Sir Walter Raleigh is beheaded at Westminster
10-29.description: Courtier, poet and explorer Sir Walter Raleigh was executed in Old Palace Yard under a treason sentence from 1603. James I revived it after Raleigh's failed expedition to Guiana attacked a Spanish settlement.

10-29.title: Mozart's Don Giovanni premieres in Prague
10-29.description: Mozart conducted the first performance of Don Giovanni at the Estates Theatre in Prague. The opera, with a libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte, blends comedy and the supernatural and is ranked among the greatest ever written.

10-29.title: A Geneva conference founds the Red Cross movement
10-29.description: An international conference called by the Geneva committee of Henri Dunant closed by adopting resolutions for national relief societies for wounded soldiers. The Red Cross movement and the 1864 Geneva Convention followed.

10-29.title: Black Tuesday: the Wall Street Crash deepens
10-29.description: More than 16 million shares were sold in a day of panic on the New York Stock Exchange. Black Tuesday became the emblem of the crash that preceded the Great Depression.

10-29.title: Hurricane Sandy makes landfall in New Jersey
10-29.description: Sandy came ashore near Atlantic City, bringing a record storm surge that flooded lower Manhattan and the New York subway. Across the Caribbean and North America it killed more than 230 people.

10-30.title: Antioch surrenders to the Arab armies
10-30.description: After the Battle of the Iron Bridge, Antioch surrendered to Muslim forces under Abu Ubayda. The fall of the great Syrian city was part of the rapid conquests that stripped Byzantium of its eastern provinces.

10-30.title: The Treaty of Tunis ends the Eighth Crusade
10-30.description: After Louis IX died of disease outside Tunis, his brother Charles of Anjou negotiated a treaty with the sultan of Tunis and the crusaders withdrew. Louis was canonised in 1297.

10-30.title: Henry VII is crowned, beginning the Tudor dynasty
10-30.description: Henry Tudor was crowned at Westminster Abbey two months after defeating Richard III at Bosworth. His marriage to Elizabeth of York united the rival houses of the Wars of the Roses.

10-30.title: The Armistice of Mudros takes the Ottomans out of the war
10-30.description: Ottoman and British representatives signed an armistice aboard HMS Agamemnon off Lemnos. Allied occupation and partition plans followed, provoking the Turkish national movement led by Mustafa Kemal.

10-30.title: Orson Welles broadcasts The War of the Worlds
10-30.description: CBS aired Orson Welles's radio adaptation of H. G. Wells's novel as a series of mock news bulletins about a Martian landing in New Jersey. Some listeners were alarmed, though newspapers exaggerated the 'panic'.

10-30.title: The Soviet Union tests the Tsar Bomba
10-30.description: A Soviet bomber dropped the largest nuclear weapon ever exploded over Novaya Zemlya in the Arctic. Its yield of about 50 megatons was some 3,000 times that of the Hiroshima bomb.

10-31.title: Romulus Augustulus is proclaimed western Roman emperor
10-31.description: The general Orestes installed his young son Romulus as emperor in the West. Less than a year later Odoacer deposed him, an event conventionally taken as the end of the Western Roman Empire.

10-31.title: Martin Luther issues his Ninety-five Theses
10-31.description: Martin Luther sent his Ninety-five Theses against the sale of indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz and, by tradition, posted them on the church door at Wittenberg. The debate they sparked became the Reformation.

10-31.title: Nevada becomes the 36th US state
10-31.description: Nevada was admitted to the Union during the Civil War, with Republicans keen on its votes for Lincoln's re-election and support for the 13th Amendment. It is still called the 'Battle Born State'.

10-31.title: Britain and France begin bombing Egypt over Suez
10-31.description: British and French aircraft attacked Egyptian airfields after Egypt rejected their ultimatum to withdraw from the Suez Canal zone. US and Soviet pressure forced a humiliating withdrawal.

10-31.title: Indira Gandhi is assassinated by her bodyguards
10-31.description: Two Sikh bodyguards shot Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in her Delhi garden, months after she ordered the army into the Golden Temple at Amritsar. Anti-Sikh violence that followed killed about 3,000 people.

10-31.title: World population reaches seven billion, UN estimates
10-31.description: The United Nations designated 31 October 2011 as the symbolic day the world's population reached seven billion. The total had doubled since the late 1960s.

11-01.title: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling is shown to the public
11-01.description: After four years of work, Michelangelo's ceiling frescoes in the Sistine Chapel were unveiled for the feast of All Saints. Its scenes from Genesis, including the Creation of Adam, became a pinnacle of Renaissance art.

11-01.title: Othello is performed before James I at Whitehall
11-01.description: The King's Men performed Shakespeare's Othello in the Banqueting House at Whitehall, the earliest recorded performance of the play. Its tragedy of jealousy and manipulation remains among his most performed works.

11-01.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Lisbon
11-01.description: On All Saints' Day a massive earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The catastrophe stirred Enlightenment debates on providence and spurred early seismology.

11-01.title: John Adams becomes the first president to live in the White House
11-01.description: John Adams moved into the unfinished President's House in Washington. The next day he wrote to his wife Abigail: 'May none but honest and wise men ever rule under this roof.'

11-01.title: The first medical school for women opens in Boston
11-01.description: Samuel Gregory opened the Boston Female Medical School, later the New England Female Medical College, with twelve students. It was the first institution founded to train women in medicine.

11-01.title: Von Spee's squadron defeats the Royal Navy at Coronel
11-01.description: Off the coast of Chile, Admiral Maximilian von Spee's German East Asia Squadron sank two British cruisers, killing Rear-Admiral Cradock and some 1,600 men. It was Britain's first naval defeat in a century.

11-01.title: The Maastricht Treaty creates the European Union
11-01.description: The Treaty on European Union came into force, establishing the EU alongside the European Communities. It introduced EU citizenship and set the path to economic and monetary union and the euro.

11-02.title: Washington issues his farewell orders to the Continental Army
11-02.description: From Rocky Hill, New Jersey, George Washington issued his Farewell Orders to the Armies of the United States. Weeks later he resigned his commission, setting a precedent of civilian control.

11-02.title: North and South Dakota become US states
11-02.description: President Benjamin Harrison signed proclamations admitting North and South Dakota on the same day. He shuffled the papers so no one would know which was signed first.

11-02.title: The Balfour Declaration backs a Jewish home in Palestine
11-02.description: Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild that Britain favoured 'a national home for the Jewish people' in Palestine, without prejudice to existing non-Jewish communities. Its consequences still shape the region.

11-02.title: Haile Selassie is crowned Emperor of Ethiopia
11-02.description: Ras Tafari Makonnen was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie I in Addis Ababa before foreign dignitaries. He ruled Ethiopia, with an interruption during Italian occupation, until his overthrow in 1974.

11-02.title: The BBC launches the world's first regular high-definition TV service
11-02.description: From Alexandra Palace in north London, the BBC began a regular public television service in what was then called high definition. It was suspended during the Second World War and resumed in 1946.

11-02.title: The first crew moves into the International Space Station
11-02.description: Expedition 1, an American astronaut and two Russian cosmonauts, docked at the International Space Station. Since then the station has been continuously occupied by humans.

11-03.title: Constantius II dies, leaving Julian sole emperor
11-03.description: Constantius II died in Cilicia while marching against his cousin Julian, who became sole Roman emperor. Julian, the last pagan emperor, tried to revive traditional cults but was killed fighting Persia in 363.

11-03.title: Henry VII and Charles VIII make peace at Étaples
11-03.description: The Peace of Étaples ended Henry VII's brief invasion of France: Charles VIII paid him a large sum and agreed to stop supporting Yorkist pretenders. The treaty helped secure the new Tudor dynasty.

11-03.title: Olympe de Gouges is guillotined
11-03.description: The playwright Olympe de Gouges, author of the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen, was executed during the Terror for writings attacking the Jacobins.

11-03.title: British and Chinese warships clash at Chuenpi
11-03.description: Royal Navy frigates fought Chinese war junks off Chuenpi near Canton, the first major clash of the First Opium War. The dispute followed Lin Zexu's destruction of British merchants' opium; China lost Hong Kong in 1842.

11-03.title: Laika becomes the first animal to orbit the Earth
11-03.description: The Soviet Union launched the dog Laika aboard Sputnik 2. She died within hours from overheating, but the flight showed a living creature could survive launch and weightlessness.

11-04.title: The Arno floods Florence
11-04.description: After days of heavy rain, the Arno burst its banks and swept away three of Florence's four bridges, including the Ponte Vecchio. The chronicler Giovanni Villani recorded the disaster in detail.

11-04.title: The poet Wilfred Owen is killed in action
11-04.description: Wilfred Owen was killed crossing the Sambre-Oise Canal in France, a week before the armistice. His poems, including 'Dulce et Decorum Est', became the defining English verse of the First World War.

11-04.title: Howard Carter finds the steps to Tutankhamun's tomb
11-04.description: Howard Carter's workers uncovered a step cut into the rock of the Valley of the Kings, leading to the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun. Its treasures caused a worldwide sensation.

11-04.title: Soviet tanks move in to crush the Hungarian Revolution
11-04.description: Soviet forces launched a massive assault on Budapest at dawn, overthrowing Imre Nagy's government. Thousands were killed, and the West did not intervene.

11-04.title: Students seize the US embassy in Tehran
11-04.description: Iranian students occupied the US embassy in Tehran and took 66 hostages. Fifty-two were held for 444 days, a crisis that soured US-Iranian relations and damaged Jimmy Carter's presidency.

11-04.title: Barack Obama is elected president
11-04.description: Barack Obama defeated John McCain to become the first African American elected president of the United States, 45 years after Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream' speech.

11-05.title: The Council of Constance opens
11-05.description: A general council met at Constance to end the Great Schism, in which three men claimed the papacy. It deposed two, accepted the resignation of the third and elected Martin V, but also condemned Jan Hus to the stake.

11-05.title: Guy Fawkes is arrested beneath Parliament
11-05.description: Shortly after midnight, Guy Fawkes was caught guarding gunpowder in a cellar under the House of Lords, foiling a Catholic plot to kill James I. Bonfires were lit in celebration, beginning the tradition of Bonfire Night.

11-05.title: British and French troops repel the Russians at Inkerman
11-05.description: In thick fog, Russian columns attacked British positions above Sevastopol. Fighting in small groups with little direction, the British, reinforced by the French, held the ridge in what became known as the 'Soldiers' Battle'.

11-05.title: Woodrow Wilson is elected US president
11-05.description: With Theodore Roosevelt and William Howard Taft splitting the Republican vote, the Democrat Woodrow Wilson won the presidency. He created the Federal Reserve and led America into the First World War.

11-05.title: Saddam Hussein is sentenced to death
11-05.description: An Iraqi tribunal sentenced Saddam Hussein to hang for the killing of 148 Shia men and boys from Dujail after a 1982 assassination attempt. He was executed on 30 December 2006.

11-06.title: Abraham Lincoln is elected president
11-06.description: Abraham Lincoln won the presidency with under 40 per cent of the popular vote, carrying only northern states. His victory prompted South Carolina to secede within weeks, followed by six more states.

11-06.title: Rutgers and Princeton play the first college football game
11-06.description: Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 in New Brunswick, New Jersey, in the first intercollegiate football match. The rules resembled soccer more than modern American football.

11-06.title: Gandhi is arrested leading a march of Indian miners
11-06.description: In South Africa, Gandhi was arrested at Palmford while leading over 2,000 striking Indian workers across the Transvaal border in defiance of discriminatory laws. The campaign won concessions in 1914.

11-06.title: Canadian troops capture Passchendaele
11-06.description: Canadian forces took the ruined village of Passchendaele, ending the Third Battle of Ypres. The British-led offensive had gained a few miles of Flemish mud at a cost of hundreds of thousands of casualties.

11-06.title: The UN General Assembly calls for sanctions on South Africa
11-06.description: Resolution 1761 condemned apartheid and urged member states to break diplomatic ties and boycott South African trade. It also set up a special committee against apartheid.

11-07.title: The Oxford Gazette, later the London Gazette, is first published
11-07.description: With the court in Oxford to escape the plague, the first issue of the Oxford Gazette appeared. Renamed the London Gazette, it is the oldest continuously published newspaper in Britain.

11-07.title: A pro-slavery mob kills Elijah Lovejoy
11-07.description: The abolitionist editor Elijah Lovejoy was shot defending his fourth printing press from a mob in Alton, Illinois. His death turned many northerners towards the anti-slavery cause.

11-07.title: Marie Curie is born in Warsaw
11-07.description: Maria Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, then under Russian rule. As Marie Curie she pioneered research on radioactivity and became the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two sciences.

11-07.title: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd
11-07.description: Bolshevik-led Red Guards took key points in Petrograd and stormed the Winter Palace overnight, toppling the Provisional Government. The October Revolution, so called from the Julian calendar, led to the Soviet state.

11-07.title: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapses
11-07.description: Four months after opening, the suspension bridge over Puget Sound twisted violently in a 40-mile-per-hour wind and fell into the water. Filmed footage of 'Galloping Gertie' transformed bridge aerodynamics.

11-08.title: Cortés enters Tenochtitlan and meets Moctezuma
11-08.description: Hernán Cortés and his Spanish and Tlaxcalan allies were received in the Aztec capital by Moctezuma II. Within days the Spaniards took the emperor hostage, and the city fell to siege in 1521.

11-08.title: The Bodleian Library opens in Oxford
11-08.description: Sir Thomas Bodley's refounded library opened to scholars at Oxford with about 2,000 books. It became one of Europe's great research libraries, now holding over 13 million printed items.

11-08.title: Wilhelm Röntgen discovers X-rays
11-08.description: Experimenting with a cathode-ray tube in Würzburg, Wilhelm Röntgen noticed a glowing screen across the room and identified a new penetrating radiation. X-rays transformed medicine and won him the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

11-08.title: Hitler launches the Beer Hall Putsch in Munich
11-08.description: Adolf Hitler burst into a Munich beer hall and proclaimed a national revolution. The coup collapsed under police fire the next day; Hitler served nine months of a five-year sentence, writing Mein Kampf.

11-08.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt is elected president
11-08.description: In the depths of the Great Depression, Franklin Roosevelt defeated Herbert Hoover in a landslide. His New Deal reshaped American government, and he was elected a record four times.

11-09.title: The Seventeenth Council of Toledo orders the enslavement of Jews
11-09.description: Accusing Jews of conspiracy, the council called by King Egica decreed the enslavement of Jews in Visigothic Spain and the removal of their children. It was among the harshest anti-Jewish measures of the early Middle Ages.

11-09.title: Napoleon's coup of 18 Brumaire topples the Directory
11-09.description: Napoleon Bonaparte and his allies began a coup against the Directory, completed the next day. The new Consulate made Napoleon First Consul and effective ruler of France.

11-09.title: Wilhelm II's abdication is announced as Germany becomes a republic
11-09.description: With revolution spreading, Chancellor Max von Baden announced the Kaiser's abdication and Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a republic in Berlin. Wilhelm fled to the Netherlands the next day.

11-09.title: Kristallnacht: Nazi pogroms sweep Germany and Austria
11-09.description: Over two nights, Nazi mobs burned hundreds of synagogues, wrecked about 7,500 Jewish businesses and killed at least 91 people. About 30,000 Jewish men were sent to concentration camps.

11-09.title: The Berlin Wall opens
11-09.description: After a confused announcement that East Germans could travel freely, crowds pressed the border crossings until guards opened the gates. The fall of the Wall led to German reunification within a year.

11-10.title: The Fourth Crusade lays siege to the Christian city of Zara
11-10.description: Crusaders unable to pay the Venetians for their fleet arrived at Zara on the Dalmatian coast and besieged it for Venice. The city fell within two weeks, and Pope Innocent III excommunicated the crusaders.

11-10.title: The Continental Congress creates the Continental Marines
11-10.description: The Continental Congress resolved to raise two battalions of Marines. The date is celebrated as the birthday of the United States Marine Corps.

11-10.title: Henry Morton Stanley finds David Livingstone at Ujiji
11-10.description: The journalist Henry Morton Stanley located the missionary-explorer David Livingstone at Ujiji, on Lake Tanganyika, by Stanley's own dating. His reported greeting, 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?', became famous.

11-10.title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk dies in Istanbul
11-10.description: Atatürk, founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey, died at Dolmabahçe Palace. Turks still pause at 9.05 in the morning on this day to mark the moment of his death.

11-10.title: The freighter Edmund Fitzgerald sinks in Lake Superior
11-10.description: The ore carrier SS Edmund Fitzgerald sank in a violent storm on Lake Superior with the loss of all 29 crew. It is the largest ship lost on the Great Lakes.

11-11.title: Pope Innocent III opens the Fourth Lateran Council
11-11.description: The largest church council of the Middle Ages met in Rome under Innocent III. It defined transubstantiation, required annual confession and ordered Jews and Muslims to wear distinguishing dress.

11-11.title: Nat Turner is hanged in Virginia
11-11.description: Nat Turner was executed at Jerusalem, Virginia, for leading the August revolt in which about 55 to 60 white people were killed. Reprisals killed many more Black people, and southern states tightened slave codes.

11-11.title: The armistice ends fighting on the Western Front
11-11.description: Signed at 5 a.m. in a railway carriage in the forest of Compiègne, the armistice between Germany and the Allies took effect at 11 o'clock. The day is marked as Armistice or Remembrance Day.

11-11.title: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is dedicated at Arlington
11-11.description: President Harding presided as an unidentified American soldier from the Western Front was buried at Arlington National Cemetery. A year earlier, Britain and France had interred their own unknown warriors.

11-11.title: Rhodesia declares independence from Britain
11-11.description: Ian Smith's white minority government issued a Unilateral Declaration of Independence to avoid majority rule. Britain and the UN imposed sanctions, and after a long guerrilla war Zimbabwe became independent in 1980.

11-12.title: Zoe becomes Byzantine empress with Romanos III
11-12.description: As her father Constantine VIII lay dying, Zoe was married to Romanos III, who became emperor. She went on to share the throne with three husbands, an adopted son and her sister Theodora.

11-12.title: Jules Léotard performs the first flying trapeze act
11-12.description: At the Cirque Napoléon in Paris, Jules Léotard swung between trapezes in the first flying trapeze act. The close-fitting garment he wore still bears his name.

11-12.title: Searchers find the tent of Scott's polar party
11-12.description: A search party found the snow-covered tent containing the bodies of Robert Falcon Scott and two companions, eight months after their deaths returning from the South Pole. Scott's diary told their story.

11-12.title: Austria is proclaimed a republic
11-12.description: A day after Emperor Charles I renounced participation in state affairs, the provisional national assembly in Vienna proclaimed the Republic of German-Austria. Habsburg rule there, dating from 1278, was over.

11-12.title: The Bhola cyclone devastates East Pakistan
11-12.description: A cyclone and storm surge struck the coast of East Pakistan, killing perhaps 300,000 to 500,000 people. Anger at the government's response fed the movement that led to Bangladesh's independence.

11-13.title: Æthelred II orders the St Brice's Day massacre of Danes
11-13.description: King Æthelred the Unready ordered the killing of Danish men in England. Victims reputedly included the sister of Sweyn Forkbeard, who launched repeated invasions and took the English crown in 1013.

11-13.title: Malcolm III of Scotland is killed at Alnwick
11-13.description: Malcolm III was killed in an ambush while besieging Alnwick Castle in Northumberland, together with his eldest son. A succession struggle followed in Scotland.

11-13.title: American forces occupy Montreal
11-13.description: Continental troops under Richard Montgomery entered Montreal unopposed during the invasion of Canada. The campaign collapsed after the failed assault on Quebec City at the end of the year.

11-13.title: Emperor Charles withdraws from Hungarian affairs
11-13.description: At Eckartsau, Charles I renounced any part in Hungary's government, two days after a similar declaration for Austria. Habsburg rule over Austria-Hungary was effectively at an end.

11-13.title: Coordinated terrorist attacks kill 130 in Paris
11-13.description: Islamic State gunmen and suicide bombers attacked the Bataclan concert hall, cafés and the Stade de France. It was the deadliest attack in France since the Second World War, and a state of emergency followed.

11-14.title: Emperor Justinian I dies
11-14.description: Justinian died in Constantinople after a 38-year reign. He reconquered North Africa and Italy, codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis and built the Hagia Sophia.

11-14.title: Moby-Dick is published in New York
11-14.description: Harper and Brothers published Herman Melville's Moby-Dick, a month after its London edition. Poorly received at first, the tale of Captain Ahab's pursuit of the white whale is now a classic of American literature.

11-14.title: Nellie Bly sets out to beat Phileas Fogg's 80 days
11-14.description: New York World reporter Nellie Bly left Hoboken to travel around the world faster than Jules Verne's fictional hero. She returned in just over 72 days, a world record at the time.

11-14.title: The Luftwaffe devastates Coventry
11-14.description: Some 500 German bombers attacked Coventry overnight, killing about 570 people and destroying the medieval cathedral. It was one of the heaviest raids of the Blitz.

11-14.title: Apollo 12 launches for the Moon
11-14.description: Apollo 12 survived two lightning strikes during launch from Cape Kennedy. Five days later Pete Conrad and Alan Bean landed precisely beside the Surveyor 3 probe in the Ocean of Storms.

11-15.title: Swiss confederates ambush the Habsburgs at Morgarten
11-15.description: Men of Schwyz, Uri and Unterwalden ambushed Duke Leopold of Austria's army on a narrow path by Lake Ägeri. The victory strengthened the young Swiss Confederation.

11-15.title: Congress adopts the Articles of Confederation
11-15.description: The Continental Congress approved the Articles of Confederation, the first constitution of the United States. Ratified in 1781, they gave the central government too little power and were replaced in 1789.

11-15.title: Sherman leaves Atlanta on his March to the Sea
11-15.description: After burning much of Atlanta, William T. Sherman's army set off for Savannah. Its destruction of railways, crops and property across Georgia aimed to break the Confederacy's capacity and will to fight.

11-15.title: A military coup makes Brazil a republic
11-15.description: Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca led a coup in Rio de Janeiro that deposed Emperor Pedro II and proclaimed the Republic of Brazil. The 64-year-old emperor went into exile in Europe.

11-15.title: The League of Nations holds its first Assembly
11-15.description: Delegates of 41 nations met in Geneva for the first Assembly of the League of Nations. Weakened by the absence of the United States, the League failed to prevent the aggression of the 1930s.

11-16.title: Queen Margaret of Scotland dies
11-16.description: Margaret, wife of Malcolm III, died in Edinburgh Castle days after learning that her husband and eldest son had been killed at Alnwick. Celebrated for her piety and church reform, she was canonised in 1250.

11-16.title: Pizarro captures the Inca ruler Atahualpa at Cajamarca
11-16.description: Francisco Pizarro's force of fewer than 200 men ambushed Atahualpa's retinue in the square of Cajamarca, killing thousands. Holding the Inca ruler captive gave the Spanish leverage over a vast empire.

11-16.title: The British capture Fort Washington on Manhattan
11-16.description: British and Hessian troops stormed Fort Washington, the last American stronghold on Manhattan, and took about 2,800 prisoners. Washington's army retreated across New Jersey.

11-16.title: UNESCO's constitution is signed in London
11-16.description: Delegates of 37 countries signed the constitution of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. It promotes cooperation in education, science and culture and lists World Heritage Sites.

11-16.title: Benazir Bhutto's party wins Pakistan's general election
11-16.description: The Pakistan Peoples Party, led by Benazir Bhutto, won the most seats in the first open election in over a decade. Weeks later she became the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority democracy.

11-17.title: Elizabeth I becomes queen of England
11-17.description: On the death of her half-sister Mary I, the 25-year-old Elizabeth succeeded to the throne. Her 44-year reign brought a Protestant church settlement, the defeat of the Spanish Armada and a flowering of literature.

11-17.title: The Suez Canal opens
11-17.description: Empress Eugénie of France led a procession of ships through the new canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. It cut thousands of kilometres from the sea route between Europe and Asia.

11-17.title: Luna 17 lands Lunokhod 1 on the Moon
11-17.description: The Soviet Luna 17 landed in the Sea of Rains and released Lunokhod 1, the first remote-controlled rover on another world. Driven from Earth, it travelled about 10 kilometres over ten months.

11-17.title: Greek troops crush the Athens Polytechnic uprising
11-17.description: A tank broke through the gates of the Athens Polytechnic, ending a student occupation against the military junta. Dozens were killed, and the junta fell the following summer.

11-17.title: Police attack students in Prague, sparking the Velvet Revolution
11-17.description: Riot police beat students at a Prague march marking the anniversary of a Nazi crackdown. Outrage fuelled mass protests that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia within six weeks.

11-18.title: Old St Peter's Basilica is dedicated, by tradition
11-18.description: According to church tradition, Pope Sylvester I dedicated Constantine's basilica over the site of St Peter's tomb on the Vatican Hill. It stood for some 1,200 years before being replaced by the present church.

11-18.title: William Tell shoots the apple, according to legend
11-18.description: Swiss tradition dates to this day William Tell's shot at an apple on his son's head in Altdorf, ordered by the Habsburg bailiff Gessler. Historians regard the tale as legend, but it became a symbol of Swiss liberty.

11-18.title: Caxton completes the first dated book printed in England
11-18.description: At Westminster, William Caxton finished printing The Dictes or Sayengis of the Philosophres, the first book printed in England to carry a date. Printing in English helped standardise the language.

11-18.title: Pope Urban VIII consecrates the new St Peter's Basilica
11-18.description: Exactly 1,300 years after the traditional dedication of the first basilica, Urban VIII consecrated the new St Peter's. Its design involved Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno over 120 years.

11-18.title: Latvia proclaims its independence
11-18.description: The People's Council in Riga declared an independent Latvian state. After a war of independence it remained free until Soviet occupation in 1940, regaining independence in 1991.

11-19.title: Columbus lands on Puerto Rico
11-19.description: On his second voyage, Christopher Columbus landed on the island the Taíno called Borikén and named it San Juan Bautista. The name of its port, Puerto Rico, later passed to the whole island.

11-19.title: The Jay Treaty is signed in London
11-19.description: John Jay and Lord Grenville signed a treaty settling disputes left over from the Revolutionary War, including British forts in the north-west. Unpopular in America, it nonetheless averted war with Britain.

11-19.title: Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address
11-19.description: At the dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, Abraham Lincoln spoke for about two minutes. His short address recast the Civil War as a struggle for 'a new birth of freedom' and government 'of the people'.

11-19.title: The Red Army launches Operation Uranus at Stalingrad
11-19.description: Soviet forces attacked the weak Romanian-held flanks north and south of Stalingrad. Within four days they encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943.

11-19.title: Anwar Sadat becomes the first Arab leader to visit Israel
11-19.description: Egypt's president Anwar Sadat flew to Israel and the next day addressed the Knesset in Jerusalem. His visit led to the Camp David Accords and the 1979 Egyptian-Israeli peace treaty.

11-20.title: Edward I is proclaimed king while returning from crusade
11-20.description: Four days after Henry III's death, his son Edward was proclaimed king though still abroad. Edward I conquered Wales, expelled England's Jews in 1290 and waged long wars against Scotland.

11-20.title: Hawke defeats the French fleet at Quiberon Bay
11-20.description: In a gale off Brittany, Admiral Edward Hawke pursued the French fleet among the rocks and shoals of Quiberon Bay and destroyed or scattered it. The victory ended French plans to invade Britain.

11-20.title: A sperm whale sinks the whaleship Essex
11-20.description: In the South Pacific, an enraged sperm whale rammed and sank the Nantucket whaleship Essex. Survivors spent about three months in open boats, resorting to cannibalism; the story inspired Moby-Dick.

11-20.title: British tanks attack in mass at Cambrai
11-20.description: Some 476 British tanks led a surprise attack at Cambrai, breaking through German lines several miles in a day. A German counter-attack soon recovered most of the ground, but the tactics pointed to the future.

11-20.title: The Nuremberg trials begin
11-20.description: The International Military Tribunal opened at Nuremberg to try 22 senior Nazi leaders for war crimes, crimes against peace and crimes against humanity. The trial laid foundations for international criminal law.

11-21.title: Mayflower passengers sign the Mayflower Compact
11-21.description: Anchored off Cape Cod, 41 male passengers of the Mayflower signed a compact binding themselves into a 'civil body politic'. The agreement became an early landmark of self-government by consent in English America.

11-21.title: Two Frenchmen make the first free flight in a balloon
11-21.description: Pilâtre de Rozier and the Marquis d'Arlandes rose from the Bois de Boulogne in a Montgolfier hot-air balloon and drifted about 9 kilometres across Paris in 25 minutes, the first untethered human flight.

11-21.title: Edison announces his phonograph
11-21.description: Thomas Edison announced his invention of the phonograph, a machine that recorded sound on tinfoil and played it back. It was the first device able to reproduce the human voice.

11-21.title: Bloody Sunday in Dublin
11-21.description: Michael Collins's IRA squad killed 14 men, mostly British intelligence officers, in Dublin that morning. In the afternoon, Crown forces fired on the crowd at a Gaelic football match in Croke Park, killing 14 civilians.

11-21.title: The Dayton Agreement is initialled, ending the Bosnian War
11-21.description: After three weeks of talks at an air base in Ohio, the leaders of Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia initialled a peace agreement. The war had killed about 100,000 people, including some 8,000 at Srebrenica.

11-22.title: Frederick II is crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome
11-22.description: Pope Honorius III crowned Frederick II emperor in St Peter's. Brilliant and controversial, the 'wonder of the world' ruled Germany and Sicily and spent much of his reign in conflict with the papacy.

11-22.title: Vasco da Gama rounds the Cape of Good Hope
11-22.description: Vasco da Gama's Portuguese fleet rounded the southern tip of Africa on its way to India. The voyage opened a direct sea route from Europe to Asia and the rise of a Portuguese trading empire.

11-22.title: President Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas
11-22.description: John F. Kennedy was shot dead while riding in an open motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas. Vice-President Lyndon Johnson was sworn in aboard Air Force One the same afternoon.

11-22.title: Juan Carlos is proclaimed king of Spain
11-22.description: Two days after Franco's death, Juan Carlos de Borbón was proclaimed king. Expected to preserve the dictatorship, he instead guided Spain's transition to a parliamentary democracy.

11-23.title: Seville surrenders to Ferdinand III of Castile
11-23.description: After a siege of more than a year, the Muslim city of Seville surrendered to Ferdinand III of Castile. Its fall left the Nasrid kingdom of Granada as the main surviving Muslim state in Iberia.

11-23.title: The pretender Perkin Warbeck is hanged at Tyburn
11-23.description: Perkin Warbeck, who had claimed to be Richard, Duke of York, the younger of the 'Princes in the Tower', was hanged after a failed escape. His death removed a persistent threat to Henry VII.

11-23.title: John Milton publishes Areopagitica
11-23.description: John Milton issued Areopagitica, an unlicensed pamphlet arguing against Parliament's censorship of printing. It became a classic defence of freedom of the press.

11-23.title: The first coin-operated phonograph plays in San Francisco
11-23.description: Louis Glass installed a coin-in-the-slot phonograph at the Palais Royale Saloon in San Francisco. Listening through tubes, customers paid a nickel a song, the ancestor of the jukebox.

11-23.title: Doctor Who is first broadcast
11-23.description: The BBC broadcast the first episode of Doctor Who, about a time-travelling alien in a police box. It became the longest-running science fiction television series in the world.

11-24.title: Theodosius I enters Constantinople
11-24.description: Emperor Theodosius I made his formal entry into Constantinople. Earlier that year he had declared Nicene Christianity the faith of the empire, and he soon removed the city's Arian bishop.

11-24.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
11-24.description: John Murray published Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, setting out evolution by natural selection. The first printing of 1,250 copies was quickly taken up, and the book transformed biology.

11-24.title: Carter uncovers the sealed doorway of Tutankhamun's tomb
11-24.description: With Lord Carnarvon present, Howard Carter's team cleared the stairway and found a sealed doorway bearing Tutankhamun's name. Two days later they looked inside.

11-24.title: Jack Ruby shoots Lee Harvey Oswald on live television
11-24.description: Nightclub owner Jack Ruby shot Lee Harvey Oswald, accused of killing President Kennedy, in the basement of Dallas police headquarters. Millions saw the shooting live on television.

11-24.title: Fossil hunters find 'Lucy' in Ethiopia
11-24.description: At Hadar, Donald Johanson and Tom Gray found the partial skeleton of a 3.2-million-year-old Australopithecus afarensis. Named Lucy, she showed that human ancestors walked upright long before brains enlarged.

11-25.title: Malcolm II of Scotland dies
11-25.description: Malcolm II died after a 29-year reign and was succeeded by his grandson Duncan I. Duncan was killed in battle by Macbeth in 1040, events Shakespeare reworked freely more than five centuries later.

11-25.title: The last British troops leave New York City
11-25.description: British forces evacuated New York, their last stronghold in the United States, and George Washington led the Continental Army into the city. 'Evacuation Day' was celebrated in New York for over a century.

11-25.title: Union troops storm Missionary Ridge
11-25.description: At Chattanooga, Union soldiers charged up Missionary Ridge beyond their orders and routed Braxton Bragg's Confederate army. The victory opened the way into Georgia.

11-25.title: Hollywood studios blacklist the 'Hollywood Ten'
11-25.description: Studio heads issued the Waldorf Statement, refusing to employ ten writers and directors cited for contempt of Congress. The Hollywood blacklist that followed ended or interrupted hundreds of careers.

11-25.title: Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands
11-25.description: The former colony of Dutch Guiana on South America's north coast became the independent Republic of Suriname. Around a third of its population emigrated to the Netherlands.

11-26.title: Captain Cook sights Maui on his return to Hawaii
11-26.description: On his second visit to the Hawaiian Islands, which he called the Sandwich Islands, James Cook sighted Maui. He was killed at Kealakekua Bay on Hawaii Island less than three months later.

11-26.title: Howard Carter looks into Tutankhamun's tomb
11-26.description: Howard Carter made a small hole in the sealed doorway and peered in by candlelight. Asked if he could see anything, he reportedly replied, 'Yes, wonderful things.'

11-26.title: Casablanca premieres in New York
11-26.description: Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premiered at the Hollywood Theatre weeks after the Allies landed in North Africa. It won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture.

11-26.title: France launches its first satellite
11-26.description: A French Diamant rocket launched the satellite Astérix from Hammaguir in Algeria. France became the third country, after the Soviet Union and the United States, to put a satellite into orbit on its own rocket.

11-27.title: Pope Urban II preaches the First Crusade at Clermont
11-27.description: Closing the Council of Clermont, Urban II urged Western knights to aid Byzantium and free Jerusalem. The response was overwhelming, and crusaders took Jerusalem in 1099.

11-27.title: Anders Celsius is born in Uppsala
11-27.description: The Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius was born. In 1742 he proposed a 100-degree temperature scale, originally with 0 for boiling water; it was later inverted to become the Celsius scale.

11-27.title: Custer's troops attack Black Kettle's camp on the Washita
11-27.description: The 7th Cavalry under George Armstrong Custer attacked a Cheyenne village on the Washita River, killing Black Kettle and many women and children. The army called it a battle; many historians call it a massacre.

11-27.title: Mayor Moscone and Harvey Milk are shot in San Francisco
11-27.description: Former supervisor Dan White shot dead Mayor George Moscone and Supervisor Harvey Milk at City Hall. Milk had been one of the first openly gay elected officials in the United States.

11-28.title: Magellan's ships enter the Pacific
11-28.description: After 38 days navigating the strait at the tip of South America, Ferdinand Magellan's three remaining ships reached the open ocean. He named it the Pacific for its calm waters.

11-28.title: Arthur Griffith launches Sinn Féin's policy
11-28.description: At a convention in Dublin, Arthur Griffith set out the Sinn Féin policy, meaning 'we ourselves', of Irish self-reliance and a separate Irish parliament. The movement later became central to the struggle for independence.

11-28.title: Albania declares independence
11-28.description: In Vlorë, Ismail Qemali raised the Albanian flag and proclaimed independence from the Ottoman Empire during the First Balkan War. The great powers recognised the new state the following year.

11-28.title: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin meet in Tehran
11-28.description: The 'Big Three' met together for the first time at the Tehran Conference. They committed to a cross-Channel invasion of France in 1944 and discussed the shape of post-war Europe.

11-29.title: Cardinal Wolsey dies on his way to face treason charges
11-29.description: Thomas Wolsey, once Henry VIII's all-powerful Lord Chancellor, died at Leicester Abbey. He had fallen from favour after failing to obtain the annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon.

11-29.title: Colorado troops massacre Cheyenne and Arapaho at Sand Creek
11-29.description: Colonel John Chivington's volunteer cavalry attacked a peaceful camp at Sand Creek, Colorado, killing about 150 to 200 people, mostly women, children and the elderly. Congressional inquiries condemned the attack.

11-29.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
11-29.description: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, recommending separate Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control. Fighting broke out the next day.

11-29.title: Johnson sets up the Warren Commission
11-29.description: President Lyndon Johnson appointed a commission under Chief Justice Earl Warren to investigate Kennedy's assassination. Its 1964 report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone.

11-30.title: Edmund Ironside dies, leaving Cnut king of all England
11-30.description: Edmund II died weeks after agreeing to divide England with the Danish king Cnut. Cnut became sole king, later also ruling Denmark and Norway in a North Sea empire.

11-30.title: Jonathan Swift is born in Dublin
11-30.description: Jonathan Swift, later Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, was born. His Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal made him one of the great satirists in English.

11-30.title: Samuel Clemens, later Mark Twain, is born
11-30.description: Samuel Langhorne Clemens was born in Florida, Missouri. As Mark Twain he wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, drawing on his boyhood on the Mississippi.

11-30.title: Scotland and England play the first international football match
11-30.description: Scotland and England drew 0-0 at Hamilton Crescent in Partick, Glasgow, before about 4,000 spectators. It is recognised by FIFA as the first official international football match.

11-30.title: The Soviet Union invades Finland
11-30.description: Soviet forces attacked Finland, starting the Winter War. Fierce Finnish resistance inflicted heavy losses before Finland ceded territory in March 1940, and the Red Army's poor showing was noted in Berlin.

11-30.title: Bill Clinton becomes the first US president to visit Northern Ireland
11-30.description: Bill Clinton addressed crowds in Belfast and Derry in support of the peace process. The visit added momentum to the talks that produced the Good Friday Agreement in 1998.

12-01.title: Charlemagne convenes an assembly in Rome to judge Pope Leo III
12-01.description: A week after arriving in Rome, Charlemagne called an assembly in St Peter's to hear charges against Pope Leo III, who cleared himself by oath. On Christmas Day Leo crowned Charlemagne emperor.

12-01.title: Henry V enters Paris in triumph
12-01.description: Henry V of England rode into Paris alongside Charles VI of France. Under the Treaty of Troyes he was regent and heir to the French throne, but his death in 1422 left the dual monarchy to his infant son.

12-01.title: Portuguese conspirators end Spanish rule in Lisbon
12-01.description: Nobles stormed the royal palace in Lisbon and proclaimed the Duke of Braganza king as John IV. The coup ended 60 years of union with Spain; the Braganza dynasty reigned until 1910.

12-01.title: Ford installs a moving assembly line for the whole car
12-01.description: At Highland Park, Michigan, Ford began building the Model T on a moving assembly line. Assembly time fell from over 12 hours to about 90 minutes, and cheap cars reshaped modern industry.

12-01.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
12-01.description: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give her seat to a white passenger. The 381-day bus boycott that followed brought Martin Luther King Jr. to national prominence.

12-01.title: Twelve nations sign the Antarctic Treaty
12-01.description: In Washington, twelve countries, including the United States and the Soviet Union, agreed to reserve Antarctica for peaceful scientific research. The treaty banned military activity and froze territorial claims.

12-01.title: Tunnellers from Britain and France meet under the Channel
12-01.description: British and French workers broke through the last wall of rock and shook hands beneath the English Channel. The tunnel opened in 1994, linking Britain to the Continent by rail.

12-02.title: Wren's new St Paul's Cathedral holds its first service
12-02.description: The choir of Christopher Wren's new St Paul's opened for worship with a thanksgiving service for the Peace of Ryswick. The cathedral, replacing the one lost in the Great Fire, was declared complete in 1711.

12-02.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor at Notre-Dame
12-02.description: In the presence of Pope Pius VII, Napoleon placed the imperial crown on his own head and then crowned Josephine. The ceremony proclaimed a new hereditary monarchy born of the Revolution.

12-02.title: Napoleon defeats Austria and Russia at Austerlitz
12-02.description: On the first anniversary of his coronation, Napoleon routed a larger Austro-Russian army at Austerlitz in Moravia. The 'Battle of the Three Emperors' knocked Austria out of the Third Coalition.

12-02.title: Fermi's team achieves the first controlled nuclear chain reaction
12-02.description: Under the stands of Stagg Field at the University of Chicago, Enrico Fermi's team started a self-sustaining chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1. It opened the way to atomic bombs and nuclear power.

12-02.title: The United Arab Emirates is founded
12-02.description: Six of the Trucial States, led by Abu Dhabi and Dubai, formed the United Arab Emirates after Britain's withdrawal from the Gulf. Ras al-Khaimah joined in 1972.

12-03.title: Francis Xavier dies within sight of China
12-03.description: The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier died of fever on Shangchuan Island while waiting to enter mainland China. He had preached in India, South-East Asia and Japan, and was canonised in 1622.

12-03.title: Moreau defeats the Austrians at Hohenlinden
12-03.description: French forces under General Jean Moreau crushed an Austrian army in snowy forest east of Munich. The defeat forced Austria to make peace at Lunéville in February 1801.

12-03.title: Georges Claude shows neon lighting at the Paris Motor Show
12-03.description: At the Paris Motor Show, the French engineer Georges Claude displayed glowing tubes of neon gas. Neon signs soon became a fixture of advertising and city nightlife worldwide.

12-03.title: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
12-03.description: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, Christiaan Barnard's team transplanted a heart into Louis Washkansky. He lived for 18 days before dying of pneumonia, but the operation launched transplant surgery.

12-03.title: Toxic gas leaks from a pesticide plant in Bhopal
12-03.description: Methyl isocyanate escaped from a Union Carbide plant in Bhopal overnight, killing thousands within days. Total deaths are estimated in the range of 15,000 or more, and hundreds of thousands suffered lasting harm.

12-04.title: Carloman dies, leaving Charlemagne sole king of the Franks
12-04.description: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.

12-04.title: The Observer is first published
12-04.description: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.

12-04.title: The National Grange is founded
12-04.description: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.

12-04.title: The Mary Celeste is found drifting and abandoned
12-04.description: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.

12-04.title: Pan Am ceases operations
12-04.description: Pan American World Airways flew its last flight after 64 years. The airline had pioneered transoceanic air travel and launched the Boeing 747, but it never recovered from deregulation, recession and the Lockerbie bombing.

12-05.title: The Senate condemns Catiline's fellow conspirators
12-05.description: After Cicero's fourth speech against Catiline, and Cato's demand for severity, the Senate voted to execute five conspirators without trial. Cicero was hailed as saviour of the Republic but later exiled for it.

12-05.title: John II creates the first franc
12-05.description: By an ordinance issued at Compiègne, the newly released John II of France created the gold franc, partly to raise his ransom. The franc remained the name of French currency until the euro.

12-05.title: Pope Innocent VIII issues a bull against witchcraft
12-05.description: The bull Summis desiderantes affectibus authorised the inquisitors Heinrich Kramer and Jacob Sprenger to pursue witches in Germany. Kramer printed it with his Malleus Maleficarum, fuelling later witch hunts.

12-05.title: Mozart dies in Vienna aged 35
12-05.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart died after a short illness, leaving his Requiem unfinished. In a career of barely three decades he wrote more than 600 works, including The Marriage of Figaro and The Magic Flute.

12-05.title: Prohibition ends in the United States
12-05.description: Utah became the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, repealing national Prohibition. The ban on alcohol had lasted almost 14 years and fed a boom in organised crime.

12-06.title: The Mongols sack Kiev
12-06.description: Batu Khan's army stormed Kiev after a siege, massacring much of the population. A traveller passing a few years later reported barely 200 houses standing; the city's ruin ended Kievan Rus as a power.

12-06.title: Spanish conquistadors found San Francisco de Quito
12-06.description: Sebastián de Benalcázar's men founded the Spanish city of Quito on the site of an Inca centre in the Andes. Its historic centre is today one of the best-preserved colonial cities in the Americas.

12-06.title: The Jacobite army turns back at Derby
12-06.description: Overruling Charles Edward Stuart, his commanders began a retreat from Derby, about 125 miles from London. The rising ended at Culloden in April 1746.

12-06.title: Edison records and plays back 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'
12-06.description: Thomas Edison spoke the nursery rhyme into his tinfoil phonograph and heard his voice played back. It was the first time a machine had reproduced recorded human speech.

12-06.title: Finland declares independence
12-06.description: The Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia, a month after the Bolshevik seizure of power. Lenin's government recognised it at the end of the month.

12-06.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed
12-06.description: Irish and British delegates signed a treaty in London creating the Irish Free State as a dominion, with Northern Ireland able to opt out. Divisions over it led to the Irish Civil War.

12-07.title: Cicero is killed on Mark Antony's orders
12-07.description: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate, Marcus Tullius Cicero was overtaken by soldiers near Formiae and killed. His head and hands were displayed in the Forum, where he had attacked Antony in his Philippics.

12-07.title: The Theatre Royal, Covent Garden, opens
12-07.description: John Rich opened his new theatre at Covent Garden with Congreve's The Way of the World. Twice rebuilt after fires, it became the Royal Opera House in 1892.

12-07.title: Marshal Ney is executed by firing squad
12-07.description: Michel Ney, whom Napoleon called 'the bravest of the brave', was shot in Paris for treason after joining his former emperor during the Hundred Days. He refused a blindfold and is said to have given the order to fire.

12-07.title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
12-07.description: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, killing more than 2,400 Americans and sinking or damaging 19 ships. The United States entered the Second World War the next day.

12-07.title: Indonesia invades East Timor
12-07.description: Indonesian forces invaded East Timor nine days after Fretilin declared independence from Portugal. The occupation cost an estimated 100,000 to 180,000 lives before a UN-supervised vote led to independence.

12-08.title: Washington's army retreats across the Delaware
12-08.description: The last of George Washington's beaten Continental Army crossed the Delaware into Pennsylvania, taking every boat to stop British pursuit. Weeks later he crossed back to strike at Trenton.

12-08.title: Pius IX defines the Immaculate Conception
12-08.description: In the bull Ineffabilis Deus, Pope Pius IX declared as dogma that the Virgin Mary was conceived without original sin. Other Christian traditions do not accept the doctrine.

12-08.title: The United States and Britain declare war on Japan
12-08.description: Franklin Roosevelt asked Congress to declare war, calling 7 December 'a date which will live in infamy'. Congress agreed within the hour, and Britain also declared war on Japan.

12-08.title: John Lennon is shot dead in New York
12-08.description: Mark David Chapman shot John Lennon outside the Dakota building in Manhattan. The killing of the former Beatle prompted vigils around the world.

12-08.title: Leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agree to dissolve the USSR
12-08.description: Meeting in the Belovezha Forest, Boris Yeltsin, Leonid Kravchuk and Stanislav Shushkevich declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and created the Commonwealth of Independent States.

12-09.title: Malcolm IV, the 'Maiden King' of Scotland, dies
12-09.description: Malcolm IV died unmarried at 24, after a reign in which he surrendered Northumbria and Cumbria to Henry II of England. His brother William the Lion succeeded him and reigned for 49 years.

12-09.title: Juan Diego reports a vision of the Virgin at Tepeyac
12-09.description: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to the Indigenous convert Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe became Mexico's most revered religious symbol.

12-09.title: Jerusalem surrenders to British forces
12-09.description: The mayor of Jerusalem surrendered the city to the British army, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule. General Allenby entered on foot two days later.

12-09.title: British forces launch Operation Compass in Egypt
12-09.description: British and Commonwealth troops attacked Italian camps in western Egypt. In two months they advanced 500 miles and took some 130,000 prisoners, before Rommel's arrival turned the tide.

12-09.title: Tanganyika becomes independent
12-09.description: Tanganyika became independent from Britain, with Julius Nyerere as prime minister. In 1964 it united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.

12-10.title: Luther burns the papal bull against him
12-10.description: Outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate, Martin Luther burned Leo X's bull threatening him with excommunication, along with books of canon law. Rome excommunicated him the following month.

12-10.title: Mississippi becomes the 20th US state
12-10.description: Mississippi was admitted to the Union. Its fertile lands became the heart of the cotton economy built on slavery, and later a key battleground of the civil rights movement.

12-10.title: Wyoming Territory gives women the vote
12-10.description: Governor John Campbell signed a law granting women in Wyoming Territory the right to vote and hold office, the first such law in the United States. Wyoming is still called the 'Equality State'.

12-10.title: Alfred Nobel dies in San Remo
12-10.description: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite, died in Italy. His will left most of his fortune to fund prizes, first awarded on the anniversary of his death in 1901.

12-10.title: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
12-10.description: Meeting in Paris, the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights without a vote against. The drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.

12-11.title: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, last native Prince of Wales, is killed
12-11.description: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed near Cilmeri during Edward I's conquest of Wales. Wales lost its independence, and in 1301 Edward gave the title Prince of Wales to his own son.

12-11.title: James II flees London
12-11.description: As William of Orange advanced, James II slipped out of Whitehall and dropped the Great Seal into the Thames. Caught at Faversham, he escaped to France later that month; Parliament treated his flight as abdication.

12-11.title: Louis XVI goes on trial before the National Convention
12-11.description: The deposed king, now called Louis Capet, appeared before the National Convention to answer charges of treason. He was convicted and guillotined in January 1793.

12-11.title: Edward VIII abdicates to marry Wallis Simpson
12-11.description: The abdication took legal effect, and that evening Edward broadcast that he could not reign 'without the help and support of the woman I love'. His brother succeeded as George VI.

12-11.title: Germany and Italy declare war on the United States
12-11.description: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Hitler and Mussolini declared war on the United States. The decision brought American power fully into the war in Europe.

12-12.title: Heraclius defeats the Persians near Nineveh
12-12.description: The Byzantine emperor Heraclius routed a Sasanian army near the ruins of Nineveh in Mesopotamia. The victory ended a 26-year war, but both exhausted empires soon fell prey to the Arab conquests.

12-12.title: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
12-12.description: At Signal Hill in Newfoundland, Guglielmo Marconi heard the Morse letter 'S' sent from Poldhu in Cornwall, some 3,500 kilometres away. The feat showed that radio could span oceans.

12-12.title: George V announces the move of India's capital to Delhi
12-12.description: At the Delhi Durbar, attended by hundreds of thousands, King-Emperor George V announced that the capital of British India would move from Calcutta to Delhi. New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931.

12-12.title: Kenya gains independence with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister
12-12.description: Kenya became independent from Britain. Jomo Kenyatta, jailed by the colonial authorities during the Mau Mau emergency, became prime minister and later the country's first president.

12-12.title: The Supreme Court halts the Florida recount in Bush v. Gore
12-12.description: By five votes to four, the US Supreme Court stopped the manual recount of presidential votes in Florida. The ruling left George W. Bush the winner of Florida, and of the presidency, by 537 votes.

12-13.title: Pope Celestine V resigns after five months
12-13.description: The hermit-pope Celestine V renounced the papacy, overwhelmed by its politics. Dante appears to condemn him for 'the great refusal', but the church later canonised him.

12-13.title: The Council of Trent opens
12-13.description: The Catholic Church's council opened at Trent in northern Italy and met, with long breaks, until 1563. It reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against Protestant teaching and reformed clerical discipline.

12-13.title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
12-13.description: Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sighted the west coast of New Zealand's South Island, the first recorded European sighting. A violent encounter with Māori in Golden Bay days later meant his crew never landed.

12-13.title: Japanese troops capture Nanjing
