12-13.description: Japanese forces took China's capital, Nanjing, and began weeks of mass killing, rape and looting. Estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to over 300,000, and the massacre remains bitterly contested.

12-13.title: British cruisers fight the Graf Spee at the River Plate
12-13.description: Three British cruisers engaged the German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee off the River Plate estuary. Damaged, she took refuge in Montevideo, and four days later her captain scuttled her.

12-14.title: An earthquake shakes Constantinople and weakens Hagia Sophia
12-14.description: A powerful earthquake damaged much of Constantinople and cracked the great dome of Hagia Sophia, which collapsed the following May. It was rebuilt higher and rededicated in 562.

12-14.title: Nostradamus is born in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence
12-14.description: Michel de Nostredame, physician and astrologer, was born in Provence. His Prophecies of 1555, written in vague rhymed quatrains, have been claimed as predictions of countless later events.

12-14.title: George Washington dies at Mount Vernon
12-14.description: George Washington died aged 67 after a throat infection, worsened by heavy bloodletting. Having twice given up power, as commander and as president, he was mourned as the father of his country.

12-14.title: Max Planck presents the quantum hypothesis
12-14.description: Before the German Physical Society in Berlin, Max Planck proposed that energy is emitted in discrete packets, or quanta. The idea, introduced to solve a problem in heat radiation, became the basis of quantum physics.

12-14.title: Roald Amundsen's party reaches the South Pole
12-14.description: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and four companions became the first people to reach the South Pole. Robert Falcon Scott's British party arrived 34 days later to find the Norwegian tent and flag.

12-15.title: The future emperor Nero is born at Antium
12-15.description: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

12-15.title: The Bill of Rights is ratified
12-15.description: Virginia's approval gave the first ten amendments to the US Constitution the required three-quarters of states. They guarantee freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly, and rights to due process.

12-15.title: Sitting Bull is killed at Standing Rock
12-15.description: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.

12-15.title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
12-15.description: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.

12-15.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens
12-15.description: After eleven years of closure and stabilisation work, the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopened to visitors. Engineers had reduced its tilt by about 44 centimetres, securing it for centuries.

12-16.title: Pepin of Herstal, ruler of the Franks, dies
12-16.description: Pepin of Herstal, the mayor of the palace who held real power over the Frankish kingdoms, died at Jupille. After a struggle, his son Charles Martel took control and laid the ground for the Carolingian dynasty.

12-16.title: Henry VI is crowned king of France in Paris
12-16.description: The ten-year-old Henry VI of England was crowned king of France at Notre-Dame. By 1453 the English had lost all their French lands except Calais.

12-16.title: The Boston Tea Party
12-16.description: Colonists, some disguised as Mohawk Indians, boarded three ships in Boston Harbor and threw 342 chests of East India Company tea into the water. Britain's punitive response pushed the colonies towards revolution.

12-16.title: Voortrekkers defeat a Zulu army at Blood River
12-16.description: A laager of about 470 Voortrekkers repelled thousands of Zulu warriors sent by King Dingane at the Ncome River. The victory became a central symbol of Afrikaner nationalism.

12-16.title: Germany launches the Battle of the Bulge
12-16.description: German forces attacked through the Ardennes in Belgium and Luxembourg, catching the Americans by surprise. The offensive was contained within weeks and used up Germany's last reserves in the west.

12-16.title: Kazakhstan declares independence
12-16.description: Kazakhstan became the last Soviet republic to declare independence, days before the USSR was dissolved. Nursultan Nazarbayev led the vast Central Asian country for nearly three decades.

12-17.title: Totila's Ostrogoths take Rome
12-17.description: After a long siege, the Ostrogothic king Totila entered Rome when Isaurian guards opened a gate. The city, fought over repeatedly in Justinian's Gothic War, was left largely depopulated.

12-17.title: Pope Paul III excommunicates Henry VIII
12-17.description: Pope Paul III published the bull of excommunication against Henry VIII, prepared in 1535 but suspended. It came after Henry's agents destroyed the shrine of Thomas Becket at Canterbury.

12-17.title: The Wright brothers make the first powered flights
12-17.description: At Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds and about 37 metres. Of four flights that day, Wilbur's longest lasted 59 seconds.

12-17.title: The Graf Spee is scuttled off Montevideo
12-17.description: Believing a superior British force waited outside, Captain Hans Langsdorff scuttled the Admiral Graf Spee in the River Plate. He took his own life three days later.

12-17.title: The Simpsons premieres as a series
12-17.description: Fox broadcast the first full episode of The Simpsons, a Christmas special. It became the longest-running American animated series and scripted primetime show.

12-18.title: Americans observe the first national day of thanksgiving
12-18.description: The Continental Congress set aside 18 December as a day of thanksgiving for the victory at Saratoga. It was the first such national observance by the new United States.

12-18.title: The 13th Amendment abolishing slavery is proclaimed
12-18.description: Secretary of State William Seward certified that the 13th Amendment had been ratified by the required number of states. It abolished slavery throughout the United States, freeing about four million people.

12-18.title: 'Piltdown Man' is presented to the Geological Society
12-18.description: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward announced fossils from Piltdown in Sussex as an early human ancestor. In 1953 they were exposed as a forgery combining a human skull and an orang-utan jaw.

12-18.title: The Battle of Verdun ends
12-18.description: After ten months of fighting, French counter-attacks closed the Battle of Verdun. About 700,000 French and German soldiers were killed, wounded or missing, and the front was almost back where it began.

12-18.title: The US launches SCORE, the first communications satellite
12-18.description: An Atlas rocket placed Project SCORE in orbit. The next day it broadcast a recorded Christmas message from President Eisenhower, the first voice transmitted from space.

12-19.title: Catholics and Huguenots clash at Dreux
12-19.description: The first major battle of the French Wars of Religion was fought at Dreux, west of Paris. Both armies' commanders were captured, and the bloody outcome showed the war would be long.

12-19.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
12-19.description: About 12,000 Continental soldiers marched into camp at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. Some 2,000 died of disease over the winter, but drilling under Baron von Steuben made the survivors a more effective army.

12-19.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
12-19.description: Charles Dickens's novella about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge went on sale and sold out its first printing by Christmas Eve. It shaped Victorian ideals of a charitable, family-centred Christmas.

12-19.title: The House impeaches President Clinton
12-19.description: The US House of Representatives impeached Bill Clinton for perjury and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky affair. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999.

12-20.title: Virginia Company ships sail for America
12-20.description: The Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery left London with about 105 colonists. In May 1607 they founded Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America.

12-20.title: The United States takes possession of Louisiana
12-20.description: In a ceremony in New Orleans, France formally handed the Louisiana Territory to the United States. The purchase roughly doubled the country's size and gave it control of the Mississippi.

12-20.title: South Carolina secedes from the Union
12-20.description: A convention in Charleston voted unanimously to leave the United States after Lincoln's election. Six more states followed before his inauguration, forming the Confederacy.

12-20.title: The United States invades Panama
12-20.description: US forces launched Operation Just Cause to remove Panama's military ruler Manuel Noriega, who was wanted in the US on drug trafficking charges. Noriega surrendered on 3 January 1990.

12-20.title: Argentina's president resigns amid riots
12-20.description: President Fernando de la Rúa resigned and fled the Casa Rosada by helicopter as protests over economic collapse left dozens dead. Days later Argentina declared the largest sovereign default to that date.

12-21.title: The Senate recognises Vespasian as emperor
12-21.description: The day after Vitellius was killed in Rome, the Senate granted Vespasian the powers of emperor, ending the Year of the Four Emperors. His Flavian dynasty restored stability and began the Colosseum.

12-21.title: A Mayflower party lands at Plymouth
12-21.description: An exploring party from the Mayflower landed at Plymouth harbour, where the Pilgrims decided to settle (11 December Old Style). Half the colonists died during the first winter.

12-21.title: The Curies identify radium
12-21.description: Working in a Paris shed, Marie and Pierre Curie detected a new, intensely radioactive element in pitchblende, announced days later as radium. Isolating it took Marie Curie another twelve years.

12-21.title: Apollo 8 launches for the Moon
12-21.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders lifted off on the first crewed flight to leave Earth's orbit. On Christmas Eve they orbited the Moon and photographed 'Earthrise'.

12-21.title: A bomb destroys Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie
12-21.description: A bomb exploded aboard a Boeing 747 over Lockerbie in Scotland, killing all 259 on board and 11 people on the ground. A Libyan intelligence officer was convicted in 2001.

12-22.title: Stephen of Blois is crowned king of England
12-22.description: Weeks after Henry I's death, his nephew Stephen was crowned at Westminster despite having sworn to support Henry's daughter, the Empress Matilda. The civil war that followed became known as the Anarchy.

12-22.title: The Old Pretender lands in Scotland, too late
12-22.description: James Francis Edward Stuart landed at Peterhead to lead the Jacobite rising. After the defeat at Preston and the stalemate at Sheriffmuir in November, the cause was failing, and he sailed back to France in February.

12-22.title: A court martial convicts Captain Alfred Dreyfus
12-22.description: A French military court convicted the Jewish officer Alfred Dreyfus of passing secrets to Germany and sentenced him to deportation for life. His innocence, and the cover-up, split France in the Dreyfus Affair.

12-22.title: The SR-71 Blackbird makes its first flight
12-22.description: Lockheed's SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft first flew at Palmdale, California. Able to cruise above Mach 3 at about 25,000 metres, it remains the fastest crewed jet-powered aircraft.

12-23.title: George Washington resigns his military command
12-23.description: In the Maryland State House at Annapolis, George Washington returned his commission to Congress. A victorious general giving up power voluntarily set a lasting precedent for civilian control of the military.

12-23.title: Jane Austen's Emma is published
12-23.description: John Murray published Emma, though its title page bore the date 1816. Austen's comedy of a confident young matchmaker is often judged her most accomplished novel.

12-23.title: Vincent van Gogh cuts off part of his ear
12-23.description: After a quarrel with Paul Gauguin in Arles, Vincent van Gogh cut off part of his left ear. Months later he entered the asylum at Saint-Rémy, where he painted The Starry Night.

12-23.title: Bell Labs demonstrates the transistor
12-23.description: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain showed colleagues at Bell Laboratories their point-contact transistor amplifying a signal. Transistors replaced vacuum tubes and made modern electronics possible.

12-24.title: Napoleon survives a bomb in the rue Saint-Nicaise
12-24.description: Royalist plotters exploded a barrel bomb in a Paris street as the First Consul's carriage passed, killing several bystanders but missing Napoleon. He used the attack to deport Jacobin opponents.

12-24.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
12-24.description: British and American negotiators signed a peace treaty at Ghent, restoring pre-war borders. News travelled slowly, and the Battle of New Orleans was fought two weeks later.

12-24.title: Fire destroys much of the Library of Congress
12-24.description: A fire in the Capitol destroyed about 35,000 of the Library of Congress's 55,000 books, including around two-thirds of the collection bought from Thomas Jefferson in 1815.

12-24.title: The Christmas Truce begins on the Western Front
12-24.description: On Christmas Eve, soldiers along parts of the front sang carols across the lines. Over the next day many British and German troops met in no man's land, swapped gifts and buried their dead.

12-24.title: Apollo 8 orbits the Moon
12-24.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first people to orbit the Moon. They photographed 'Earthrise' and read from Genesis in a Christmas Eve broadcast seen by millions.

12-25.title: The earliest recorded Christmas on 25 December
12-25.description: A Roman calendar compiled in 354 records the birth of Christ celebrated in Rome on 25 December 336, the earliest evidence for the date. Why it was chosen remains debated.

12-25.title: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor
12-25.description: During Christmas Mass in St Peter's, Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans. It revived a western imperial title unused since 476.

12-25.title: William the Conqueror is crowned at Westminster
12-25.description: William of Normandy was crowned king of England in Westminster Abbey. Norman soldiers, mistaking the congregation's acclamation for a riot, set fire to nearby houses.

12-25.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
12-25.description: On Christmas night, George Washington led about 2,400 soldiers across the ice-choked Delaware River. At dawn they surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton.

12-25.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
12-25.description: In a televised address, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned. That evening the Soviet flag was lowered from the Kremlin and replaced by the Russian tricolour.

12-26.title: Washington defeats the Hessians at Trenton
12-26.description: Washington's army surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton, capturing about 900 soldiers with few American losses. The victory revived the Revolution after months of defeat.

12-26.title: The Decembrist revolt fails in St Petersburg
12-26.description: Army officers led troops onto Senate Square to refuse allegiance to Nicholas I and demand reform. Cannon fire dispersed them; five leaders were hanged, and the Decembrists inspired later Russian radicals.

12-26.title: The Curies announce the discovery of radium
12-26.description: A paper presented to the French Academy of Sciences announced radium, a new element found in pitchblende by Marie and Pierre Curie with Gustave Bémont. It later proved vital in early cancer treatment.

12-26.title: An earthquake and tsunami devastate the Indian Ocean
12-26.description: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra sent tsunamis across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in 14 countries. Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand were worst hit.

12-27.title: Justinian dedicates Hagia Sophia
12-27.description: Emperor Justinian dedicated the new church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built in under six years. It was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years and later served as a mosque and a museum.

12-27.title: HMS Beagle sails with Charles Darwin aboard
12-27.description: HMS Beagle left Plymouth on a surveying voyage with the 22-year-old naturalist Charles Darwin. His observations over the five-year journey shaped his later theory of evolution.

12-27.title: Peter Pan opens on the London stage
12-27.description: J. M. Barrie's play Peter Pan, or the Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up opened at the Duke of York's Theatre. Its story of Neverland, Captain Hook and Tinker Bell became a children's classic.

12-27.title: Soviet special forces kill Afghanistan's leader Hafizullah Amin
12-27.description: As Soviet troops poured into Afghanistan, commandos stormed the Tajbeg Palace in Kabul and killed President Amin. The decade-long war that followed cost hundreds of thousands of Afghan lives.

12-28.title: Edward the Confessor's Westminster Abbey is consecrated
12-28.description: Edward the Confessor's new abbey church at Westminster was consecrated, though the king was too ill to attend and died a week later. Every crowned English monarch since 1066 has been crowned there.

12-28.title: Galileo observes Neptune without realising it
12-28.description: While observing Jupiter, Galileo recorded a faint 'star' that was in fact Neptune. He did not recognise it as a planet, and its formal discovery came only in 1846.

12-28.title: John C. Calhoun becomes the first US vice-president to resign
12-28.description: John C. Calhoun resigned the vice-presidency to take a Senate seat, where he could better defend South Carolina during the Nullification Crisis. He had served under both John Quincy Adams and Andrew Jackson.

12-28.title: The Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film screening
12-28.description: At the Grand Café in Paris, Auguste and Louis Lumière projected ten short films to a paying audience. The screening is often taken as the birth of cinema.

12-28.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina
12-28.description: A powerful earthquake and tsunami struck the Strait of Messina, destroying Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria. Around 75,000 to 80,000 people died, making it Europe's deadliest recorded earthquake.

12-29.title: Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
12-29.description: Four knights, believing they were carrying out Henry II's wishes, killed Archbishop Thomas Becket in his cathedral. Becket was canonised in 1173, and Canterbury became one of Europe's great pilgrimage sites.

12-29.title: British forces capture Savannah
12-29.description: A British expedition took Savannah, Georgia, opening a new campaign in the American South. The southern strategy brought early gains but ended with surrender at Yorktown in 1781.

12-29.title: Texas becomes the 28th US state
12-29.description: Nine years after winning independence from Mexico, Texas was admitted to the Union as a slave state. The annexation helped provoke the Mexican-American War the following year.

12-29.title: US troops massacre Lakota at Wounded Knee
12-29.description: While disarming a band of Lakota at Wounded Knee Creek, South Dakota, the 7th Cavalry opened fire, killing some 250 to 300 men, women and children. It marked the end of the Plains wars.

12-29.title: Firebombs start the 'Second Great Fire of London'
12-29.description: German bombers dropped thousands of incendiaries on the City of London, starting some 1,500 fires. Much of the square mile burned, but St Paul's Cathedral survived amid the smoke.

12-30.title: Richard, Duke of York, is killed at Wakefield
12-30.description: Lancastrian forces defeated and killed Richard, Duke of York, near Wakefield. His son Edward avenged him at Towton three months later and took the throne as Edward IV.

12-30.title: The Gadsden Purchase treaty is signed
12-30.description: US minister James Gadsden signed a treaty in Mexico City buying land south of the Gila River for a railway route. It fixed the modern border of southern Arizona and New Mexico.

12-30.title: Grigori Rasputin is murdered in Petrograd
12-30.description: Nobles led by Prince Felix Yusupov killed Rasputin, the mystic whose influence over the imperial family had become a scandal (17 December, Old Style). The murder did not save the monarchy, which fell weeks later.

12-30.title: The Soviet Union is formally established
12-30.description: Delegates from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian Federation approved the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. It lasted until 1991.

12-30.title: Saddam Hussein is executed in Baghdad
12-30.description: The former Iraqi president was hanged for crimes against humanity over the Dujail killings. A leaked mobile phone video of the jeering at his execution caused controversy.

12-31.title: Emperor Commodus is assassinated
12-31.description: Conspirators including his mistress Marcia and the praetorian prefect had the wrestler Narcissus strangle Commodus in his bath. The murder ushered in the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.

12-31.title: Elizabeth I charters the East India Company
12-31.description: Elizabeth I granted a monopoly of English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope to a company of London merchants. The East India Company eventually ruled much of India until 1858.

12-31.title: Edison gives a public demonstration of electric lighting
12-31.description: Thomas Edison lit his Menlo Park laboratory and nearby streets with incandescent lamps for crowds who came by special train. The display showed electric light could be a practical system.

12-31.title: Truman proclaims the end of hostilities in the Second World War
12-31.description: President Truman formally proclaimed the cessation of hostilities, more than a year after Japan's surrender. The legal state of war with Germany and Japan ended later, with peace treaties.

12-31.title: The last Soviet institutions cease to function
12-31.description: By the end of the year, all remaining institutions of the Soviet Union had ceased to operate, days after Gorbachev's resignation. Fifteen independent states took its place.

12-31.title: Boris Yeltsin resigns and hands power to Vladimir Putin
12-31.description: In a New Year's Eve television address, Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly resigned as president of Russia. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin became acting president and won election in March 2000.
